profile.plan: Fiends that trigger when a card effect discards them, so the deck throws its own hand away on purpose and turns each discard into a search, a Special Summon or removal.

hooks.label: Discards your own hand
hooks.why: Grapha, Snoww, Sillva and the rest only work when a card effect discards them, so any outside card that makes you discard is an activator.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Dark World monster is a Fiend, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: Sends its own cards from the Deck to the GY; Tearlaments monsters sent there by a card effect Fusion Summon by shuffling materials from the hand, field and GY back into the Deck.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Scheiren, Havnis and Merrli Fusion Summon when a card effect sends them to the GY, so every outside card that mills is another way to start.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The deck mills three to five cards at a time, so outside monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: The Main Deck Tearlaments monsters are all Aqua, and their Fusions ask for Aqua materials.

profile.plan: A Level 7 Psychic Xyz deck that freely Special Summons its own monsters, keeps banishing the opponent's cards face-down to lock their zones with Shangri-Ira, and recycles everything it banishes.

hooks.label: Level 7 self-summoners
hooks.why: Shangri-Ira needs 2+ Level 7 monsters and Kashtira Birth Normal Summons Level 7s without Tributing, so every Level 7 that Special Summons itself is free Xyz material.

hooks.label: Banished-trigger cards
hooks.why: Tearlaments Kashtira and Scareclaw Kashtira banish a card from your hand or GY as part of their own Summon, so outside cards that do something when they are banished get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Kashtiratheosis, Kashtira Big Bang, Kashtira Akstra and Kashtira Overlap all have effects that trigger when they are banished, so outside cards that banish your hand, Deck or GY set those off.

hooks.label: Face-down banishers
hooks.why: Shangri-Ira locks one of the opponent's Main Monster Zones or Spell & Trap Zones every time a card they own is banished face-down, so more face-down banishing from outside means more locked zones.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Kashtira Birth lets you Normal Summon Level 7 monsters without Tributing, so an extra Normal Summon turns one tribute-less body into two and makes a Rank 7 Xyz possible.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Kashtira Main Deck monster except Riseheart is Psychic, and Shangri-Ira is a Psychic Xyz Monster, so Psychic support reaches nearly the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Wyrm Synchro deck that makes Level 4 Tuner Tokens, Synchro Summons with them, then repeatedly banishes cards to trigger its own graveyard and on-field effects.

hooks.label: Banishes any card
hooks.why: Chengying, Swordsoul Strife, The Abyss Dragon Swordsoul and The Golden Swordsoul all trigger whenever a card is banished, so any outside card that banishes turns their effects on.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Almost every Swordsoul monster and Synchro is a Wyrm, and Chixiao, Taia and Strife all need Wyrm cards as material, cost or target, so Wyrm-locked support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wyrm that triggers when banished
hooks.why: Chixiao and Taia banish a Wyrm monster from the hand or GY as a cost and Strife banishes Wyrms from hand, Deck or GY, so an outside Wyrm with an effect when it is banished is used for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Swordsoul Auspice Chunjun Tributes 1 monster to Special Summon itself from the hand, so an outside monster with an effect when it is Tributed gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Swordsoul of Mo Ye only starts the combo off a Normal or Special Summon and every Swordsoul Main Deck monster competes for the one Normal Summon, so extra Normal Summons let you play a second one.

profile.plan: A Tribute Summon deck: it puts Continuous Spells and Traps on the field, Tributes them instead of monsters to bring out its Level 5-9 Wyrm bosses, and those bosses answer the opponent while the Spells and Traps refund themselves from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Continuous Spells/Traps that float
hooks.why: Ignis Heat, Majesty Maiden, Dinomight Knight and Master Peace can Tribute a Continuous Spell/Trap you control instead of a monster, so an outside Continuous Spell/Trap that does something when it is sent from the Spell & Trap Zone to the GY turns the Tribute cost into profit.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Master Peace, Metaltron XII and the Level 5-6 True Draco monsters all have to be Tribute Summoned, so effects that grant an extra Normal Summon or an additional Tribute Summon put a boss on board the turn they are drawn.

hooks.label: Monsters that float when destroyed
hooks.why: Dragonic Diagram destroys a card you control or in hand to search, True Draco Apocalypse destroys your own card to halve the opponent's stats and Mariamne needs two monsters destroyed, so outside monsters with an effect when they are destroyed by card effect are free fuel.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Every True Draco monster is a Wyrm, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Wyrms apply to the entire deck.

hooks.label: Searches Continuous Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Each Tribute Summon in the deck wants a Continuous Spell/Trap already on the field to pay for it, so cards that add or place a Continuous Spell/Trap from the Deck keep the engine supplied.

profile.plan: A Spell-dense control deck that keeps its Main Monster Zone empty, Link Summons Sky Striker Ace monsters into the Extra Monster Zone, swaps them with Raye/Roze, and recycles its Quick-Play Spells while counting toward 3 or more Spells in the GY.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Sky Striker Ace Link Monster, plus Cyanos, Aileron and the Sages, is a Machine, and Cyanos even locks your Extra Deck Summons into Machine monsters.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with Spells
hooks.why: Widow Anchor, Afterburners, Jamming Waves, Shark Cannon, Scissors Cross, Vector Blast and Hercules Base all check for 3 or more Spells in your GY, so anything that puts Spells there powers the whole deck up.

hooks.label: Spells that want to be banished
hooks.why: Sage of Strength - Akash, Sage of Wisdom - Himmel, Sage of Benevolence - Ciela, Surgical Striker - S.P.E.C.T.R.A. and Azalea Temperance all banish Spells from your hand or GY as a cost, so a Spell with an effect when it is banished is free value.

hooks.label: Spell activation payoffs
hooks.why: The deck fires off several Sky Striker Spells every turn, and Multirole re-Sets them from the GY while Kagari recovers them, so cards that trigger each time a Spell Card is activated keep going off.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger in the GY
hooks.why: Multirole, Linkage!, Area Zero and Zeke all send one of your own cards to the GY as a cost, so a monster with an effect when it is sent to the GY is used for free.

hooks.label: Spell discard outlets
hooks.why: Cyanos, Ciela, Akash and Himmel Special Summon themselves by discarding a Spell from your hand, turning any Spell you would rather have in the GY than in hand into a body.

profile.plan: A Tribute Summon combo deck that dumps Clown Crew monsters onto the field, then Tributes them for high-Level Tribute Summons so every Tribute cashes in for card draw, extra attacks or wiping the opponent's Extra Deck monsters.

hooks.label: Tributing your own monsters
hooks.why: Nearly every Clown Crew monster has an 'If this card is Tributed' effect (Biancaviso, Flair, Meteor, Diabolo, Fiends, Cappello, Dristy), so outside cards that Tribute your monsters turn into searches, Extra Deck hate and removal for free.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes its own monsters as cost (Clown Crew Rehearsal, Malabarisme, Finale, plus Biancaviso's own Tribute Summon), so any outside monster with an effect when it is Tributed gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: Effects triggered by Tributes
hooks.why: Rehearsal, Malabarisme, Soiree Operations, Biancaviso and New Face all Tribute monsters repeatedly, so outside cards that trigger whenever a monster is Tributed get a trigger every turn.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Biancaviso and Soiree Operations let you Tribute Summon during the opponent's Main Phase and the whole deck loops through Tribute Summoning, so extra Normal/Tribute Summons keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Cheap-to-Tribute Level 5+ bosses
hooks.why: Clown Crew Fiends gives Tribute Summoned monsters +1000 ATK, Dristy a second attack, Diabolo double piercing and Cappello 1500 DEF loss, so any high-Level monster you can Tribute Summon with one Tribute becomes a payoff.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior and LIGHT support
hooks.why: Every Clown Crew monster is LIGHT and all but Biancaviso are Beast-Warrior, so Type and Attribute support searches and revives the entire deck.

profile.plan: A Dragon beatdown deck built on Level 7 Normal Monsters and 'Red-Eyes' naming, using Red-Eyes Fusion dumps, GY revival and rank 7 Xyz to field big Dragons with burn and negation on top.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Red-Eyes Darkness Metal Dragon Special Summons a Dragon from the hand or GY and banishes a face-up Dragon to summon itself, and almost every Red-Eyes monster is a Dragon.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: The Black Stone of Legend, Paladin of Dark Dragon, Red-Eyes Alternative Black Dragon and Red-Eyes Darkness Dragon all Tribute a monster as the cost to Special Summon a Red-Eyes from the Deck or hand, so outside monsters that do something when Tributed get that for free.

hooks.label: Extra Fusion Summoning
hooks.why: The deck wins through Red-Eyes Fusion, Meteor Black Comet Dragon, Red-Eyes Slash Dragon and Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon, so outside cards that Fusion Summon or set up Fusion Materials add extra bodies the archetype's own Fusion Spell cannot.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Machine deck that Special Summons Cyber Dragon and its look-alikes, stacks Level 5 bodies into Nova/Infinity, and Fusions with Machine materials by banishing and shuffling its own monsters.

hooks.label: LIGHT Machine support
hooks.why: Every Cyber Dragon monster is a LIGHT Machine, and both Cyber Emergency and Cyber Repair Plant only ever look for LIGHT Machine monsters, so any outside card that supports that Type or Attribute helps the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning LIGHT Machines
hooks.why: Cyber Dragon Special Summons itself from the hand when only your opponent controls a monster, and Nova needs two Level 5 Machines, so outside Machines that Special Summon themselves are free Xyz material.

hooks.label: Discard-trigger monsters
hooks.why: Cyber Dragon Nachster discards 1 other monster as the cost to Special Summon itself, so outside monsters that do something when they are discarded get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Recovers banished Machines
hooks.why: Nova, Cybernetic Overflow, Cyber Network, Cyber Pharos and Super Strident Blaze all banish your own LIGHT Machine monsters, and Cyberload Fusion only uses face-up banished cards, so outside cards that bring banished Machines back reload the deck.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck of Flip monsters that trigger when sent to the GY by card effects, using Shaddoll Fusion to send materials from the Deck and flipping its monsters to control the field.

hooks.label: Sent to GY triggers
hooks.why: Every Shaddoll monster has an effect when sent to the GY by a card effect, so outside monsters with similar triggers get value from Shaddoll Fusion, Squamata and Sinister Shadow Games.

hooks.label: Mills a monster
hooks.why: Shaddoll Fusion and Squamata send Shaddoll monsters from the Deck to the GY to trigger their effects, so outside cards that send any monster from Deck to GY do the same.

hooks.label: Fusion Material triggers
hooks.why: The deck Fusion Summons constantly using monsters from the hand and field, so outside monsters with effects when used as Fusion Material give extra value.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-up
hooks.why: The deck Sets its Shaddoll monsters and flips them with Sinister Shadow Games or Resh Shaddoll Incarnation; outside cards that flip a face-down monster face-up trigger the FLIP effects.

profile.plan: The deck revolves around Blue-Eyes White Dragon and its many forms, using Level 1 LIGHT Tuners to Synchro Summon, Fusion and Ritual Summoning powerful Dragons, and constantly reviving or searching the iconic Normal Monster.

hooks.label: Sends a Dragon to GY
hooks.why: The White Stone of Legend and The White Stone of Ancients trigger when sent to the GY, and Blue-Eyes Abyss Dragon, Jet Dragon and Chaos Form all want Blue-Eyes White Dragon in the GY.

hooks.label: Revives a Dragon Normal Monster
hooks.why: Blue-Eyes White Dragon is a Normal Monster, and True Light and Beacon of White Special Summon it from the GY, so outside cards that do the same are extra copies of that effect.

hooks.label: Ritual searcher
hooks.why: The deck Ritual Summons Blue-Eyes Chaos MAX Dragon and Blue-Eyes Chaos Dragon with Chaos Form, so outside Ritual support that searches a Ritual Monster or Ritual Spell helps assemble the combo.

hooks.label: Normal Monster searcher
hooks.why: Blue-Eyes White Dragon is a Normal Monster, and the deck needs it in hand for Blue-Eyes Alternative White Dragon and Dictator of D., so outside cards that search a Normal Monster are extra copies of that.

profile.plan: A DARK Spellcaster deck that searches out and Special Summons Dark Magician, then uses it as Fusion and Ritual material, with effects that trigger whenever a Spell/Trap is activated.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck monster in the archetype is a Spellcaster, and cards like Magician Navigation, Palladium Oracle Mana and Dark Magic Expanded reward controlling or summoning them.

hooks.label: Spells/Traps with GY effects
hooks.why: Magicians' Souls sends Spells/Traps from your hand or field to the GY as a cost, and Magician's Robe discards them, so Spells/Traps with an effect when sent to the GY get value for free.

hooks.label: Spellcasters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Illusion Magic, Magician's Rod and Magicians' Combination all Tribute Spellcaster monsters as a cost, so Spellcasters with an effect when Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Level 6+ Spellcasters with GY effects
hooks.why: Magicians' Souls sends a Level 6 or higher Spellcaster from your Deck to the GY as a cost, so any such monster with a GY effect triggers immediately.

profile.plan: A Fiend deck that pays Life Points every turn and grinds the GY: the chess Archfiends pay upkeeps, Heiress and Gilfer want to be sent to the Graveyard, and Bone Archfiend climbs into the DARK Dragon 'Red Dragon Archfiend' Synchros.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: The whole archetype is Fiend: Masterking Archfiend needs 2 Fiend monsters, Archfiend's Ghastly Glitch needs a Fiend on board, and Archfiend Emperor locks you into Fiend-only Special Summons.

hooks.label: Puts your Fiends in the GY
hooks.why: Archfiend Heiress adds an 'Archfiend' card when a card effect sends her to the GY, Archfiend of Gilfer equips itself from the GY, and Pandemonium searches whenever an Archfiend is destroyed, so outside cards that discard, destroy or send your own Fiends turn those triggers on.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Tuners
hooks.why: Bone Archfiend restricts you to DARK Dragon Synchro Monsters and dumps a Fiend Tuner from the Deck, while Red Nova Dragon, King Calamity and Tyrant each demand 2 Tuners, so extra Tuners that put themselves on board are exactly the material the deck lacks.

hooks.label: Pays Life Points
hooks.why: Masterking Archfiend's once-per-chain effect triggers whenever you pay LP, sending a Fiend from your Deck to the GY, so any outside card that pays LP as a cost keeps converting into Archfiend set-up.

hooks.label: Sends a Level 8+ monster to the GY
hooks.why: A Deal with Dark Ruler is an 'Archfiend' card that Special Summons Berserk Dragon whenever a Level 8 or higher monster you control was sent to the Graveyard this turn, so outside cards that send or destroy your own big monsters pay for it.

profile.plan: A Warrior Fusion deck: it Normal Summons Elemental HEROes and fuses them (Polymerization, Miracle Fusion, Neos Fusion) into Attribute-blending Fusion Monsters and Xtra HERO Links, with every material and every HERO earning value on its way to the GY or the banish pile.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon cards
hooks.why: Every Elemental HERO Fusion Monster is 'Must be Fusion Summoned', and Blazeman, Liquid Soldier and Sunrise all fetch the Fusion Spells that do it, so outside cards that Fusion Summon are extra engine.

hooks.label: Polymerization support
hooks.why: Blazeman adds 'Polymerization' from the Deck and every named Elemental HERO Fusion is made with it, so outside cards that fetch, recur or reuse Polymerization act as extra copies of the deck's key card.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger in the GY
hooks.why: Fusion Materials are sent to the GY, and Blazeman, Prisma and Neos Fusion send monsters there from the Deck, so outside monsters with an 'if this card is sent to the GY' effect get their value for free.

hooks.label: Fusion Material triggers
hooks.why: Absolute Zero, The Shining and Escuridao each fuse a HERO with a second monster (WATER, LIGHT, DARK), so outside monsters with an effect when they are used as Fusion Material pay off during the Summon.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: Miracle Fusion banishes its Fusion Materials from the field or GY, so outside monsters with an 'if this card is banished' effect are free fuel that turns into a second effect.

hooks.label: Destiny HERO monsters
hooks.why: Xtra HERO Cross Crusader Special Summons a 'Destiny HERO' from the GY and can Tribute one to add any 'HERO' monster from the Deck, so outside Destiny HERO monsters extend every Link play.

profile.plan: A collection of draw cards that banish from the Deck/Extra Deck face-down or shuffle cards back into the Deck, aiming to draw as many cards as possible.

hooks.label: Benefits from banished cards
hooks.why: Pot of Desires, Pot of Prosperity, and Pot of Extravagance banish cards face-down, so monsters like Gren Maju Da Eiza that count banished cards grow huge.

hooks.label: Recycles banished cards
hooks.why: The archetype banishes many cards face-down, and Pot of Acquisitiveness shuffles banished monsters back; cards like Necroface can shuffle all banished cards back to reuse them.

hooks.label: Fills the GY
hooks.why: Pot of Avarice and Jar of Avarice need 5 cards in the GY to shuffle back and draw, and Pot of Dichotomy needs different Types, so outside cards that send cards from the Deck to the GY help meet these requirements.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Pot of The Forbidden is a Flip Effect Monster with a powerful FLIP effect; outside cards that flip it face-down let you reuse its effect.

profile.plan: A co-link toolbox of Fiend Link Monsters: each discards a card on Link Summon to destroy, bounce or Set something, and draws if it is co-linked, so the deck chains small Links into protected co-linked boards.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger on discard
hooks.why: Phoenix, Cerberus, Unicorn, Goblin, Gryphon and Mermaid all discard 1 card as the cost of their Link Summon effect, so any monster with an effect when discarded gets that for free.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Seven of the nine Knightmares are Fiend Link Monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole engine.

hooks.label: Link Summon on opponent's turn
hooks.why: Every Knightmare's discard-and-remove effect triggers on Link Summon, so a Link Monster that can Link Summon during the opponent's turn re-uses one and dodges the Main Phase.

profile.plan: A LIGHT-and-DARK pile deck: it fills the GY with LIGHT and DARK monsters, then banishes them in pairs to Summon 3000-ATK Chaos bosses or Synchro Summon with a LIGHT Tuner plus DARK non-Tuners.

hooks.label: Mills LIGHT/DARK monsters
hooks.why: Chaos Space, Chaos Grepher, Chaos Ruler and Chaos Valkyria all put LIGHT and DARK monsters into the GY, which is the exact fuel the archetype's Summoning costs banish from the GY.

hooks.label: Monsters that pay off when banished
hooks.why: Chaos Sorcerer, Chaos Emperor Dragon, The Chaos Creator, Chaos Betrayer and Chaos Nephthys all banish LIGHT and DARK monsters from the GY as their cost, so outside LIGHT or DARK monsters with a 'if this card is banished' effect get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Field Spell access
hooks.why: Chaos Daedalus stops the opponent targeting your LIGHT and DARK monsters while a Field Spell is up and banishes cards up to the number of face-up Field Spells, and Chaos Zone is itself a Field Spell.

hooks.label: Banishes a LIGHT and a DARK to summon itself
hooks.why: Chaos Sorcerer, The Chaos Creator, Chaos Betrayer and Chaos Nephthys all Special Summon themselves by banishing 1 LIGHT and 1 DARK monster from the GY, so outside monsters with the same Summoning procedure share the deck's GY fodder and extend its boss line.

profile.plan: A DARK Warrior Fusion deck that uses Fusion Destiny to fuse straight from the hand or Deck into boss monsters like Destroyer Phoenix Enforcer, then keeps trading and recycling the Graveyard for extra summons, draws and burn.

hooks.label: Monsters with a GY trigger
hooks.why: Fusion Destiny uses monsters from the hand or Deck as Fusion Material and Dangerous sends a Destiny HERO from the hand or Deck to the GY, so any monster that does something when it is sent to the GY gets its effect for free.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when discarded
hooks.why: Dark Angel, Blade Master and Dynatag discard themselves for their effects, while Destiny Draw and Dangerous discard a card as a cost, so outside monsters that do something when discarded are pure upside in those slots.

hooks.label: Fodder that likes being destroyed
hooks.why: Destroyer Phoenix Enforcer's Quick Effect destroys 1 card you control as well as 1 card on the field, so monsters that trigger when they are destroyed turn that cost into value every turn.

hooks.label: DARK Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Destiny HERO monster, from Malicious and Diamond Dude to Plasma and Dogma, is a DARK Warrior, so cards that search, revive or boost Warriors or DARK monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: DARK HERO monsters
hooks.why: Fusion Destiny locks you into DARK "HERO" monsters for the turn and Destroyer Phoenix Enforcer asks for a "HERO" material plus a Destiny HERO, so other DARK HERO monsters slot straight into the same Extra Deck recipes.

profile.plan: A DARK Dragon Link deck that uses Rokket monsters as material and revives them from the GY to build into large Borrel bosses with control and negation effects.

hooks.label: DARK Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Borrel monster is a DARK Dragon, and many Borrel monsters require DARK Dragon monsters as material for their Link, Fusion or Xyz Summons.

hooks.label: Monsters that float when destroyed
hooks.why: Borrelshroud Dragon, Trisborrel Dragon, Borreload Liberator Dragon and Borreload Riot Dragon all destroy your own monsters as cost or effect, so outside monsters with an effect when destroyed get value.

hooks.label: Revives DARK monsters
hooks.why: Borrel Supplier, Borreload eXcharge Dragon and Borreload Furious Dragon all Special Summon from the GY, so outside cards that revive DARK monsters from the GY add more ways to rebuild the board.

profile.plan: A Fusion Summoning deck that uses Fallen of Albaz and Despia to summon Level 8 Dragon and Fiend Fusion Monsters, often sending and banishing its own LIGHT and DARK monsters as material, with Bystial monsters as a secondary engine.

hooks.label: Fusion Monsters with GY effects
hooks.why: Branded in High Spirits and Branded in Central Dogmatika send Fusion Monsters from the Extra Deck to the GY, and Branded Expulsion Tributes them, so Fusion Monsters that trigger when sent to the GY get their effects for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT/DARK monsters with banish effects
hooks.why: The deck banishes LIGHT/DARK monsters to Fusion Summon with Branded in Red and Branded in White, and to activate Branded Regained and Branded Befallen, so LIGHT/DARK monsters with banish triggers get their effects.

hooks.label: LIGHT/DARK Dragon self-summoners
hooks.why: Branded Regained revives Bystial monsters, Branded Beast needs a Bystial, and Branded Befallen protects them, so LIGHT/DARK Dragon monsters that banish a LIGHT/DARK monster to Summon themselves are ideal partners.

hooks.label: Dragon GY Fusion
hooks.why: The deck fills the GY with Dragon monsters through its Fusion Summons, and Dragon's Mirror can use them as materials for a Fusion Summon while triggering Branded Regained.

hooks.label: Normal Trap setters
hooks.why: The deck has many powerful Normal Traps like Branded Banishment and Branded Expulsion, so effects that Set a Normal Trap directly from the Deck give access to them.

profile.plan: A Cyberse/FIRE Link-climbing deck that fills its GY with its own monsters and reincarnation-Link Summons by using a Link Monster with the same name as the entire material.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is Cyberse, and the Link-1s ask for Cyberse materials, so generic Cyberse searchers and revives work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: FIRE support
hooks.why: The Link Monsters require FIRE Effect Monsters as material, and many effects only revive or search FIRE monsters, so generic FIRE support advances the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends FIRE to GY
hooks.why: The deck constantly wants its FIRE Cyberse monsters in the GY to fuel revives, searches and Link climbs, so effects that send FIRE monsters from the Deck to the GY set up those triggers.

hooks.label: Discard outlets for FIRE
hooks.why: The deck's GY effects and self-revives often start by discarding a FIRE Cyberse monster, so outside cards that discard from the hand for cost or effect enable those plays.

hooks.label: FIRE Link Material triggers
hooks.why: The deck Link Summons repeatedly using FIRE Effect Monsters, so FIRE monsters that trigger when used as Link Material or sent to the GY as material give free advantage.

profile.plan: Play a going-second hand-trap suite: hold the board empty, discard a Mulcharmy from hand to draw a card for every Summon the opponent makes, then break their board with the huge hand you built.

hooks.label: Punishes opponent's Summons
hooks.why: Fuwalos, Purulia and Meowls each draw whenever the opponent Summons, so any outside card that also triggers on the opponent's Summon punishes the same combo turn.

hooks.label: Live on an empty board
hooks.why: All three Mulcharmy can only be discarded while you control no cards, so the deck keeps its field completely empty — outside cards that also demand that, like Evenly Matched, fit the same turn.

hooks.label: Hand-size monsters
hooks.why: Fuwalos and Purulia draw once for every Summon the opponent makes, leaving a hand of ten or more cards, so monsters that grow with the cards in your hand become enormous.
phrases: for each card in your hand

hooks.label: Discard-cost Spells and Traps
hooks.why: The Mulcharmy leave you with a hand far larger than the End Phase shuffle-down allows, so Spells and Traps that discard a card as cost turn those excess cards into removal.

profile.plan: A combo deck that uses Pendulum Summoning and the self-damaging Dark Contract cards to Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link Summon Fiend monsters, with effects that trigger on taking damage.

hooks.label: Effect damage triggers
hooks.why: D/D Orthros and D/D/D Rebel King Leonidas Special Summon themselves when you take effect damage, and the Dark Contract cards inflict damage on you every Standby Phase.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every D/D monster is a Fiend-Type, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Tribute triggers
hooks.why: Go! - D/D/D Divine Zero King Rage can Tribute 1 other monster to apply an effect, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get that for free.

hooks.label: Pendulum Zone placement
hooks.why: D/D/D Abyss King Gilgamesh places 2 D/D Pendulum monsters from the Deck into the Pendulum Zones, and the deck relies on its Pendulum Zones.

profile.plan: A Synchro Summoning deck of Winged Beast/DARK monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand, search with a Continuous Spell when they are Normal Summoned, and use GY effects to Synchro Summon powerful Winged Beast bosses.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck monster in this archetype is a Winged Beast, so cards that search, revive or boost Winged Beasts work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills Winged Beast/DARK
hooks.why: Several monsters in this archetype need monsters in the GY to activate their effects, so sending a Winged Beast or DARK monster from the Deck to the GY sets up those plays.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: This archetype has monsters that Tribute a monster as a cost, so outside monsters that get an effect when Tributed give you value for that cost.

hooks.label: Triggers as Synchro Material
hooks.why: The deck Synchro Summons constantly, and one of its monsters triggers when sent to the GY as Synchro Material, so outside monsters with effects when used as Synchro Material get value from every Synchro Summon.

hooks.label: Places counters on opponent's monsters
hooks.why: The archetype's Synchro monsters place and remove counters on opponent's monsters, so outside cards that place counters on opponent's monsters give those effects more targets.

profile.plan: A Dragon toolbox that Special Summons itself from the hand by banishing LIGHT or DARK monsters out of either Graveyard, then grinds the opponent down with Level 6 bodies, Rank 6 and Synchro plays and disruption.

hooks.label: Mills LIGHT and DARK monsters
hooks.why: Magnamhut, Druiswurm, Saronir and Baldrake all Special Summon themselves by banishing a LIGHT or DARK monster from either GY, so every card that loads the Graveyards gives them a target.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be banished
hooks.why: The Bystials' own Summoning banishes LIGHT or DARK monsters from the GYs, so monsters that do something when they are banished turn that cost into free value.

hooks.label: Branded Spells and Traps
hooks.why: The Bystial Lubellion places a "Branded" Continuous Spell/Trap from the Deck and Bystial Saronir sends "Branded" Spells/Traps from the Deck to the GY, so the archetype is built to run the Branded engine.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Bystial is a Dragon and Bystial Dis Pater is a Synchro that asks for a Tuner plus Dragon non-Tuner materials, so generic Dragon support advances the whole deck.

profile.plan: A WIND Winged Beast deck that Normal Summons 'Harpie Lady' over and over, popping a Spell/Trap with Harpies' Hunting Ground each time and bouncing monsters with Harpie Conductor and Cyber Slash Harpie Lady.

hooks.label: WIND monster support
hooks.why: Harpie Lady 1 gives all WIND monsters 300 ATK, Harpie Conductor needs 2 WIND monsters, and Feather Rest and Harpie Lady - Elegant Egotist lock the turn into WIND, so generic WIND support touches nearly every card in the deck.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Harpies' Hunting Ground pumps every Winged Beast 200 ATK/DEF and Harpy Harpist searches Level 4 Winged Beast monsters, so Winged Beast support applies to almost the whole archetype.

hooks.label: Payoffs for bouncing WIND
hooks.why: Harpie Conductor and Cyber Slash Harpie Lady repeatedly return Harpie monsters to the hand, so cards that trigger when a WIND monster you control goes back to the hand fire on the deck's own plays.

hooks.label: Spells/Traps that want destroying
hooks.why: Harpies' Hunting Ground destroys a Spell/Trap every time a Harpie Lady is Summoned, so spare Continuous Spells and Traps with an effect when they are destroyed get used for free.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of DARK Spellcasters that constantly destroys its own scales and monsters, so each Magician that pops becomes a search, a revival or a Special Summon, while the Extra Deck fills up with face-up Pendulum Monsters to recycle.

hooks.label: Destroys your own cards
hooks.why: Purple Poison, Black Fang, Double Iris, Acrobatic, Chronograph and Astrograph Magician all trigger when a card you control is destroyed by battle or card effect, so any outside card that pops your own Pendulum Monster becomes a search, a revival or a Special Summon.

hooks.label: Pendulum Extra Deck recovery
hooks.why: Amazing Pendulum, Pendulum Paradox, Oafdragon Magician and Star Pendulumgraph all return face-up Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck to the hand, and the deck's whole loop depends on reusing the monsters its destroyed scales send there.

hooks.label: Pendulum Zone fillers
hooks.why: Wisdom-Eye Magician, Astrograph Sorcerer, Chronograph Sorcerer and Supreme King Gate Magician put a Pendulum Monster straight into the Pendulum Zone from the Deck, and every Magician needs a partner Scale in the other zone.

hooks.label: DARK Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Magician main deck monster is a Spellcaster and most are DARK, and Purple Poison, Double Iris, Black Fang and Xiangke all single out DARK Spellcaster-Type monsters to boost, double battle damage on, revive or negate with.

hooks.label: Rewards your own pops
hooks.why: Six Magician cards trigger on 'if a card(s) you control is destroyed by battle or card effect' and the deck destroys its own Scales on purpose, so outside monsters with that same trigger get a free Special Summon or a search every turn.

profile.plan: Link Summon 'Code Talker' Link Monsters using Cyberse monsters, many of which can be used from the hand as material and trigger when sent to the GY, then use their pointing zones, co-links and 'Cynet' Spell/Traps to control the board.

hooks.label: Cynet Spell/Trap
hooks.why: Micro Coder can add a 'Cynet' Spell/Trap from the Deck, so any outside 'Cynet' card is a search target.

hooks.label: Cyberse from hand as material
hooks.why: Micro Coder, Code Generator, Code Radiator and Code Exporter can all be used from the hand as Link Material for a 'Code Talker' monster, so other Cyberse monsters with that ability provide extra material.

hooks.label: Cyberse Link Material trigger
hooks.why: The deck's Cyberse monsters get effects when sent from hand or field to the GY as material for a 'Code Talker' Link Summon, so outside Cyberse monsters with a similar trigger fit.

hooks.label: Firewall Link Monster
hooks.why: Protectcode Talker has an effect if you control a 'Firewall' Link Monster, so outside 'Firewall' Link Monsters enable that.

hooks.label: Extra Cyberse Normal Summon
hooks.why: Cynet Optimization lets you Normal Summon an extra Cyberse monster, so outside cards that give additional Normal Summons for Cyberse monsters fit.

hooks.label: Attribute change
hooks.why: Cynet Codec searches a Cyberse monster with the same Attribute as the Code Talker Special Summoned, so cards that change a monster's Attribute let you search different cards.

profile.plan: A defensive Level 1 Fiend/Fairy toolbox that turns being discarded, Tributed or destroyed by battle into searches, Special Summons and protection, with sub-engines for Fusion, Ritual and Number Xyz.

hooks.label: Discard enablers
hooks.why: Kuriboh, Kuriboo, Kuribeh, Clear Kuriboh, Ankuriboh, Kuribohrn and Darkuriboh all activate when discarded, so any outside card that discards a Level 1 monster from your hand sets them off.

hooks.label: Tribute outlets
hooks.why: Relinkuriboh draws when Tributed and Kuribandit, Linkuriboh and Winged Kuriboh LV10 Tribute themselves for effects, so outside cards that Tribute a Level 1 monster give you those triggers.

hooks.label: 300 ATK/200 DEF support
hooks.why: Kuriboh - Multiply! searches a monster with 300 ATK/200 DEF and Kuribah Special Summons one, a stat line shared by almost every Kuriboh.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Most Kuriboh monsters are Fiends, and Kuribeh can Normal Summon a Fiend from hand, so Fiend search, revival and boosts work across the deck.

hooks.label: Fusion Summoning Spells
hooks.why: Darkuriboh, Sabatiel and Winged Kuriboh Sabatiel LV10 all search Polymerization or a Fusion Spell, so any Spell that Fusion Summons is a target.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: Sphere Kuriboh can be banished from the GY as material for a Ritual Summon, so Ritual Spells and Ritual Monsters that need a Level 1 Fiend fit.

profile.plan: A control deck that pays Life Points to negate Summons and card activations with Counter Traps, using LP gain to offset the costs and protecting Aesir monsters.

hooks.label: Refunds LP paid
hooks.why: The Solemn Counter Traps pay half your LP or fixed amounts, so cards like Life Absorbing Machine that gain LP back from payments keep you solvent.

hooks.label: Searches or recovers Counter Traps
hooks.why: The deck is entirely Counter Traps, so any card that adds a Counter Trap from the Deck or GY to the hand increases consistency.

hooks.label: Aesir monsters
hooks.why: Solemn Authority targets an 'Aesir' monster you control, so you need Aesir monsters in the deck to use it.

hooks.label: Benefits from Continuous Traps
hooks.why: Solemn Wishes and Solemn Authority are Continuous Traps, so cards like Uria, Lord of Searing Flames that grow stronger from Continuous Traps in the GY fit.

hooks.label: Activates Traps immediately
hooks.why: The Solemn Counter Traps are powerful but slow to Set, so cards that let you activate a Trap the turn it was Set (like Temple of the Kings) let you use them right away.

hooks.label: Punishes opponent's banished cards
hooks.why: Solemn Accusation can make your opponent banish all copies of a card from their hand and Deck, so cards that deal damage per banished card (like D.D. Dynamite) become finishers.

profile.plan: A deck that Tribute Summons Level 5-8 Monarchs to trigger their powerful effects, using cards that provide extra Tributes, search Monarch Spell/Traps, and lock the opponent out of the Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Two-Tribute monsters
hooks.why: Erebus, Ehther, and the Mega Monarchs can be Tribute Summoned by Tributing a single Tribute Summoned monster, and cards like The First Monarch and Restoration of the Monarchs already treat monsters as 2 Tributes, so outside monsters that do the same let you drop a 2800 ATK Monarch with one Tribute.

hooks.label: Tribute opponent's monster
hooks.why: The Monarchs Stormforth lets you Tribute an opponent's monster for a Tribute Summon, and Thestalos the Shadowfire Monarch can Tribute an opponent's monster, so outside cards like Soul Exchange that do the same are extra copies of that effect.

hooks.label: Send S/T from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Erebus and Ehther send Monarch Spell/Traps from the Deck to the GY to activate their effects, and Pantheism and The Prime Monarch need Monarch Spell/Traps in the GY, so outside cards like Foolish Burial Goods that send Spell/Traps from the Deck to the GY fuel the whole engine.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: The Mega Monarchs get extra effects if Tributed a monster of the same Attribute, and Eidos the Underworld Monarch can change an Attribute, so outside cards like DNA Transplant or Scroll of Bewitchment that change Attributes make those bonus effects easier to achieve.

hooks.label: Continuous Trap draw
hooks.why: The deck runs many Continuous Traps like March of the Monarchs, Return of the Monarchs, and The Monarchs Erupt, so outside cards like Magic Planter that send a Continuous Trap to the GY to draw 2 turn used-up traps into more cards.

hooks.label: GY self-revivers
hooks.why: The deck needs constant Tribute fodder for its Tribute Summons and cannot use the Extra Deck, so outside monsters like Treeborn Frog or Plaguespreader Zombie that Special Summon themselves from the Graveyard provide a reusable Tribute every turn.

profile.plan: Summon Level 8 LIGHT Dragons, above all Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon, then stack them into Rank 8 Xyz monsters like Number 62 and Number 107 and keep detaching material to negate, destroy and attack again.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 8s
hooks.why: Every Rank 8 in the deck (Number 62, Number 107, Number 90, Neo Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon) asks for Level 8 monsters, and Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon also Special Summons itself by Tributing two monsters with 2000 or more ATK.

hooks.label: Xyz Material triggers
hooks.why: Galaxy-Eyes Afterglow Dragon fires when it is detached to pay an Xyz effect and Galaxy-Eyes Cloudragon attaches itself from the GY, so monsters with effects while stacked as Xyz Material get used by the constant detaching on Number 90, Number 107, Number 62 and the rest.

hooks.label: Dragon Type support
hooks.why: Almost the whole deck is Dragon-Type, Number 95: Galaxy-Eyes Dark Matter Dragon sends three Dragon-Type monsters from the Deck to the GY, and the Dragon Xyz monsters are the deck's win condition.

hooks.label: Monsters that pay off when Tributed
hooks.why: Hyper Galaxy Tributes a monster with 2000 or more ATK, Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon Tributes two such monsters to Special Summon itself, and Galaxy-Eyes Cloudragon Tributes itself, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Equip Spells as material
hooks.why: Galaxy-Eyes Full Armor Photon Dragon takes up to 2 Equip Cards equipped to it and attaches them as Xyz Material, so any outside card that keeps equipping to it is a free material every turn.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster protection
hooks.why: Nearly every Galaxy-Eyes monster is LIGHT and Galaxy-Eyes Cipher X Dragon protects LIGHT monsters you control from targeting, while Starliege Photon Blast Dragon shields the 2000+ ATK ones, so LIGHT-wide support stacks with them.

profile.plan: A DARK Warrior toolbox that fills the GY with Level 3 monsters, Xyz Summons Rank 3 DARK monsters, and Rank-Ups into bigger DARK Xyz while banishing its own GY cards for searches, revives and extra materials.

hooks.label: DARK GY millers
hooks.why: Rank-Up-Magic Force banishes DARK monsters from your GY as material, and Torn Scales, Ragged Gloves and Rusty Bardiche all send Phantom Knights cards from the Deck to the GY, so outside millers that stock DARK monsters keep the engine running.

hooks.label: DARK Warrior support
hooks.why: All Phantom Knights monsters are DARK and the Main Deck ones are Warriors, so DARK or Warrior support applies to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 3 DARK self-summoners
hooks.why: Break Sword, Malevolent Scythe and Cursed Javelin need Level 3 DARK materials, and the deck relies on monsters like Silent Boots and Doomed Soleret that Special Summon themselves.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from GY
hooks.why: Rank-Up-Magic Force banishes DARK monsters from your GY as cost, and many Phantom Knights effects banish cards from the GY, so outside DARK monsters with a banished-from-GY trigger get free value.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Torn Scales discards 1 card to send a Phantom Knights card from the Deck to the GY, and Fragile Armor sends a Phantom Knights card from the hand to the GY, so outside DARK monsters with discard triggers are live costs.

profile.plan: A LIGHT deck that mills its own Deck to the Graveyard, turning every mill into resources and eventually Summoning Judgment Dragon or using Twilightsworn to banish for Punishment Dragon.

hooks.label: Mills your Deck
hooks.why: Every Lightsworn End Phase effect sends cards from the Deck to the GY, and Wulf, Felis and Lightsworn Dragonling Special Summon or search when they are sent there, so extra milling is extra value.

hooks.label: Triggers in the GY
hooks.why: The deck constantly sends cards from the Deck to the GY, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when they are sent to the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: Banishes LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Punishment Dragon needs 4 banished Lightsworn, and the Twilightsworn monsters banish Lightsworn from the hand or GY as cost, so outside cards that banish LIGHT monsters fuel both.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Almost every Lightsworn monster is LIGHT, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: The deck runs several Dragon Lightsworn (Gragonith, Judgment Dragon, Punishment Dragon, Michael, Judgment) and Lightsworn Dragonling searches a Dragon with 3000 ATK/2600 DEF.

hooks.label: Tuners that revive themselves
hooks.why: Judgment, the Dragon of Heaven needs 4 Tuners with different names in the GY, and the deck's Synchro Summons want Tuners; Tuners that can Special Summon themselves from the GY are reusable material.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 (and climbing) Xyz deck: it Xyz Summons 'Utopia' monsters, stacks Rank-Up/Rank-Down Magic and ZW equips on top of them, and pays for every effect by detaching Xyz Material.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic cards
hooks.why: Number S0: Utopic ZEXAL and Number 99: Utopic Dragon can each be Xyz Summoned by discarding a 'Rank-Up-Magic' Spell Card and using a 'Utopia' monster as material, so every Rank-Up-Magic in the deck is a free Rank 0 or Rank 10 boss.

hooks.label: Free Level 4 LIGHT bodies
hooks.why: Number C39: Utopia Ray and Number S39: Utopia Prime ask for 3 Level 4 LIGHT monsters while Number 39: Utopia only needs 2 Level 4 monsters, so LIGHT Level 4 monsters that Special Summon themselves are extra Xyz Material for free.

hooks.label: Extra Xyz Material
hooks.why: Every 'Utopia' Xyz Monster pays for its effects by detaching material (Number 39 negating attacks, Utopia the Lightning's 5000 ATK, Utopia Ray's ATK drain), so outside cards that attach material for free buy more activations.

hooks.label: Revives Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: The deck churns through Rank 1-6 'Utopia' Xyz Monsters and already recycles them with Number 99: Utopic Dragon, Number C39: Utopia Ray V and ZW - Ultimate Shield, so outside cards that Special Summon Xyz Monsters back keep the climb going.

hooks.label: Onomato family support
hooks.why: Utopic Onomatopoeia is always treated as a 'Zubaba', 'Gagaga', 'Gogogo' and 'Dododo' card and Special Summons one of each from the hand, so cards that search or support that four-name family supply its material.

profile.plan: Give the opponent a huge Kaiju by Tributing their monster, then Special Summon your own Kaiju for free, and spend the Kaiju Counters piled on Kyoutou Waterfront, The Kaiju Files and Kaiju Capture Mission on negates, board wipes and stat-halving.

hooks.label: Tributes the opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Every Kaiju Special Summons itself to the opponent's field by Tributing a monster they control, and Kyoutou Waterfront places a Kaiju Counter for each card sent from the field to the GY, so outside Tribute-removal both removes and fuels the counter engine that pays for Gameciel and Dogoran.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Kyoutou Waterfront is the deck's engine - it gains a Kaiju Counter whenever a card is sent from the field to the GY and adds a "Kaiju" monster to the hand once it has 3 or more - so any card that finds a Field Spell from the Deck starts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Control return cards
hooks.why: A Kaiju Special Summoned to the opponent's field is still owned by you, so a card that returns control to the original owners (Owner's Seal, Remove Brainwashing) takes the Kaiju back after it has eaten the opponent's monster with its Tribute summon.

hooks.label: Monsters that summon to the opponent
hooks.why: The Kaiju's signature move is Special Summoning itself from the hand to the opponent's field by Tributing their monster, and cards that do the same (Lava Golem, Santa Claws, The Winged Dragon of Ra - Sphere Mode) are extra copies of that un-targetable removal whose Tributes put cards from the field into the GY for Kyoutou Waterfront's Kaiju Counters.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck that Normal Summons Aleister the Invoker to search Invocation, then fuses him with Attribute monsters from the hand, field or either GY into Invoked Fusion Monsters that cover every Attribute.

hooks.label: Banished-trigger monsters
hooks.why: Invocation banishes monsters as Fusion Material and several Invoked monsters banish themselves from the GY, so outside monsters with an effect when banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Discard or hand-to-GY triggers
hooks.why: Aleister the Invoker sends itself from the hand to the GY, Invoked Mechaba sends a card from the hand to negate, and Aleister the Invoker of Madness discards, so outside monsters that trigger on being discarded or sent from the hand get free effects.

hooks.label: Fusion Material triggers
hooks.why: Invocation and Invoked Sorath use monsters from the hand, field and GY as Fusion Material, so outside monsters with effects when used as material provide value during the Fusion Summon.

hooks.label: Fusion Summoning cards
hooks.why: Magical Meltdown stops your Fusion Summoning effects from being negated and stops the opponent responding when a monster is Fusion Summoned that way, so any outside card that Fusion Summons is protected and advances the plan.

hooks.label: Fills opponent's GY
hooks.why: Invocation can banish monsters from either player's GY as Fusion Material, so outside cards that make the opponent discard or mill monsters give you extra Attributes to fuse with.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Fiend deck that Link Summons into Link Monsters which equip themselves to your monsters, then Fusion Summons using materials from the hand, field, GY and Equip Zones, turning everything sent to the GY into another body.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Fiendsmith monster is a LIGHT Fiend, and Fiendsmith's Tract searches LIGHT Fiends while Engraver, Desirae and Lacrima shuffle them back from the GY, so generic LIGHT Fiend support touches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills LIGHT Fiends to the GY
hooks.why: Fiendsmith's Sequence Fusion Summons by shuffling its materials from your GY, and Engraver, Desirae and Lacrima each shuffle a LIGHT Fiend from the GY back into the Deck, so outside cards that put LIGHT Fiends into the GY feed all of them.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fiends with GY effects
hooks.why: Fiendsmith's Rextremende sends 1 LIGHT Fiend from your Deck or Extra Deck to the GY, and Fiendsmith's Lacrima adds back or revives a banished/GY LIGHT Fiend, so outside LIGHT Fiends that trigger when sent to the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: Cards that like being discarded
hooks.why: Fiendsmith's Tract and Fiendsmith's Rextremende both make you discard a card, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded are pure advantage in this deck.

hooks.label: Fusion Summoning effects
hooks.why: The deck Fusion Summons through its own means — Tract and Kyrie from the GY, Sequence by shuffling GY materials — so outside effects that Fusion Summon open extra routes into Fiendsmith's Lacrima (2 LIGHT Fiends) and the Fiendsmith Fusions.

profile.plan: Dogmatika is an anti-Extra Deck control deck that sends Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link monsters from both Extra Decks to the GY, then Ritual Summons LIGHT Spellcaster bosses and banishes those monsters for value.

hooks.label: Sends Extra Deck to GY
hooks.why: The deck sends Extra Deck monsters to the GY as Ritual material and for monster effects, so outside cards that do the same give it the fuel its GY banishing and Extra Deck triggers need.

hooks.label: Extra Deck GY effects
hooks.why: Because the deck sends Extra Deck monsters to the GY constantly, outside Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link monsters that trigger when sent there turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Extra Deck banish effects
hooks.why: The deck banishes Extra Deck monsters from the GY to Special Summon and as Ritual material, so outside Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link monsters with effects when banished are free value.

hooks.label: Fusion using either field
hooks.why: The deck already Fusion Summons with monsters on either field, so outside Fusion effects that use both sides' monsters clear the opponent's Extra Deck and put it in the GY for the deck's banish effects.

hooks.label: Ritual card searchers
hooks.why: The deck Ritual Summons its boss from hand, Deck and GY and needs both a Ritual Monster and its Ritual Spell, so outside cards that add Ritual cards to the hand set up the whole play.

hooks.label: Discards Level 8 monsters
hooks.why: Many Dogmatika monsters are Level 8, so outside cards that discard a Level 8 as a cost turn those high-Level bodies into extra cards or effects.

profile.plan: A DARK Plant Fusion deck that places Predator Counters to shrink the opponent's monsters to Level 1, then uses them as Fusion Material for DARK Fusion Monsters.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Predaplant monster is DARK, and the Fusion Monsters ask for DARK materials, so cards that search, revive or boost DARK monsters strengthen the whole deck.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: The Main Deck Predaplants are all Plant, and Chlamydosundew and the Fusions use Plant monsters, so Plant search and revival cards fit.

hooks.label: Fusion from either field
hooks.why: Predaprime Fusion uses monsters from either field, and Chlamydosundew turns Predator-Countered monsters into DARK, so effects that Fusion Summon with the opponent's monsters steal their board.

hooks.label: Plant GY revival
hooks.why: Ophrys Scorpio and Predaplanning send monsters to the GY, and Byblisp revives itself from there, so outside Plant monsters that Special Summon themselves from the GY get a free body.

profile.plan: A Dragon deck whose small Dragonmaids bounce themselves back to the hand at the start of the Battle Phase to Special Summon the big Level 7-9 Dragonmaids, which bounce back at the end, while fusing the same monsters into Dragon Fusion Monsters.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Dragonmaid monster is a Dragon, and House Dragonmaid, Sheou and Lady's Dragonmaid all ask for Dragon Fusion Material, so cards that search, revive or boost Dragons work for the whole deck.

hooks.label: Dragon Fusion Summoning
hooks.why: Dragonmaid Changeover Fusion Summons a Dragon Fusion Monster from the hand or field and Lady's Dragonmaid Fusion Summons one by shuffling materials back from the field and banishment, so outside cards that Fusion Summon Dragon monsters add more Fusions.

hooks.label: Bounces your own Dragons
hooks.why: House Dragonmaid destroys an opponent's monster whenever another face-up Dragon you control returns to the hand, and the whole deck loops by bouncing itself, so outside cards that return your own monsters to the hand trigger it.

hooks.label: Dumps Dragons in the GY
hooks.why: Chamber, Parlor, Kitchen, Nurse and Laundry Dragonmaid Special Summon a Level 7-9 Dragonmaid from the hand or GY, so sending big Dragons from the Deck to the GY supplies both the bounce targets and Fusion Material.

hooks.label: Self-summoning big Dragons
hooks.why: Dragonmaid Sheou needs 1 Level 5 or higher Dragon as Fusion Material and House Dragonmaid needs any Dragon, so Level 5 or higher Dragons that Special Summon themselves give material without spending the Normal Summon the small Dragonmaids need.

profile.plan: A deck that relies on Toon World/Toon Kingdom to Special Summon Toon monsters that can attack directly, using Toon Kingdom's face-down banishing to protect them and fuel banished-card payoffs.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Toon Kingdom is a Field Spell that the deck needs to function, so any card that adds or activates a Field Spell from the Deck makes the deck more consistent.

hooks.label: Banished-card payoffs
hooks.why: Toon Kingdom banishes cards from the top of your Deck face-down, so monsters that gain ATK from banished cards become huge beaters.

hooks.label: LP gain from Spells
hooks.why: Toon World costs 1000 LP to activate and Toon monsters pay 500 LP to attack, so cards that gain LP when a Spell is activated offset the cost.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Blue-Eyes Toon Dragon, Manga Ryu-Ran, Toon Summoned Skull and Toon Dark Magician Girl need Tributes to be Special Summoned, so monsters that Special Summon themselves provide free fodder.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell payoffs
hooks.why: Toon World is a Continuous Spell, so extra copies can be sent to the GY for value with cards that reward sending Continuous Spells.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Quick-Play Spells that target any face-up monster to negate its effects, cut its ATK or make it untouchable — disruption and battle tricks rather than a fixed deck.

hooks.label: Spell-activation payoffs
hooks.why: All six Forbidden cards are Spell Cards you fire off on either player's turn, so outside cards that trigger when a Spell Card is activated are fuelled by the whole archetype.

hooks.label: Self-reviving GY monsters
hooks.why: Forbidden Droplet sends any number of cards from your hand or field to the GY as its cost, so outside monsters that Special Summon themselves from the GY turn that cost into a free body.

hooks.label: Recycles Spells from the GY
hooks.why: Every Forbidden card is a Spell that lands in the GY after it resolves, so outside cards that add a Spell Card back from the GY hand you another activation of one.

profile.plan: A beatdown deck of EARTH Machine monsters that Tribute Summons huge 'Ancient Gear Golem'-style beaters, protects them from backrow while they attack, and Fuses them into giant piercing bosses.

hooks.label: EARTH Machine support
hooks.why: Every Ancient Gear monster is an EARTH Machine, Ancient Gear Ballista needs 2 EARTH Machine monsters as Link Material, and Ancient Gear Box searches EARTH Machine monsters with 500 ATK/DEF.

hooks.label: Gadget Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Ancient Gear Gadjiltron Dragon, Gadjiltron Chimera, Ancient Gear Hydra and Ancient Gear Reactor Dragon all gain extra effects when Tribute Summoned by Tributing a 'Gadget' monster.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Spell/Trap
hooks.why: Geartown, Ancient Gear Fortress, Ancient Gear Tank and Ancient Gear Catapult all trigger when a card you control is destroyed, so outside cards that pop your own Spell/Trap turn them on.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Ancient Gear Golem, Ultimate Pound and Beast cannot be Special Summoned and must be Tribute Summoned, while Ancient Gear Advance turns a Tribute into a tribute-free Normal Summon, so extra Normal Summons are worth more here.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Ancient Gear Advance Tributes a monster as cost and Ancient Gear Statue and Ancient Gear Cannon Tribute themselves, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Machine monsters to discard
hooks.why: Ancient Gear Golem - Ultimate Pound discards 1 Machine monster to attack again and Ancient Gear Frame and Ancient Gear Drill discard a card as cost, so outside Machine monsters with an effect when discarded or sent to the GY fit.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck that quickly Fusion Summons Level 8 or higher Fusion Monsters using LIGHT and DARK bodies from the hand and field, then recurs them from the GY while punishing the opponent's LP and Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Extra Deck millers
hooks.why: Guiding Quem and Despian Luluwalilith both trigger when a card leaves the Extra Deck, so outside cards that send Extra Deck monsters to the GY hand you a free revival, ATK boost and effect negation.

hooks.label: "Branded" Spell/Trap
hooks.why: Aluber the Jester of Despia adds a "Branded" Spell/Trap from the Deck, and Despian Tragedy Sets one from the GY, so outside "Branded" Spell/Traps are tutored by the archetype's own starters.

hooks.label: Fallen of Albaz cards
hooks.why: Guiding Quem sends a "Fallen of Albaz" or a card that mentions it from the Deck to the GY, then revives one, so every outside card that mentions Fallen of Albaz is fuel and a target.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger as material
hooks.why: Despian Quaeritis, Masquerade and the Theater all Fusion Summon using monsters from the hand or field, so outside monsters with an effect when used as Fusion Material get their value for free.

profile.plan: A control deck of Flip Spellcasters that steal the opponent's monsters by Attribute, upgrade into 1850 ATK Familiar-Possessed beaters by sending those monsters to the GY, and Link Summon into Charmers that revive the opponent's Graveyard.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-up
hooks.why: Aussa, Hiita, Eria, Wynn, Lyna and Dharc the X Charmer only take control when their FLIP effect resolves, so any outside card that flips a face-down monster face-up triggers a steal.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: Each Charmer only steals a monster of one Attribute, so outside cards that change an opponent's monster's Attribute make any opposing monster a legal target for whichever Charmer you have.

hooks.label: Fills the opponent's GY
hooks.why: Dharc Gloomy, Hiita Ablaze and the other Link Charmers Special Summon a monster from the opponent's Graveyard, so cards that put the opponent's monsters into the GY hand them targets.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Charmer, Familiar-Possessed, Channeler and Link monster in the deck is a Spellcaster, and Familiar-Possessed - Lyna and Unpossessed even search Spellcasters out of the Deck.

hooks.label: Effects when sent to the GY
hooks.why: Familiar-Possessed - Aussa and friends Special Summon themselves by sending a face-up Charmer and a matching face-up monster you control to the GY, so outside monsters with a Graveyard trigger get used for free.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon cards
hooks.why: Charmers of the Grand Circle is a Fusion Monster made from 2+ "Charmer" or "Familiar-Possessed" monsters, but the archetype has no Fusion Spell of its own, so outside cards that Fusion Summon are what actually bring it out.

profile.plan: Reveals Danger! monsters in hand so the opponent randomly picks one to discard; each Danger! then Special Summons itself from the hand, draws a card, and turns being discarded into a search, a revive or removal.

hooks.label: Discard outlets
hooks.why: Every Danger! monster has a second effect that triggers when it is discarded, so outside cards that make you discard upgrade a hand of Danger!s into Special Summons, searches and removal.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Danger! Zone, Second Expedition into Danger! and each Danger!'s own reveal effect discard cards from your hand, so outside monsters that do something when discarded fire for free.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: All seventeen Danger! monsters are DARK, so any card that searches, revives, boosts or protects DARK monsters works on the entire deck.

profile.plan: A Warrior swarm deck: it floods the field with differently-named Six Samurai from the hand, stacks Bushido Counters on its Continuous Spells, and turns the bodies into Warrior Synchro (Shi En) and Rank 4 Xyz plays.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Warrior, and Legendary Lord Six Samurai - Enishi boosts all Warrior monsters while Shi En needs a Warrior Tuner as material.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 4 Warriors
hooks.why: Legendary Six Samurai - Kizan and Grandmaster of the Six Samurai Special Summon themselves while you control a Six Samurai, so outside monsters that do the same give free Warrior bodies for Battle Shogun of the Six Samurai and for Rank 4 or Synchro Summons.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Legendary Six Samurai - Kageki Special Summons a Six Samurai from the hand when it is Normal Summoned, and Six Samurai United, Shien's Dojo and Gateway of the Six gain a Bushido Counter from every Six Samurai Normal Summon, so an extra Normal Summon is an extra counter and another body.

hooks.label: Tributes your own monsters
hooks.why: Legendary Six Samurai - Shinai adds a Six Samurai from the Graveyard when it is Tributed on the field, so any outside card that Tributes your Warrior monsters as a cost turns into recovery.

hooks.label: Sends Warriors to the Graveyard
hooks.why: Enishi, Shien's Chancellor and Legendary Six Samurai - Enishi both banish Six Samurai from the Graveyard as their cost, and Legendary Secret of the Six Samurai banishes one to copy it, so outside cards that put Warrior monsters into the GY fuel the whole plan.

profile.plan: An Equip-Spell engine of Warrior monsters: the Noble Knights and Infernoble Knights equip themselves and each other with Noble Arms, recycle everything from the GY, and turn every equip, dump and destruction into searches, Special Summons or removal.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Noble Knight and Infernoble Knight is a Warrior, and Isolde, Two Tales of the Noble Knights needs two Warriors as Link Material and searches a Warrior from the Deck.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior support
hooks.why: The Infernoble half — Renaud, Oliver, Ogier, Maugis, Astolfo — are all FIRE Warriors, and Renaud, Durendal, Joyeuse and Roland search or revive FIRE Warrior monsters by name.

hooks.label: Equip Spell recovery
hooks.why: Isolde sends Equip Spells from the Deck to the GY, and Emperor Charles and Captain Roland want an Equip Spell in the hand or GY every turn, so cards that add or revive Equip Spells keep the engine fed.

hooks.label: Equip Spells that recycle
hooks.why: Isolde, Captain Roland and Ogier all send Equip Spells from the Deck to the GY, so an outside Equip Spell that does something when it is sent to the GY or destroyed gets used for free, just like the Noble Arms.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior GY fodder
hooks.why: Ogier sends a FIRE Warrior from the Deck to the GY and Astolfo banishes a FIRE Warrior from the hand or GY as a cost, so outside FIRE Warriors with a GY or banish trigger get activated for free.

hooks.label: Equips a monster from the GY
hooks.why: Ogier, Maugis, Oliver and Captain Roland all equip themselves to a Warrior from the GY, and Infernoble Knight Emperor Charles destroys a card whenever an Equip Card becomes equipped, so outside cards that re-equip monsters add removal.

profile.plan: A deck that Tribute Summons the three Egyptian Gods—Obelisk, Slifer and Ra—by flooding the field with Tribute fodder and using cards like Soul Crossing and Ancient Chant to cheat out the three-Tribute costs.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: The Gods need three Tributes each, and Reactor Slime already turns into two Slime Tokens; any outside card that Special Summons Tokens gives you free Tribute fodder.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Obelisk, Slifer and Ra each require 3 Tributes; Ancient Chant gives an extra Tribute Summon, so any outside card that grants another Normal Summon or lets you Tribute Summon without Tributes accelerates them.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes monsters constantly—for Tribute Summons and for Obelisk/Sun God Unification effects—so outside monsters that do something when Tributed give you value from the cost.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: The entire deck is built around Tribute Summoning the Egyptian Gods; cards that reward or enable Tribute Summoning (like The Monarchs Stormforth) fit naturally.

hooks.label: Protects Tribute Summoned monsters
hooks.why: All three Gods are Tribute Summoned, so outside cards that shield or boost Tribute Summoned monsters keep your boss alive.

hooks.label: Divine-Beast support
hooks.why: Every Egyptian God monster is a Divine-Beast, so any outside card that supports Divine-Beast monsters works on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A control deck that sets multiple Trap Hole cards to destroy, banish, or negate the opponent's Summoned monsters, punishing every Summon.

hooks.label: Traptrix monsters
hooks.why: Traptrix Holeutea banishes itself from the GY to revive a 'Traptrix' monster, and Traptrix monsters search and support Trap Hole cards.

hooks.label: Normal Trap searchers/setters
hooks.why: Traptrix Holeutea can be activated the turn it is Set by discarding a Normal Trap, and the deck is built on Normal Trap cards, so cards that add Normal Traps to your hand or set them from the Deck provide consistency and fodder.

hooks.label: Banished-payoff monsters
hooks.why: Dimensionhole banishes a monster you control until your next Standby Phase, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when they are banished get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Ryzeal monsters
hooks.why: Ryzeal Plasma Hole interacts with 'Ryzeal' Xyz Monsters, attaching them from the GY and enabling an Xyz Summon, so Ryzeal cards fit the deck.

hooks.label: X-Saber monsters
hooks.why: Saber Hole can only be activated while you control an 'X-Saber' monster, so X-Saber monsters enable it.

hooks.label: Trap-GY banishers
hooks.why: Treacherous Trap Hole can only be activated if you have no Trap Cards in your Graveyard, so outside cards that banish Trap Cards from your GY keep it live.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck that uses Black Rose Dragon's field wipe and Plant/Dragon Tuners to summon Level 7 Rose Dragons, then revives its Plants and Dragons from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Almost every Main Deck Rose Dragon monster is a Plant or asks for one, from Rose Lover and Garden Rose Maiden to Rose Paladin's Level 7 Plant search, so Plant search, revival and ATK boosts all advance the deck.

hooks.label: Sends Plant to GY
hooks.why: Black Rose Dragon, Splendid Rose, Rose Lover and Mark of the Rose all banish Plant monsters from the GY as cost, so outside cards that send Plant monsters from the Deck to the GY fuel every one of them.

hooks.label: Plant banished from GY
hooks.why: The deck repeatedly banishes Plant monsters from the GY — Black Rose Dragon for its ATK-lowering effect, Splendid Rose for its second attack, Rose Lover to Summon from hand — so outside Plant monsters that trigger when banished get free effects.

hooks.label: Synchro Material triggers
hooks.why: Red Rose Dragon and White Rose Dragon both have effects when sent to the GY as Synchro Material, and the deck Synchro Summons constantly, so outside monsters that trigger when used as Synchro Material get their effects for free.

profile.plan: Banishes its own Beast, Beast-Warrior and Winged Beast monsters from the Graveyard to Link Summon those Types straight out of the Extra Deck, while its members send themselves to the GY to search and set up.

hooks.label: Level 3 or lower Beast fodder
hooks.why: Fraktall sends 1 Level 3 or lower Beast, Beast-Warrior or Winged Beast from the Deck to the GY, so small monsters of those Types that do something in the GY become free value.

hooks.label: Banished-effect Beasts
hooks.why: Fraktall, Nervall, Kitt and Kerass banish Beast, Beast-Warrior and Winged Beast monsters from the GY as the cost of their Extra Deck Summon, so those Types with a banish trigger get used for free.

hooks.label: Beast / Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Tri-Brigade monster is Beast, Beast-Warrior or Winged Beast and their Link Summons allow only those Types as material, so Type support lifts the entire deck.

hooks.label: Fallen of Albaz Fusions
hooks.why: Mercourier can only negate a monster effect while you control a Fusion Monster that mentions 'Fallen of Albaz' as material, and it searches that card when banished.

hooks.label: Sends your own monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Fraktall, Kitt and Stand-Off only function by sending your own monsters to the GY, and every Tri-Brigade monster has an effect when it is sent there.

profile.plan: The deck Xyz Summons Winged Beast Rank 4 monsters, then uses Rank-Up-Magic to climb into higher-Rank Raidraptor Xyz Monsters that can attack multiple times or destroy the opponent's board.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Raidraptor monster is a Winged Beast, so cards that search, revive or boost Winged Beasts work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Raidraptor monster is DARK, and many effects (e.g., Rank-Up-Magic Revolution Force, Raidraptor's Phantom Knights Claw) refer to DARK Xyz Monsters.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic spells
hooks.why: Raidraptor - Tribute Lanius, Raidraptor - Brave Strix and Raidraptor - Wise Strix add or Set Rank-Up-Magic Spells from the Deck, and Raidraptor - Necro Vulture recovers them from the GY.

hooks.label: Effects when detached
hooks.why: The deck detaches Xyz Material constantly (Force Strix, Arsenal Falcon, Ultimate Falcon, etc.), so monsters with effects when detached from an Xyz Monster get value.

profile.plan: A DARK Dragon deck that Link Summons using its own monsters as material, destroying its own Rokkets to trigger their End Phase revival and swarming the field with DARK monsters for Borrel Link Monsters.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Rokkets like Magnarokket, Silverrokket and Autorokket have effects when destroyed on the field by card effect, and cards like Rokket Tracer, Squib Draw and Tactical Exchanger destroy your own cards to trigger them, so outside cards that destroy your own DARK Dragon monsters fit.

hooks.label: Triggers when destroyed
hooks.why: The deck constantly destroys its own cards, so outside DARK Dragon monsters that have effects when destroyed can be used as fodder for Rokket Tracer, Squib Draw or Tactical Exchanger.

hooks.label: Triggers when used as Link Material
hooks.why: Noctovision Dragon draws a card when sent to the GY as Link Material, and the deck Link Summons constantly, so outside monsters with effects when used as Link Material get extra value.

hooks.label: Sends DARK Dragon from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Absorouter Dragon adds a Rokket from Deck when sent to the GY, and Rokket Barrage sends a DARK Dragon from Deck to GY to summon itself, so outside cards that send DARK Dragon monsters from Deck to GY trigger those effects.

hooks.label: DARK Dragon support
hooks.why: The entire Rokket archetype is DARK Dragon monsters (with a Cyberse exception), and the Extra Deck lock only allows DARK monsters, so cards that support DARK Dragon monsters fit the deck.

profile.plan: A Fiend deck that destroys its own monsters and Set Spells/Traps to trigger 'when this card is destroyed' summons and Link Summons, then turns the opponent's monsters into Link material.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Unchained monster is a Fiend, the Link Monsters ask for Fiend material, and Aruha, Rakea and Shma lock you into Fiend-only Special Summons, so anything that searches, revives or boosts Fiends works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when destroyed
hooks.why: Aruha, Rakea, Sarama, Shma, Shara, Yama, Disaster and every Unchained Spell/Trap reward you for destroying your own cards, so outside cards with an effect when they are destroyed get activated for free.

hooks.label: Destroys your own cards
hooks.why: Unchained Soul of Sharvara, Rakea, Shyama, Kamura and Escape of the Unchained all destroy a card you control to Special Summon or to trigger the destroyed card's effect, so more self-destruction is more gas.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with Fiends
hooks.why: Lord of Yama and Disaster revive Fiend monsters from the GY and Disaster gains 300 ATK for each Unchained card there, so sending Fiends from the Deck to the GY sets up every revival.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Fiends
hooks.why: The Link Monsters need bodies, and Yama/Lord of Yama want monsters in hand or GY, so Fiends that Special Summon themselves from the hand or GY are free Link material under the Fiend-only lock.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck that climbs into Dragon Synchro bosses, whose key monsters Tribute themselves as cost to negate destruction or Summons and then come back, so it wants to Tribute its own field over and over and to load the GY with Tuners and Level 1 Dragons.

hooks.label: Monsters with a Tribute trigger
hooks.why: Stardust Dragon, Stardust Warrior, Accel Synchro Stardust Dragon and Victim Sanctuary all Tribute themselves as cost, and Stardust Trail revives whenever a monster you control is Tributed, so any monster that does something when Tributed gets value for free.

hooks.label: Cards that Tribute your monsters
hooks.why: Stardust Trail Special Summons itself from the hand or GY whenever a monster you control is Tributed, and Stardust Synchron's hand/GY effect is activated by Tributing a monster, so outside effects that Tribute your own field are activators.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every boss here is a Dragon (Stardust Dragon, Sifr, Spark, Chronicle Spark), so cards that search, revive or protect Dragons apply to the whole win condition.

profile.plan: A DARK Zombie deck that pays Life Points to Normal and Tribute Summon its Vampires, mills the opponent's Deck to trigger Vampire Kingdom, and steals monsters out of the opponent's Graveyard, winning battles to resurrect what it destroys.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Vampire monster except Vampire Hunter is a Zombie, Vampire Kingdom boosts Zombie-Type monsters, and Vampire Grace, Vampire Sucker and Crimson Knight Vampire Bram all require Zombies.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Vampire is DARK, and Shadow Vampire and Vampire Duke can only be used as material for the Xyz Summon of a DARK monster.

hooks.label: Fills the opponent's GY
hooks.why: Vampire Lord, Vampire Lady, Vampire Duke and Vampire Grace make the opponent send cards from their Deck to the GY, which triggers Vampire Kingdom to destroy a card and leaves targets for Vampire Sucker, Fascinator and Voivode to steal.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Vampire's Desire sends 1 monster you control to the GY as a cost and The Zombie Vampire mills both Decks, so outside monsters with an effect when sent to the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon enablers
hooks.why: The deck's big plays are Tribute Summoning Level 5-8 Vampires like Vampire Voivode and Vampire Dragon, and Vampire Sucker even lets you Tribute an opponent's Zombie for it.

profile.plan: A stun/control deck built on the Necrovalley Field Spell, which boosts its Spellcaster monsters while sealing both Graveyards, backed by Flip effects, Tribute Summoned bosses and a Spellcaster Fusion.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Gravekeeper's monster is a Spellcaster, and Necrovalley gives them all +500 ATK/DEF, so generic Spellcaster support applies to the whole deck.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Almost all Gravekeeper's monsters are DARK, so cards that search, revive or pay costs with DARK monsters work on the deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell tutors
hooks.why: Necrovalley is the deck's engine and Gravekeeper's Commandant is its only in-archetype searcher, so any card that adds or puts a Field Spell from the Deck onto the field is another copy of Necrovalley.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Gravekeeper's Chief, Visionary and Oracle want to be Tribute Summoned with Gravekeeper's monsters, and Necrovalley Throne already grants an extra Normal Summon, so more Normal Summons mean more big bodies.

hooks.label: Flip support
hooks.why: Spy, Guard and Ambusher only get their effects when flipped face-up, and Spy and Nobleman Summon in face-down Defense Position, so outside cards that flip your monsters face-up re-use them.
