profile.plan: A Fairy/LIGHT Ritual control deck that Ritual Summons Herald of Perfection or Herald of Ultimateness and negates the opponent's plays by sending Fairy monsters from the hand to the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Ritual support
hooks.why: Herald of Perfection and Herald of Ultimateness can only be Ritual Summoned by Dawn of the Herald and Oracle of the Herald, so anything that finds or recycles Ritual monsters and Ritual Spells assembles the win condition.

hooks.label: Fairy and LIGHT support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Herald is a Fairy, and the Ritual bosses negate by sending Fairy-Type monsters from the hand to the Graveyard, so Fairy and LIGHT support feeds both halves of the deck.

hooks.label: Fairies sent from the hand
hooks.why: Herald of Perfection, Herald of Ultimateness and the miniature Heralds pay their negation cost with Fairy monsters sent from the hand to the Graveyard, so Fairies that do something once they land there are double value.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Dawn of the Herald and Oracle of the Herald Tribute monsters from the hand or field for the Ritual Summon, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get used for free.

profile.plan: A Reptile Ritual deck that Ritual Summons Level 8 DARK Reptile bosses straight out of the Deck, then repeatedly Tributes its own Reptiles so every Tribute becomes a search and a revived Ritual Monster.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Mitsurugi monster is a Reptile, Mitsurugi Ritual Tributes Reptile monsters from the hand, Deck or field, and Futsu no Mitama no Mitsurugi revives one, so anything that searches, dumps or revives Reptiles feeds the whole engine.

hooks.label: Ritual support
hooks.why: Mitsurugi Ritual and Mitsurugi Mirror Ritual Summon Reptile Ritual Monsters from the Deck, hand or GY, so cards that add Ritual Monsters or Ritual Spells to hand, or Ritual Summon generically, add consistency.

hooks.label: Tributes your Reptiles
hooks.why: Aramasa, Saji and Kusanagi all trigger when they are Tributed to add a Mitsurugi card, so outside cards that Tribute a Reptile you control turn into searches for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: The Mitsurugi Ritual Monsters add a Mitsurugi card and Special Summon themselves back when Tributed, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed cash in on the same Tributes.

profile.plan: A Rank 10 Machine Xyz deck that swarms Level 10 EARTH Machine monsters, overlays them into Superdreadnought Rail Cannons, and detaches materials for burn, protection and removal.

hooks.label: Attach Xyz Material from GY
hooks.why: Barrage Blast detaches any number of materials to destroy cards, and Derricrane triggers when detached, so attaching an extra monster from the GY to a Machine Xyz gives more removal.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when detached
hooks.why: The deck detaches materials constantly for Gustav Max, Super Dora, Barrage Blast and Flying Launcher, so outside monsters with an effect when detached get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Special Summon Level 10 from hand
hooks.why: The deck needs two Level 10 monsters on the field for its Rank 10 Xyz Summons, so cards like Xyz Reception that put a Level 10 from hand onto the field provide the missing material.

hooks.label: Send EARTH Machine from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Night Train Blue Traveler, Special Schedule and Train Connection all want specific EARTH Machine monsters in the GY, so sending one from the Deck sets up revives and equips.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when used as Xyz Material
hooks.why: Every Rank 10 Xyz Summon uses two Level 10 monsters as material, so outside monsters with an effect when used as Xyz Material give extra value on the way to Gustav Max or Juggernaut Liebe.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck that fuses with monsters from the hand (and Deck) to send its own Dracotail monsters to the GY, where they Set backrow and revive the Fusion Monsters that were sent there.

hooks.label: Fusion Material substitutes
hooks.why: Arthalion, Gulamel and Shaulas all ask for '1 "Dracotail" monster + 1 monster in the hand', and Faimena/Mululu fuse from the hand, so a monster that substitutes for the named material makes any hand monster a valid fusion partner.

hooks.label: Fusion-material triggers
hooks.why: Rahu Dracotail and the Dracotail Fusions send monsters to the GY as Fusion material, so outside monsters that do something when they are used as Fusion material get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Dragon and Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Dracotail monster is either a Dragon or a Spellcaster, and Mululu locks your Extra Deck into those Fusion Monsters, so support for either Type applies to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Hand-material Fusion Spells
hooks.why: Faimena and Mululu Fusion Summon during the Main Phase using monsters from the hand, so more Fusion Summoning Spells that also use hand monsters keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Deck-milling cards
hooks.why: Arthalion, Gulamel and Shaulas Special Summon themselves from the GY when 2 or more monsters are sent to the GY at the same time, so effects that send several monsters from the Deck to the GY turn those revives on.

profile.plan: A reactive control deck: it keeps the field empty so the PSY-Framegear Tuners can Special Summon themselves and PSY-Frame Driver from the hand, Deck or GY to negate the opponent's Summons, monster effects, Spells, Traps and attacks, then Synchro Summons PSY-Framelord Omega or Zeta on the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every PSY-Frame monster and both PSY-Framelords are Psychic, so cards that search, revive or boost Psychic monsters work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Psychic
hooks.why: PSY-Framelord Lambda adds a PSY-Frame card from the Deck whenever a face-up Psychic monster you control is banished face-up, and removing your own monster also reopens the empty field the PSY-Framegears require.

hooks.label: Sends Psychics to the GY
hooks.why: The PSY-Framegears Special Summon PSY-Frame Driver from the hand, Deck or GY, and PSY-Frame Multi-Threader Special Summons itself from the GY when a PSY-Frame Tuner is Summoned.

hooks.label: Special Summons a Psychic
hooks.why: PSY-Framegear monsters cannot be Normal Summoned/Set and must be Special Summoned by a card effect, so any outside effect that Special Summons a Psychic monster puts a gear or PSY-Frame Driver onto the board.

profile.plan: A Wyrm deck that Special Summons its Effect Monsters while you control no Effect Monsters, then uses them to Link and Synchro Summon non-Effect Wyrm monsters, which protect the board and enable the Tenyi Spirits' banished effects.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Every Tenyi monster is a Wyrm, and the Link and Synchro summons need Wyrm materials, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Wyrms helps the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Wyrm to GY
hooks.why: Tenyi Spirit - Adhara, Vishuda and the others banish themselves from the GY, and Tenyi Spirit - Mula Adhara needs 2+ Wyrm in the GY/banished, so any card that sends a Wyrm from Deck to GY sets up those effects.

profile.plan: A WATER Synchro deck: churn out Ice Barrier monsters (many Level 2 or lower), discard and send cards from hand to the GY as costs, and climb into Trishula, Gungnir, Brionac and Dewloren for banishing, destruction and bouncing.

hooks.label: WATER monster support
hooks.why: Every Ice Barrier monster is WATER, and Revealer of the Ice Barrier and Mirror Mage of the Ice Barrier lock you into Special Summoning WATER monsters only, so outside cards that search, revive or boost WATER monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Brionac, Gungnir, Geomancer and Strategist of the Ice Barrier all discard cards from the hand as a cost, so outside cards that gain an effect when they are discarded are free ammunition.

hooks.label: Level 5+ WATER in the GY
hooks.why: The 'Ice Barrier' Normal Trap sends 1 Level 5 or higher WATER monster from your Deck to the GY, so outside high-Level WATER monsters with an effect when sent to the GY turn that into value.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that sets its scales to Pendulum Summon Level 7 Odd-Eyes Dragons, then uses them as material for Xyz, Synchro, Fusion and Ritual bosses, recycling destroyed Pendulum Monsters through the Extra Deck and Pendulum Zones.

hooks.label: Extra Deck Pendulum summoners
hooks.why: Destroyed Odd-Eyes monsters go to the Extra Deck face-up, and Odd-Eyes Solblaze Dragon, Performapal Odd-Eyes Seer and Odd-Eyes Vortex Dragon all feed off those cards, so anything that Special Summons a Pendulum Monster from the Extra Deck is another payoff.

hooks.label: Pendulum Scale placers
hooks.why: The deck only Pendulum Summons Level 7 while the right scales are up, and apart from Odd-Eyes Arcray Dragon it has few ways to put a Pendulum Monster straight into the Pendulum Zone.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Odd-Eyes Advance Dragon, Odd-Eyes Lancer Dragon, Odd-Eyes Wizard Dragon and Odd-Eyes Saber Dragon all Tribute a monster to Special Summon themselves, and Odd-Eyes Advent Tributes Pendulum Monsters, so outside monsters that do something when Tributed are free material.

profile.plan: A Ritual/Fusion deck that drops Relinquished and the Eyes Restrict Fusions, then steals the opponent's monsters as Equip Spells to become huge, untouchable walls that reflect the opponent's own attacks back at them.

hooks.label: Ritual searchers
hooks.why: Relinquished can only be Ritual Summoned with "Black Illusion Ritual", so cards that add a Ritual Monster or Ritual Spell from the Deck get the deck to its boss and to the Ritual Spell that summons it.

hooks.label: Level 1 enablers
hooks.why: Relinquished Anima needs a Level 1 monster as Link Material and Black Illusion Ritual Tributes a monster of Level 1 or higher, so outside cards that Special Summon Level 1 monsters from the hand, Deck or GY supply both.

hooks.label: Dumps DARK Spellcasters
hooks.why: Golden-Eyes Idol equips an opponent's monster when it is sent to the GY by a card effect and Illusionist Faceless Magician revives a Fusion or Relinquished from the GY, so outside cards that send DARK Spellcasters from the hand or Deck to the GY set both up.

hooks.label: Forces the opponent to attack
hooks.why: Relinquished equips the attacker and turns the battle damage it takes into effect damage to the opponent, and Nightmare-Eyes Restrict forces every opposing attack into itself, so cards that make the opponent's monsters attack push that damage through.

hooks.label: DARK Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a DARK Spellcaster except Nightmare-Eyes Restrict, whose Fusion Materials must be Fiend, Illusion or Spellcaster, so generic Spellcaster and DARK support applies to the whole deck.

profile.plan: A banish-control deck: it removes its own monsters from play so D.D. Survivor, D.D. Scout Plane, D.D. Patrol Plane and D.D. Telepon bring themselves back in the End Phase, turning every banish into board presence and a growing banished pile that D.D. Dynamite and D.D. Post cash in.

hooks.label: Banishes your own monsters
hooks.why: D.D. Survivor, D.D. Scout Plane, D.D. Patrol Plane and D.D. Telepon all Special Summon themselves back when they are banished, so an outside card that banishes a monster you control turns into a free returning body.

hooks.label: Monsters that want banishing
hooks.why: The deck removes its own cards from play constantly through D.D. Post, D.D. Seeker and D.D. Patrol Plane, so outside monsters with an 'if this card is banished' effect get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Revives banished monsters
hooks.why: D.D.R. - Different Dimension Reincarnation, D.D.M. - Different Dimension Master and Dark Dimension Soldier all Special Summon your banished monsters, so outside cards that revive banished monsters reuse the same pile the deck is building.

hooks.label: Banishes the opponent's cards
hooks.why: D.D. Dynamite burns for 300 per card of the opponent's that is removed from play, and D.D. Crow and D.D. Designator banish from the opponent's hand and Graveyard, so more outside banishing raises that damage.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Most of the deck's monsters — D.D. Warrior Lady, D.D. Assailant, D.D. Survivor, D.D. Warrior, D.D. Guide, D.D. Destroyer, D.D. Unicorn Knight, Dark Dimension Soldier and D.D. Esper Star Sparrow — are Warriors, so Warrior support searches and revives the whole deck.

profile.plan: A DARK Machine combo deck: it fills the GY with Orcust, then banishes those Orcust from the GY to Special Summon, search and negate, Link Summoning Galatea and friends that shuffle the banished Machines back for even more effects.

hooks.label: Mills DARK Machine monsters
hooks.why: Orcust Harp Horror, Cymbal Skeleton, Brass Bombard and Knightmare all banish themselves from the GY to Summon, search or dump another DARK Machine, so any outside card that sends DARK Machines from the Deck to the GY loads the whole engine.

hooks.label: Machines that love being Tributed
hooks.why: Orcustrated Release Tributes 2 Machine monsters as its cost, so outside Machine monsters with an effect when they are Tributed turn that cost into a free payoff.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be banished
hooks.why: Orcustrated Core banishes 1 monster from your field or GY as its cost, so outside monsters that trigger when they are banished get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Sent from the hand to the GY
hooks.why: Orcustrated Babel and Galatea-I both send a card from your hand to the GY as a cost, so outside cards that trigger on being sent from the hand to the GY convert that cost into value.

hooks.label: DARK Machine support
hooks.why: Every Orcust monster is a DARK Machine and their GY effects lock you into DARK Special Summons, so support that names Machine or DARK reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Banishes Machine monsters from the GY
hooks.why: Longirsu, Galatea and Orcustrion all target your banished Machine monsters to shuffle them back into the Deck, and Dingirsu attaches banished Machines as material, so outside cards that banish Machines from your GY supply that ammo.

profile.plan: A trap-control deck: Normal Traps Special Summon the Labrynth Fiends, which then Set and recycle more Normal Traps, and every monster that leaves the field to a Normal Trap turns on draws, summons and hand destruction.

hooks.label: Monsters that want discarding
hooks.why: Labrynth Chandraglier, Labrynth Stovie Torbie and Labrynth Cooclock all discard a card as the cost of their effects, so outside monsters that gain something when they are discarded pay for it.

hooks.label: Normal Traps that remove monsters
hooks.why: Arianna, Lovely Labrynth, Chandraglier, Stovie Torbie and Cooclock all trigger when a monster leaves the field by your Normal Trap effect, so outside Normal Traps that clear the opponent's field keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Labrynth monster is a Fiend, Welcome Labrynth locks you into Fiend Special Summons and Big Welcome Labrynth and Labrynth Labyrinth both revive Fiends.

hooks.label: Normal Traps with a GY effect
hooks.why: Ariane the Labrynth Servant sends a Normal Trap from your hand or Set field to the GY as cost, and Lovely Labrynth can Set Normal Traps back from the GY, so outside Normal Traps that do something in the GY are never dead.

profile.plan: The deck repeatedly destroys its own FIRE monsters with card effects, so each destroyed Fire King floats back as a search, a Special Summon or a board wipe, and the Level 8 bodies eventually become a Rank 8 Garunix Eternity that destroys everything again.

hooks.label: Destroys your own FIRE monsters
hooks.why: Every Fire King payoff — Barong's search, Ulcanix's add, Yaksha's pop, Garunix's revival — only starts when a FIRE monster you hold in hand or control is destroyed by a card effect, so outside cards that pop your own FIRE monsters are the engine's ignition.

hooks.label: FIRE monsters that float
hooks.why: The deck destroys its own FIRE monsters every turn, so outside FIRE monsters with an effect that triggers when they are destroyed — effects that revive themselves, search or burn — get that destruction for free.

hooks.label: Pays off when FIRE is destroyed
hooks.why: Sacred Fire King Garunix and Legendary Fire King Ponix revive themselves off any originally-FIRE monster destroyed by battle or card effect, so outside cards that also gain something whenever your FIRE monster is destroyed stack up with the archetype's own triggers.

hooks.label: FIRE Beast/Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Garunix, Ulcanix, Onslaught and Echelon all search or Summon FIRE Beast, Beast-Warrior and Winged Beast monsters, and every Fire King is one of those Types, so support naming those Types or the FIRE Attribute boosts the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Thunder deck that discards its own monsters from the hand to search, revive and Fusion Summon, then banishes them from the GY to pay for Colossus, Titan and Thunder Dragon Fusion.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Thunder monster and every Fusion asks for Thunder materials, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Thunder monsters work on the whole theme.

hooks.label: Thunder hand effects
hooks.why: Thunder Dragon Titan, Colossus, Dragonduo and Dragonlord all trigger on a Thunder monster's effect being activated in the hand, so outside Thunder monsters that use themselves from the hand (Thunder Dragon, Dragondark, Dragonroar and Dragonhawk all discard themselves) fire those payoffs again.

hooks.label: Banishes your Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Thunder Dragondark, Dragonroar, Dragonhawk and Dragonmatrix each do something when they are banished, and Colossus, Titan, Dragonlord and Thunderstormech pay their costs by banishing Thunder monsters from the Deck, hand or GY.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: Titan, Colossus, Dragonlord, Dragonduo, Discharge and Thunderstormech all banish cards from the GY as costs, so outside monsters sitting in the GY with an effect when they are banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon from the GY
hooks.why: Thunder Dragon Fusion shuffles Thunder Fusion Materials from the field, GY and face-up banished cards, so extra cards that Fusion Summon using materials in the GY or banished pile give the deck more Colossus and Titan.

profile.plan: A Machine-Type toolbox of 'roid' monsters that fuses its named pieces into Vehicroid Fusion bosses (and Synchro Summons with the Speedroid Tuners), treating the Graveyard as a second hand.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every 'roid' monster and every Vehicroid Fusion in the deck is Machine-Type, so search, revival and ATK boosts that name Machine reach the entire deck.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: The Speedroid half of the archetype is entirely WIND, and Taketomborg and Rubberband Plane lock you into WIND Special Summons for the rest of the turn.

hooks.label: Extra Fusion Summoning
hooks.why: Vehicroid Connection Zone and Megaroid City exist only to put Vehicroid Fusion Monsters on the field, so any further way to Fusion Summon using the named 'roid' materials is welcome.

hooks.label: Machines that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Mixeroid can Tribute any Machine monster to Special Summon a non-WIND 'roid' from the Deck, so outside Machines with an effect when Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Fills the Graveyard with Machines
hooks.why: Mixeroid banishes Machine monsters from your Graveyard to Special Summon a 'roid' Fusion Monster of matching Level, so outside cards that send Machines from the Deck or hand to the GY set it up.

hooks.label: Machine GY recovery
hooks.why: Ambulanceroid Special Summons a 'roid' monster whenever one is added from your Graveyard to your hand, so outside cards that recover a Machine from the GY trigger it for free.

profile.plan: A Spell-heavy control deck whose Quick-Play Spells skip the next Battle Phase to banish the top cards of the opponent's Deck and Special Summon Runick Fusion monsters to the Extra Monster Zone, grinding the opponent out by deck-out while Runick Fountain recycles the Spells and lets them be fired on the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Hugin and Munin both discard 1 card on being Special Summoned to search the Field or Continuous Spell, so any outside monster with an effect when it is discarded turns that cost into free value.

hooks.label: Banishes the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Every Runick Quick-Play Spell banishes the top cards of the opponent's Deck, so outside cards that banish from the opponent's Deck directly shorten the clock to a deck-out.

hooks.label: Makes the opponent draw
hooks.why: Sleipnir the Runick Mane Special Summons a Runick Token whenever the opponent adds a card from the Main Deck to their hand, and Runick Golden Droplet is happy to hand them a draw, so cards that serve the opponent a card make bodies for free.

hooks.label: Spell Counter payoffs
hooks.why: Runick Allure banishes the top card of the opponent's Deck every time a Quick-Play Spell activates, and the deck fires three or more of them each turn, so cards that load up on Spell Counters do so immediately.

hooks.label: Field Spell search
hooks.why: Runick Fountain is the card that lets the Runick Quick-Play Spells be used on the opponent's turn and recycles them from the GY, but only Hugin searches it, so extra ways to find or place a Field Spell keep the engine online.

hooks.label: Effect damage finishers
hooks.why: Each Runick Quick-Play Spell skips your next Battle Phase and no Runick Fusion monster can deal meaningful battle damage, so outside cards that inflict effect damage are the deck's second, battle-free win condition.

profile.plan: The deck Ritual Summons Level 8 Black Luster Soldier monsters using LIGHT and DARK monsters from the hand, Deck and GY as material, and banishes those attributes from the GY to summon Chaos Envoys and power up its boss monsters.

hooks.label: Sends LIGHT/DARK to GY
hooks.why: Super Soldier Synthesis sends 1 LIGHT and 1 DARK from the hand and Deck to the GY, and Envoy of the Beginning, Envoy of the Evening Twilight and Envoy of Chaos all banish LIGHT and DARK monsters from the GY, so extra ways to fill the GY with those attributes are welcome.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from GY
hooks.why: The deck's Envoy monsters and Super Soldier Ritual banish LIGHT and DARK monsters from the GY as cost, so outside LIGHT/DARK monsters with effects that trigger when banished from the GY get a free activation.

hooks.label: Searches Ritual Spells
hooks.why: The deck needs Ritual Spells to summon its Black Luster Soldier Ritual Monsters, and Gateway to Chaos only searches one when it has 3 Spell Counters, so outside cards that add Ritual Spells are useful.

hooks.label: Searches Ritual Monsters
hooks.why: The deck needs Black Luster Soldier Ritual Monsters in hand to Ritual Summon, so outside cards that add Ritual Monsters speed up the deck.

hooks.label: Level 8 monster support
hooks.why: The deck is full of Level 8 monsters (the Black Luster Soldier Ritual Monsters and the Envoy monsters), so cards that discard or Tribute Level 8 monsters for advantage work well.

profile.plan: A Cyberse/DARK Link deck that repeatedly banishes its own monsters as cost, then pays LP to Special Summon them back from the banished pile and turns the banished Maliss Traps into ATK and recursion.

hooks.label: Banishes your own monsters
hooks.why: White Rabbit, Chessy Cat, Dormouse, March Hare and every Maliss Link boss pay 300 or 900 LP to Special Summon themselves or search the moment they are banished, so any card that banishes your own DARK Cyberse monster from the hand, Deck or GY becomes a free body or search.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Maliss monster and every Maliss Link boss is a Cyberse, so Cyberse searchers, revives and stat boosts reach the whole deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Maliss in Underground is the deck's engine - it banishes a Maliss card on activation and, with three banished Maliss Traps, gives every Maliss Link Monster 3000 ATK - so cards that find or place a Field Spell from the Deck set that up.

profile.plan: A Synchro Summoning deck that uses Junk Synchron and other Tuners to revive Level 2 or lower monsters and climb into Warrior Synchro bosses like Junk Warrior and Junk Destroyer.

hooks.label: Level 2 or lower Tuner self-summoners
hooks.why: Junk Synchron revives Level 2 or lower monsters, and the deck needs Tuners for Synchro Summons, so a Level 2 or lower Tuner that Special Summons itself gives you both a body and a Tuner for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when used as Synchro Material
hooks.why: Jet Synchron and Junk Converter both trigger when they are sent to the GY as Synchro Material, so outside monsters with the same trigger turn every Synchro Summon into an extra search or revival.

hooks.label: Special Summons a Tuner
hooks.why: Starlight Junktion Tributes a Tuner to Special Summon a Synchron from the Deck, and Junk Converter searches one by discarding a Tuner, so cards that Special Summon Tuners from the Deck or GY keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Adds a Tuner to hand
hooks.why: Junk Meister and Junk Converter search Junk and Synchron cards, and the deck lives on finding its Tuners, so outside cards that add a Tuner to hand are extra copies of that search.

hooks.label: Searches Warrior or Machine
hooks.why: The Main Deck Junk monsters are Warriors and Machines, and Junk Meister reveals a Warrior Synchro to Special Summon itself, so searching either Type finds your starters and extenders.

hooks.label: Changes a monster's Level
hooks.why: Junk Meister reduces a Junk monster's Level by up to 2 and Junk Changer shifts it by 1, so outside Level-changing effects let you hit exact Synchro levels the deck could not otherwise reach.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck of LIGHT Spellcaster and Illusion monsters that constantly sends its own Spell/Traps from the hand or field to the GY as activation fuel, then Sets them back and climbs into Level 6 and Level 8 Synchro Tuners.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck White Forest monster is a LIGHT Spellcaster, and Rciela adds a LIGHT Spellcaster monster from the Deck.

hooks.label: Spell/Trap that triggers in GY
hooks.why: Elzette, Astellar, Rciela, Rucia and Diabell all send 1 Spell/Trap from your hand or field to the GY as a cost, so outside Spell/Traps with a 'sent to the GY' effect get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Illusion support
hooks.why: Diabell and Poplar are Illusion Synchro Monsters, Scourge of the White Forest revives an Illusion monster from the GY, and Beware counts Illusion monsters for its condition.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck made almost entirely of Fiend Tuners that climbs Level 1-3 'Resonator' monsters into DARK Dragon Synchro Monsters, especially the Red Dragon Archfiend line, and locks itself into that path while searching Fiends and Normal Summoning repeatedly.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Resonator monster is a Fiend Tuner, so outside cards that search, revive or strengthen Fiends apply to the whole archetype.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Red Resonator, Chain Resonator, Soul Resonator and Darkness Resonator all give value the moment a Resonator is Normal Summoned, so outside cards that add a Normal Summon or trigger on one keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Red Dragon Archfiend support
hooks.why: Vision Resonator searches a Spell/Trap that mentions Red Dragon Archfiend and the deck's goal is to summon it, so outside cards built around Red Dragon Archfiend slot straight in.

hooks.label: Triggers when used as material
hooks.why: The deck Synchro Summons every turn and Resonant Destruction rewards Resonators being sent as Synchro Material, so outside monsters with an effect when used as material get that value for free.

profile.plan: A Machine/WATER Synchro deck that destroys its own cards to summon Crystron Tuners from the Deck, then Synchro Summons during the opponent's turn while banishing and recycling its own cards.

hooks.label: Machine and WATER support
hooks.why: Every Crystron monster is a Machine and WATER, and Smiger, Thystvern, Rosenix and Prasiortle lock you into Machine-Type Synchro Monsters, so cards that support Machine or WATER monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Banished from GY trigger
hooks.why: Smiger, Thystvern, Rosenix, Prasiortle, Tristaros, Crystron Inclusion, Crystron Impact and Crystron Entry all banish themselves from the GY as cost, so outside cards with an effect when banished from the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Destroyed trigger
hooks.why: The main deck Crystron monsters destroy a face-up card you control to summon a Crystron Tuner from the Deck, and the Crystron Synchro monsters all trigger when destroyed, so outside cards that float when destroyed are easy to use.

hooks.label: Mills Machine or WATER
hooks.why: The deck wants Crystron monsters in the GY to banish for effects, so outside cards that send a Machine or WATER monster from the Deck to the GY (like Foolish Burial) fuel the whole engine.

profile.plan: @Ignister is a Cyberse combo deck that swarms the field with monsters of every Attribute, turns them into Link, Ritual, Fusion, Synchro and Xyz bosses, and locks itself into Cyberse Special Summons while filling the GY with Link Material.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every @Ignister monster and every boss is Cyberse, and Ignister A.I.Land forbids you from Special Summoning anything except Cyberse monsters, so Cyberse-only support works on the entire deck.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Ten of the archetype's monsters are DARK, and Backup @Ignister searches a DARK Cyberse monster while Wizard @Ignister revives one from the GY.

hooks.label: Wants to be Link Material
hooks.why: Doyon @Ignister, Bururu @Ignister and Linkslayer @Ignister all trigger when they are sent to the GY as material, so outside Cyberse monsters with an effect when used as material get turned on for free by every Link, Synchro and Fusion Summon the deck performs.

profile.plan: A Level 5 deck that Normal Summons its monsters without Tribute, stacks two of them into Rank 5 Xyz Monsters, and then uses those Xyz Monsters' detach effects to answer whatever the opponent plays from hand or GY.

hooks.label: Level 5 extenders
hooks.why: Every K9 Xyz Monster asks for two Level 5 materials, and Jokul reveals itself plus another Level 5 monster in hand to Special Summon both, so free Level 5 bodies are exactly what the deck is short of.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon cards
hooks.why: Izuna, Jokul, Lantern and Noroi are all Level 5 monsters that can be Normal Summoned without Tributing, so an extra Normal Summon puts a second Rank 5 material on board in one turn.

hooks.label: Xyz Material refill
hooks.why: Ripper, Jacks, Hound and Werewolf all detach a material as the cost of their Quick Effects, so anything that attaches material back to an Xyz Monster keeps the negations and multi-attacks online.

hooks.label: Level 5 millers
hooks.why: Lantern revives a Level 5 non-Pyro K9 from the GY, Lupis revives itself from the GY and Special Release Experiment Summons a K9 from the GY, so sending Level 5 monsters from the Deck to the GY sets all of them up at once.

hooks.label: Generic Rank 5 Xyz
hooks.why: K9-LC Release Restraint can target any Rank 5 Xyz Monster you control, so outside Rank 5 Xyz are interchangeable bases the deck climbs from into its own K9 Xyz Monsters.

profile.plan: A DARK Fairy deck that pays 1000 LP over and over to re-apply its own 'Darklord' Spells and Traps from the Graveyard, Tribute Summons huge Fairies and Fusion Summons DARK Fairy bosses.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Darklord monster is a Fairy, and Indulged Darklord, Djehuty and Gulgolet lock you into Special Summoning and activating only Fairy monsters, so generic Fairy support lifts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fairies with Graveyard triggers
hooks.why: Darklord Asmodeus sends a Fairy from the Deck to the Graveyard, Condemned Darklord discards a card and Darklord Dance banishes Fairies from the Graveyard as material, so DARK Fairies that do something from the Graveyard get used for free.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Darklord Morningstar and Darklord Desire cannot be Special Summoned and are Tribute Summoned, Capricious Darklord lets you Tribute Summon a Fairy during the Main Phase, and Condemned Darklord lets you Tribute Summon 2-Tribute Fairies by banishing 2 monsters instead.

hooks.label: "Forbidden" Quick-Play Spells
hooks.why: Darklord Gulgolet and Darklord Djehuty both search a "Forbidden" Quick-Play Spell, so the deck can run them as extra copies of whatever those cards grab.

profile.plan: A deck of EARTH Insect hand traps that Special Summon themselves in response to the opponent's Summons, clogging their field and punishing Extra Deck and Synchro Summons, while using the Graveyard and same-name Insects for follow-up.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is an Insect, so cards that search, revive, or protect Insects support the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Insects to GY
hooks.why: Super Armored Robot Armed Black Iron 'C' needs 3 Insect monsters with the same name in the GY, and Retaliating 'C' and Shiny Black 'C' use the GY, so sending Insects there sets up the deck's payoffs.

hooks.label: Tributes your Insect
hooks.why: Retaliating 'C' searches an EARTH Insect with 1500 or less ATK when it is sent from the field to the GY, so effects that Tribute or send an Insect you control trigger it.

hooks.label: Banished-matter monsters
hooks.why: Retaliating 'C' makes any card sent to the GY be banished instead while it is face-up, so monsters that trigger when banished get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Shiny Black 'C' Squadder is a Level 4 Normal Insect, so cards that add or Special Summon Normal Monsters from the Deck give the deck a 2000 ATK body and Xyz material.

profile.plan: A toolbox of 'Guardian' monsters whose Summons are gated behind specific Equip Spells, which the deck then converts into banishes, destruction, battle protection, Ritual plays and Level 7-8 Dragon recursion.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: Guardian Baou, Kay'est, Ceal, Tryce, Elma and Grarl can only be Summoned while their named Equip Spell is face-up, and Guardian Elma can re-equip any Equip Spell from the Graveyard, so cards that fetch Equip Spells from the Deck or GY are the deck's real consistency engine.

hooks.label: Ritual support
hooks.why: Skull Guardian, Protector of the Voiceless Voice searches Ritual Monsters and Guardian of the Voiceless Voice Special Summons it and pumps a Ritual Monster with the combined ATK of the field, so any Ritual engine feeds the deck's secondary plan.

hooks.label: Spell Counter cards
hooks.why: Power of the Guardians puts a Spell Counter on itself on every attack and removes one to save the equipped monster from destruction, so cards that place or consume Spell Counters amplify that loop.

hooks.label: Equip Spell senders
hooks.why: Guardian Elma re-equips any appropriate Equip Spell from the Graveyard, Guardian Eatos banishes with an Equip Spell sent to the GY and Guardian of Felgrand revives after Tributing itself, so effects that drop Equip Spells into the GY set up all three.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Psychic deck that Special Summons its monsters from hand into columns when 2 or more cards share a column, then uses column-based removal, negation and searches, with World Legacy and Orcust cards as support.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Mekk-Knight is a Psychic monster, so generic Psychic support like Emergency Teleport can Special Summon them from the Deck and trigger their effects.

hooks.label: World Legacy cards
hooks.why: Girsu sends a 'World Legacy' card from Deck to GY, Morning Star discards one to search, and World Legacy Key recovers them, so more outside World Legacy cards give fodder and utility.

hooks.label: Orcust cards
hooks.why: Girsu can send an 'Orcust' card from Deck to GY, and Enlilgirsu requires an 'Orcust' Link Monster, so outside Orcust cards fit the mixed strategy.

hooks.label: Opponent-field token makers
hooks.why: The Mekk-Knights Special Summon themselves when 2 or more cards are in the same column, and Blue Sky searches based on opponent's cards in its column, so outside cards that put tokens on the opponent's field set up columns.

hooks.label: Self-summoning opponent monsters
hooks.why: The deck wants cards in columns to enable its own Special Summons and column effects, so outside monsters that Special Summon themselves to the opponent's field (like Kaiju) give you a column target while removing a threat.

profile.plan: A control deck that Sets its Level 5 LIGHT Fairy monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as Spells, then Special Summons them during the opponent's turn when those Set cards are destroyed, turning the opponent's turn into a board of disruptive Xyz plays.

hooks.label: Destroys your own backrow
hooks.why: Every Artifact Sets itself in the Spell & Trap Zone as a Spell and only Special Summons itself once that Set card is destroyed and sent to the GY, so outside cards that pop your own Spell/Trap are activators.

hooks.label: Fairy and LIGHT support
hooks.why: Every Artifact monster and the Xyz Artifact Durendal are LIGHT Fairies, so cards that search, revive or boost Fairies or LIGHT work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Summons Level 5 monsters
hooks.why: Durendal and Artifacts Unleashed both need Level 5 monsters on the field, and the Artifacts can only be Set from the hand, so outside cards that Special Summon Level 5 monsters supply the material.

profile.plan: An EARTH Insect/Plant deck that sets, searches and recycles "Hole" Normal Trap Cards for removal, while its Traptrix monsters trigger on their own Normal and Special Summons to build Link and Rank 4 Xyz boards.

hooks.label: Hole Normal Traps
hooks.why: Traptrix Myrmeleo searches "Hole" Normal Traps, Traptrix Sera Sets them from the Deck, Traptrix Atrax activates them from hand and Traptrix Rafflesia copies them, so any outside "Hole" Normal Trap plugs straight into the engine.

hooks.label: Normal Trap finders
hooks.why: Traptrix Sera Sets a "Hole" Normal Trap from the Deck whenever another Traptrix effect resolves, and Traptrix Atrax lets them be activated from hand, so cards that add or Set Normal Traps keep the engine fed.

hooks.label: Traps to the Graveyard
hooks.why: Traptrix Dionaea and Traptrix Vesiculo Set "Hole" Normal Traps from the Graveyard, and Traptrix Atypus banishes Normal Traps from the GY for 1000 ATK and a destruction, so milling Normal Traps is pure value.

hooks.label: Insect and Plant support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Traptrix is an EARTH Insect or Plant, Traptrix Allomerus revives Level 4 Insect or Plant monsters and Traptrix Atypus needs Insect/Plant bodies, so generic Insect and Plant support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Monsters that want banishing
hooks.why: Traptrip Garden banishes 1 monster you control to Special Summon a Traptrix from the hand or GY, so an outside monster that pays you back when it is banished turns that cost into an extra effect.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Myrmeleo, Dionaea, Mantis and Pudica only fire when Normal Summoned, so extra Normal Summons add another search, revival or banish on top of Traptrip Garden's own extra Summon.

profile.plan: A deck that assembles the five Forbidden One pieces in hand to win outright, or dumps them into the Graveyard to fuel Exodia Necross, Exodius and The Legendary Exodia Incarnate instead.

hooks.label: Mills or discards your monsters
hooks.why: Contract with Exodia needs all five Forbidden One pieces in the Graveyard to Summon Exodia Necross, Exodius shuffles the Graveyard back and grows off it, and The Legendary Exodia Incarnate recovers a piece from the Graveyard each End Phase.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: The four limbs are Normal Monsters, so anything that searches, revives or recycles Normal Monsters gathers the pieces into the hand for the win or into the Graveyard for Exodius.

hooks.label: Spellcaster / DARK support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is a DARK Spellcaster, so cards that search, revive or boost Spellcasters and DARK monsters reach the whole deck.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Exodia, the Legendary Defender is Tribute Summoned with 5 Tributes and The Legendary Exodia Incarnate is Special Summoned by Tributing a Forbidden One monster, so extra Tribute Summons and Tribute fodder speed both up.

profile.plan: A Beast-Warrior Fusion deck that mills and discards its own Lunalight monsters into the GY to trigger their effects, then Fusion Summons Dancers that attack multiple times and wipe the opponent's board.

hooks.label: Mills a DARK Beast-Warrior
hooks.why: Kaleido Chick, Emerald Bird, Yellow Marten, Silver Hound, Crimson Fox and Scarlet Tiger all trigger when a card effect sends them to the GY, so any outside card that mills or sends a DARK Beast-Warrior is another starter.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Luna Light Perfume, Gold Leo and Masquerade all discard a card as part of their effects, so an outside monster with an effect when it is discarded gets that for free.

hooks.label: Polymerization searchers
hooks.why: Black Sheep searches Polymerization from the Deck, Kaleido Chick recovers it from the GY and Masquerade returns it from the GY or banishment, so extra copies or tutors of Polymerization keep the Fusion Summons coming.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Lunalight monster is a Beast-Warrior and Sabre Dancer gains 200 ATK for each Beast-Warrior in the GYs or banished, so Beast-Warrior support lifts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon Spells
hooks.why: Lunalight Fusion, Lunalight Masquerade and Wolf's Pendulum effect all Fusion Summon Lunalight Fusion Monsters, and Serenade Dance rewards any Fusion Summon to your field, so generic Fusion Spells add more Dancers.

profile.plan: A Spell-heavy control deck that chains its 'Spellbook' Spell Cards to search, recover and banish from the Graveyard, then cashes the pile in for Spellcaster-Type Xyz and Level 5 or higher Spellcaster bosses.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Spellcaster-Type, and Spellbook of Fate, Spellbook of Wisdom, Spellbook of Power and Amores of Prophecy all require or target a Spellcaster-Type monster.

hooks.label: Spellcasters that like the GY
hooks.why: Spellbook of Knowledge sends a Spellcaster you control to the Graveyard, and Spellbook of Life and Emperor of Prophecy banish Spellcaster-Type monsters, so Spellcasters with an effect when they are sent there or banished get their trigger for free.

hooks.label: Sends Spell Cards to the GY
hooks.why: Spellbook of Fate, Hierophant of Prophecy, Fool of Prophecy and Spellbook Library of the Heliosphere all count Spell Cards sitting in your Graveyard, so cards that put Spell Cards there from the Deck charge them up.

hooks.label: Spell Counter cards
hooks.why: Spellbook Star Hall gains a Spell Counter every time a 'Spellbook' Spell is activated and converts them into ATK and a Spellcaster search, so outside cards that place or spend Spell Counters share the deck's Spell-heavy resource.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Spellcasters
hooks.why: Empress of Prophecy and Hierophant of Prophecy need Level 5 and Level 7 Spellcaster-Type materials and Crowley, the First Propheseer needs 2 Spellcasters, so Spellcaster monsters that Special Summon themselves supply bodies this Spell-heavy deck struggles to put on board.

profile.plan: Gladiator Beasts attack, then at the end of the Battle Phase shuffle themselves into the Deck to Special Summon another Gladiator Beast from the Deck (or shuffle field materials into the Deck for a Fusion), looping battle after battle.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Laquari, Darius, Attorix, Noxious and the Beast-Warrior Fusion Monsters are the deck's backbone, so cards that search, revive or pump Beast-Warriors reach its key pieces.

hooks.label: Battle protection for your monsters
hooks.why: A Gladiator Beast only tags out at the end of a Battle Phase in which it attacked or was attacked and survived, and their ATK is low, so cards that keep your monsters alive through battle let them swing for free.

hooks.label: Forces the opponent to attack
hooks.why: The shuffle-back also triggers when a Gladiator Beast is attacked, and Noxious Special Summons itself when the opponent declares a direct attack, so cards that force or redirect attacks start the engine on the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: The deck can only start by Normal Summoning a Gladiator Beast to attack with, so an extra Normal Summon gives a second body for a Fusion or another tag-out in the same Battle Phase.

profile.plan: A Level 2 Aqua/WATER swarm deck: Swap Frog, Substitoad and Treeborn Frog flood the field and the Graveyard so it can make Rank 2 Toadally Awesome, negate the opponent's plays with Aqua monsters, and grind back with Frog and WATER recovery.

hooks.label: WATER monsters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Swap Frog Special Summons itself by discarding 1 other WATER monster, so a WATER monster with an effect when it is discarded turns that cost into free value.

hooks.label: Aqua monsters with Graveyard triggers
hooks.why: Toadally Awesome negates by sending 1 Aqua-Type monster from your hand or face-up field to the Graveyard, and Swap Frog sends Level 2 or lower WATER Aqua monsters from the Deck or field there, so Aqua monsters that do something when sent to the GY get paid for by those costs.

hooks.label: Aqua and WATER support
hooks.why: Every Frog in the deck is an Aqua WATER monster, and Toadally Awesome asks for Level 2 Aqua materials while adding a WATER monster back from the Graveyard, so anything that supports either Type or Attribute helps the whole deck.

hooks.label: Monsters that pay you when Tributed
hooks.why: Substitoad Tributes 1 monster to Special Summon a Frog from the Deck and Tradetoad Tributes 1 Aqua-Type monster to revive a Frog from the Graveyard, so monsters that trigger when they are Tributed are free fuel for the engine.

hooks.label: Sends Aqua WATER to the Graveyard
hooks.why: Swap Frog sends a Level 2 or lower WATER Aqua monster from the Deck to the Graveyard, and the deck wants that Graveyard loaded so Ronintoadin can banish a Frog to revive itself and Toadally Awesome can add a WATER monster back, so outside copies of that send effect are extra setup.

profile.plan: A Trap deck that fires Normal Traps straight from the hand to negate the opponent's plays, then locks itself out of named Attributes and reloads by Setting more Traps from the Deck or GY.

hooks.label: Trap-to-GY enablers
hooks.why: Dominus Impulse and Dominus Purge only destroy the negated card if you have a Trap in the GY, and Dominus Spark and Dominus Spiral give the opponent a free Summon if you have none.

hooks.label: Discard payoff monsters
hooks.why: Dominusteer Rosepamela adds Dominus Purge from the Deck and then discards 1 card, so monsters that trigger when discarded get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Normal Trap setters
hooks.why: The whole deck is Normal Traps you want to fire from the hand, and Dominusteer Rosepamela only Sets one of them per Summon, so more copies Set from the Deck are extra negates.

hooks.label: Spellcaster and LIGHT support
hooks.why: Dominusteer Rosepamela is a LIGHT Spellcaster and the deck's only monster, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT Spellcasters keep the engine running.

profile.plan: Normal Summons its Level 7 Warrior Gaias without Tributing, fuses one with a Level 5 Dragon into "Gaia the Dragon Champion" for the Spiral Spell/Trap payoffs, and Tributes its own Knights to fetch Black Luster Soldier plays.

hooks.label: Tributers of your monsters
hooks.why: Charging Gaia the Fierce Knight adds a Black Luster Soldier when Tributed and Arisen Gaia the Fierce Knight Special Summons one, so outside cards that Tribute your own Level 7 Warriors turn them into value.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Gaia monster is a Warrior, so cards that search, revive, boost or protect Warriors work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: Equips its own Dragon Tuners to its Winged Beast monsters, then Synchro Summons Dragon Synchro Monsters that keep equipping cards and banishing the opponent's.

hooks.label: Dragon & Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Dragunity monster is either a Dragon or a Winged Beast, and every Synchro Summon combines the two Types, so support for either Type works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Dragons to the GY
hooks.why: Dux, Legionnaire, Vajrayana and Luin all equip a Dragon from the Graveyard, and Dragon Ravine dumps a Dragon from the Deck, so extra Deck-to-GY effects for Dragons feed the engine.

hooks.label: Discarded from the hand
hooks.why: Dragon Ravine, Senatus and Gae Dearg all discard a card as the cost of their effects, so outside cards that do something when they are discarded get that for free.

profile.plan: Ninjas hide in face-down Defense Position and flip themselves up for effects, while Ninjitsu Art Traps Tribute them to cheat Beast, Insect, Dragon and other big monsters straight out of the Deck.

hooks.label: Face-down Defense Position setters
hooks.why: Meizen the Battle Ninja cannot be targeted while you control a face-down Defense Position monster, and Mitsu the Insect Ninja, Kagero the Cannon Ninja, Green Ninja, Tobari and Jioh all want your own Ninja face-down, so cards that turn monsters face-down or Summon them that way feed the whole deck.

hooks.label: Flip-up enablers
hooks.why: Armed Ninja, White Ninja and Crimson Ninja are FLIP monsters, and Kagero, Baku, Tobari, Jioh, Yaguramaru and Yellow Ninja all trigger when a Ninja is Special Summoned or flipped face-up, so outside cards that flip your own face-down monsters up start those effects.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Almost every Ninja is a Warrior - Hanzo, Sasuke, Shingetsu, Yellow Ninja and Twilight Ninja Getsuga all live on that Type - and Blade Armor Ninja asks for two Level 4 Warrior-Type materials.

hooks.label: Ninjitsu Art cheat targets
hooks.why: Ninjitsu Art of Transformation, Ninjitsu Art of Super-Transformation and Ninjitsu Art of Duplication Special Summon Beasts, Winged Beasts, Insects, Dragons, Dinosaurs and Sea Serpents from the Deck, so monsters that cannot be Normal Summoned/Set become free bosses.

hooks.label: Traps that want the GY
hooks.why: Upstart Golden Ninja sends a Trap from your hand to the GY to Special Summon a Ninja from the Deck, so Trap cards that do something when they are sent to the GY turn that cost into extra value.

profile.plan: Places its monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, then cashes them in for Special Summons, board wipes and a seven-material Fusion boss.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: The deck's Field Spells are central, so outside cards that add or place a Field Spell from the Deck get to them faster.

hooks.label: Protects Field Spells
hooks.why: The deck's Field Spells are key continuous pieces, so outside cards that stop them from being destroyed or targeted keep the engine running.

hooks.label: DARK GY summons
hooks.why: The deck can turn its monsters in the GY DARK, so outside monsters that Special Summon themselves by banishing DARK monsters from the GY have fodder.

hooks.label: Fusion from the Graveyard
hooks.why: The deck's big Fusion Monster needs seven of its monsters, and they pile up in the GY; outside Fusion Spells that use materials from the GY can summon it.

hooks.label: Symmetric board wipes
hooks.why: The deck's monsters replace themselves in the Spell & Trap Zone when destroyed, so outside cards that destroy all monsters are less harmful and can trigger its destruction payoffs.
phrases: destroy all monsters on the field

hooks.label: Protects your backrow
hooks.why: The deck's monsters live in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, so outside cards that protect Spell/Trap Cards keep the engine alive.

profile.plan: A LIGHT swarm deck that floods the field with Level 4 Photon monsters (and their Tokens) to Xyz Summon, while Normal-Summon triggers, GY effects and a small Ritual sub-line keep the engine running.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster support
hooks.why: Every Photon monster is LIGHT, and Photon Sanctuary, Photon Delta Wing and Photon Veil only let you Summon, Special Summon or shuffle LIGHT monsters.

hooks.label: Level 4 LIGHT extenders
hooks.why: Accellight, Photon Lead, Photon Veil and Photon Booster all reach only Level 4 or lower LIGHT monsters, and Photon Papilloperative is a Rank 4 that wants Level 4 material.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Photon Emperor grants an additional Normal Summon of a LIGHT monster, and Photon Sabre Tiger, Photon Caesar, Photon Wyvern, Photon Leo, Photon Delta Wing and Lillybot all trigger when Normal Summoned.

hooks.label: Cards that dump LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Photon Emperor and Photon Jumper both trigger when they are sent to the GY, and Kuriphoton sends a Photon monster from the hand to the GY, so any outside card that discards or mills LIGHT monsters is another starter.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: Luminous Dragon Ritual is the deck's only way into Paladin of Photon Dragon and nothing in the archetype searches it, so outside cards that add Ritual Spells from the Deck complete that line.

profile.plan: A Synchro Summon combo deck that uses many Machine-Type Tuner monsters to Synchro Summon repeatedly, often during the opponent's turn, and rewards each Synchro Summon with draws, damage or Tokens.

hooks.label: Machine Duplication targets
hooks.why: Many of the deck's Tuner monsters are Machine-Type with 500 or less ATK, so any card that Special Summons such monsters from the Deck gives you multiple Tuners at once.

hooks.label: Draw on Synchro Summon
hooks.why: One of its Synchro Monsters draws a card when Synchro Summoned, and the deck Synchro Summons many times per turn, so cards that draw on each Synchro Summon turn each Summon into advantage.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: One of its monsters lets you Normal Summon an extra Tuner monster each turn, so outside cards that grant an additional Normal Summon let you extend further.

hooks.label: Effects when used as Synchro Material
hooks.why: The deck Synchro Summons constantly, so outside monsters that give you value when they are used as Synchro Material act as free extenders.

profile.plan: A Psychic/WIND and Wyrm/EARTH deck of Level 3 and Level 6 monsters that Special Summon themselves by sending a Virtual World card of a different type from the Deck to the GY, climbing into Synchro and Rank 3/6/9 Xyz plays while its Continuous Spell/Trap Gates banish themselves from the GY for value.

hooks.label: Psychic and Wyrm support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Virtual World monster is Psychic or Wyrm (Lulu, Nyannyan, Laolao are Psychic; Lili, Jiji, Toutou are Wyrm), and Oto-Hime - Toutou needs a Psychic or Wyrm monster as its discard cost.

hooks.label: Special Summons Level 3 monsters
hooks.why: Hime - Nyannyan Special Summons itself from the GY whenever any Level 3 monster is Summoned to your field, and Shell - Jaja and Dragon - Longlong are Rank 3 Xyz that need Level 3 material.

hooks.label: Special Summons Level 6 monsters
hooks.why: Kirin - Lili, Roshi - Laolao and Oto-Hime - Toutou are Level 6, so outside cards that bring out Level 6 bodies feed Phoenix - Fanfan's Xyz Summon and the Level 3 + Level 6 Synchro into Kyubi - Shenshen.

hooks.label: Profits from being banished
hooks.why: Kyubi - Shenshen replaces every send from the field to the GY with a banish, and the Gate cards banish themselves from the GY, so an outside card with an "if this card is banished" effect gets it for free.

hooks.label: Psychic or Wyrm to discard
hooks.why: Oto-Hime - Toutou's GY effect discards 1 Psychic or Wyrm monster as a cost to revive itself as a Tuner, so an outside Psychic or Wyrm monster with a discard trigger gets used for free.

profile.plan: A collection of Book Spells that manipulate battle positions (face-up/face-down), revive Zombies, and equip Spellcasters, used as a flexible disruption and support package.

hooks.label: Discard triggers
hooks.why: Book of Lunar Eclipse discards a card as cost, so monsters that gain effects when discarded get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Book of Life Special Summons a Zombie from your GY, so cards that support Zombies by sending them to the GY or reviving them work with it.

hooks.label: Face-down monster support
hooks.why: Book of Moon and Book of Eclipse can turn your own monsters face-down, enabling cards that need a face-down monster you control.

hooks.label: Banish face-down monsters
hooks.why: Book of Moon, Eclipse and Lunar Eclipse turn opponent's monsters face-down, so cards that banish face-down monsters can remove them permanently.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck that mixes its own Normal Monsters and Type-specific partner monsters from the hand, Deck and GY into Gem-Knight Fusion Monsters, with Lazuli, Obsidian, Nepyrim and Alexandrite turning every sent material into another monster or Fusion Summon.

hooks.label: Fetches Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Gem-Knight Lazuli adds a Normal Monster from the GY, Gem-Knight Obsidian revives a Level 4 or lower Normal Monster, Gem-Knight Alexandrite Summons a Gem-Knight Normal Monster from the Deck, and Garnet, Lapis, Sapphire, Tourmaline and Crystal are all Normal Monsters.

hooks.label: Gemini support
hooks.why: Gem-Knight Amber, Sardonyx and Iolite are Gemini monsters that count as Normal Monsters in the GY until they are Normal Summoned again, which feeds Lazuli, Obsidian and Emerald, so cards that make that second Normal Summon or support Gemini monsters are live.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fusion fodder
hooks.why: Gem-Knight Seraphinite asks for 1 LIGHT monster, and Brilliant Fusion and Crystal Rose dump the materials from the Deck into the GY, so a LIGHT monster that pays off when it is sent there is value for free.

hooks.label: Type-matched Fusion material
hooks.why: The Gem-Knight Fusions name a monster Type as their second material - Prismaura a Thunder, Amethyst an Aqua, Citrine a Pyro, Zirconia a Rock and Lady Rose Diamond a Fairy - and Brilliant Fusion, Gem-Knight Dispersion and Crystal Rose send those materials from the Deck or hand to the GY.

hooks.label: Deck-to-GY senders
hooks.why: Gem-Knight Lazuli, Gem-Knight Nepyrim, Crystal Rose and Gem-Knight Hollowcore all trigger when a Gem-Knight is sent from the Deck to the GY, so any outside card that mills a monster is another starter for the Fusion Summons.

profile.plan: A deck of Level 3 DARK Fiends that self-destruct if you control a non-Burning Abyss monster, but when sent to the Graveyard they trigger effects that search, revive, banish or burn, so the deck mills and discards itself to Xyz Summon Dante, Link Summon Cherubini, and overwhelm the opponent.

hooks.label: Mills a BA monster
hooks.why: Every Malebranche has an effect when sent to the Graveyard, so any card that sends a Level 3 DARK Fiend from your Deck to the GY triggers Scarm, Graff, Cir and the rest.

hooks.label: Discards a BA monster
hooks.why: The Malebranche only need to be sent to the Graveyard, so discarding a Level 3 DARK Fiend from your hand as a cost triggers its Graveyard effect.

hooks.label: Summons a Level 3 Fiend
hooks.why: Dante and Cherubini need Level 3 monsters, and Tour Guide From the Underworld summons a Level 3 Fiend from the Deck to make them immediately.

hooks.label: Fiend/DARK support
hooks.why: The whole Main Deck is Level 3 DARK Fiends, so cards that support Fiends or DARK monsters, especially those that mention Level 3, can search, revive or protect them.

hooks.label: Ritual support
hooks.why: Malacoda needs 'Good & Evil in the Burning Abyss', so cards that add Ritual Spells or Ritual Monsters from the Deck set up the Ritual Summon.

hooks.label: Fiend that mills itself
hooks.why: Fiendish Rhino Warrior protects your Fiends from the self-destruct effect and, when sent to the GY, sends a Fiend from Deck to GY, triggering another Malebranche.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Xyz deck: Level 4 LIGHT Pyro and FIRE Thunder monsters Special Summon themselves from the hand, then stack into Rank 4 Xyz Monsters that keep reloading material from the GY and detaching it as fuel.

hooks.label: Level 4 GY effects
hooks.why: Palm Ryzeal sends 1 Level 4 monster from your hand or Deck to the GY to gain its ATK, so Level 4 monsters with an effect in the GY are sent there for free.

hooks.label: Xyz material payoffs
hooks.why: Ryzeal Detonator, Ryzeal Duo Drive and Ryzeal Cross all detach materials to attack, destroy, add cards or negate, so monsters that do something when detached as Xyz material get paid again and again.

profile.plan: A Pendulum Dragon deck that Pendulum Summons Level 7 monsters to Xyz Summon Rank 7 Dragons, places monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, and turns the destruction of its own Pendulum monsters into revivals and extra attacks.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every card in the archetype is a Dragon, and key Summons (Xyz, Fusion, Tribute) require Dragon monsters as material or Tributes.

hooks.label: Searches Pendulum Monsters
hooks.why: The deck needs Pendulum Scales to Pendulum Summon Level 7, and some of its monsters recover Dragon Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck; outside cards that add Pendulum Monsters from the Deck set up scales.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: The archetype has cards that Special Summon themselves by Tributing your monsters, so outside monsters with effects when Tributed turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monster
hooks.why: Several Pendulum monsters in the archetype trigger when a card you control is destroyed by battle or card effect, so outside cards that destroy your own Dragon Pendulum monster turn them on.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster Pendulum deck that accumulates Spell Counters on its cards to summon monsters, negate activations, and destroy the opponent's field.

hooks.label: Spell Counter generators
hooks.why: The deck's engine is built on placing and removing Spell Counters; Endymion, Magister, and Servant all need them to activate, and Magical Citadel stores them.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Endymion monster is a Spellcaster, and the deck's key summons (Selene, Magister, Lab) require Spellcasters, so generic Spellcaster support fits.

hooks.label: Discard triggers
hooks.why: Servant of Endymion discards a card to place Spell Counters on all your cards, and Endymion, the Master Magician discards a Spell to destroy a card, so outside cards with discard effects get free value.

hooks.label: Banished Spellcaster triggers
hooks.why: Genni, the Maid of Endymion banishes a Spellcaster you control to Special Summon a 'Witchcrafter' from the Deck, so outside Spellcasters with banish effects get value.

hooks.label: Witchcrafter support
hooks.why: Verre, the Maid of Endymion adds a 'Witchcrafter' Spell/Trap or 'Magical Dimension', and Genni, the Maid of Endymion Special Summons a 'Witchcrafter' monster from the Deck.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that fills both Pendulum Zones to summon many monsters at once, then uses destruction effects to search, Fusion Summons with its Pendulum monsters, and boosts ATK above original values for extra draws and revives.

hooks.label: Odd-Eyes monsters
hooks.why: Performapal Gentrude and Performapal Splashmammoth search or Special Summon 'Odd-Eyes' cards, and Performapal Popperup can Special Summon them from the hand.

hooks.label: Magician Pendulum Monsters
hooks.why: Performapal Popperup and Performapal Smile Sorcerer count 'Magician' Pendulum Monsters as valid targets, and Performapal Celestial Magician adds one from the Deck.

hooks.label: Polymerization and Fusion support
hooks.why: Performapal Trump Witch adds 'Polymerization' from the Deck or Graveyard, so any card that mentions Polymerization or provides Fusion Summoning is useful.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monsters that trigger when destroyed
hooks.why: Performapal Pendulum Sorcerer destroys cards you control to search, and Performapal Lizardraw destroys itself to draw, so outside Pendulum Monsters with destruction triggers get value.

hooks.label: Sets Spell/Trap cards
hooks.why: Performapal Five-Rainbow Magician doubles ATK when you have 4 or more Set cards in your Spell & Trap Zones, so cards that Set Spells/Traps from the Deck or Graveyard help reach that.

profile.plan: Summons the three Level 10 boss monsters by feeding Continuous Spells, Continuous Traps and Fiend monsters, then protects them with a Field Spell and grinds back the Continuous cards from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Fiends
hooks.why: The DARK boss must Tribute 3 Fiend-Type monsters and the alternate DARK boss Tributes 3 monsters, so Fiends that Special Summon themselves provide Tribute fodder without using the Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Tributable monsters
hooks.why: The deck Tributes monsters for the DARK boss, for its alternate's Graveyard recovery, and for the Level 1 that summons a boss from hand, so monsters with a Tribute trigger get value.

hooks.label: Mills Continuous Traps
hooks.why: The FIRE boss gains 1000 ATK for each Continuous Trap in the GY, and the deck can send Traps from hand or Deck to the GY, so outside cards that dump Continuous Traps grow it.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck that Ritual Summons any Ritual Monster by Tributing LIGHT Machine monsters (the Drytrons are 2000 ATK Level 1 bodies that revive each other off a Tribute), so each Tribute becomes a search and a big Ritual boss hits the field.

hooks.label: Negating Ritual bosses
hooks.why: Meteonis Drytron can Ritual Summon any Ritual Monster from the hand or GY and the Level 1 Drytrons pay its Machine-ATK cost, so the deck splashes outside Ritual bosses that negate.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Machines
hooks.why: Meteonis Drytron pays for a Ritual with Machine monsters from the hand or field whose total ATK covers it, so a Machine that Special Summons itself is a free body for the cost.

hooks.label: Ritual Monsters with Tribute triggers
hooks.why: Alpha Thuban, Zeta Aldhibah and the other Drytrons Tribute a Ritual Monster from the hand or field as their cost, so an outside Ritual Monster with an effect when it is Tributed triggers for free.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Drytron monster is a Machine and Meteonis Drytron can only be paid with Machine monsters, so outside Machine support reaches the entire deck.

hooks.label: Ritual piece searchers
hooks.why: Alpha Thuban adds a Ritual Monster and Zeta Aldhibah adds a Ritual Spell, so outside cards that fetch Ritual Monsters or Ritual Spells from the Deck build the same two-card Ritual setups.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Beast combo deck of Level 1 monsters that Link Summon Yummy★Snatchy, treat Link-1 monsters as Level 1 Tuners, and Synchro Summon Level 2 Yummy Way Tuners whose on-Summon and Quick Effects flood the field and trigger the Yummy Field Spells.

hooks.label: LIGHT Beast support
hooks.why: Every Yummy monster is a LIGHT Beast, and Yummyusment☆Mignon and Yummy★Redemption count LIGHT Beast monsters on your field and in your GY for ATK boosts and debuffs.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Yummy★Snatchy places a Yummy Field Spell from the Deck and Marshmao☆Yummy places a Yummy Field or Continuous Spell/Trap from the Deck or banishment, so outside cards that retrieve Field Spells keep the engine going.

profile.plan: An Attribute toolbox: the deck keeps FIRE, DARK and EARTH monsters in hand and reveals them to pay for Quick Effects, while its big monsters Special Summon themselves from the hand and keep bouncing back to be reused.

hooks.label: Attribute searchers
hooks.why: Razen, Dr. Mad Love and Jiaolong all need monsters with the listed Attributes sitting in hand to reveal, so any card that adds a FIRE, DARK or EARTH monster to the hand is more fuel.

hooks.label: Self-summoning hand monsters
hooks.why: Jiaolong, Pantera, Hollie Sue, Pluton HG, Heavy Borger and Caesar Valius all Special Summon themselves from the hand, and the deck keeps returning its monsters to the hand so they can be Summoned again.

hooks.label: Bounce your own monsters
hooks.why: Razen and Dr. Mad Love search when they are Normal or Special Summoned, so an outside card that returns a monster you control to the hand lets you Summon it again for a second search.

hooks.label: FIRE, DARK and EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Quick Effect in the deck is paid for by revealing FIRE, DARK and/or EARTH monsters in hand, so generic support for those three Attributes feeds the entire engine.

hooks.label: Trap-setting support
hooks.why: "Vanquish Soul, Start!" Sets a Vanquish Soul Trap from the Deck each End Phase and the deck runs Snow Devil, Trinity Burst and Calamity Caesar, so cards that Set or recover Traps add more disruptions.

profile.plan: A Fusion Summoning deck that uses 'Fallen of Albaz' as material to bring out Level 8 Fusion Monsters with disruptive and recursive effects, often sending materials from the Deck to the GY and triggering GY effects.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons from the Deck
hooks.why: Lubellion and the other Albaz Dragons need specific materials, so a card that Fusion Summons by sending materials from the Deck to the GY sets up the GY and the board at once.

hooks.label: Sends Fusion Monster to GY
hooks.why: The Albaz Dragons have powerful GY effects, so sending them from the Extra Deck to the GY fuels those effects.

hooks.label: Dogmatika cards
hooks.why: The Dragon that Devours the Dogma can add a 'Dogmatika' card from the Deck to the hand when sent to the GY, so including Dogmatika cards gives you targets and synergy.

hooks.label: Ecclesia cards
hooks.why: The Dragon that Devours the Dogma gains 500 ATK and is unaffected by other cards' effects while an 'Ecclesia' monster is on the field or in either GY, so Ecclesia cards boost it.

hooks.label: Searches a Level 4 DARK Dragon
hooks.why: Every Albaz Dragon Fusion Monster requires 'Fallen of Albaz' as material, so cards that can add a Level 4 DARK Dragon from the Deck to the hand set up your Fusion Summons.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons using opponent's monsters
hooks.why: With 'Fallen of Albaz' on your field, cards like Super Polymerization can use the opponent's monsters as Fusion Material to Summon the Albaz Dragons, turning their board into your Fusion Summon.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster toolbox that equips its Extra Deck monsters to monsters as Equip Spells, using Level 4 Spellcaster bodies to Xyz, Synchro and Fusion Summon, and turning each equipped Magistus into control, negation or protection.

hooks.label: Spellcaster revival
hooks.why: Rilliona, the Magistus of Verre recycles banished Level 4 or lower Spellcasters, Zoroa, the Magistus of Flame Special Summons a Level 4 Spellcaster from the GY, and Magistus Vritra revives a Level 4 or lower Magistus, so outside revival effects for Spellcasters give the deck more material.

hooks.label: Equip Spell support
hooks.why: The Extra Deck Magistus monsters — Aiwass, Ninaruru, Rilliona and Vahram — only use their best effects while they are Equip Cards, so outside cards that search, recover or protect Equip Spells add consistency.

hooks.label: Spell Counter support
hooks.why: Magia Magic - Thunder of Judgment can remove 2 Spell Counters from your field instead of sending a face-up Magistus card, so outside cards that place Spell Counters enable its second activation condition.

hooks.label: Invoked Fusion partners
hooks.why: Crowley, the Gifted Magistus can be treated as 'Aleister the Invoker' as Fusion Material, so outside Invoked Fusion Monsters can use it as their named material.

profile.plan: A Link-heavy LIGHT Fairy deck that burns the opponent with 200-damage pings whenever they activate cards or add to hand, then turns that damage into Link and Fusion payoffs.

hooks.label: Fairy/LIGHT support
hooks.why: Every Trickstar monster is a LIGHT Fairy, and the Link Monsters require Fairy materials, so generic Fairy and LIGHT support searches, revives and boosts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Reacts to effect damage
hooks.why: Narkissus, Noble Angel, Band Drumatis and Band Sweet Guitar all trigger when your opponent takes effect damage, so outside cards that also punish effect damage add extra value.

hooks.label: Continuous burn Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Trickstar's 200-damage pings are small, so Continuous Spells/Traps that repeatedly inflict damage (like Dark Room of Nightmare) trigger the deck's damage payoffs and add up quickly.

hooks.label: Banishes from opponent's GY
hooks.why: Rhodode inflicts 200 damage each time a card is banished from the opponent's GY, so any outside card that banishes from the opponent's GY becomes a damage source.

hooks.label: Makes the opponent draw/add to hand
hooks.why: Lycoris inflicts 200 damage for each card added to the opponent's hand, so cards that force the opponent to draw or add cards (like Dark Bribe or Present Card) turn into burn.

hooks.label: Self-summoning LIGHT Fairy monsters
hooks.why: The deck Link Summons constantly and Foxglove Witch needs Fairy monsters, so LIGHT Fairy monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand provide free Link Material.

profile.plan: A swarm of Level 2 Thunder monsters that Special Summon themselves, Xyz Summon Rank 2 and Link 2 bosses, and lock both players into Level/Rank/Link 2 monsters while turning each spare Level 2 body into a negate.

hooks.label: Level 2 Summon triggers
hooks.why: Gigantic Spright Special Summons a Level 2 monster from the Deck, Spright Elf revives one from the GY, and Spright Starter and Spright Double Cross Summon more, so an outside Level 2 monster with an effect when it is Special Summoned triggers on every one of those plays.

hooks.label: Level 2 monsters with GY effects
hooks.why: Spright Sprind sends 1 Level 2 monster from the Deck to the GY when it is Link Summoned, so outside Level 2 monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when detached
hooks.why: Gigantic Spright and Spright Sprind both detach 1 Xyz Material as the cost of their effects, so outside monsters that do something when they are detached as Xyz material pay off every turn.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Every Spright monster is a Thunder monster, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Thunder monsters work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 2 monsters
hooks.why: Spright Blue, Spright Jet and the other Sprights only Special Summon themselves from the hand while you control a Level/Rank 2 monster, so an outside Level 2 monster that can Special Summon itself provides that body without using up the Normal Summon.

profile.plan: A Union monster deck that equips LIGHT Machine monsters for protection, then banishes the Union monsters from the field or GY to Fusion Summon ABC-Dragon Buster and its components, recycling them from the banished pile to repeat.

hooks.label: Union monster support
hooks.why: A-Assault Core and B-Buster Drake search Union monsters when sent from the field to the GY, and every Main Deck monster is a Union monster that equips to a LIGHT Machine.

hooks.label: LIGHT Machine support
hooks.why: Every ABC monster is a LIGHT Machine, and the Union monsters can equip to any LIGHT Machine monster you control.

hooks.label: Mills LIGHT Machines
hooks.why: ABC-Dragon Buster and the other Fusions banish their materials from the field or GY, so sending A, B, C from the Deck to the GY sets up the Fusion Summon.

hooks.label: Discard payoffs
hooks.why: ABC-Dragon Buster, XYZ-Dragon Cannon and XYZ Hyper Cannon all discard a card as cost, so outside cards that do something when discarded turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Banished revival
hooks.why: ABC-Dragon Buster banishes itself to Special Summon three banished LIGHT Machine Union monsters, and XYZ Combine revives banished X, Y, Z; outside revival for banished LIGHT Machines adds backup.

profile.plan: An Illusion-monster Fusion deck that cheats out its Azamina Fusions by feeding 'Sinful Spoils' cards from the hand and field to the GY, then grinds with revival, destruction and battle-damage payoffs.

hooks.label: Sinful Spoils cards
hooks.why: The Hallowed Azamina, Azamina Debtors and Azamina Determination each send 'Sinful Spoils' cards from your hand and/or field to the GY as the price of Special Summoning an Azamina Fusion, and Queen Azamina counts herself as one.

hooks.label: Illusion monster support
hooks.why: Every Azamina Fusion names 1 Illusion monster as material and Azamina Moa Regina revives an Illusion monster from the GY, so effects that search, Summon or boost Illusion monsters fuel the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends your Illusions to the GY
hooks.why: Queen Azamina Special Summons itself whenever it is sent to the GY by an activated effect, so effects that discard or send your Illusion monsters from the hand or field give you a free body.

profile.plan: A Field Spell deck built around keeping Umi (or a card treated as Umi) on the field, boosting and enabling WATER monsters that attack, negate, Tribute and send Umi to the GY for mass removal.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Every Umi card needs the Field Spell on the field, and A Legendary Ocean, Magellanica and Forgotten Temple of the Deep are themselves Umi, so anything that adds or activates a Field Spell from the Deck keeps the engine running.

hooks.label: Field Spell protection
hooks.why: The Legendary Fisherman, Deepsea Warrior, Mermaid Knight and the trap effects only work while Umi is face-up, and Daedalus, Codarus and Abyss-strom send Umi to the GY as a cost, so protecting the Field Spell is vital.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster toolbox that pays for its monsters' Quick Effects by discarding Spell Cards from the hand, recurs those Spells from the GY in the End Phase, and Fusion Summons Spellcaster bosses.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Witchcrafter monster is a Spellcaster, Madame Verre boosts your battling Spellcaster in damage calculation and Haine stops your other Spellcasters being targeted.

hooks.label: Spells with GY effects
hooks.why: Genni, Schmietta, Pittore, Verre, Haine and Edel all pay for their Quick Effects by discarding a Spell Card, so an outside Spell that does something when it is sent to the GY is free value.

hooks.label: Triggers on your Tributed Spellcaster
hooks.why: Genni, Pittore, Potterie, Schmietta and Edel all Tribute themselves for their Main Phase effect, and Marka Tributes itself from the hand or field, so an outside card that reacts when a Spellcaster you control is Tributed gets a free activation.

profile.plan: A Plant deck that gains Life Points over and over so its 'if you gain LP' effects keep firing, keeping its LP above the opponent's to switch on every Aroma monster's bonus.

hooks.label: Plant support
