hooks.why: Every Aroma monster except Aroma Jar is a Plant, and Aromage Jasmine, Aromaseraphy Sweet Marjoram, Aromaseraphy Rosemary and Aromalilith Magnolia all search, boost, revive or protect Plant monsters you control.

hooks.label: Life Point gain
hooks.why: Aromage Jasmine, Laurel, Rosemary, Bergamot, Cananga, Marjoram, the Aromaseraphy Synchros, Aroma Garden and Humid Winds all trigger 'if you gain LP', so any outside card that gains LP fires the whole engine.

hooks.label: Plants that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Aromaseraphy Jasmine and Aromalilith Rosemary Tribute a monster they point to as a cost for a Special Summon or a banish, so an outside Plant with an effect when it is Tributed is paid for free.

hooks.label: Plants that trigger in the GY
hooks.why: Blessed Winds sends a Plant from the hand or field to the GY for 500 LP and Aroma Blend banishes Plant monsters from the GY as Fusion material, so outside Plants with an effect when they are sent to the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Plant monsters
hooks.why: Aromaseraphy Jasmine and Aromalilith Rosemary need Plant bodies for Link material and to Tribute, and Aromalilith Rosalina locks you into Plant monsters for the rest of the turn.

profile.plan: A Zombie/FIRE Synchro deck that banishes its own monsters to trigger effects, then recycles the banished Zombies to keep Synchro Summoning.

hooks.label: Banishes your Zombies
hooks.why: Shiranui Solitaire, Spiritmaster, Squire and others have effects when they are banished, so any outside card that banishes a Zombie from your GY, field or Deck triggers them.

hooks.label: Zombie monsters with banished effects
hooks.why: The deck banishes Zombies constantly, so outside Zombie monsters that do something when they are banished add to the toolbox.

hooks.label: Sends Zombies from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Shiranui Style Solemnity and Synthesis send Zombies from Deck to GY to set up banishing, so outside mill effects for Zombies do the same.

hooks.label: Special Summons banished Zombies
hooks.why: Shiranui Solitaire and Skillsaga Supremacy recover banished Zombies, so outside cards that do the same keep the engine going.

hooks.label: 0 DEF Zombie support
hooks.why: Many Shiranui effects, like Solitaire, Shogunsaga and Samsara, specifically reference Zombie monsters with 0 DEF, so cards that support that niche are valuable.

profile.plan: A Reptile control deck that blankets the opponent's monsters in Venom Counters to drain their ATK with Venom Swamp, while loading the Graveyard with Reptiles so Vennominon and Vennominaga grow huge and keep reviving themselves.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Vennominon and Vennominaga are Reptile monsters that gain 500 ATK for every Reptile-Type monster in your Graveyard, and both Venom Shot and their own revival need Reptiles, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Reptiles strengthens the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Reptiles to the GY
hooks.why: Venom Shot sends a Reptile-Type monster from the Deck to the Graveyard, and Vennominon and Vennominaga feed on exactly those Reptiles, so any outside effect that mills Reptiles is more fuel for the bosses.

hooks.label: Reptiles with Graveyard effects
hooks.why: The deck fills its Graveyard with Reptiles on purpose through Venom Shot and the bosses' revivals, so outside Reptile monsters that do something when they are sent to the Graveyard trigger for free.

hooks.label: Revives Reptiles from the GY
hooks.why: Vennominon and Vennominaga banish another Reptile from the Graveyard to Special Summon themselves back, so outside cards that Special Summon Reptile monsters from the Graveyard keep the deck's bosses on the field.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Dragon deck that Tributes its own Hieratic monsters as costs and Xyz material, and every Tribute triggers a Special Summon of a Dragon-Type Normal Monster from the hand, Deck or GY, which it then stacks into Rank 6 and Rank 8 Dragon Xyz Monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters with Tribute triggers
hooks.why: Hieratic Sun Dragon Overlord of Heliopolis and Hieratic Seal of the Heavenly Spheres Tribute 1 or more monsters from your hand or field as a cost, so an outside monster that does something when it is Tributed gets its effect for free.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Hieratic monster, the Normal Monsters it Summons and both Overlords are Dragon-Type, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Dragons reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Level 6-8 Dragons
hooks.why: Hieratic Dragon King of Atum needs Level 6 Dragon material and both Heliopolis Overlords need Level 8 monsters, so outside Dragons of those Levels that Special Summon themselves are extra Xyz material, just like Tefnuit.

hooks.label: Loads Dragon Normal Monsters into the GY
hooks.why: Hieratic Dragon of Asar banishes a LIGHT Dragon and a Dragon-Type Normal Monster from the GY to Summon itself and Sutekh needs three Dragon-Type Normal Monsters there, so any card that sends them from the Deck to the GY sets those Summons up.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Heliopolis Tributes any number of monsters from the hand and field and Heavenly Spheres Tributes 1 monster to bounce, so Tokens are free Tribute fodder that also feeds the Tributed Hieratic triggers.

profile.plan: A Dragon-only Link climb: Elpy and Pisty turn Level 4 or lower Dragons into Link Material while summoning Dragons from the Deck and GY into zones that two Link Monsters point to, backed by Normal Monster fodder and a Fusion made from banished Link Monsters.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Guardragon monster is a Dragon and Pisty, Elpy and Agarpain stop you Special Summoning anything else, so only Dragon support can be used.

hooks.label: Sends Normal Monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Garmides and Promineses Special Summon themselves from the GY whenever a Normal Monster is sent to your GY, and Guardragon Shield and Corewakening treat that as their fuel.

hooks.label: Dragons that trigger in the GY
hooks.why: Corewakening sends an Effect Monster from the hand to the GY and Garmides sends a Dragon from the hand to the GY, so Dragon monsters that do something when sent there get it for free, and Pisty then revives them.

profile.plan: Level 1 FIRE monsters that swarm each other and repeatedly move monsters in and out of the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, so the board keeps recycling itself while it builds toward Flamberge Dragon and Diabellstar.

hooks.label: FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Snake-Eye monster is FIRE and the deck searches, revives and places FIRE monsters from the GY, so generic FIRE support reaches every card in it.

hooks.label: Triggers when sent to the GY
hooks.why: Ash, Oak and Birch pay their cost by sending 2 face-up cards they control to the GY (including themselves) and Flamberge Dragon triggers when it is sent from the hand or field to the GY, so FIRE monsters with a GY trigger get used for free.

hooks.label: Places monsters as Continuous Spells
hooks.why: Flamberge Dragon, Snake-Eyes Diabellstar, Poplar and Divine Temple of the Snake-Eye all tuck monsters into the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells and then Special Summon them back, so outside cards that do the same give the deck more cards to loop.

hooks.label: Special Summons itself when searched
hooks.why: Snake-Eyes Poplar shows how hard the deck searches Level 1 FIRE monsters, so any Level 1 FIRE monster that Special Summons itself when it is added to the hand turns every search into an extra body.

hooks.label: Pyro support
hooks.why: Snake-Eye Ash, Poplar, Oak and Birch are all Pyro, and those are the cards that loop each other out of the Deck, so Pyro support hits the deck's engine pieces.

profile.plan: World Legacy is a Machine/DARK Link deck that Link Summons using World Legacy monsters, punishes the opponent's Extra Deck Summons, and uses Tribute Summoning to trigger World Legacy effects and search.

hooks.label: DARK Machine support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck World Legacy monster is a Machine/DARK, so outside cards that search, revive or protect Machines or DARKs work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: World Legacy - "World Key" grants an extra Tribute Summon by discarding a World Legacy card, and World Legacy - "World Crown" rewards being Tributed, so outside monsters that pay off being Tributed get used.

hooks.label: Extra Deck summon punishers
hooks.why: World Legacy - "World Chalice" can Tribute itself to send an Extra Deck Summoned monster to the GY, World Legacy - "World Lance" makes Tokens when one appears, and World Gears of Theurlogical Demiurgy summons a World Legacy monster, so outside cards that punish Extra Deck Summons fit.

hooks.label: Orcust monsters
hooks.why: World Legacy - "World Wand" can banish itself from the GY to Special Summon a banished "Orcust" monster, making Orcust cards direct partners.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Spellcaster deck that Xyz Summons on the opponent's turn by punishing any card that leaves the GY, then uses its Xyz monsters to banish, bounce and negate.

hooks.label: Moves cards out of the GY
hooks.why: Exosister Martha can Xyz Summon when any card moves out of either GY, so cards that banish or return cards from the GY trigger her.

hooks.label: Forces opponent to move GY
hooks.why: The other Exosisters only trigger when the opponent moves cards out of the GY, so cards that force the opponent to banish or return their GY cards trigger the whole team.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Exosister is a LIGHT Spellcaster, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT Spellcasters work on the whole engine.

hooks.label: Rank 4 Xyz with Quick Effects
hooks.why: Exosister Arment and the Main Deck monsters' effects let the deck Xyz Summon during the opponent's turn, so Rank 4 Xyz monsters with Quick Effects give you disruption.

profile.plan: Ojama swarms 0-ATK LIGHT Beast Normal Monsters and uses Ojama Country to swap ATK/DEF into beaters, Ojamagic and Ojama Pink triggers when cards are sent from hand to the GY, and Ojama King/Knight lock the opponent's Monster Zones while Ojama Trio/Duo flood their field with Tokens.

hooks.label: Sends your hand to the GY
hooks.why: Ojamagic and Ojama Pink both trigger when they are sent from the hand to the GY, and Ojama Country's Special Summon costs sending an "Ojama" card from the hand to the GY.

hooks.label: Summons Normal Monsters from Deck
hooks.why: Ojama Delta Hurricane, Ojamandala and Ojamassimilation all need Ojama Green, Yellow and Black together, so effects that Special Summon Level 2 LIGHT Beast Normal Monsters from the Deck assemble the three at once.

hooks.label: Beast support
hooks.why: Every Ojama monster is a Beast, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Beasts works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Monster Zone lock
hooks.why: Ojama King and Ojama Knight make the opponent's Monster Zones unusable, so other cards that lock Monster Card Zones stack the same lock.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Ojama Country is the deck's engine and Ojama Emperor gains 3000 ATK and effect immunity only while it is in a Field Zone, so cards that fetch or place Field Spells from the Deck are worth a slot.

hooks.label: Summons Beast monsters
hooks.why: Ojama Emperor is a Link-3 needing 3 Beast monsters and Ojama Red swarms Beasts out of the hand, so cards that Special Summon Beasts supply its material.

profile.plan: A deck of Level 1 Fairy 'memory' starters that Xyz Summon Rank 2 Purrely Xyz Monsters using Quick-Play Spells as material, stacking up materials until they upgrade into the Rank 7 Expurrely bosses.

hooks.label: Discard payoff monsters
hooks.why: Purrely Happy Memory, Sleepy Memory, Pretty Memory, Delicious Memory and Epurrely Noir all discard a card as a cost, so an outside monster that does something when it is discarded gets its effect for free.

hooks.label: Level 1 summoners
hooks.why: Purrely and Purrelyly are Level 1 and their effects trigger on any Normal or Special Summon, and one of them must be on the field as the sole material for the Rank 2 Purrely Xyz Summon, so cards that Special Summon a Level 1 monster from the hand, Deck or GY start the engine.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Purrely monster and every Purrely Xyz Monster is a Fairy, so cards that search, revive or boost Fairies reach the whole deck.

hooks.label: Xyz Material enablers
hooks.why: Expurrely Happiness and Expurrely Noir can be Xyz Summoned over a Rank 2 Purrely Xyz Monster that has 5 or more materials, so cards that attach material to an Xyz Monster get the deck to its bosses faster.

profile.plan: A Psychic engine that pays 600 LP to search and Special Summon its monsters, then Synchro, Fusion or Xyz Summons into Level 8 and Rank 8 bosses while using Level 3 Psychic monsters in the GY.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: The main P.U.N.K. engine is built on Psychic monsters (Ze Amin, Sharakusai, Madame Spider, Wa Gon, Dragon Drive, FEVER), so cards that search, revive or boost Psychics work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: LP-payment triggers
hooks.why: P.U.N.K. cards constantly pay 600 LP to activate their effects, so outside cards that trigger when your LP are paid get value every turn.

hooks.label: Psychic LP-payers
hooks.why: P.U.N.K. JAM Extreme Session draws a card whenever a Psychic monster you control pays LP to activate its effect, so outside Psychic monsters with LP costs turn into draws.

profile.plan: A control deck whose Zombie boss keeps coming back from the GY by eating Spells and Traps, using the Eldlixirs to flood the board with Zombies while Golden Land cards grind the opponent out.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Eldlich monster is a Zombie and every Eldlixir locks you into Special Summoning only Zombie monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Zombies help the whole deck.

hooks.label: Spell/Traps with GY uses
hooks.why: Eldlich the Golden Lord sends a Spell/Trap from your hand or a Spell/Trap you control to the GY as its cost, so outside Spells and Traps that do something when sent to the GY are free fuel.

hooks.label: Zombies that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Eldlich the Mad Golden Lord Tributes 1 Zombie monster each turn to take control of an opponent's monster, so outside Zombies with an effect when they are Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Dumps Spells/Traps to the GY
hooks.why: Cursed Eldland, the Eldlixirs and El Dorado Adelantado all feed on Spell/Trap cards sitting in or banished from the GY, so outside cards that send a Spell/Trap from the Deck to the GY stock the engine.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Fairy deck that Fusion Summons Melodious Fusions by using monsters from the hand, Deck, field and Pendulum Zones as material, backed by Pendulum scales and Diva protection.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Melodious monster is a LIGHT Fairy, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT Fairy monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fairy monsters with GY effects
hooks.why: Fortissimo, Soprano and Melodious Concerto send monsters used as Fusion Material to the GY, so outside LIGHT Fairies with an effect when sent there get value.

profile.plan: Fusion Summons Frightfur Fusion Monsters using Edge Imp and Fluffal monsters as material, sending Edge Imp monsters to the GY to trigger searches and revivals.

hooks.label: Fusion Substitute monsters
hooks.why: The deck Fusion Summons using specific 'Edge Imp' and 'Fluffal' monsters as material, so monsters that can substitute for any Fusion Material open up plays.

hooks.label: Sends DARK Fiends to the GY
hooks.why: Edge Imp Sabres revives itself from the GY, Toy Vendor adds an Edge Imp from the Deck when sent to the GY, and Edge Imp Cotton Eater burns for each Frightfur in the GY, so filling the GY with Fiends is valuable.

hooks.label: Sends Continuous Spells to the GY
hooks.why: Toy Vendor is a Continuous Spell that adds an 'Edge Imp Sabres' or 'Fluffal' from the Deck when it is sent to the GY.

hooks.label: Discards DARK Fiends
hooks.why: Edge Imp Chain adds a 'Frightfur' card when sent from the hand to the GY, and Edge Imp Sabres can revive itself if sent to the GY, so discarding Fiends triggers them.

hooks.label: Searches Polymerization
hooks.why: Frightfur Patchwork adds a Polymerization from the Deck, and the deck Fusion Summons using Polymerization, so extra ways to get it are useful.

hooks.label: Fusion Material triggers
hooks.why: The deck Fusion Summons frequently, so monsters that gain effects when used as Fusion Material provide extra value.

profile.plan: A slow control deck that keeps its Level 1-4 DARK monsters face-down, flips them up for effects, turns the opponent's whole board face-down so Ghostricks can attack directly, and eventually wins through Ghostrick Angel of Mischief's ten Xyz Materials.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-up
hooks.why: Jiangshi, Doll, Siren, Warwolf, Yeti and Fairy all have 'When this card is flipped face-up' effects, so any outside card that flips your face-down monsters up triggers them without spending your Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Flips opponent's monsters down
hooks.why: Mansion, Parade and Museum let Ghostricks attack directly only while every opposing monster is face-down, and Nekomusume, Witch, Scare and Doll all flip the opponent's monsters down, so more of that effect is the deck's win route.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Material
hooks.why: Ghostrick Angel of Mischief wins the Duel at ten Xyz Materials and the Rank 1-3 Ghostrick Xyz all pay for their effects by detaching, so effects that attach material feed both the win condition and the toolbox.

hooks.label: Field Spell enablers
hooks.why: Mansion, Parade and Museum are the deck's engine and Ghostrick Renovation, or Treat and Festival all check for a card in the Field Zone, so anything that finds or plays a Field Spell keeps the lockdown and direct attacks online.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Ghostrick can only be Normal Summoned while you already control a Ghostrick, and Ghostrick Mummy grants an extra Normal Summon of one, so extra Normal Summons are how the deck builds board and Xyz Material.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Ghostrick monster is DARK and Ghostrick Mummy forbids Special Summoning anything but DARK monsters, so Attribute support aimed at DARK covers the entire deck.

profile.plan: A Tuner-heavy Synchro deck that triggers effects when its monsters are sent to the GY as Synchro Material, gains an extra Normal Summon for Tuners, and can Synchro Summon on the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Tuner Special Summon
hooks.why: Kewl Tune Cue Special Summons a Tuner from the hand, Deck or GY, and the deck needs many Tuners on the field to Synchro Summon.

hooks.label: Tuner search
hooks.why: Kewl Tune Reco and Mix add 'Kewl Tune' monsters to your hand, and the deck can use a Tuner in hand as Synchro Material, so any Tuner search is useful.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: JJ 'Kewl Tune' grants an extra Normal Summon of a Tuner each turn, and the deck's Tuners have effects when Normal Summoned.

hooks.label: Synchro Material trigger
hooks.why: Every Kewl Tune Tuner triggers when sent to the GY as Synchro Material, so outside Tuners with the same trigger give extra value.

hooks.label: Opponent's turn Synchro
hooks.why: Kewl Tune Remix, Clip and B2B let you Synchro Summon during your opponent's turn, so cards that allow or reward that fit.

profile.plan: A combo deck that repeatedly destroys its own Memento monsters by card effect as fuel, turning each destruction into a search, a revival or a Fusion Summon, and building toward the huge 'Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation'.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monster
hooks.why: Angwitch, Dark Blade, Mace, Tatsunootoshigo and Bone Party all require destroying a 'Memento' monster you own as fuel, and Shleepy, Akihiron, Horned Dragon and Mementomictlan all reward a monster being destroyed by a card effect.

hooks.label: Punishes your monster's destruction
hooks.why: The deck blows up its own Memento monsters several times per turn, so any outside card whose effect triggers when a monster you control is destroyed gets a free activation every time.

hooks.label: Sends monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Mementotlan-Horned Dragon Special Summons itself while you have 3 or more differently named 'Memento' monsters in the GY, and Combined Creation needs 5 different names shuffled back from the hand and GY, so extra ways to put monsters into the GY speed up both bosses.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon support
hooks.why: Mementotlan Shleepy Fusion Summons a 'Memento' Fusion Monster from the Extra Deck using monsters from the hand or field, and Mementomictlan Tecuhtlica - Creation King is a 3-material Fusion, so any outside card that helps Fusion Summon adds extra copies of the deck's best play.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Mementomictlan is the deck's engine piece: it Special Summons a lower-Level 'Memento' monster whenever one you control is destroyed, blocks Spell/Trap responses in battle, and Sets a 'Memento' Spell/Trap from the GY each End Phase.

profile.plan: An EARTH Plant/Insect/Rock control deck that Synchro Summons Naturia Beast and Barkion (and Fuses Exterio) to negate the opponent's Spells and Traps, milling its own Deck to pay the negation costs and grinding back with Graveyard revives.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Barkion banishes 2 cards from the Graveyard and Exterio removes a Graveyard card to negate, while Beast's negation and Camellia's Tribute-replacement send the top cards of the Deck to the GY, so outside mill effects stock the resource the deck runs on.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Sunflower, Vein, Horneedle, Ladybug, Mole Cricket and Sacred Tree all Tribute your own monsters to pay a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be milled
hooks.why: Beast, Barkion, Camellia, Butterfly, Rock and Marron send cards from the top of your Deck to the GY, so outside monsters that trigger when they are sent from the Deck to the Graveyard are used for free.

hooks.label: Plant and Insect support
hooks.why: Nearly every Main Deck Naturia is a Plant or Insect (Camellia, Rosewhip, Strawberry, Horneedle, Fruitfly, Mole Cricket), and Naturia Pineapple turns your whole board into Plant-Type.

profile.plan: Places A-Counters on the opponent's monsters to weaken them, then removes those counters to steal monsters, destroy cards, and summon Reptile Synchro and Link monsters.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Nearly every Alien is a Reptile, and their Link and Synchro monsters ask for Reptile materials, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Reptiles fits.

hooks.label: Reptile mill
hooks.why: Alien Stealthbuster places A-Counters when sent to the GY, and Alien Shocktrooper M-Frame revives Reptiles from the GY, so milling Reptiles fuels both.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Alien Dog Special Summons itself when you Normal Summon an Alien, and Alien Ammonite revives an Alien when Normal Summoned, so extra Normal Summons trigger them again.

hooks.label: Steal opponent's monster
hooks.why: The deck can take control of monsters with A-Counters, and outside cards that steal monsters give material for Synchro or Link Summons, or can be Tributed for Cosmic Horror Gangi'el.

hooks.label: Destroy your own Reptile
hooks.why: Alien Shocktrooper M-Frame revives Reptiles when destroyed, and Code A Ancient Ruins places A-Counters when an Alien is destroyed, so cards that destroy your own Reptiles trigger them.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck that parks its own monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as face-up Continuous Traps, Special Summons them back during the Main Phase, and uses them plus any outside bodies to Synchro Summon Level 8 and Level 12 bosses, often on the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Level 8 Synchro fodder
hooks.why: Auxila and Legatia are Level 12 Synchros made with 1 Tuner + 1+ non-Tuners, and the deck's own Tuners (Primera, Atrii) are only Level 4, so an outside Level 8 monster that Special Summons itself completes the levels.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Tuner
hooks.why: Every Centur-Ion Synchro asks for exactly 1 Tuner and Stand Up Centur-Ion! lets you Synchro Summon immediately after any Special Summon, so an outside Tuner that Special Summons itself is extra material that never uses your Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Synchro Material payoff
hooks.why: The deck Synchro Summons over and over, feeding its own monsters and anything else on board into Auxila, Legatia and Primera Primus, so outside monsters that do something when used as Synchro Material trigger for free.

hooks.label: Rewards Synchro Summons
hooks.why: Stand Up Centur-Ion! Synchro Summons the moment any monster is Special Summoned, and Emeth VI and Chimerea work on the opponent's turn, so outside cards that pay off a Synchro Monster being Special Summoned fire on both turns.

hooks.label: Revives Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: Centur-Ion Phalanx and Primera Primus are built to pull cards back out of the GY, and the Level 12 bosses are often spent as material, so outside cards that Special Summon a Synchro Monster from the GY recycle them.

profile.plan: A Rock/Synchro combo deck: it Special Summons its own Tuners, fills the board with Level 4 or lower Rocks excavated from the top of the Deck, and Synchro Summons Rock monsters whose Quick Effects need an Attribute monster in the GY.

hooks.label: Rock monster support
hooks.why: Every Adamancipator monster is a Rock, and Adamancipator Friends locks you into Special Summoning only Rock monsters for the rest of the turn, so generic Rock search, revival and boosting cards work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Deck-top stacking
hooks.why: The excavate effects of Researcher, Analyzer, Seeker and Conductor only pay off if the top 5 cards are Rocks, which Laputite, Signs and Conductor set up by placing cards on top of the Deck.

hooks.label: Send monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Dragite, Raptite, Leonite and Tiamite all need a WATER, WIND, FIRE or DARK monster in the GY before their Quick Effects work, so effects that send monsters from the Deck to the GY switch them on.

profile.plan: A WATER Cyberse Link Summoning deck that swarms the field with WATER monsters, Link Summons into Marincess Link Monsters that equip themselves from the GY, and grinds with GY banishing effects and battle protection.

hooks.label: WATER self-summoners
hooks.why: The deck needs many WATER monsters on the field to Link Summon, and many Marincess monsters Special Summon themselves; outside WATER monsters that do the same provide free materials.

hooks.label: WATER Link Material payoff
hooks.why: Marincess Link Monsters require WATER materials, and Blue Tang and Springirl trigger when sent to the GY as material for a WATER Link Summon, so outside WATER monsters with effects when used as Link Material get the same trigger.

hooks.label: Banishes from your GY
hooks.why: Many Marincess monsters (Sea Horse, Pascalus, Springirl, Basilalima, Crown Tail) banish themselves or other Marincess from the GY to activate effects, so outside cards that banish a WATER monster from your GY can enable those effects.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Every Marincess monster is WATER, and their Extra Deck monsters require WATER materials, so cards that search, revive or boost WATER monsters help the whole deck.

profile.plan: A quick-play Spell/Trap toolbox around Diabellstar and Azamina that pays costs with its own monsters, Sets itself back from the GY, and converts Illusion and Spellcaster monsters into removal.

hooks.label: Illusion, Spellcaster and Fiend support
hooks.why: Sinful Spoils of the White Forest needs you to control a Fiend, Illusion or Spellcaster monster to do anything, and Morrian, Subdual and Awakening all key off Illusion or Spellcaster monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters that pay off as cost
hooks.why: Silvera sends a Diabellstar monster from the hand or field to the GY, Sanctification discards a card and Deception Tributes a monster, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed, discarded or sent to the GY get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Monsters held as Continuous Spells
hooks.why: Winter Raven's Forest places a monster face-up in its owner's Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell and Sanctification Special Summons a face-up Monster Card from yours, so cards that move monsters in and out of the Spell & Trap Zone are extra copies of that engine.

profile.plan: A Machine deck that uses its own monsters as ammunition — discarding and sending Machines to the GY as cost — to cheat out Level 7 or higher Machina bodies from the hand, Deck and Graveyard, while Union monsters equip for protection and Citadel/Armored Unit/Defense Perimeter punish the opponent whenever a Machine you control is destroyed.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Machina monster is a Machine, and Machina Unclaspare, Machina Citadel, Machina Armored Unit and Machina Defense Perimeter all name Machine monsters, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Machines works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Machines that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Machina Fortress, Machina Irradiator, Machina Air Raider and Machina Redeployment all discard Machine monster(s) as a cost, so outside Machines with an effect when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Machine
hooks.why: Machina Citadel Special Summons itself from the GY when a face-up EARTH Machine you control is destroyed, Machina Armored Unit Special Summons a Machine from the Deck when a Machine is destroyed by battle, and Machina Defense Perimeter recovers a Machine when one is destroyed.

hooks.label: Dumps Machines into the GY
hooks.why: Machina Possesstorage, Machina Irradiator, Machina Ruinforce and Machina Fortress Special Summon themselves or revive Machina monsters from the Graveyard, so outside cards that send Machine monsters from the Deck or hand to the GY load that Graveyard for them.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that uses a Scale 0 / Scale 13 pair to Pendulum Summon DARK monsters, stacks them into Supreme King Dragon Xyz/Synchro/Fusion bodies, and eventually assembles the four Dragon materials for Supreme King Z-ARC.

hooks.label: Pendulum Zone placers
hooks.why: Supreme King Gate Zero and Supreme King Gate Infinity are the archetype's only Scales at 0 and 13, so outside cards that put Pendulum Monsters straight into the Pendulum Zone keep that low/high pair available.

hooks.label: Odd-Eyes Pendulum monsters
hooks.why: Miracle of the Supreme King can destroy a Supreme King Z-ARC you control to Special Summon 1 "Odd-Eyes" Pendulum Monster from the Deck or Extra Deck, ignoring its Summoning conditions.

hooks.label: Polymerization/Fusion Spells
hooks.why: Supreme King Z-ARC must be Fusion Summoned and Supreme King Gate Zero searches a "Polymerization" Spell Card or "Fusion" Spell Card, so outside Fusion Spells are extra ways to assemble its four Dragon materials.

profile.plan: A WIND Quick-Play Spell deck that keeps activating Mystical Space Typhoon and its own Quick-Play Spells — re-Setting them when MST blows them up — to trigger monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand and grow into the Level 9 bosses.

hooks.label: Mills Spells to the GY
hooks.why: Swen, Eldam, Meghala and Varuroon, the Vibrant Vortex all need Mystical Space Typhoon in the GY to Special Summon themselves or to negate a monster effect, so any card that sends a Spell/Trap from the Deck to the GY switches the whole deck on.

hooks.label: Quick-Play Spell searchers
hooks.why: Krosea, Fonix, Varuroon and Meghala Special Summon themselves or shuffle cards away every time a Quick-Play Spell is activated, and Mandate shuffles three Quick-Play Spells back to draw, so any card that adds a Quick-Play Spell from the Deck or GY is more engine fuel.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Every Radiant Typhoon monster is WIND, Mandate pumps all your WIND monsters, and Krosea and Meghala lock you into WIND Special Summons for the rest of the turn, so generic WIND support never misses.

hooks.label: Spell-activation payoffs
hooks.why: The deck fires several Quick-Play Spells every turn to trigger its monsters, so outside cards that gain counters, draw or summon whenever a Quick-Play Spell is activated get fed for free.

hooks.label: Self-summoning WIND extenders
hooks.why: Swen, Eldam and Meghala drop themselves from the hand for free, so more WIND monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand add bodies without breaking the WIND-only Summon lock.
phrases: Special Summon this card (from your hand)

profile.plan: A Level-climbing Dragon deck: WIND Dragons of Level 3, 5, 7 and 10 upgrade into each other by sending themselves or other monsters from the hand to the GY, then use the GY (and DARK monsters) as ammunition to blow up the opponent's board.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Armed Dragon LV5, LV7, both Thunder LV3/LV5/LV7 and both LV10s all send a monster from your hand to the GY as the cost of their destruction effects, so an outside monster that does something once it is in the GY pays you twice.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Fist Armed Dragon and Ojama Pajama discard a card as the cost of their effects (and Armed Dragon Thunder LV10 discards for its Quick Effect), so an outside card with a discard trigger gets its effect for free.

hooks.label: Mills DARK monsters
hooks.why: Dark Armed Dragon and Dark Armed Dragon Punisher both need exactly 3 DARK monsters in the GY and banish them to destroy cards, so outside cards that send DARK monsters from the Deck to the GY are how you set that count up.

hooks.label: WIND Dragon support
hooks.why: Almost every Armed Dragon is a WIND Dragon, and Armed Dragon Thunder LV5 searches Level 5 or higher WIND Dragons while Drill Armed Dragon boosts WIND Dragons and banishes them from the GY.

hooks.label: Ojama engine cards
hooks.why: Ojamatch sends an Ojama card to the GY to add an Ojama monster plus an Armed Dragon and Normal Summon it, and Ojama Pajama protects your Armed Dragons while reviving the Ojamas you banish.

profile.plan: A Ritual engine of Level 3-6, 0-ATK monsters that reveal a Ritual Monster or Ritual Spell from hand to Special Summon themselves plus a partner from the Deck and search the Ritual pieces, providing Tribute fodder for Ritual Summoning any Ritual Monster while locked out of the Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Discard fodder
hooks.why: Chalislime and Crealtar both reveal themselves in hand and discard 1 card as a cost, so monsters with an effect when they are discarded get a free trigger.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: The engine only starts when you reveal a Ritual Monster from hand, so effects that add a Ritual Monster from the Deck to the hand start the whole combo.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: Candoll and Bookstone need a Ritual Spell in hand to reveal, so effects that add a Ritual Spell from the Deck to the hand start the whole combo.

profile.plan: A Dark Fusion deck that Fusion Summons Fiend 'Evil HERO' monsters using named Elemental HERO, Fiend, Rock and Warrior materials, then protects and powers them up with Dark Fusion support.

hooks.label: Fusion Material substitutes
hooks.why: Inferno Wing, Lightning Golem and Wild Cyclone name specific Elemental HERO monsters, so outside cards that can substitute for a named Fusion Material provide the missing piece.

hooks.label: Elemental HERO support
hooks.why: Several Evil HERO Fusions require Elemental HERO Avian, Burstinatrix, Sparkman, Clayman, Wildheart or Neos, so outside cards that search or revive Elemental HERO monsters supply those exact materials.

hooks.label: Generic Fusion Spells
hooks.why: Supreme King's Castle lets you Fusion Summon Dark Fusion-only monsters with other effects, and Infernal Rider lets you Fusion Summon them using other cards' effects, so ordinary Fusion Spells become usable.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Evil HERO Malicious Edge can be Tribute Summoned with 1 Tribute, and Evil HERO Infernal Prodigy draws when Tributed to Tribute Summon a HERO, so cards that give extra Tribute Summons or support Tribute Summoning fit.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Almost every Evil HERO monster is a Fiend, and Supreme King's Castle boosts a battling Fiend, so outside cards that search, revive or power up Fiends work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: The deck recycles its 'Madolche' monsters from the Graveyard into the Deck to trigger searches and sets, keeping the Graveyard empty for Puddingcess and Counter Traps, and Xyz Summons into Fairy bosses that shuffle away the opponent's cards.

hooks.label: Shuffles your GY away
hooks.why: Madolche Ticket and Salon trigger when a 'Madolche' card is returned from your GY or field to the hand or Deck, so outside cards that shuffle or bounce your EARTH monsters trigger them and keep the Graveyard empty.

hooks.label: Field Spell searcher
hooks.why: Madolche Chateau is the deck's key Field Spell, shuffling all Madolche from the GY and boosting ATK/DEF, so outside cards that search Field Spells get it consistently.

hooks.label: Empty Graveyard payoff
hooks.why: Madolche Puddingcess gains 800 ATK/DEF and Madolche Nights and Tea Break require no monsters in your Graveyard, so outside cards with the same condition benefit from the empty Graveyard the deck maintains.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Madolche monster is EARTH, so cards that support EARTH monsters work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: An EARTH Machine deck that stacks Levels to Xyz Summon Rank 5/7/9 Machines, Tributes or banishes its own Machines to revive those Xyz from the GY, and grinds the opponent down with battle-position tricks and material detaches.

hooks.label: EARTH Machine support
hooks.why: Every Infinitrack monster is an EARTH Machine, and their searches, materials and Tributes all name EARTH Machine monsters, so any card that supports Machine or EARTH boosts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Tributing or banishing your Machines
hooks.why: Infinitrack Road Roller Special Summons itself whenever an EARTH Machine monster is Tributed or banished face-up, and the Level 5 Infinitracks need an EARTH Machine Tribute to Summon themselves.

hooks.label: Machines that want banishing
hooks.why: Crab Crane and Drag Shovel banish 1 Machine monster from your GY as cost, so outside Machine monsters with an effect when they are banished get it for free.

hooks.label: Machines that want Tributing
hooks.why: The Level 5 Infinitracks Special Summon themselves by Tributing 1 EARTH Machine monster, so outside EARTH Machine monsters with an effect when they are Tributed turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Extra Xyz material
hooks.why: River Stormer, Earth Slicer and Mountain Smasher detach materials to destroy cards or gain ATK, and Infinitrack Goliath and Heavy Forward already show the deck wants cards that attach themselves to an Xyz Monster as material.

profile.plan: Vision HERO monsters hide in the Spell & Trap Zone as face-up Continuous Traps, then Special Summon back, get banished by Vision Fusion, or become fusion material for HERO Fusion bosses like Trinity.

hooks.label: Damages your own LP
hooks.why: Increase, Poisoner, Minimum Ray and Multiply Guy each place themselves from the GY into the Spell & Trap Zone as a face-up Continuous Trap when you take battle or effect damage, so any outside card that burns your own Life Points turns them on.

hooks.label: Warrior and DARK support
hooks.why: Every Vision HERO is a Warrior DARK monster and their Fusions ask for HERO monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Warriors or DARK monsters work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Polymerization support
hooks.why: Vision Fusion Fusion Summons a HERO Fusion Monster and Vyon can banish a HERO from the GY to add Polymerization, so extra Fusion Spells and Polymerization pieces keep the Trinity and Adoration plays coming.

hooks.label: Trap Monsters
hooks.why: Witch Raider can Tribute Trap(s) you control for its Tribute Summon and the deck already stuffs its Spell & Trap Zone with Vision HERO cards treated as Continuous Traps, so self-summoning Trap Monsters are free tribute material.

hooks.label: Sends monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Vyon sends a HERO from the Deck to the GY and later banishes one from the GY to add Polymerization, while Gravito recovers banished HEROs, so outside cards that stock your GY feed every one of those costs.

profile.plan: A Cyberse toolbox that Normal Summons Level 4 monsters, then Xyz Summons Rank 4 or Synchro Summons Level 8/12 using them, with GY effects and Extra Monster Zone payoffs.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is Cyberse, and several effects lock you into Cyberse Special Summons from the Extra Deck, so generic Cyberse searchers, revivers and boosts advance the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Cyberse to the GY
hooks.why: Several archetype monsters trigger when sent to the GY, and a Normal Summoned Tuner revives a Level 4 Cyberse from the GY, so outside cards that send Cyberse monsters from the Deck to the GY set up those payoffs.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Material
hooks.why: The Rank 4 Xyz monsters only get their searches, sends and protection by detaching materials, so outside cards that attach extra material give them more uses.

profile.plan: A DARK Fiend pile that Ritual Summons The Masked Beast with Curse of the Masked Beast, Special Summons Masked Beast Des Gardius by Tributing Grand Tiki Elder or Melchid the Four-Face Beast, and leans on Equip Spell 'Masks' plus Trap recovery for disruption.

hooks.label: Ritual support
hooks.why: The Masked Beast is a Level 8 Ritual Monster that only Curse of the Masked Beast can bring out, so outside Ritual searchers and Ritual Summon effects fetch the pieces or pay the 8 Levels of Tribute for it.

hooks.label: Fiend and DARK support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype — Melchid the Four-Face Beast, Grand Tiki Elder, Nuvia the Wicked, The Masked Beast and Masked Beast Des Gardius — is a DARK Fiend, so Fiend or DARK support reaches the entire deck.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Melchid the Four-Face Beast and Grand Tiki Elder are Normal Monsters and Masked Beast Des Gardius can only be Special Summoned by Tributing one of them, so cards that search or revive Normal Monsters assemble that play.

hooks.label: Equip Spell support
hooks.why: Mask of the Accursed, Mask of Brutality and The Mask of Remnants are all Equip Spells, so outside cards that add Equip Spells from the Deck or GY, or that equip monsters, keep the Mask engine supplied.

hooks.label: DARK Fiend fodder
hooks.why: Curse of the Masked Beast Tributes 8 Levels of monsters and Masked Beast Des Gardius needs two Tributes including a named Fiend, so cards that Special Summon DARK Fiends from hand, Deck or GY provide free bodies for both.

profile.plan: A Normal Monster toolbox that declares vanilla names to Special Summon them from the hand, Deck or GY, fills the GY with differently-named Normal Monsters to pump its own Dragons, and Tribute Summons Primite Imperial Dragon to wipe the opponent's board.

hooks.label: Normal Monster searchers
hooks.why: Primite Drillbeam wants a Normal Monster revealed from the hand and Lordly Lode only declares a name, so cards that add a Normal Monster from the Deck to the hand supply both the revealed card and a known name.

hooks.label: Mills Normal Monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Primite Dragon Ether Beryl Tributes itself to send a Normal Monster from the Deck to the GY, and Lordly Lode's ATK boost, Drillbeam's condition, Howl's take-control target and Imperial Dragon's Type/Attribute banish all read Normal Monsters in the GY.

hooks.label: Fusion Summoning for the boss
hooks.why: Primite Dragon Nether Berzelius is a Fusion Monster needing a Primite monster plus Normal Monsters, but the archetype contains no Fusion Spell of its own, so outside Fusion Summoning is the only way to bring it out.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Primite Imperial Dragon can only be Normal Summoned by Tributing 1 Normal Monster and pays off when Tribute Summoned, while Ether Beryl Sets a Primite Spell/Trap off a Normal Summon, so extra Normal/Tribute Summons turn both into the same turn.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Primite monster, including the boss Primite Dragon Nether Berzelius, is a Dragon, so Dragon tutors, revivals and boosters work on the whole archetype.

profile.plan: A Rank 8 Machine Xyz deck: it floods Level 8 Gimmick Puppet monsters onto the field, overlays them into Number 15/40/88 and their Chaos 'C' forms with Rank-Up-Magic, and grinds the opponent down with repeated detach effects that destroy cards and burn.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: Gimmick Puppet Fantasix Machinix adds a 'Rank-Up-Magic' Spell from your Deck and Puppet Parade Sets one directly from the Deck, while Number C88 can only be Summoned by a 'Rank-Up-Magic' targeting Number 88.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Gimmick Puppet monster is a Machine, Gimmick Puppet Chimera Doll needs 2 Machine monsters and locks you into Machine Xyz Monsters, and Condolence Puppet protects a Machine Xyz Monster you control.

hooks.label: Free Level 8 bodies
hooks.why: The deck's Xyz plays need two Level 8 monsters at once, and its own Level 8s (Gimmick Puppet Dreary Doll, Magnet Doll, Nightmare, Cattle Scream) all Special Summon themselves from the hand or Graveyard, so outside Level 8 monsters that do the same are extra overlay material.

hooks.label: Extra Xyz material
hooks.why: Number 15 detaches up to twice per turn, Number 40, Number C15, Number C40 and Number C88 detach every turn, Gigantes Doll detaches 2 at once and Cattle Scream detaches as its Summoning cost, so cards that attach material give those effects more uses.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Xyz toolbox built from Level 4 DARK monsters, using Kerykeion to grind and extra Normal Summon and Ophion to lock the opponent out of high-Level Special Summons.

hooks.label: Sends DARK to GY
hooks.why: Kerykeion's Graveyard effect and Salamandra's ATK gain both need monsters in the GY, so outside cards that send DARK monsters from the Deck to the GY set both up.

hooks.label: DARK banished from GY
hooks.why: Salamandra banishes any monster from your Graveyard as a cost, so outside DARK monsters with an effect when banished from the GY get value for free.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Kerykeion lets you Normal Summon a monster for 1 less Tribute and grants an extra Normal Summon, so cards that help Tribute Summon Golem and Coppelia fit.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck of small DARK Machine monsters that Normal Summon themselves to equip Level 3 or lower Dragons out of the Graveyard for ATK, then fuse those equipped bodies into Machine bosses that keep equipping from either GY.

hooks.label: Dragon-to-Graveyard mill
hooks.why: Cyberdark Horn, Edge and Keel equip a Level 3 or lower Dragon from the GY when Normal Summoned, and Cyberdarkness Dragon equips a Dragon or Machine from the GY, so anything that puts a Dragon in the GY hands them an equip target.

hooks.label: Other 'Cyber' monsters
hooks.why: Cyberdark Chimera locks you into Dragon or Machine "Cyber" monsters as Fusion Material and Cyberdark End Dragon must fuse with Cyber End Dragon, so the wider Cyber family slots straight into the Fusion Summons.

hooks.label: Fusion Spell support
hooks.why: Cyberdark Chimera adds Power Bond from the Deck and Cyberdark Inferno adds a "Polymerization" or "Fusion" Spell when destroyed, so extra ways to Fusion Summon feed the deck's Machine bosses.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger in the GY
hooks.why: Cyberdark Cannon sends a monster from the Deck to the GY during damage calculation, Cyberdark Chimera sends a Cyberdark monster from the Deck, and Cybernetic Horizon sends Dragons/Machines from hand and Deck, so Dragon and Machine monsters with a "sent to the GY" trigger are pure value.

profile.plan: An EARTH Warrior battle deck that forces the opponent's monsters to attack into protected Amazoness, punishes every battle, and Fusion Summons Amazoness boss monsters with Polymerization.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Amazoness except the two Tigers is a Warrior, and Amazoness Pet Liger King even revives an "Amazoness Warrior monster", so generic Warrior support searches, revives and boosts nearly the whole deck.

hooks.label: Polymerization searchers
hooks.why: Amazoness War Chief Sets "Polymerization" directly from the Deck and Amazoness Spiritualist adds it to the hand, and it is the main route into Amazoness Empress, Augusta and Pet Liger King.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Amazoness Archer Tributes 2 monsters for its burn and Amazoness Scouts Tributes itself for protection, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed are free material.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monster
hooks.why: Amazoness Village Special Summons from the Deck whenever an Amazoness monster is destroyed by a card effect, and Amazoness Shamanism, Pet Liger King and the Pendulum effects already destroy your own cards, so outside effects that destroy a monster you control start the loop.

hooks.label: Punishes opponent's attacks
hooks.why: Amazoness Archers, Amazoness Tiger and Amazoness Pet Liger King force the opponent's monsters to attack, while Amazoness Swords Woman sends the battle damage back, so outside cards that trigger on an opponent's attack declaration are always live.

profile.plan: A Rank 8/9 Xyz deck that climbs Cipher monsters to Level 8, overlays into LIGHT Dragon 'Galaxy-Eyes Cipher' Xyz, then steals the opponent's monsters and copies their names for huge same-name payoffs.

hooks.label: Discard-payoff monsters
hooks.why: Cipher Twin Raptor discards a card to Special Summon a Cipher monster and Cipher Mirror Knight discards itself to revive one, so any monster that does something when discarded is used for free.

hooks.label: Galaxy-Eyes support
hooks.why: Cipher Bit and Double Cipher both name 'Galaxy-Eyes' Xyz Monsters and Cipher Blade Dragon needs a Rank 8 'Galaxy-Eyes' as material, so Galaxy/Photon cards reach the deck's bosses.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: Rank-Up-Magic Cipher Ascension turns a Rank 8 Cipher Xyz into a Rank 9, and any other Rank-Up-Magic card can rank Galaxy-Eyes Cipher Dragon straight into Neo Galaxy-Eyes Cipher Dragon or Blade Dragon.

hooks.label: Level 8 self-summoners
hooks.why: Galaxy-Eyes Cipher Dragon is made from 2 Level 8 monsters, so free Level 8 bodies are exactly the raw material the Cipher Wing and Cipher Biplane Level-climb is built to produce.

hooks.label: Attaches itself as material
hooks.why: Cipher Etranger and Cipher Bit attach themselves to a Cipher Xyz as Xyz Material, and the detach effects of Cipher Dragon, Blade Dragon and Neo Galaxy-Eyes want as much material as they can get.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Nearly every Cipher monster, including the LIGHT Dragon Xyz bosses, is LIGHT, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT monsters work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: The deck swarms with Fur Hire monsters of different names and Types, triggering each other's effects when they are Special Summoned, and uses Link Summons to bring out Extra Deck monsters that reward having many different Types.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Rookie Fur Hire and Donner, Dagger Fur Hire Tribute a monster as cost, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Traps that revive from GY
hooks.why: The on-field Fur Hire monsters trigger when a Fur Hire is Special Summoned while you control them, so a Trap that Special Summons a Fur Hire from the GY during the opponent's turn triggers those effects again.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: The deck relies on Fandora, the Flying Furtress and Fandora, the Flying Fighting Furtress, so cards that search or Set Field Spells get to them faster.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when discarded
hooks.why: Fandora, the Flying Fighting Furtress lets you add a Fur Hire from Deck and discard any card as part of its effect, so outside monsters that trigger when discarded by a card effect get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Rookie Fur Hire and Donner, Dagger Fur Hire Tribute a monster as cost, and the Link Monsters need monsters of different Types, so Tokens provide free fodder and material.

profile.plan: Gagaga manipulates its monsters' Levels to Xyz Summon a variety of Ranks, then uses the Xyz Monsters' detach effects and the Main Deck monsters' effects when used as Xyz Material to gain advantage.

hooks.label: Monster with detach effect
hooks.why: Gagaga Ganbara Knight, Gagaga Mancer and Gagaga Girl - Cell Phone Subtraction all trigger when detached from an Xyz Monster, so outside monsters with the same trigger get value from being used as Xyz Material.

hooks.label: Monster with Xyz Material effect
hooks.why: Gagaga Head and Gagaga Girl grant effects to the Xyz Monster that uses them as material, so outside monsters that do the same add value to any Xyz Summon.

hooks.label: Level-changing Spell
hooks.why: Gagaga Magician, Gagaga Girl, Gagaga Sister and Gagaga Utopic Tactics all manipulate Levels to set up Xyz Summons, so outside Spells that change Levels of your monsters open up more Xyz plays.

hooks.label: Onomat support
hooks.why: Gagagaga Girl and Gagaga Ganbara Knight search and support the Onomat series (Zubaba, Gagaga, Gogogo, Dododo), so outside cards that support Onomat help the whole engine.

profile.plan: A Rank 1 Xyz deck that swarms Level 1 Winged Beast monsters to build Xyz Monsters with many materials, which then detach them for searching, protection, bouncing and direct attacks.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Lyrilusc monster is a Winged Beast, so cards that support the Winged Beast Type (searching, reviving, Tributing them) work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: All Lyrilusc monsters are WIND, so cards that support the WIND Attribute (boosting, searching, Special Summoning WIND monsters) fit the deck.

hooks.label: Tributes Winged Beast monsters
hooks.why: The deck's monsters are all Winged Beast, so they can pay the cost of cards that Tribute a Winged Beast to activate powerful effects, like Icarus Attack.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Materials
hooks.why: The Rank 1 Xyz monsters all gain effects from the number of materials attached, and Bird Sanctuary and Celestine Wagtail attach materials, so outside cards that attach materials (like Xyz Reborn or Overlay Regen) give extra detaches.

hooks.label: Triggers when detached
hooks.why: Assembled Nightingale, Recital Starling, Promenade Thrush and Ensemblue Robin all detach materials constantly, so outside monsters that get an effect when detached (like Zoodiac Ratpier) give free value.

profile.plan: A Dinosaur beatdown deck that fights from behind: its monsters Special Summon themselves and get their bonuses while the opponent has more monsters, then lock the opponent into attacking the deck's high-ATK Link, Synchro and Fusion bosses.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every Dinowrestler monster is a Dinosaur, and Iguanodraka discards and Tributes Dinosaur monsters as cost, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Dinosaurs works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed or discarded
hooks.why: Iguanodraka discards 1 other Dinosaur to Special Summon itself and Tributes a Dinosaur to revive a Dinowrestler, so outside Dinosaurs with an effect when they are Tributed or discarded get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent monsters
hooks.why: Pankratops, Capaptera, Valeonyx, Coelasilat, Eskrimamenchi and World Dino Wrestling all only turn on while your opponent controls more monsters than you do, so cards that hand the opponent extra bodies switch the whole deck on.

hooks.label: Punishes the opponent's attacks
hooks.why: World Dino Wrestling lets each player attack with only 1 monster and King T Wrextle, Giga Spinosavate and Chimera T Wrextle make every opposing monster attack only them, so 'when your opponent's monster declares an attack' effects always get a legal trigger at the deck's chosen target.

profile.plan: Earthbound parks a Field Spell in the Field Zone, Tribute Summons Level 10 DARK Fiend-adjacent Immortals that attack directly and are immune to targeting, and backs them with DARK Synchro and Fusion bosses.

hooks.label: Field Spell enablers
hooks.why: Every Earthbound Immortal destroys itself if there is no face-up Field Spell, and Earthbound Geoglyph and Earthbound Prison only function from the Field Zone.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: The Earthbound Immortals are Level 10 and need two Tributes, Earthbound Geoglyph treats a Synchro Monster as two Tributes for that Tribute Summon, and Offering to the Immortals hands you two Ceremonial Tokens for it.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Earthbound Immortal Uru, Earthbound Immortal Cusillu, Earthbound Release and Offering to the Immortals all Tribute your own monsters, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get their payoff for free.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: The Prisoner Tuners, Earthbound Greater Linewalker, Earthbound Linewalker and every Earthbound Fusion and Synchro Monster are Fiend-Type, so Fiend support touches most of the deck.

profile.plan: A Normal-Summon ladder of Level 1 Winged Beasts that each fetch and immediately Normal Summon the next one, ending on Tribute Summoned Level 10 Winged Beast bosses (Empen, Snowl) while Special Summoning stays locked out.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Floowandereeze & Robina and Floowandereeze & Eglen each Normal Summon another Winged Beast right after their search, and Floowandereeze & Snowl allows three Normal Summons a turn, so outside cards that grant or perform extra Normal Summons extend the same chain without ever Special Summoning.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Floowandereeze monster is a Winged Beast, and the deck's searches (Eglen, Robina, Advent of Adventure, Dreaming Town) all name Winged Beast monsters, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Winged Beasts works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Payoff for being banished
hooks.why: The deck banishes its own cards constantly as cost or effect - Empen and Snowl banish a card from the hand, Advent of Adventure banishes a Winged Beast from hand or field, Magnificent Map banishes from the Deck and Stri banishes from the GY - so monsters that reward being banished get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Rewards Tribute Summoned monsters
hooks.why: Empen, Snowl and Scary Sea all only pay off while you control a Tribute Summoned monster, so outside cards that boost, protect or feed off Tribute Summoned monsters line up with the deck's win condition.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck that Ritual Summons its whole hand: exact-Level Ritual Spells fuel WATER Ritual Monsters, the small monsters replace themselves when Tributed, and every boss is also a hand trap that discards itself.

hooks.label: Tributing your monsters
hooks.why: Shurit, Avance, Emilia, Great Sorcerer, Ariel, Exa and Dance Princess only search or revive when a card effect Tributes them, so outside cards that Tribute a monster you control turn them into free advantage.

hooks.label: Banishing your monsters
hooks.why: Great Sorcerer and Exa trigger when they are banished, and Nekroz of Metaltron's Pendulum effect needs a 'Nekroz' card banished face-up, so outside cards that banish your own WATER monsters are live.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster support
hooks.why: Every Nekroz boss says it must be Ritual Summoned, so outside cards that add Ritual Monsters or Ritual Spells to the hand, or that Ritual Summon (Nekroz Cycle even revives from the GY), are extra copies of the engine.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Almost every Nekroz monster, including Brionac, Trishula, Valkyrus and Areadbhair, is WATER, and the Ritual Spells Tribute WATER bodies, so cards that search, revive or boost WATER monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level-changing effects
hooks.why: Nekroz Ritual Spells need the Tributed monsters' Levels to total exactly the Ritual Monster's Level (Ariel even shifts her own Level for this), so outside effects that change a monster's Level let you reach exact totals with the bodies you have.

profile.plan: A Link-climbing beatdown deck: the small Crusadia monsters Special Summon themselves into zones its Link Monsters point to, the Link Monsters grow by the original ATK of whatever they point at, and then one huge Link Monster with doubled battle damage and piercing swings for game.

hooks.label: World Legacy monsters
hooks.why: Crusadia Equimax can Tribute a "World Legacy" monster it points to for its negate, and Crusadia Vanguard Tributes one to Special Summon from the Deck or GY, so World Legacy monsters are the archetype's built-in second half.

hooks.label: Summons into a linked zone
hooks.why: Crusadia Draco and Crusadia Reclusia only trigger when they are Normal or Special Summoned to a zone a Link Monster points to, and Magius, Regulex and Spatha all search whenever an Effect Monster is Special Summoned to one of their zones.
phrases: zone a Link Monster points to

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Effect Monsters
hooks.why: Every Crusadia main deck monster Special Summons itself from the hand in Defense Position, which feeds Magius's search and provides the Link material for Regulex, Spatha and Equimax, so outside monsters that deploy themselves the same way are free bodies.

hooks.label: Big monsters to point at
hooks.why: Equimax, Regulex and Spatha gain ATK equal to the combined original ATK of the monsters they point to, and a monster they point to cannot attack, so a high-Level monster that Special Summons itself and never needs to attack is pure ATK for the Link Monster.

hooks.label: Extra attacks and ATK boosts
hooks.why: The deck finishes with a single Link Monster: Crusadia Maximus doubles the battle damage it inflicts, Crusadia Leonis gives it piercing and Crusadia Revival lets it attack every monster once, so anything that adds more damage or more attacks to a Link Monster stacks with those.

profile.plan: Runs the Field Spell Numeron Network, which copies the deck's Normal Spells, to drop four Numeron Gate Xyz Monsters at once with Numeron Calling and stack their ATK-doubling until the Duel ends.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Numeron Calling only does anything while Numeron Network sits in your Field Zone, so any outside card that adds or places a Field Spell from the Deck is another way to get the engine online.

hooks.label: Field Spell protection
hooks.why: Numeron Network must stay in the Field Zone for Numeron Calling to Special Summon the Numeron Gate Xyz Monsters, so effects that stop a Field Spell being destroyed or removed keep the deck's whole plan alive.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 1s
hooks.why: Number 1, 2, 3 and 4 are Rank 1 Xyz Monsters needing three Level 1 monsters each, so Level 1 monsters that Special Summon themselves let you build a Numeron Gate without waiting on Numeron Calling.

hooks.label: Dumps Xyz from Extra Deck
hooks.why: Numeron Chaos Ritual wants four of your 'Number' Xyz Monsters banished or in the GY, so effects that send Xyz Monsters from the Extra Deck to the GY fill that requirement without using up field presence.

profile.plan: Zoodiacs stack: any one Beast-Warrior monster becomes a Rank 4 Xyz that overlays onto the next, so a single body snowballs into a ladder of Xyz Monsters whose Xyz Materials are detached as removal, searches and recursion every turn.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Zoodiac monster is an EARTH Beast-Warrior, Zoodiac Broadbull searches Beast-Warrior monsters that can be Normal Summoned, and Zodiac Sign protects your Beast-Warriors from attacks.

hooks.label: Detached Xyz Material payoff
hooks.why: Zoodiac Drident, Broadbull, Chakanine and Tigermortar all detach an Xyz Material as a cost every turn, so monsters that do something when they are detached get used for free.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Zoodiac Ramram, Bunnyblast and Kataroost each fetch a Zoodiac card from the GY, Deck or hand when destroyed by card effect, and Zoodiac Barrage turns destroying one of your own cards into a Special Summon from the Deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when destroyed
hooks.why: Zoodiac Barrage destroys a face-up card you control to Special Summon from the Deck and Zodiac Sign destroys a monster in your hand or field as a substitute, so outside cards that pay off when destroyed are free fodder.

hooks.label: Attaches monsters as Xyz Material
hooks.why: The Zoodiac Xyz Monsters gain ATK and DEF from every Zoodiac attached, Zoodiac Boarbow wants 12 or more Xyz Materials, and Zoodiac Gathering can spend materials from another Xyz Monster you control.

profile.plan: The deck uses Prank-Kids monsters as Fusion and Link material, triggering their effects to summon more from the Deck, then Tributes the Fusion/Link monsters for disruptive effects and loops resources from the GY.

hooks.label: Mills a monster to GY
hooks.why: The main deck Prank-Kids only trigger when sent to the GY as material, but having them in the GY lets Prank-Kids Rocket Ride and Weather Washer revive them, and Prank-Kids Pranks shuffles them back to draw.

hooks.label: Summons a Level 5 or lower Fusion
hooks.why: Prank-Kids Rocket Ride and Weather Washer are Level 5 Fusion Monsters that can be Special Summoned by Instant Fusion, then Tributed for their effects to revive Prank-Kids and disrupt the opponent.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Prank-Kids Fansies, Dodo-Doodle-Doo and Battle Butler are Thunder monsters, and the deck can banish cards from hand with Rocksies, so Thunder Dragon-style cards that banish themselves or trigger when banished fit.

profile.plan: A FIRE Machine/Warrior control deck that Special Summons its 'Rescue-ACE' monsters from the Deck and Sets Quick-Play Spells and Normal Traps it can fire the turn they are Set, while its monsters Tribute themselves to answer the opponent's monster effects.

hooks.label: FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Rescue-ACE monster is FIRE and Rescue-ACE Arbitrator is a Link-4 that needs 2+ FIRE monsters as material, so cards that search, revive or pump FIRE monsters lift the whole deck.

hooks.label: Machine and Warrior support
hooks.why: The searchers Air Lifter, Monitor, Impulse and Quick Attacker are Warriors while Hydrant, Turbulence, Preventer, Fire Engine and Arbitrator are Machines, so Type support reaches every part of the deck.

hooks.label: FIRE self-Summoners
hooks.why: Arbitrator asks for 2+ FIRE monsters and Quick Attacker locks the Extra Deck to FIRE for the turn, so FIRE monsters that Special Summon themselves are free Link material and free bodies.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Air Lifter and Monitor add a Spell or Trap when they are Normal Summoned and Hydrant searches in the Main Phase, while HQ's extra Normal Summon only covers Rescue-ACE monsters, so outside extra Summons fire those effects again.

hooks.label: Summons to the opponent's field
hooks.why: Rescue-ACE Fire Engine Special Summons a Level 4 or lower Rescue-ACE monster from the hand, Deck or GY whenever a monster is Special Summoned to the opponent's field, which cards that drop a monster onto their side do for you.

profile.plan: A defense-position deck: Superheavy Samurai monsters attack while in face-up Defense Position using their DEF for damage, and nearly every effect switches off if any Spell or Trap is in the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Superheavy Samurai monster is Machine-Type and Warlord Susanowo, Ogre Shutendoji and Stealth Ninja all name a Machine-Type Tuner as material, so Machine search, revival and stat boosts cover the whole deck.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Flutist, Transporter, Soulpeacemaker and General Coral all Tribute Superheavy Samurai monsters as a cost, so an outside monster with an effect when it is Tributed turns that cost into free value.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Scarecrow discards a monster and Steam Train King discards up to two cards as costs, so outside monsters that trigger when they are discarded add value to every discard the deck makes.

hooks.label: Defense Position attackers
hooks.why: Big Benkei gives Superheavy Samurai monsters the ability to attack while in face-up Defense Position and apply their DEF for damage, so outside monsters that already fight this way share the deck's whole damage plan.
phrases: attack while in face-up Defense Position

profile.plan: A Zombie Synchro ladder that revives its Synchro Monsters from the GY by banishing other Zombies, triggering effects and Mayakashi Mayhem when they return.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Mayakashi monster is a Zombie, and the Link Monsters and Synchro ladder all use Zombie monsters as material, so cards that search, revive or boost Zombies improve the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills a Zombie
hooks.why: Yuki-Musume sends a Zombie from the Deck to the GY, and the Synchro revival costs banish another Zombie from the GY, so more effects that put Zombies in the GY set up the whole ladder.

hooks.label: Banished Zombie payoff
hooks.why: Each Mayakashi Synchro revives itself by banishing another Zombie from your GY, so outside Zombies that do something when they are banished turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Revives Zombie Synchro
hooks.why: Mayakashi Mayhem only triggers when a Zombie Synchro Monster is Special Summoned from outside the Extra Deck, and the Mayakashi Synchros all revive themselves from the GY, so outside revival effects create extra Mayhem triggers and restart the ladder.

profile.plan: A Level 9 boss deck: Generaider Boss Stage floods the field with Generaider monsters and Generaider Tokens while the opponents' searches and draws feed the bosses' Quick Effects, which Tribute monsters to negate, banish, destroy, revive or swarm more Level 9 bodies for Rank 9 Xyz plays.

hooks.label: Makes the opponent draw
hooks.why: Generaider Boss Stage Special Summons a Generaider monster from the Deck whenever your opponent adds a card from the Main Deck to their hand, and Harr punishes that same event, so any outside card that feeds your opponent cards starts your engine.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Loptr, Hela, Utgarda, Dovelgus, Frodi, Nidhogg and Generaider Boss Bite all Tribute monsters as a cost, and each accepts a different Type alongside Generaider monsters, so a monster of those Types with an effect when it is Tributed pays for itself.

hooks.label: Revives on the opponent's turn
hooks.why: Generaider Boss Stage Special Summons Generaider Tokens whenever you Special Summon a Generaider monster during your opponent's turn, so a Trap that brings a Level 9 Generaider back from the GY turns into a full board.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Generaider Boss Loot stops your opponent's monsters from targeting your Generaider Effect Monsters for attacks while you control a Token, so extra Tokens keep the boss monsters alive outside your opponent's turn.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Fiend and Beast Synchro deck whose monsters trigger when they are discarded or sent from the hand to the GY, so it deliberately empties its own hand to Synchro Summon and to fire off removal, revival and control-stealing effects.

hooks.label: Discards or mills your hand
hooks.why: Fabled Lurrie, The Fabled Cerburrel, The Fabled Ganashia, Fabled Krus, The Fabled Catsith, The Fabled Peggulsus and Fabled Marcosia all do something the moment a card effect discards them, so any outside card that discards is another trigger.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Fabled Raven, Fabled Gallabas, Stairway to a Fabled Realm and Fabled Treason throw away cards as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Fabled Levilazebul Tributes any number of Fabled monsters to steal the opponent's monsters, and Fabled Dyf and Fabled Topi Tribute themselves, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed slot straight in.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Every Fabled monster, including the Synchros, is LIGHT, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT monsters work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: The Fiend half of the deck (Fabled Grimro, Kushano, Soulkius, Ragin, Valkyrus, Leviathan, Levilazebul and the rest) is all Fiend, and Fabled Valkyrus even discards a Fiend to draw.

hooks.label: Beast support
hooks.why: The Beast half of the deck (The Fabled Cerburrel, Ganashia, Catsith, Chawa, Nozoochee, Abanc, Behilmoth, Peggulsus and the Synchros Unicore and Kudabbi) all share the Beast Type.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck that repeatedly destroys its own 'Scrap' monsters with 'Scrap' card effects to trigger searches and Special Summons, then Synchro Summons into 'Scrap' Dragons that destroy the opponent's cards.

hooks.label: Triggers when destroyed
hooks.why: Scrap Dragon, Scrap Wyvern and Scrapstorm repeatedly destroy your own cards, so outside cards that gain advantage when destroyed by card effect turn that into value.

hooks.label: Machine GY effects
hooks.why: Scrap Recycler sends a Machine monster from your Deck to the GY, so outside Machine monsters that trigger when sent to the GY get an extra use.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Scrap monster is EARTH, so any card that supports EARTH monsters works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Synchro Material effects
hooks.why: The deck Synchro Summons constantly, so outside monsters that trigger when used as Synchro Material turn each Synchro Summon into extra advantage.

profile.plan: A contact-Fusion deck: it banishes its own Ritual Beast monsters (as cost and as Fusion material), fuses on the field without Polymerization, then bounces the Ulti Fusions back to the Extra Deck to revive a banished Ritual Beast Tamer and Spiritual Beast pair.

hooks.label: Banishes your own cards
hooks.why: Ritual Beast Ambush, Ritual Beast Return, Ritual Beast's Bond, Ulti-Kimunfalcos and Ulti-Nochiudrago all Special Summon out of the banished pile, so any outside card that banishes your own Ritual Beast monsters from hand, Deck or Graveyard is pure setup.

hooks.label: Revives banished monsters
hooks.why: Every Ulti Fusion returns itself to the Extra Deck to Special Summon a banished Tamer and Spiritual Beast in Defense Position, and Ritual Beast Ambush, Ritual Beast Return and Ritual Beast's Bond read from the same pile, so outside cards that Special Summon from banishment extend the loop.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Ritual Beast Tamer (Elder, Wen, Lara, Winda, Zeframpilica, Zefrawendi) and the Ulti-Gaiapelio, Ulti-Kimunfalcos and Ulti-Reirautari bosses are Psychic, so Psychic searchers and Emergency Teleport-style Special Summons fetch the deck's Normal Summon starters.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Almost the whole archetype — every Spiritual Beast plus Elder, Wen, Winda and the two Pendulum Tamers — is WIND, so generic WIND support can search, revive or protect the deck's bodies.

hooks.label: Zefra Pendulum monsters
hooks.why: Ritual Beast Tamer Zeframpilica Special Summons a 'Ritual Beast' or 'Zefra' monster from the Graveyard and Zefrawendi adds a face-up 'Zefra' monster from the Extra Deck, while their Scales 1 and 7 Pendulum Summon the 'Ritual Beast' and 'Zefra' monsters the deck needs.

profile.plan: An Xyz-focused LIGHT deck that swarms Level 3-6 monsters, manipulates their Levels and detaches Xyz Materials for control effects.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster support
hooks.why: Every Constellar monster is LIGHT, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when detached
hooks.why: Constellar Xyz Monsters like Pleiades and Ptolemy M7 detach materials constantly, so outside monsters with effects when detached as Xyz Material get free value.

hooks.label: Special Summons an Xyz
hooks.why: Constellar Star Chart draws whenever a Constellar Xyz Monster is Special Summoned, so outside cards that revive or Special Summon Xyz Monsters trigger it.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Pollux, Leonis and Delteros all grant extra Normal Summons of Constellar monsters, so outside cards that add another Normal Summon speed up the Xyz plays.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Kaus, Twinkle and Cygnian change Levels to reach different Xyz Ranks, so outside cards that modify Levels give the deck more flexibility.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: The Level 5 and 6 Constellar monsters need Tributes, and Sombre reduces that cost, so outside cards that help Tribute Summon are welcome.

profile.plan: A Machine/WIND deck that generates Mecha Phantom Beast Tokens to protect its monsters, then Tributes them for effects while Synchro, Xyz, and Link Summoning into boss monsters like Dracossack and Auroradon.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Mecha Phantom Beast monster is a Machine-Type, so cards that search, revive or boost Machines work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Every Mecha Phantom Beast monster is a WIND monster, so cards that support WIND monsters benefit the entire archetype.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Auroradon can Tribute up to 3 monsters for its effect, and the deck needs extra bodies for Synchro and Link Summons, so outside cards that Special Summon Tokens provide additional fodder.

hooks.label: Tributes your monsters
hooks.why: Harrliard triggers when a monster you control is Tributed to activate a card or effect, so any outside card that Tributes your monsters will Special Summon a Token for free.

hooks.label: Mills Machines
hooks.why: O-Lion and Blue Impala have effects that trigger or activate in the Graveyard, so outside cards that send Machine monsters from the Deck to the GY set those up.

profile.plan: A WATER Sea Serpent deck whose monsters, when sent to the Graveyard to pay for another WATER monster's effect, search, revive, destroy or Special Summon, so it wants cheap ways to keep feeding its own monsters to the GY.

hooks.label: WATER monsters that dump cards
hooks.why: Every Atlantean (Neptabyss, Dragoons, Heavy Infantry, Marksman, Mermail Shadow Squad) triggers when it is sent to the GY to activate a WATER monster's effect, so any WATER monster that discards from hand or mills from Deck as cost sets one off.

hooks.label: Sea Serpent and WATER support
hooks.why: The entire Main Deck is Sea Serpent WATER monsters and Neptabyss and Atlantean Dragoons both search from the Type, so support for the Type or the Attribute reaches every card in the deck.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning low-Level WATER fodder
hooks.why: Poseidra, the Atlantean Dragon Tributes three Level 3 or lower WATER monsters and Call of the Atlanteans Special Summons three Level 3 or lower Sea Serpents, so cheap WATER monsters that Special Summon themselves feed both.
