profile.plan: A slow Machine toolbox that Normal Summons one Gadget after another, each searching the next, then turns every destroyed Gadget into a free Special Summon from the Deck while Dread Dynamo and Stronghold the Moving Fortress swing for huge ATK.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every useful Gadget is a Machine, and Platinum Gadget needs 2 Machine monsters as Link Material, so anything that searches, revives, protects or boosts Machines powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Machine
hooks.why: Gold Gadget, Silver Gadget and Platinum Gadget all Special Summon a Level 4 Gadget from the Deck when they are destroyed by battle or card effect, so effects that destroy your own Machines turn them into extra bodies.

hooks.label: Morphtronic partners
hooks.why: Gadget Gamer Tributes itself to Special Summon a Morphtronic from your hand and Gadget Arms recovers Morphtronic Spell/Traps from the Graveyard, while Gadget Box is treated as a Morphtronic card, so the two themes are built to share a deck.

hooks.label: Morph Counter cards
hooks.why: Gadget Box places 3 Morph Counters on itself and removes one per turn to Special Summon a Machine token, so outside cards that place or use Morph Counters keep that engine supplied.

profile.plan: A Plant deck that Tributes its own monsters as cost to trigger effects, swarming the field and Xyz Summoning into Rank 4 and 6 Plant monsters while disrupting the opponent.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Every Rikka monster is a Plant and the deck's effects require Tributing Plant monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Plants work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Tribute-trigger monsters
hooks.why: Rikka Glamour and Snowdrop the Rikka Fairy Tribute Plant monsters as cost, so outside Plant monsters with an effect when Tributed give extra value.

hooks.label: Tribute payoffs
hooks.why: Primula, Erica and Kanzashi all trigger when a Plant monster is Tributed, so outside cards that also reward Tributing a Plant fit the same engine.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Mudan the Rikka Fairy triggers when Normal Summoned (or Special Summoned by a Plant), so extra Normal Summons for Plants let you trigger it more.

hooks.label: Plant Token generators
hooks.why: The deck needs Plant monsters to Tribute for its effects, so cards that Special Summon Plant Tokens give free fodder.

profile.plan: A Trap-based deck that Special Summons its Paleozoic Traps from the GY as Level 2 Aqua Normal Monsters when any Trap is activated, then uses them as Xyz and Link material for Rank 2 and Link 2 bosses.

hooks.label: Sends Traps from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Paleozoic Marrella sends a Trap from your Deck to the GY, and every Paleozoic Trap needs to be in the GY to Special Summon itself when a Trap is activated.

hooks.label: Sets Traps from Deck
hooks.why: Paleozoic Cambroraster Sets a Paleozoic Trap directly from the Deck, and Opabinia lets you activate them from hand, so outside cards that Set Traps from Deck give more activations to trigger the GY effects.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: Every Paleozoic monster is Aqua, so cards that search, revive or boost Aqua monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Revives Aqua monsters from GY
hooks.why: The Paleozoic Traps Special Summon themselves from the GY as Aqua monsters, so outside cards that revive Aqua monsters can bring back used copies or other Aqua monsters for Xyz and Link Summons.

profile.plan: A swarm of Level 2 Beast monsters that bounce themselves back to hand whenever the opponent Summons or targets them and re-Summon themselves in the End Phase, Xyz Summoning into Rank 2 Beast bosses that detach, negate and bounce.

hooks.label: Beast support
hooks.why: Every Melffy monster is a Beast, Melffy Hide-and-Seek protects Beast monsters, Melffy Mommy attaches Beast monsters as material, and the Rank 2 Xyz and Beast Fusions all ask for Beast materials.

hooks.label: Triggers when detached
hooks.why: Melffy of the Forest, Joyous Melffys, Melffy Playhouse and Melffy Godmommy all detach Xyz materials as a cost, so a monster that pays you back when it is detached is material the deck is glad to spend.

hooks.label: Fusion material Beasts
hooks.why: Melffy Rabbys and Melffy Playtime Surprise Fusion Summon using monsters from the hand or field, and Melffys' Joyful Surprise asks for a Beast monster, so an outside Beast with an effect when used as material turns a Fusion Summon into extra value.

hooks.label: Beasts that summon themselves
hooks.why: Melffy Rabbys Special Summons any number of Beast monsters from the hand and every Melffy returns to hand and re-Summons itself in the End Phase, so Beasts that Special Summon themselves from the hand keep the Rank 2 Xyz plays coming.

hooks.label: Beast GY fodder
hooks.why: Melffy Hide-and-Seek needs three differently named Beasts in the GY, Melffy Pony adds a Level 2 or lower Beast from the GY, Melffy Tag revives one and Melffys' Joyful Surprise Special Summons a Beast from there.

profile.plan: Synchro Summon repeatedly, using Tuner Synchro Monsters to climb into Level 10 and 12 bosses during the opponent's turn, while the smaller T.G. monsters search each other when destroyed.

hooks.label: Synchro Material payoffs
hooks.why: T.G. Tank Grub and T.G. Jet Falcon already reward being used as Synchro Material, so outside monsters with the same text get that payoff for free when the deck climbs.

hooks.label: Opponent-turn Tuner Synchros
hooks.why: T.G.'s biggest Synchro Monsters require a Tuner Synchro Monster as material, and the archetype's own (Wonder Magician, Star Guardian, Mighty Striker) all Synchro Summon during the opponent's Main Phase, so outside Tuner Synchros with that text serve the same role.

hooks.label: Destroy your own monsters
hooks.why: T.G. Warwolf, Striker, Booster Raptor, Rush Rhino and Cyber Magician all search a T.G. monster during the End Phase if they were destroyed on the field that turn, so outside cards that destroy your own monsters turn into searches.

hooks.label: Special Summon Level 1 monsters
hooks.why: T.G. Booster Raptor, Gear Zombie, Rocket Salamander, Tank Grub, Cyber Magician and Drill Fish are all Level 1, and they are the deck's combo starters, so outside cards that Special Summon Level 1 monsters from hand or Deck set up Synchro plays.

hooks.label: Send monsters from Deck to GY
hooks.why: T.G. Mighty Striker sends a T.G. card from Deck to GY, and T.G. Screw Serpent, Over Dragonar and Halberd Cannon all revive from the GY, so outside cards that send monsters from Deck to GY set up those comebacks.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster control deck that grinds with Trap Cards: every Trap activation flips up Multifaker, which brings out more Altergeist monsters, and the deck recycles its own cards from the field and GY while negating the opponent's plays.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Altergeist monster is a Spellcaster, so searchers, revivers, stat boosts and locks that name the Spellcaster Type work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Trap activation payoff
hooks.why: Multifaker Special Summons itself and then another Altergeist from the Deck every time you activate a Trap Card, so outside cards that reward Trap activations ride the exact same plays.

hooks.label: Tributing your own monsters
hooks.why: Hexstia, Primebanshee and Memorygant Tribute your own monsters as cost, and almost every Altergeist monster triggers when it is sent from the field to the GY, so outside cards that Tribute your monsters cash those effects in.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: The deck repeatedly Tributes its own monsters for Hexstia's negation, Primebanshee's Summon and Pixiel's excavate, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get that trigger for free.

hooks.label: Set Traps from Deck
hooks.why: Marionetter Sets an Altergeist Trap from the Deck on Normal Summon and Adminia does the same on Link Summon, so outside cards that Set Traps from the Deck keep the Trap activations that Multifaker feeds on coming.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Xyz deck that attaches cards from the Deck, GY and opponent's GY as Xyz material, then detaches different types (Monster, Spell, Trap) for disruptive effects, while its monsters Tribute themselves or revive from the GY.

hooks.label: Sends DARK monsters to GY
hooks.why: Time Thief Bezel Ship, Temporwhal and Regulator all have effects in the GY, so sending DARK monsters from the Deck to the GY sets them up.

hooks.label: Spells/Traps that attach themselves as Xyz material
hooks.why: Time Thief Redoer and Double Barrel want Spell and Trap materials to detach, so Spells and Traps that attach themselves to an Xyz Monster provide those types without using the archetype's own cards.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when detached
hooks.why: The deck detaches Xyz materials for Redoer, Double Barrel, Perpetua, Winder and Bezel Ship, so outside monsters with effects when detached from an Xyz Monster get used for free.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when attached
hooks.why: The deck Xyz Summons constantly, so outside monsters used as Xyz material will be attached, and any effect when attached to an Xyz Monster gives extra value.

hooks.label: Psychic or Machine support
hooks.why: The Xyz monsters are Psychic and the Main Deck monsters are Psychic or Machine, so cards that search, revive or boost those Types work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Trap-heavy DARK Dinosaur deck that keeps paying half its LP to Fusion Summon Dinomorphia Fusions out of the Deck and to fire Normal and Counter Traps, with every monster reviving another from the GY when it is destroyed.

hooks.label: DARK Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every Dinomorphia monster, including Kentregina, Rexterm and Stealthbergia, is a DARK Dinosaur, so Type and Attribute support searches, revives or protects the entire deck.

hooks.label: Pays your own LP
hooks.why: Therizia, Diplos, Rexterm's Quick Effect and nearly every Dinomorphia Trap pay half your LP, and the payoffs (Stealthbergia's free Traps, Rexterm's lock, the GY damage-prevention) all switch on at 2000 LP or less.

hooks.label: Sets Traps from the Deck
hooks.why: Therizia Sets a Dinomorphia Trap directly from the Deck and the whole deck wins on Trap disruption, so outside cards that Set Normal or Counter Traps from the Deck are another copy of that play.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Dinosaur
hooks.why: Therizia, Diplos, Kentregina, Stealthbergia and Rexterm all Special Summon a Dinomorphia from the GY when they are destroyed by battle or card effect, and Brute and Sonic already destroy your own Dinomorphia monster as their cost.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with Traps
hooks.why: Therizia and Diplos banish a Trap from the GY as the cost of reviving a Dinomorphia, so outside cards that send Traps from the Deck to the GY turn on those revives.

profile.plan: An EARTH Warrior/Beast-Warrior Synchro deck that floods the field with X-Saber Tuners and Level 4 bodies, revives them from the Graveyard over and over, and converts its battles and Gottoms' Tributes into random discards from the opponent's hand.

hooks.label: Attacks the opponent's hand
hooks.why: Gottoms, Airbellum and Urbellum all rip random cards out of the opponent's hand, so outside cards that also discard from the opponent's hand pile on the same disruption.

hooks.label: Punishes destroying by battle
hooks.why: Uruz, Sword of Sparkles, At One With the Sword, Garsem and Fulhelmknight all pay off when an X-Saber destroys a monster in battle, so outside cards triggering on that same event stack with them.

hooks.label: Synchro Material effects
hooks.why: The deck Synchro Summons constantly with its many Tuners, so outside monsters that do something when used as Synchro Material trigger for free off those Summons.

hooks.label: Turns monsters into Defense
hooks.why: Fulhelmknight revives a Level 4 or lower X-Saber from the Graveyard when it destroys a Defense Position monster, so outside cards that force the opponent's monsters into Defense Position switch that effect on.

profile.plan: The deck uses Wyrm-Type monsters of different Attributes that replace themselves when destroyed, Synchro Summoning during the opponent's turn and locking the opponent with Chaofeng.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Wyrm
hooks.why: Every Yang Zing monster triggers when destroyed by battle or card effect, so any card that destroys a Wyrm you control starts the chain of searches and Special Summons.

hooks.label: Wyrm-Type support
hooks.why: All Yang Zing monsters are Wyrm-Type, and the Synchro monsters ask for Wyrm materials, so cards that support Wyrms help the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Wyrm to GY
hooks.why: Filling the Graveyard with Wyrms sets up Yang Zing Path, Chiwen's revival and Baxia's revival, so cards that send a Wyrm from the Deck to the GY are valuable.

hooks.label: Special Summons a Wyrm
hooks.why: The deck needs Wyrms on the field to Synchro Summon, especially during the opponent's turn with the Quick Synchro effects, so cards that Special Summon Wyrms from the Deck or GY are useful.

hooks.label: Reacts to being destroyed
hooks.why: The deck destroys its own cards with Yazi, Baxia and Yang Zing Brutality, so outside monsters that trigger when destroyed will get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Zefra support
hooks.why: Zefraniu and Zefraxi search 'Yang Zing' or 'Zefra' Spells/Traps and can be used with Zefra monsters, so any card that mentions Zefra works with the deck's Pendulum half.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck that summons Level 8 Spellcaster and Warrior Ritual Monsters with "Light and Darkness Ritual", paying with Tributes from hand/field or by banishing monsters from the GY, while Quick-Play Spells and Continuous Traps dig through the Deck for the pieces.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: The deck exists to Ritual Summon its Level 8 Ritual Monsters with "Light and Darkness Ritual", so any outside card that adds a Ritual Monster or Ritual Spell from the Deck starts the engine.

hooks.label: Monsters that pay when Tributed
hooks.why: "Light and Darkness Ritual" Tributes monsters from your hand or field as Ritual material, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed turn that cost into cards.

hooks.label: Reacts to being discarded
hooks.why: Celtic Mystic discards 2 cards and Mind Shuffle discards 1, so outside cards that do something when they are discarded get thrown away as free fuel.

hooks.label: Ritual material from the GY
hooks.why: "Light and Darkness Ritual" banishes monsters from your GY as Ritual material, so Ritual material that banishes itself from the GY for a Ritual Summon is extra ammunition.

profile.plan: An Xyz toolbox that summons 'Super Quantum' monsters of different Attributes and Levels, uses them to Xyz Summon 'Super Quantal Mech Beast' monsters with matching Attributes, and stacks materials to build a protected Great Magnus.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Magnacarrier, Black Layer and Green Layer all discard cards as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when discarded turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Triggers when detached as material
hooks.why: Magnaformation can attach any face-up monster to a 'Super Quant' Xyz Monster, and the Mech Beasts detach materials for their effects, so outside monsters that reward being detached get value.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every 'Super Quantal Mech Beast' Xyz Monster is a Machine, so cards that boost or revive Machines work on the deck's entire Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Red Layer, Blue Layer, Green Layer and White Layer all trigger when Normal Summoned, so an extra Normal Summon lets you resolve two of those effects in one turn.

profile.plan: A Rank 3 (and Rank 6) Xyz deck whose monsters Special Summon themselves from the hand or GY by detaching Xyz Material from either field, then steal the opponent's monsters and Spells/Traps as material for the Goblin Xyz.

hooks.label: Xyz Material generators
hooks.why: Goblin Biker Big Gabonga, Goblin Bikers Gone Bonkers and Goblin Biker Grand Pileup all win by piling material onto a Goblin Xyz, and the self-summoning Goblin Bikers pay by detaching that material, so anything that attaches Xyz Material keeps the engine running.

hooks.label: Monsters that want detaching
hooks.why: Goblin Biker Boom Mach, Clatter Sploder and Mean Merciless detach Xyz Material from a monster on either field as their Summoning cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are detached as material get used for free.

hooks.label: Level 3 self-summoners
hooks.why: The whole Goblin Biker core is Level 3, Xyz Summoning into Goblin Biker Troika Griare and Goblin Biker Big Gabonga, so Level 3 monsters that Special Summon themselves supply extra Rank 3 material.

hooks.label: Level 6 self-summoners
hooks.why: Goblin Bikers Gone Wild is a Level 6 that Normal Summons itself without Tributing and leads into Goblin Bikers Gone Bonkers and Goblin's Crazy Beast, so Level 6 monsters that Special Summon themselves enable the Rank 6 plays.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Goblin Biker Grand Breakout Tributes 1 monster to Special Summon a Goblin monster from the Deck, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Goblin Biker Grand Bash grants an extra Normal Summon of a Goblin each turn, and Dugg Charger, Clatter Sploder, Mean Merciless and Gogogo Goblindbergh all trigger on being Normal Summoned, so outside effects that give more Normal Summons keep the chain going.

profile.plan: Spams free Special Summons while you control an Adventurer Token, then leans on the deck's Field Spells and self-re-equipping Equip Spells to swing with a 2000 ATK token and burn or draw off its battles.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Water Enchantress of the Temple places a Field Spell from the Deck, and Forest of Lost Flowers and Zaralaam the Dark Palace each add another Field Spell from the Deck or GY, so any card that finds a Field Spell keeps that loop going.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: Dunnell, the Noble Arms of Light and Starlit Papillon only pay off while equipped, and Thunder Discharge and Breath of Resurrection already fetch them from the hand or GY, so effects that add Equip Spells are extra copies of the deck's key pieces.

hooks.label: Sends Equip Spells to the GY
hooks.why: Starlit Papillon and Dunnell, the Noble Arms of Light equip themselves to an Adventurer Token when they are sent to the GY, so effects that send Equip Spells from the Deck to the GY put them straight onto the field.

hooks.label: Monsters that like Equip Cards
hooks.why: Starlit Papillon, Dunnell, the Noble Arms of Light and the deck's Traps equip to any monster you control, so outside monsters whose own effects reward being equipped get their bonuses for free.

hooks.label: Extra attacks and piercing
hooks.why: Forest of Lost Flowers draws and Zaralaam the Dark Palace burns whenever your Adventurer Token destroys a monster by battle, so effects that let that 2000 ATK token attack again or punch through Defense Position monsters convert those triggers.

profile.plan: A Flip deck that sets its monsters face-down to Special Summon Subterror Behemoths from the hand, then flips them face-up for removal and control, using The Hidden City to search and re-flip.

hooks.label: Flip monster searcher
hooks.why: Subterror Guru and Subterror Behemoth Fiendess add Flip monsters from the Deck, so outside cards that search Flip monsters give the deck more ways to start.

hooks.label: Flip monster reviver
hooks.why: Subterror Behemoth Fiendess and Subterror Fiendess Special Summon Flip monsters from the hand or GY, so outside cards that revive Flip monsters extend the deck's plays.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Subterror monster is EARTH, so cards that search, revive or boost EARTH monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-down
hooks.why: The Subterror Behemoth monsters Special Summon themselves from the hand when a face-up monster you control is flipped face-down, so outside cards that flip your own monsters face-down trigger that condition.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-up
hooks.why: The deck relies on Flip effects and Subterror Behemoth Fiendess adds a Flip monster when a monster it points to is flipped face-up, so outside cards that flip your Set monsters face-up trigger those effects.

hooks.label: Benefits from being Tributed
hooks.why: Subterror Nemesis Warrior Tributes itself and other monsters to Special Summon a Subterror from the GY, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get that effect for free.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Level 3 Neo-Spacian monsters with different names and attributes that Contact Fuse with Elemental HERO Neos, then bounce back to the Extra Deck so the deck can reassemble the pieces and fuse again.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon support
hooks.why: Contact Gate locks the turn's Extra Deck Summons to Fusion Monsters and the archetype's payoffs (Neo-Spacian Marine Dolphin, Twinkle Moss, the Neos Contact Fusions) are all Fusion Monsters, so anything that Fusion Summons or supports it advances the plan.

hooks.label: Payoff when discarded
hooks.why: Neo-Spacian Aqua Dolphin and Marine Dolphin discard 1 card as the cost of their hand-peeking effect, so outside monsters that trigger when discarded get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Payoff when sent to GY
hooks.why: Cross Porter sends 1 monster you control to the Graveyard to Special Summon a Neo-Spacian from the hand, so outside monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Elemental HERO Neos partners
hooks.why: Contact Gate and every Contact Fusion the deck makes require a face-up Fusion Monster listing 'Elemental HERO Neos' as material, so cards that search, revive or protect that material are the deck's engine.

hooks.label: Normal Monster summoners
hooks.why: The Fusion material 'Elemental HERO Neos' is a Normal Monster, so cards that Special Summon a Normal Monster from the hand, Deck or Graveyard put the required material on the field.

profile.plan: A WATER deck that discards its own monsters to Special Summon Mermail bosses and trigger Graveyard effects, then Xyz Summons Rank 3 and 7 monsters.

hooks.label: WATER GY triggers
hooks.why: The deck discards and sends WATER monsters to the GY as cost, so WATER monsters with effects when sent there get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Mills WATER monsters
hooks.why: The deck wants WATER monsters in the GY to fuel its revival and Level-boost effects, so cards that send WATER from the Deck to the GY set them up.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is WATER, so cards that search, revive or boost WATER monsters help the whole strategy.

hooks.label: Aqua/Fish/Sea Serpent support
hooks.why: The deck's monsters are Aqua, Fish or Sea Serpent, so support for these Types works on the whole archetype.

hooks.label: Level 7 support
hooks.why: The deck has four Level 7 monsters that can be Special Summoned from hand, so cards that support Level 7 monsters (like Sacred Sword of Seven Stars) help.

profile.plan: A Legendary Dragon deck: The Fang of Critias sends a Trap and The Claw of Hermos sends a monster to the GY to fuse out their signature Dragons, or Legend of Heart Tributes a Warrior and banishes Legendary Dragon Spells to field the three Legendary Knights and unite them into Timaeus the Knight of Destiny.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Legend of Heart Tributes 1 Warrior monster to Special Summon the Legendary Knights, and Rocket Hermos Cannon and Goddess Bow need a Warrior as the material The Claw of Hermos sends.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Time Magic Hammer is made by sending a Spellcaster with The Claw of Hermos, and Timaeus the United Dragon needs a Spellcaster in hand or on the field to Special Summon itself and as Fusion material.

hooks.label: Mentions Dark Magician
hooks.why: Timaeus the United Dragon Special Summons itself by sending 1 Spell/Trap that mentions "Dark Magician" from your hand or face-up field to the GY.

hooks.label: Monsters that want the GY
hooks.why: The Claw of Hermos sends a Warrior or Spellcaster monster from your hand or field to the GY as the cost of its Summon, so monsters with an effect when they are sent there get used for free.

profile.plan: A Fiend/DARK deck of 0-ATK Yubel forms that cannot be destroyed by battle and reflect the attacker's ATK as damage, chaining into bigger forms when destroyed while paying an End Phase Tribute every turn.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Yubel must Tribute 1 other monster during every End Phase or destroy itself, so a steady supply of Tokens keeps the whole chain alive.

hooks.label: Monsters that pay you back when Tributed
hooks.why: Yubel's End Phase upkeep Tributes 1 other monster every turn, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Monsters that float when destroyed
hooks.why: Yubel - Terror Incarnate destroys all other monsters on the field during your End Phase and Yubel forms replace themselves when destroyed, so outside monsters that search or Special Summon themselves when destroyed get used for free.

hooks.label: Fiend and DARK support
hooks.why: Every Yubel monster is a Fiend and DARK, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends or DARK monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Forces the opponent to attack
hooks.why: Yubel and its forms take no battle damage and reflect the attacker's ATK back, and Spirit of Yubel can Special Summon itself from the hand when the opponent declares an attack, so making the opponent swing is pure profit.

hooks.label: Fusion using the opponent's field
hooks.why: Yubel - The Loving Defender Forever is Fusion Summoned with 1+ Effect Monsters on the field, so cards that let you fuse away monsters from either side turn the opponent's board into your Level 12 boss.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster deck of Level 4 and 5 Pendulum and effect monsters that Special Summon themselves, dodge self-inflicted effect damage, and stack into Rank 4 and Rank 5 Xyz, with Plushfire, Fire Dancer and Water Dancer rewarding being destroyed.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Performage monster, including Trapeze Magician, Trapeze High Magician and Trapeze Witch, is a Spellcaster, so cards that search, revive or boost Spellcasters lift the whole deck.

hooks.label: Pendulum Summon support
hooks.why: Ball Balancer, Wind Drainer, Plushfire, Fire Dancer, Water Dancer, Mirror Conductor and Cup Tricker are Pendulum monsters, and the deck wants to Pendulum Summon them back from the face-up Extra Deck for Xyz material.

hooks.label: Payoff for taking damage
hooks.why: Trick Clown deals 1000 to you, Plushfire 500, Mirror Conductor 500 and Flame Eater 500, so outside cards that trigger when you take effect damage are switched on by the deck itself.

hooks.label: Destroy your own Spellcaster
hooks.why: Plushfire, Fire Dancer and Water Dancer all Special Summon or weaken the opponent when they are destroyed by battle or card effect, and Ball Balancer already destroys a Performage itself, so outside cards that destroy your own Level 4 Spellcasters are live.

hooks.label: Fills your Graveyard
hooks.why: Trick Clown Special Summons when it is sent to the GY, Shadow Maker sends a Performage from the Deck, and Damage Juggler, Stilts Launcher and Trick Box all use the GY, so outside cards that send Spellcasters from the Deck to the GY set all of that up.

profile.plan: A Link-climbing deck that uses its three low-Level Normal Monsters as Link Material and turns every World Chalice monster sent from the field to the GY into a revival from the hand, building up Imduk, Auram, Ib and Ningirsu.

hooks.label: Normal Monster revival
hooks.why: The archetype's Normal Monsters are its Link Material and Guardragon's GY revival targets, so cards that Special Summon Normal Monsters from the Deck or GY keep Imduk and Ib the Justiciar supplied.

hooks.label: Sends your field to GY
hooks.why: Imduk, Ningirsu, Ib the Priestess and Auram all Special Summon a World Chalice monster from your hand when they are sent from the field to the GY, so outside cards that Tribute or send your own monsters off the field turn into free bodies.

hooks.label: Triggers when sent to GY
hooks.why: The deck Link Summons constantly, sending its own monsters to the GY as Link Material, so outside monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Linked monster support
hooks.why: Guardragon negates effects that target your linked monster, Ib the Priestess protects itself while linked, Auram and World Legacy's Heart revive and protect Link Monsters that point to others, so cards that care about being linked fit the deck.

profile.plan: A deck of Level 10 Fairies that Normal Summon themselves for free while your field is empty, survive every battle untouched, then fire huge end-of-Battle-Phase payoffs (halving LP, burning, shuffling the opponent's field away) before shuffling themselves back into the Deck.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every card in the deck is a Fairy, and Sephylon, the Ultimate Timelord Special Summons a Level 8 or higher Fairy from your hand or GY, so any Fairy searcher, reviver or booster hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 10 support
hooks.why: Empty Machine's discard cost wants a Level 10 monster, every Timelord is Level 10, and cards that protect or rank up Level 10 monsters keep the deck's Normal Summoned bodies alive or turn two of them into a Rank 10.

hooks.label: Forces the opponent to attack
hooks.why: Michion, Sandaion, Metaion, Kamion and the rest only trigger 'at the end of the Battle Phase, if this card battled', so cards that drag the opponent's monsters into attacking your Timelords give you a second round of those effects each turn.

hooks.label: Makes the opponent draw
hooks.why: Lazion, the Timelord inflicts 1000 damage every time your opponent draws a card, and Gabrion, the Timelord already forces the opponent to draw when it shuffles their cards away, so extra forced draws become burn.

hooks.label: Cards that pay LP
hooks.why: Hailon, the Timelord inflicts damage equal to the LP difference only while your LP is lower, and Sadion, the Timelord resets your LP to 4000 only below 4000, so any card that pays LP as a cost charges both payoffs.

profile.plan: A Synchro-climb deck of WIND (and a few DARK) Dragon Synchro Monsters that negate and destroy the opponent's effects and gain the destroyed monster's ATK, built out of Tuners, Tuner Synchro Monsters and Pendulum materials.

hooks.label: Speedroid cards
hooks.why: Clear Wing Fast Dragon's Pendulum effect requires a face-up 'Speedroid' Tuner to be sent to the GY, and Clear Wing Synchro Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons is always treated as a 'Speedroid' card.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Almost every Clear Wing Synchro Monster is WIND, Crystal Clear Wing Synchro Dragon searches a WIND monster when it leaves the field, and Speedroid Clear Wing Wonder counts the different Types among your WIND Synchro Monsters.

profile.plan: Jinzo shuts off every Trap Card and Trap effect on the field, then beats down with self-Summoning Machine/DARK monsters, Rank 6 Xyz plays and Trap-destruction burn while the opponent's back row is dead.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Jinzo monster is a Machine, Psychic Wave needs a Machine you control, Cosmos Channelling Summons Machine monsters from hand or GY and Everlasting Alloy protects only your Machine monsters.

hooks.label: Takes control of monsters
hooks.why: Cosmos Channelling sends a monster you control that is owned by your opponent to the GY to Special Summon a Machine, and Jinzo - Layered takes control of an opponent's monster, so effects that steal monsters are fuel.

hooks.label: Level 6 self-Summoners
hooks.why: Jinzo - Layered is a Rank 6 Xyz that needs two Level 6 monsters, and Jinzo, Psychic Megacyber and Jinzo the Machine Menace (as Level 6) are all Level 6, so more easily Summoned Level 6 monsters extend into it.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Jinzo - Jector, Jinzo the Machine Menace, Psychic Megacyber and Jinzo - Layered all Tribute monsters as a cost, so outside monsters that do something when Tributed get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Puts Traps in the GY
hooks.why: Jinzo the Machine Menace Special Summons itself while a Trap is face-up on the field or in either GY, and Jinzo - Layered, Jector and Jinzo - Lord all read Traps, so a Trap sent to the GY turns those on.

hooks.label: Mills Machine monsters
hooks.why: Cosmos Channelling Special Summons a Machine monster from your hand or GY and Psychic Wave recovers a Machine from your GY, so effects that send Machine monsters to the GY feed both.

profile.plan: A Zombie/DARK Level 6 deck built on the Continuous Trap 'Call of the Haunted': it Sets and reuses that Trap to revive its monsters from the GY, its monsters get effects when Special Summoned, and it tops out on a Rank 6 Zombie Xyz that returns cards to the hand.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck monster is a Zombie and the Xyz asks for 2 Level 6 Zombie monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Zombies serve the whole deck.

hooks.label: Cards that like being discarded
hooks.why: Pumpking the King of Grave Ghosts discards 1 card to Set a 'Call of the Haunted', so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Zombies that work from the GY
hooks.why: Call of the Haunted revives a monster from the GY in Attack Position and the Rank 6 Xyz detaches its Zombie materials, so outside Zombies with an effect when sent to the GY get used a second time.

hooks.label: Continuous Trap set-up
hooks.why: The whole engine needs 'Call of the Haunted' on the field and Call of the Forgotten exists to Set up to 3 of them from the Deck and GY, so outside cards that fetch or Set Continuous Traps do the same job.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck of Level 6 Spellcasters and Fiends that Special Summon themselves into the center Main Monster Zone, then climb into Level 7 and Level 10 'Elfnote' Synchro Monsters while loading the field with its own Continuous Spells and Traps.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Lucina, Tinia, Fortuna and Regina are all Spellcasters, and Elfnote June Pride's material is '1 Tuner + 1 non-Tuner Spellcaster monster', so any card that searches, revives or boosts Spellcasters works on the whole main deck.

hooks.label: Monsters with GY triggers
hooks.why: Elfnotes: Welcome Home and Elfnotes: Rhapsodia of Madness send a monster from your hand or field to the GY as their cost, and Elfnote Regina does the same, so outside monsters that do something when sent to the GY are free value.

hooks.label: Synchro Material payoffs
hooks.why: Elfnote Power Patron and Elfnote Regina both trigger when they are sent to the GY as Synchro Material, so any outside Tuner or material with that same trigger extends the deck's Synchro engine.

hooks.label: Spell/Trap GY triggers
hooks.why: Elfnotes: Quatrain of Succession sends another Spell/Trap from your hand or field to the GY as cost, so outside Spells and Traps that do something when they hit the GY are free fuel for its Token.

profile.plan: Fills the Graveyard with Skull Servant names to power up King of the Skull Servants, then revives it and protects it with The Lady in Wight.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Wightprince triggers when sent to the GY, and King of the Skull Servants' ATK depends on the number of 'Skull Servant' and 'King of the Skull Servants' in the GY, so any card that sends a Zombie from the Deck to the GY advances the deck.

hooks.label: Discards your own Zombies
hooks.why: Wightprince triggers when sent to the GY from the hand, so outside discard outlets that target Zombies can trigger its effect and start the engine.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is a Zombie, so cards that search, revive, or mill Zombies work with the whole deck.

hooks.label: Returns banished Zombies to GY
hooks.why: King of the Skull Servants banishes Skull Servants from the GY to revive itself, and Wightmare returns banished Skull Servants to the GY, so effects that refill the GY from the banished pile are valuable.

hooks.label: Special Summons banished Zombies
hooks.why: Wightmare can Special Summon banished 'The Lady in Wight' or 'King of the Skull Servants', so outside effects that Special Summon banished Zombies provide similar recovery.

profile.plan: A Level-4 stun-beatdown deck whose 1900-ATK monsters survive each End Phase by feeding a specific Normal Spell from the hand to the GY (or revealing a matching monster), Tributing themselves for Quick-Effect negations while locking down LIGHT, DARK and Special Summoned monsters.

hooks.label: Rock monster support
hooks.why: Guardian, Overload, Sandman, Wall and Boulder are all Rock-Type and their End Phase upkeep is paid by revealing a Rock monster in the hand, while Supplier Special Summons itself when a face-up Rock you control is sent to the GY, so cards that search or revive Rocks keep the whole suite alive.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Rooklord and Valafar can each be Tribute Summoned with a single Koa'ki Meiru monster, and Guardian, Overload, Sandman and Wall Tribute themselves for their Quick Effects, so cards that grant extra Normal Summons or reward Tribute Summoning fit the deck.

hooks.label: LIGHT and DARK lockdown
hooks.why: Drago stops both players Special Summoning LIGHT and DARK monsters, while Doom, Powerhand and Beetle negate, disable or reposition LIGHT and DARK monsters, so outside cards that shut those Attributes down extend the same anti-meta plan.

hooks.label: Special Summon punisher
hooks.why: Ice and Tornado destroy Special Summoned monsters and Automatic Laser destroys anything the opponent summons with 1000 or more ATK, so outside cards that destroy or stop Special Summoned monsters pile onto the same stun plan.

hooks.label: Level 3 or lower GY triggers
hooks.why: Gravirose sends a Level 3 or lower monster from your Deck to the GY every Standby Phase, so outside low-Level monsters that do something when sent to the GY are pure profit.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck that summons LIGHT Fairy Ritual Monsters with Machine Angel Ritual, using on-Tribute effects and GY manipulation to gain advantage.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: The deck needs its Ritual Spells to summon its monsters, and Idaten searches a Ritual Spell when Ritual Summoned, so any card that adds a Ritual Spell or Ritual Monster to hand is valuable.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fairy support
hooks.why: All Cyber Angel Ritual Monsters are LIGHT Fairy, Benten adds a LIGHT Fairy from Deck when Tributed, and Magnificent Machine Angel targets a LIGHT Fairy, so cards that support that Type and Attribute bolster the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Fairy or Warrior to GY
hooks.why: Machine Angel Absolute Ritual can shuffle Fairy or Warrior monsters from the GY as Ritual material, so outside cards that send those Types from the Deck to the GY enable larger Ritual Summons.

hooks.label: Tributing your own monsters
hooks.why: Benten and Idaten have effects when they are Tributed, and the deck's own Spells Tribute them as cost, so outside cards that Tribute a monster you control can trigger those effects.

profile.plan: FIRE Dragon monsters that Synchro Summon from their own bodies during the Battle Phase, so the deck attacks first and turns each battle into a bigger Synchro body.

hooks.label: FIRE Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Tenpai Dragon monster is a FIRE Dragon, and Genroku locks you into Dragon Special Summons for the rest of the turn once it resolves.

hooks.label: FIRE Dragon searchers
hooks.why: Genroku Special Summons itself as a Tuner the moment it is added to your hand by a card effect, so any effect that adds a FIRE Dragon monster is a free body.

hooks.label: Synchro Summon payoffs
hooks.why: Three of the four monsters Synchro Summon with a Quick Effect in the Battle Phase, so the deck can Synchro Summon several times in a single turn.

profile.plan: A Synchro toolbox that uses Fleuret de Fleur to revive low-Level Tuners, Sauge de Fleur to search Level 1 Plant monsters, and Baronne de Fleur as a Level 10 Synchro boss with negation and revival.

hooks.label: Destruction triggers
hooks.why: Sauge de Fleur destroys a monster you control to Special Summon itself from your hand, so monsters with effects when destroyed give extra value.

hooks.label: Revival targets
hooks.why: Baronne de Fleur can return itself to the Extra Deck to Special Summon a Level 9 or lower monster from your GY, so monsters with effects when Special Summoned get a free trigger.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: Fleuret de Fleur is an Equip Spell that can re-equip itself to a Synchro Monster, so cards that add Equip Spells help assemble the combo.

profile.plan: A HERO deck that uses the 'Mask Change' Quick-Play Spells to morph its monsters into Masked HERO Fusion bosses, matching Attribute and Level to pick the right form for the situation.

hooks.label: HERO monsters of all Attributes
hooks.why: Mask Change and Mask Change II need a 'HERO' monster on the field with the right Attribute and a low enough Level, so outside HERO cards supply the Attributes the Extra Deck asks for.

hooks.label: Discard payoff monsters
hooks.why: Mask Change II discards 1 card as its cost, so outside monsters that do something when discarded give the deck a free effect every time it morphs into a Masked HERO.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Masked HERO is a Warrior, so Type-wide searching, revival and ATK boosts apply to the whole Extra Deck the deck is built around.

hooks.label: Extra attacks and piercing
hooks.why: Anki, Dian and Divine Wind only trigger when they destroy an opponent's monster by battle, so cards that let a Warrior attack again or pierce Defense Position monsters turn those payoffs on.

hooks.label: HERO Fusion monsters
hooks.why: Form Change swaps a 'HERO' Fusion Monster you control for a Masked HERO of the same Level, so outside HERO Fusions of Level 6 or 8 are the natural swap targets.

profile.plan: A Plant and Dragon Synchro deck that climbs into Black Rose Dragon and its variants with Plant Tuners, shifts Levels, recycles Plants from the Graveyard, and nukes the field with Black Rose Dragon and Ruddy Rose Dragon.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Rage Rose Witch makes every Plant monster you control indestructible by card effects, Twilight Rose Black Knight gives Plants 1000 ATK and shifts their Levels, and Black Rose Garden turns every face-up monster on the field into a Plant.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Bramble Rose Dragon, Ruddy Rose Dragon, Ruddy Rose Witch and Rose Shaman all Tribute themselves as a cost, and Rose Papillon hands you an extra Level 7 or higher Tribute Summon, so outside monsters that pay off when Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Easy Level 7+ Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Rose Papillon lets you Tribute Summon one Level 7 or higher monster in Attack Position in addition to your Normal Summon or Set, so big monsters that Tribute Summon themselves slot straight in.

profile.plan: A Beast-Warrior/FIRE toolbox that Sets "Fire Formation" Continuous Spells and Traps from the Deck and turns them into searches, Special Summons and Rank 3/4, Synchro, Fusion and Link plays.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: All 29 cards are Beast-Warrior, and Tiger King, Swan, Eagle and Peacock only work with Beast-Warrior or FIRE bodies, so Type support advances the whole deck.

hooks.label: Revives Beast-Warriors from the GY
hooks.why: Lion Emperor adds a FIRE monster from the Graveyard, Spirit revives a Level 3 FIRE monster and Dragon revives a "Fire Fist" monster, so outside cards that Special Summon Beast-Warrior or FIRE monsters from the GY extend the same resource loop.

profile.plan: A combo deck that blows up its own DoomZ cards to search, Set and Special Summon, keeps an Equip Card on its monsters so they can Xyz Summon WIND Machine Xyz Monsters using their Level as Rank, and grinds the opponent down with those Xyz.

hooks.label: Machine and WIND support
hooks.why: Every DoomZ Xyz Monster is a WIND Machine and DoomZ Command "D.O.O.M.D.U.R.G." only grants its effects to a WIND Machine Xyz Monster, so support that names Machine or WIND boosts the whole end board.

hooks.label: Equip Spells that recur
hooks.why: Amalthe, Elara and Drastea only get their Quick Effect Xyz Summon while equipped with an Equip Card, and DoomZ Command "A.D.R.A.S.T.E.I.A." shows the payoff of re-equipping itself from the GY.

hooks.label: Floats when destroyed by effect
hooks.why: Jupredo's Pendulum effect, DoomZ Raiders, DoomZ Break - Diactorus and DoomZ XIII Over - Graflareio all destroy cards on your own field, so an outside card with an effect when it is destroyed by card effect gets that trigger for free.

hooks.label: Destroys your own cards
hooks.why: DoomZ V Five - Amalthe and DoomZ VII Seven - Elara search or Set whenever they are destroyed by card effect, and DoomZ Raiders, Drastea and Power Patron DoomZ are all built around having your own cards blown up.

profile.plan: A Trap-monster control deck: its Continuous Traps Special Summon themselves as LIGHT Zombie Normal Monsters, it grinds into Eldlich the Golden Lord and Eldlixir Spell/Traps, and it fuses Zombies into Level-10 boss monsters.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Golden Land card is a Zombie or is summoned by Tributing/Fusing Zombies, so generic Zombie search, revival and boosts work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Zombies that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Golden Land Forever! and Fallen Angel of the Golden Land both pay by Tributing a Zombie, so Zombies with an effect when they are Tributed give value for the cost.

hooks.label: Eldlixir Spell/Traps
hooks.why: Each Golden Land Trap banishes itself from the GY in the End Phase to Set an Eldlixir Spell/Trap straight from the Deck, so those cards are the deck's second engine.

profile.plan: A Fairy deck that leans on The Sanctuary in the Sky to switch on free Special Summons, searches and Quick Effects, filling the GY with Fairies to banish for Master Hyperion's destruction while keeping a Life Point lead.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Fairy (Earth, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus, Pluto), so cards that search, revive, boost or protect Fairies work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Mills LIGHT Fairies
hooks.why: Uranus sends one of the deck's monsters from the Deck to the GY to change its own Level, and Master Hyperion, Jupiter and Pluto all banish LIGHT Fairies out of the GY as cost, so extra ways to load the GY with LIGHT Fairies fuel every one of them.

hooks.label: Places a Field Spell
hooks.why: Uranus's free Special Summon, Earth's search for Master Hyperion, Hyperion's second destruction, Jupiter's revival, Pluto's Quick Effect and Saturn's burn all switch on only while the deck's Field Spell is face-up on the field or in the GY, so any extra way to put it there is live.

hooks.label: Fairies that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Protector of The Agents - Moon Tributes a Fairy monster as cost to destroy an opponent's card and Saturn Tributes itself to burn, so outside Fairy monsters with an effect when they are Tributed trigger for free.

hooks.label: Monsters that profit from being banished
hooks.why: Pluto banishes any monster from the GY as cost on every one of its turns, and Hyperion and Jupiter banish Fairies from the GY, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished are used for free.

hooks.label: Life Point gain
hooks.why: The Agent of Force - Mars gains ATK and DEF equal to the Life Point gap and Judgment - Saturn burns for that gap, while Creation - Venus and Destruction - Venus pay LP, so cards that gain you Life Points keep both payoffs online.

profile.plan: A FIRE Dinosaur beatdown-Synchro deck that swarms Dinosaurs, wins battles to trigger search-and-Summon effects, and turns a loaded Graveyard into Synchro Summons and boss Summons.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every Jurrac monster is a FIRE Dinosaur and the Extra Deck Synchros ask for Dinosaur materials, so cards that search, revive or boost Dinosaurs work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Floating Dinosaur monsters
hooks.why: Jurrac Stego destroys a card you control to send a Dinosaur to the GY and Jurrac Volcano destroys a Dinosaur you control to Special Summon from the Deck, so a Dinosaur that replaces itself when destroyed is free material.

hooks.label: Dinosaurs that return when banished
hooks.why: Jurrac Astero banishes 2 Dinosaurs from the Graveyard to negate a Summon, Jurrac Volcano banishes one to protect its monsters and Jurrac Titano banishes one for ATK, so Dinosaurs that trigger or revive when banished pay those costs by themselves.

hooks.label: Mills Dinosaurs into the GY
hooks.why: Jurrac Giganoto grows with Jurracs in the Graveyard while Astero, Volcano and Titano banish Dinosaurs from it, so effects that send Dinosaurs from the Deck to the Graveyard feed every one of those.

profile.plan: A Pendulum Fusion deck of Psychic FIRE monsters that destroys its own cards to Set Metalfoes Spells/Traps, triggers 'when destroyed' effects, and Fusion Summons using Pendulum Monsters from the hand, field and Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monsters that activate when destroyed
hooks.why: Metalfoes Pendulum Effects destroy a face-up card you control to Set a Metalfoes Spell/Trap, and Raremetalfoes Bismugear and Parametalfoes Melcaster reward being destroyed, so an outside Pendulum Monster that replaces itself when destroyed is a perfect target.

hooks.label: Fusion Monsters that activate when sent to the GY
hooks.why: Metalfoes Mithrilium and Metalfoes Orichalc trigger when sent from the field to the GY, and Metalfoes Fusion Summons send materials there, so outside Fusion Monsters with GY effects provide extra value.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Metalfoes monster is Psychic, so cards that search, revive or boost Psychic monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Metalfoes monster is FIRE, and Metamorformation boosts their ATK/DEF, so generic FIRE support fits.

hooks.label: Cards that destroy your own Pendulum Zone cards
hooks.why: Every Metalfoes Pendulum Effect targets another face-up card you control to destroy, and destroying a card in your Pendulum Zone triggers Heavymetalfoes Electrumite's draw effect.

profile.plan: A control deck that uses King's Sarcophagus to Special Summon Level 8 Horus monsters from the GY, triggers their effects when the opponent removes your other cards, and sends cards from hand to the GY as cost.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when sent to GY
hooks.why: Imsety, King's Sarcophagus and Horus the Black Flame Deity send cards from your hand (and field) to the GY as cost, so monsters with effects that trigger when they are sent to the GY get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Sends monsters from Deck to GY
hooks.why: The Horus monsters can Special Summon themselves from the GY while you control King's Sarcophagus, so any card that sends them from the Deck to the GY sets up a free Special Summon.

hooks.label: Searches Continuous Spells
hooks.why: The whole deck depends on King's Sarcophagus, a Continuous Spell, so cards that add a Continuous Spell from the Deck to your hand help find it.

hooks.label: Discards a Level 8 monster
hooks.why: All Horus monsters are Level 8, so cards that discard a Level 8 monster as cost (like Trade-In) have plenty of fodder.

hooks.label: Special Summons Tokens
hooks.why: The Horus monsters trigger when another card you control leaves the field by an opponent's card effect, so Tokens are ideal fodder for the opponent's removal.

profile.plan: A WATER/Aqua deck of Flip and face-down Defense Position monsters that keeps bouncing the opponent's cards to the hand and grinds them down behind the Level 6 Synchro Penguin Brave.

hooks.label: Face-down Defense Position Summoners
hooks.why: Penguin Soldier, Penguin Ninja and Glacial Beast Polar Penguin only fire once they are flipped up, and Penguin Brave adds a Penguin from the Deck in face-down Defense Position, so more face-down bodies mean more triggers.

hooks.label: Flips your Set monsters up
hooks.why: Penguin Soldier and Nightmare Penguin trigger when flipped face-up, and Penguin Brave's Quick Effect flips a face-down WATER monster face-up, so outside cards that flip your Set monsters speed the whole engine up.

hooks.label: Discard payoffs
hooks.why: Royal Penguins Garden discards 1 card every Main Phase and First Penguin discards as a cost, so monsters that do something when discarded get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Aqua and WATER support
hooks.why: Every Penguin monster is WATER and most are Aqua, so anything that searches, revives or boosts Aqua or WATER monsters works on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A control-burn deck that uses Vijam the Cubic Seed as a recurring wall, places Cubic Counters to negate effects and prevent attacks, and then Special Summons Level 10 Fiends like Crimson Nova to deal massive damage and halve the opponent's LP.

hooks.label: Level 1 Fiend support
hooks.why: Vijam the Cubic Seed is a Level 1 Fiend that the deck sends to the GY to boost ATK and revives for Cubic Counters, so cards that search, Summon or dump a Level 1 Fiend are extra copies.

hooks.label: Discard fodder
hooks.why: Pritima the Infinity Cubic Vessel and Cubic Bodhi both discard a card as cost, so outside cards with an effect when discarded turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Prevents effect damage
hooks.why: Crimson Nova the Dark Cubic Lord makes you take 3000 damage each End Phase, so outside cards that prevent effect damage keep you alive while it burns the opponent.

hooks.label: Forces opponent to attack
hooks.why: Cubic Ascension and Cubic Rebirth both trigger when the opponent declares an attack, so outside cards that force attacks turn those traps into Special Summons and counter placement.

hooks.label: Discards a Level 10
hooks.why: Crimson Nova the Dark Cubic Lord is a Level 10 monster you want to draw into to Special Summon, so outside cards that discard a Level 10 to draw help you dig through the deck.

profile.plan: A defensive Aqua/WATER deck that hides behind high-DEF Trap monsters and Slime Tokens, steering the opponent's attacks into a Revival Jam that keeps coming back.

hooks.label: Aqua and WATER support
hooks.why: Every card in the archetype is an Aqua/WATER monster, from Change Slime and Gruesome Goo up to Egyptian God Slime, so Aqua and WATER support reaches the entire deck.

hooks.label: Continuous Trap support
hooks.why: Metal Reflect Slime and Egyptian God Slime are Continuous Traps that Special Summon themselves as Level 10 monsters, so effects that search, Set or recover Continuous Traps keep the deck's walls coming.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 10 monsters
hooks.why: Metal Reflect Slime and Egyptian God Slime both land on the field as Level 10 monsters, so extra Level 10 monsters that put themselves into play become Rank 10 Xyz material.

hooks.label: Sun God cards
hooks.why: Egyptian God Slime, Protector of the Sun God adds a "Sun God" card from the Deck when it is Special Summoned, so the whole Sun God package is fetchable off the deck's best wall.

hooks.label: Gemini support
hooks.why: Magical Reflect Slime only gains its battle-damage redirection after a second Normal Summon, so Gemini support that grants that Summon or protects Gemini monsters is live.

profile.plan: A combo deck that gathers Queen's, King's and Jack's Knight to Fusion Summon Arcana Knight Joker or Special Summon Arcana Triumph Joker, recycling the Knights through the Graveyard every End Phase.

hooks.label: LIGHT Warrior support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a LIGHT Warrior, and Joker's Straight locks the Extra Deck to LIGHT Warrior monsters, so Warrior/LIGHT support applies to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Summons Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Queen's Knight and Jack's Knight are Normal Monsters, so outside cards that Special Summon Normal Monsters from the Deck or Graveyard assemble Fusion materials without spending the Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Joker's Straight discards 1 card to start the combo and Arcana Triumph Joker discards 1 card to blow up the opponent's field, so outside cards that pay you back when discarded get that value for free.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Jack's Knight is a Level 5 Normal Monster and Thunderspeed Summon Normal Summons a Level 10 monster, so outside cards that feed or enable Tribute Summons get those bodies out without eating the deck's summons.

hooks.label: Fusion Spell access
hooks.why: Arcana Knight Joker is a Fusion of the three Knights but the archetype has no Fusion Spell of its own, so outside cards that Fusion Summon or fetch Polymerization are what actually complete the boss.

profile.plan: Mills both players' Decks to trigger effects that send cards from hand or Deck to the GY, then uses the GY-loaded 'Exchange of the Spirit' to set more Traps and shuffle away the opponent's Graveyard.

hooks.label: EARTH Fairy support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is an EARTH Fairy, and their effects search, revive and swarm EARTH Fairy monsters, so support for that Type and Attribute powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent
hooks.why: Kelbek the Ancient Vanguard and Agido the Ancient Sentinel Special Summon themselves when a card is sent from the hand or Deck to the opponent's GY, so any card that mills the opponent's Deck or forces them to discard sets them off.

hooks.label: Sends your monsters to GY
hooks.why: Kelbek, Agido and Blast Held by Destiny all have effects that trigger when they are sent from the hand or Deck to the GY, so outside cards that send monsters from your hand or Deck to the GY activate them.

hooks.label: Monsters with GY effects
hooks.why: The deck mills its own Deck and discards for cost, so any monster that has an effect when it is sent to the GY gets value for free.

hooks.label: Sends Traps to GY
hooks.why: The archetype's Traps and Quick Effects all get stronger if 'Exchange of the Spirit' is in the GY, so outside cards that send Trap Cards from the Deck to the GY help assemble that condition.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck that gathers Nordic Tuners and low-Level Nordic monsters, using Gullveig of the Nordic Ascendant to banish cards from hand/field and flood the field so it can climb into the Level 10 Aesir Synchro Monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: Gullveig of the Nordic Ascendant banishes up to 3 cards from your hand and/or field to Special Summon Nordic monsters, and Alviss of the Nordic Alfar even triggers when banished by a Nordic Link Monster, so outside monsters with 'when this card is banished' effects are turned on for free.

hooks.label: Beast-Type support
hooks.why: Tanngrisnir, Tanngnjostr, Guldfaxe, Garmr and Gullinbursti of the Nordic Beasts are all Beast-Type, as are the Nordic Beast Tokens they make, so Beast support strengthens the whole Beast half of the deck.

hooks.label: Adds or Summons a Tuner
hooks.why: The Aesir Synchro Monsters need a 'Nordic' Tuner as material, and the deck's only Tuners are Vanadis, Guldfaxe, Valkyrie, Svartalf, Mara and Gullinbursti, so anything that adds or Special Summons a Tuner from the Deck finds the missing piece.

hooks.label: Sends monsters from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Vanadis of the Nordic Ascendant and Alviss of the Nordic Alfar deliberately dump Nordic monsters from the Deck into the GY, which Svartalf, Gullinbursti, Mimir and Nordic Relic Hlidskjalf then recover or revive, so outside cards that send monsters from the Deck to the GY work the same way.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon enablers
hooks.why: Dverg of the Nordic Alfar exists purely to give an extra Normal Summon of a Nordic monster, and Ljosalf, Svartalf, Gullinbursti and Nordic Smith Ivaldi only get their effects when Normal Summoned, so extra Normal Summons are extra triggers and extra Synchro material.

profile.plan: Infernoids Special Summon themselves by banishing 'Infernoid' monsters from the hand or GY while the total Levels of your Effect Monsters are 8 or lower, and use Quick Effects that Tribute a monster to banish from the opponent's GY.

hooks.label: Mills Fiend/FIRE monsters
hooks.why: Infernoids must banish 'Infernoid' monsters from the hand or GY to Special Summon themselves, and Void Launch sends them from the Deck to the Graveyard, so any card that mills Fiend or FIRE monsters fuels the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Every Infernoid has a Quick Effect that Tributes 1 monster as a cost to banish a card from the opponent's Graveyard, so monsters with an effect when they are Tributed give you extra value for that cost.

hooks.label: Summons Tokens
hooks.why: Infernoids can only Special Summon themselves while the total Levels and Ranks of all Effect Monsters you control are 8 or lower, and Tokens are not Effect Monsters, so any card that Special Summons Tokens gives you free Tribute fodder without raising that total.

hooks.label: Triggers on GY banish
hooks.why: Infernoids banish themselves from the Graveyard as the cost to Special Summon, and Infernoid Flood has an effect when a card is banished from your GY, so outside cards that trigger when your cards are banished from the GY get value from every summon.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Infernoid monster is a Fiend, so cards that support Fiends can search, revive or boost the entire deck.

profile.plan: The deck is a control-burn strategy using 0 ATK monsters that cannot be destroyed by battle and reflect battle damage to the opponent, equipped with Equip Spells to enable their effects and force the opponent to attack into them.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: Every Mikanko monster triggers when an Equip Card is equipped to it, and Mikanko Kagura's power depends on Equip Spells in the GY, so adding Equip Spells from the Deck or GY is a core consistency boost.

hooks.label: Ritual support
hooks.why: The deck Ritual Summons Ohime and Arahime with Mikanko Kagura, so cards that add Ritual Spells or Ritual Monsters improve consistency.

hooks.label: Mills Equip Spells
hooks.why: Mikanko Kagura destroys cards based on the number of Equip Spells with different names in the GY, so sending Equip Spells from the Deck to the GY powers up that effect.

hooks.label: Equip Spells with GY effects
hooks.why: The deck sends many Equip Spells to the GY (Mikanko Kagura, Mikanko Shinbu, etc.), so Equip Spells that do something when sent there give extra value.

hooks.label: Forces opponent to attack
hooks.why: Mikanko monsters only reflect damage when they are attacked, and Heavenly Gate forces attacks; additional cards that force attacks make the strategy more consistent.

profile.plan: A Zombie Ritual deck: it loads the GY with Zombie monsters, then Ritual Summons Vendread monsters by Tributing or banishing those Zombies, and the Ritual Monsters hand the main-deck Vendreads' effects to each other.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Vendread monster is a Zombie and Revendread Origin banishes Zombie monsters from the GY as Ritual material, so generic Zombie support helps the whole deck.

hooks.label: Revives Zombies from the GY
hooks.why: Revendread Origin and Ravenous Vendread Ritual Summon by Tributing monsters or banishing Zombies from the GY, and Revendread Slayer and Vendread Chimera banish Zombies from the GY, so reviving Zombies keeps material available.

hooks.label: Sends Zombies to the GY
hooks.why: Vendread Striges Special Summons itself when sent to the GY and Scar of the Vendread searches a Vendread Spell/Trap when sent there, so effects that send Zombies from the Deck to the GY start those plays and fill the GY for the Ritual Spells.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell and Monster searchers
hooks.why: Each play needs a Ritual Spell (Revendread Origin, Revendread Evolution, Ravenous Vendread) together with a Ritual Monster, and the deck only recovers them after a Ritual Summoned Revendread Slayer or Vendread Battlelord is sent to the GY.

hooks.label: Tributes your Zombies
hooks.why: Ritual Summons here are paid for with Tributes, and Scar of the Vendread Special Summons itself from the GY whenever a monster on the field is Tributed, so outside Tribute outlets on Zombies are extra value.

profile.plan: The deck uses Continuous Spell/Trap 'Fire Formation' cards to search, boost and extra Normal Summon Beast-Warrior monsters, especially Fire Fist, and can Fusion or Ritual Summon Beast-Warrior bosses.

hooks.label: Fire Fist cards
hooks.why: The deck's Fusion and Ritual monsters revive Fire Fist monsters, and Ultimate Fire Formation - Sinto and Fire Fortress atop Liang Peak specifically need a Fire Fist on the field, so outside Fire Fist cards are natural partners.

hooks.label: Sends Continuous Spell/Trap to GY
hooks.why: Fire Formation - Ingen and Fire Formation - Domei both have effects that trigger when they are sent from the Spell & Trap Zone to the GY, so outside cards that can send your own Continuous Spell/Trap there give you those effects for free.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Fire Formation card boosts or enables Beast-Warrior monsters, and the Field Spell adds and Special Summons them, so any outside card that supports the Beast-Warrior Type fits.

profile.plan: A stun shell that shuts the opponent's Spell and Trap Cards down — forcing them to be Set before activation, negating Spells outright and sealing Spell/Trap activation during the Battle Phase — while grinding out small advantages with its own monsters.

hooks.label: Spell Counter generators
hooks.why: Anti-Spell needs 2 Spell Counters on your side of the field to negate a Spell, so any outside card that stocks Spell Counters on your field switches that Counter Trap on.

hooks.label: Insect Token makers
hooks.why: Anti-Aircraft Flower only asks for an Insect-Type monster to Tribute each time, so outside cards that Special Summon Insect Tokens hand it free ammunition every turn.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Antialian grants an extra Normal Summon of a Cyberse monster after it battles and rewards you for being on Cyberse, so generic Cyberse support and Cyberse bodies fit it directly.

hooks.label: Sets Spells from the Deck
hooks.why: Anti-Spell Fragrance forces both players to Set Spells before activating them, so outside cards that Set Spell Cards straight from the Deck or GY let your own Spells keep working under your own lock.

profile.plan: A FIRE Dragon Synchro deck that uses Sangen Spell/Traps to protect its monsters, search Level 4 or lower FIRE Dragons, and trigger extra effects once 3 or more attacks have been declared in a turn.

hooks.label: FIRE Dragon support
hooks.why: All Sangen monsters are FIRE Dragon, and Sangen Summoning protects only FIRE Dragon monsters while Sangen Kaiho requires all your monsters to be FIRE Dragon.

hooks.label: Forces opponent attacks
hooks.why: Sangenpai Transcendent Dragion and Sangen Kaiho trigger when 3 or more attacks are declared in a turn, and Transcendent Dragion itself forces the opponent's monsters to attack, so more forced attacks help you reach that count.

hooks.label: Extra attacks
hooks.why: The Sangen GY effects and Sangen Kaiho need 3 or more attacks declared in a turn, so effects that let your FIRE Dragon monsters attack multiple times help you reach that threshold.

hooks.label: Sends FIRE Dragon to GY
hooks.why: Sangenpai Bident Dragion can revive a FIRE Dragon from your GY when Synchro Summoned, so loading the GY with FIRE Dragon monsters gives it a target.

profile.plan: A stall/alternate-win deck: Destiny Board places the four Spirit Message Continuous Spells during your opponent's End Phases, and holding all five on the field wins the Duel while Dark Sanctuary turns the Messages into untargetable Fiend beaters and negates attacks.

hooks.label: Discard fodder
hooks.why: Dark Spirit's Mastery discards 1 card as its cost to add Destiny Board or a Level 8 Fiend, so monsters that do something when discarded turn that cost into free value.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Dark Sanctuary Special Summons the Spirit Message cards as Fiend Normal Monsters and Sentence of Doom adds Fiend monsters from your GY or banished pile to your hand, so Fiend support touches almost every card in the deck.

hooks.label: Dumps Spells/Traps to the GY
hooks.why: Sentence of Doom places a Spirit Message card from your hand, Deck or GY into the Spell & Trap Zone, and Dark Spirit's Mastery recycles from the GY, so outside cards that send Continuous Spells/Traps from the Deck to the GY set up the win condition.

hooks.label: Protects your Spells & Traps
hooks.why: Destiny Board only wins while it and all four Spirit Message cards are face-up on your field, and its own text sends every one of them to the Graveyard the moment any of them leaves, so protecting face-up Spells/Traps keeps the alternate win alive.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck of differently-Typed Illusion, Dragon, Warrior, Fairy and Spellcaster monsters that Fusion Summons from hand and field, rewards controlling 3 or more different Monster Types, and uses a Field Spell that discards Spells/Traps to search its monsters.

hooks.label: Extra Fusion Summoning
hooks.why: Every payoff is a Fusion Summon — Artmage Masterwork -Succession-, Artmage Non-Finito and Artmage Power Patron all Fusion Summon, and Artmage Vandalism -Assault- lets any monster count as an "Artmage" Fusion Material.

hooks.label: Spell/Trap that likes the GY
hooks.why: Artmage Academic Arcane Arts Acropolis and Artmage Non-Finito discard 1 Spell/Trap as a cost, and Artmage Movement -Pedigree- and Artmage Peripeteia -Turmoil- already reward being sent to the GY that way, so outside Spells/Traps with the same trigger are free value.

hooks.label: Field Spell placers
hooks.why: Artmage Academic Arcane Arts Acropolis is the whole engine (an extra Normal Summon of "Medius the Pure" plus a monster search) and Artmage Masterwork -Succession- gives 500 ATK while a card is in the Field Zone.

hooks.label: Fusion Material substitutes
hooks.why: Artmage Diactorus names "Medius the Pure" as Fusion Material, so a monster that can substitute for a specifically named Fusion Material fills that slot without searching.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Machine/FIRE Xyz deck that stacks Springans monsters from the hand, field and GY onto its Xyz Monsters as material, then detaches them for removal and swarming, with Fallen of Albaz Fusions used as extra material.

hooks.label: Machine and FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Springans monster and every Springans Xyz Monster is a Machine FIRE monster, so support that names Machine or FIRE applies to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills Machine monsters
hooks.why: Springans Brothers and Tri-Brigade Springans Kitt revive a monster when sent from the hand or Deck to the GY, and Rockey, Branga, Pedor and Captain Sargas attach themselves from the GY, so sending Machines there fuels both halves.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz material
hooks.why: Rockey, Brothers, Captain Sargas, Branga and Pedor all attach themselves to a Springans Xyz Monster as material, and Exblowrer, Sargas, Gung-Ho! Springans! and Tally-ho! Springans! pay materials, so effects that attach material keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Albaz partners
hooks.why: Gung-Ho! Springans! and Springans Kitt search "Fallen of Albaz" and monsters that mention it, and Springans Call! and Merrymaker attach its Fusion Monsters from the Extra Deck to a Springans Xyz Monster as material.

hooks.label: Branded Spells and Traps
hooks.why: Springans Kitt adds a "Branded" Spell/Trap from the Deck, GY or banishment, so more Branded Spells and Traps give Kitt something to fetch.

profile.plan: A WATER/Aqua control deck built around the Field Spell Icejade Cenote Enion Cradle, using Icejade Creation monsters that equip themselves to WATER monsters and recurring Icejades from the GY, before Synchro Summoning Icejade Gymir Aegirine as a protective boss.

hooks.label: Field Spell enablers
hooks.why: Icejade Kosmochlor Special Summons itself while a face-up card is in the Field Zone, and Icejade Curse's floodgate and Kosmochlor's ATK drain only apply while Icejade Cenote Enion Cradle is on the field.

hooks.label: Equips to your WATER monsters
hooks.why: Icejade Ran Aegirine's name becomes Icejade Cenote Enion Cradle while equipped with an Equip Card, and Icejade Creation Kingfisher and Icejade Creation Aegirocassis only use their effects while equipped to a monster.

hooks.label: Aqua and WATER support
hooks.why: Every Icejade monster is an Aqua WATER monster, and Tremora, Acti, Tinola, Aegirine and Icejade Cenote Enion Cradle all name WATER (or Icejade) monsters as what they Summon, send, boost or revive.

hooks.label: Destroys your own WATER monster
hooks.why: Icejade Tremora, Icejade Acti and Icejade Tinola all banish themselves from the GY to revive an Icejade monster when a face-up WATER monster you control is destroyed by battle or card effect, so a card that destroys your own WATER monster becomes a free Summon.

profile.plan: Cheats out Level 10-12 Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link bosses that each demand three big materials, backs them with face-down banishing, and uses the Pendulum boss Vidolium to recycle one Fusion, one Synchro and one Xyz into a 5000 ATK body.

hooks.label: Artmage monsters
hooks.why: Nerva the Power Patron of Creation is a Fusion Monster that requires 3 "Artmage" monsters as material, so its intended partners come from that separate archetype.

hooks.label: DoomZ monsters
hooks.why: Jupiter the Power Patron of Destruction Special Summons 1 "DoomZ" monster from your GY whenever it detaches a material, so DoomZ bodies are the payoff it is built to revive.

hooks.label: Elfnote monsters
hooks.why: Junora the Power Patron of Tuning stops the opponent using monsters in the same column as your "Elfnote" monsters as Fusion, Synchro, Xyz or Link material, so Elfnote bodies make the lock live.

hooks.label: Equip Spell support
hooks.why: Jupiter the Power Patron of Destruction can be Xyz Summoned using a single monster equipped with 3 or more Equip Cards, and it re-equips Equip Spells from your GY, so anything that stacks Equip Spells accelerates it.

hooks.label: DARK Fairy support
hooks.why: Terminus searches a DARK Fairy and Vidolium, Purification Power Patron and the archetype's Fairy line are DARK Fairies, so DARK Fairy support reaches the whole engine.

hooks.label: Level 10 material
hooks.why: Jupiter the Power Patron of Destruction needs 3 Level 10 monsters as Xyz material and both Nerva and Junora are Level 10, so cards that Special Summon Level 10 monsters supply the deck's materials.

profile.plan: A Rock/EARTH Graveyard-Fusion deck: Fossil Fusion banishes a Rock monster plus a monster of a Level band out of either GY to bring out battle-focused Fossil Fusion Monsters whose piercing, multi-attacks and burn finish the game.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Fossil Fusion and Miracle Rupture both require Rock monsters (Fossil Fusion banishes 1 Rock monster from your GY as material, Miracle Rupture sends a Level 4 or lower Rock from the Deck), and every Fossil Fusion Monster is itself a Rock.

hooks.label: Dumps monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Fossil Fusion banishes its Fusion Materials out of the GYs and Weathering Soldier searches when a card effect sends it to the GY, so any outside mill is another way to load materials.

hooks.label: Rock monsters with GY triggers
hooks.why: Fossil Fusion banishes a Rock monster from your GY as material, so a Rock monster that does something when sent to the GY is both fuel and value.

hooks.label: Discard payoffs
hooks.why: Flint Cragger discards 1 card when Special Summoned and Fossil Warrior Skull King discards 1 card for its Quick Effect, so cards that trigger when discarded are free advantage.

hooks.label: Banished payoffs
hooks.why: Fossil Fusion banishes players' monsters from the GY as material and the Fossil Fusion Monsters banish themselves from the GY for their effects, so monsters with effects while banished get paid twice.

hooks.label: Defense Position makers
hooks.why: Every Fossil Fusion Monster inflicts piercing battle damage (and Skullgios flips the opposing monster's ATK and DEF), so effects that put the opponent's monsters in Defense Position turn them into damage.

profile.plan: A Fairy/LIGHT beatdown deck that punches through Defense Position monsters for piercing damage and draws off the battle damage, backed by The Sanctuary in the Sky and a Counter Trap negate engine.

hooks.label: Searches Counter Traps
hooks.why: Sacred Arch-Airknight Parshath adds a Counter Trap from the Deck when it deals battle damage and Celestial Knightlord Parshath digs for Sanctuary cards, so outside cards that fetch Counter Traps keep the negation loop stocked.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Parshath card, Darknight Parshath included, is a Fairy, and Celestial Knightlord Parshath needs 2+ Fairy monsters as Link material and banishes Fairy monsters from the GY.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Airknight Parshath, Nova Summoner, Sacred Arch-Airknight Parshath and Avenging Knight Parshath all specify LIGHT Fairies, so LIGHT support reaches nearly the whole deck.

hooks.label: Cards listing The Sanctuary in the Sky
hooks.why: Celestial Knightlord Parshath adds 'The Sanctuary in the Sky' or any card that specifically lists it, and Sanctum of Parshath copies its name, so outside cards built around that Field Spell slot straight in.

hooks.label: Turns monsters to Defense
hooks.why: Airknight Parshath, Neo-Parshath and their kin all inflict piercing battle damage and trigger on dealing battle damage, so outside cards that flip an opponent's monster into Defense Position hand them a soft target to draw off.

profile.plan: A Pyro/FIRE burn deck that fills the Graveyard with its own monsters so Scattershot, Rimfire and Emperor pay off, while 'Blaze Accelerator' Continuous Spells clear the opponent's board and every effect chips away at their LP.

hooks.label: Blaze Accelerator cards
hooks.why: Scattershot's board wipe, Volcanic Rocket's search, Rimfire's placement and Emperor's Summon all key off 'Blaze Accelerator' cards, so the deck has to borrow them from outside.

hooks.label: Mills Pyro monsters
hooks.why: Volcanic Scattershot and Volcanic Rimfire only trigger when they are sent to the GY, and Emperor feeds on banished Pyro monsters, so any effect that dumps Pyro monsters into the Graveyard starts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Pyro monsters with GY effects
hooks.why: Fire Ejection sends any Pyro monster from the Deck to the GY, so outside Pyro monsters that do something when they hit the Graveyard get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Pyro support
hooks.why: Every Volcanic monster is a Pyro, Fire Ejection requires a Pyro to send, and Emperor wants three of them banished, so cards that search, revive or support Pyro monsters lift the whole deck.
