hooks.label: Burn damage boosters
hooks.why: Scattershot, Slicer, Hammerer, Emperor and the Bomb Tokens all inflict effect damage, so outside cards that add extra damage each time the opponent is burned multiply every one of those effects.

profile.plan: The deck manipulates the Levels of its Machine monsters to boost their ATK and enable Synchro Summons, using Field Spells that increase Levels and search on destruction.

hooks.label: Low-ATK Machine summoners
hooks.why: All F.A. Main Deck monsters have 0 ATK, so cards like Machine Duplication that Special Summon Machines with 500 or less ATK from the Deck can instantly flood the field with F.A. monsters.

hooks.label: Field Spell support
hooks.why: The deck relies on F.A. Field Spells (City Grand Prix, Off-Road Grand Prix, Circuit Grand Prix) for Level boosts and searches, so cards that search or activate Field Spells from the Deck are key.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every F.A. monster is a Machine, so cards that support the Machine Type (like Limiter Removal or Machine Assembly Line) boost the whole deck.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Most F.A. Main Deck monsters are WIND (Auto Navigator, Hang On Mach, Whip Crosser, Sonic Meister, Turbo Charger), so WIND support cards can search or revive them.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Machine Tuners
hooks.why: The deck needs Tuners for its Synchro Summons, and only has Auto Navigator, so Machine Tuners that Special Summon themselves (like Deskbot 001) provide extra Synchro material.

hooks.label: Sends Spells/Traps from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Foolish Burial Goods can send an F.A. Field Spell to the GY to be banished by F.A. Winners for its win condition, or send F.A. Pit Stop/Downforce to the GY to later banish for their effects.

profile.plan: LIGHT Reptile 'Worm' monsters that flip themselves face-down to re-trigger their FLIP effects, grind the opponent down with flip removal and milling, then finish with Tribute-Summoned Worm King/Queen or a Fusion Summoned Worm Zero.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-up
hooks.why: The whole deck is FLIP Effect Monsters — Worm Apocalypse, Cartaros, Jetelikpse, Linx, Victory, Dimikles, Millidith, Falco, Opera, Noble and Hope — so any outside card that flips a face-down monster face-up re-arms a Worm for free.

hooks.label: Sets your Reptiles face-down
hooks.why: Worm Falco, Worm Erokin and Medusa Worm flip your own Reptile Worms face-down so their FLIP effects can be used again, so outside cards that Set a monster face-down extend the same loop.

hooks.label: Reptile-Type support
hooks.why: Worm Xex, Cartaros, Prince, King, Queen and Zero all name Reptile-Type 'Worm' monsters, so generic Reptile-Type search, revival and protection cards work on nearly every card in the deck.

hooks.label: Insect-Type support
hooks.why: Worm Bait needs an Insect on the field, Aztekipede banishes an Insect from the Graveyard to Special Summon itself, and Shield Worm mills for each face-up Insect you control.

hooks.label: Sets your Spells and Traps
hooks.why: Worm Illidan places a Worm Counter every time a card is Set on your side of the field and removes 2 to destroy any card the opponent controls, so cards that Set directly from the Deck or Graveyard hand it free counters.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoffs
hooks.why: Worm King and Worm Queen can be Tribute Summoned with a single Reptile-Type 'Worm', then Tribute more Worms to destroy any card or Special Summon from the Deck, so outside monsters that reward you for Tribute Summoning share the same setup.

profile.plan: A Fairy deck that Fusion Summons 'Frightfur' monsters using 'Polymerization' and monsters that trigger when sent to the GY as Fusion Material.

hooks.label: Fusion Material substitutes
hooks.why: The deck's own substitute card shows it needs replacements for the specific monsters its Fusions name, so outside monsters that can replace named Fusion Materials do the same job.

hooks.label: Fusion Material triggers
hooks.why: The deck's monsters all trigger when sent to the GY as Fusion Material, so outside monsters with the same trigger gain advantage from every Fusion Summon.

hooks.label: Polymerization searchers
hooks.why: The deck's monsters can add 'Polymerization' from the Deck or Graveyard, so outside cards that do the same give it more consistent access to its Fusion Spell.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck monster in the archetype is Fairy-Type, so generic Fairy support — searching, reviving, boosting — works on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A deck that Special Summons its monsters from the hand by equipping a monster from the GY to them, then uses those equipped monsters as Equip Cards to grant effects, negate, destroy or bounce.

hooks.label: Sends a monster of the right Type to the GY
hooks.why: Therion monsters Special Summon themselves from the hand by targeting a Machine, Plant, Warrior, Reptile, Psychic or Aqua monster in the GY, so any card that sends one of those Types from the Deck to the GY gives them a target.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when sent to the GY
hooks.why: Therion effects like Regulus, Lily, Alasia and Charge send cards from the hand or field to the GY as cost, so outside monsters with an effect when sent to the GY or discarded get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Special Summons from the Spell & Trap Zone
hooks.why: Therion monsters often end up as Equip Cards in the Spell & Trap Zone, and cards like Empress Alasia and Irregular Special Summon them from there; outside cards that can do the same give more ways to bring them back.

profile.plan: A tag-out deck: the Psychic pilots banish themselves to Special Summon the Machine ships from the hand, and the ships float into a lower-Level Kozmo from the Deck when they are destroyed, paying Life Points all the way.

hooks.label: Machine-Type support
hooks.why: Every ship — Kozmo Dark Destroyer, Sliprider, Forerunner, Dark Eclipser, Landwalker, DOG Fighter, Delta Shuttle and Dark Planet — is a Machine, so Machine search, revival and stat support hit the deck's bosses.

hooks.label: Psychic-Type support
hooks.why: Kozmo Tincan, Farmgirl, Strawman, Goodwitch, Wickedwitch, Soartroopers, Dark Lady and Scaredy Lion are all Psychic, and Kozmo Soartroopers revives a Psychic 'Kozmo' while Kozmo Lightsword only equips to one.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Every Machine Kozmo floats when it is destroyed by battle or card effect, and Kozmojo and Kozmo Landwalker already trade one Kozmo for value, so an outside card that destroys a monster you control becomes a free Special Summon from the Deck.

hooks.label: Chaos banish LIGHT and DARK
hooks.why: The pilots are LIGHT Psychics and the enforcers are DARK, so both Attributes pile up in the Graveyard and Chaos-style monsters that Special Summon themselves by banishing a LIGHT and a DARK from the GY have fuel.

hooks.label: Banished pile recovery
hooks.why: Every Psychic Kozmo banishes itself to tag out and Kozmotown and Kozmo Strawman bring those banished monsters back, so the deck accumulates a large banished pile that outside cards can Special Summon or recover.

profile.plan: A DARK Spellcaster deck built around Dark Magician: it searches and Special Summons Dark Magician and cards that name it, then turns LP swings, face-down cards and dice rolls into damage, protection and negation.

hooks.label: DARK Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Dark Magical Curtain Special Summons any DARK Spellcaster from the hand or Deck, and Dark Paladin - Wave-Motion and Ancient Sorcerer are DARK Spellcasters themselves.

hooks.label: Searches or summons Dark Magician
hooks.why: Dark Magical Circle reveals 'Dark Magician' or a Spell/Trap that mentions it from the top of the Deck and banishes when it is Summoned, and Dark Magical Curtain adds a Spell/Trap that mentions 'Dark Magician'.

hooks.label: Life Point gain
hooks.why: Sorcerer of Sebek makes each player take 1000 damage whenever a player gains LP and gains you LP off battle damage, so any outside card that gains you LP becomes a burn engine.

hooks.label: Fills the field face-down
hooks.why: King of Yamimado Special Summons itself while 'Yami' or 2 or more face-down cards are on the field and cannot be destroyed or targeted while you control a face-down card, so outside cards that Set cards face-down turn it on.

hooks.label: Dice-roll cards
hooks.why: Armor Wizard Pazoo can negate an opponent's activated effect while you control a card with an effect that requires a die roll, turning any dice-roll card into blanket negation.

hooks.label: Pay Life Points
hooks.why: Armor Wizard Pazoo grants the equipped monster 2100 ATK/DEF while your LP are 4000 or less, so paying Life Points into that range switches it on.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of DARK Fiend 'Abyss Actor' monsters that Sets 'Abyss Script' Spells from the Deck for removal, then recycles its destroyed Pendulum Monsters between the Extra Deck and the field to beat down.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Abyss Actor monster is a Fiend, and Super Producer even asks for a Fiend as Link Material, so Fiend searchers, revives and boosters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Pendulum monster
hooks.why: Wild Hope, Sassy Rookie, Leading Lady and Liberty Dramatist all float when an Abyss Actor Pendulum Monster is destroyed, and Super Producer destroys a face-up card you control as a cost.

hooks.label: Mills Spells to the GY
hooks.why: Mellow Madonna gains ATK for each Abyss Script Spell in the GY, and Superstar, Evil Heel and Abysstainment all recover those Spells from the GY, so any card that puts Spells in the GY is fuel.

hooks.label: Monsters that want destroying
hooks.why: Super Producer destroys a face-up card you control to place Abyss Playhouse - Fantastic Theater or an Abyss Actor in your Pendulum Zone, so outside monsters with an effect when they are destroyed get that trigger for free.

hooks.label: Pendulum Zone setup
hooks.why: Hyper Director and Super Producer can only place Abyss Actor Pendulum Monsters in the Pendulum Zone, so outside cards that put a Pendulum Monster into a Pendulum Zone help complete both scales for the deck's Pendulum Summons.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Ritual deck that uses Lo as an entire Tribute and swarms LIGHT Ritual Warrior/Dragon monsters, supported by Continuous Spells/Traps that place, recover and re-Ritual Summon.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Every Voiceless Voice Ritual Summon Tributes monsters from the hand or field, so outside monsters that do something when Tributed (or used as Ritual material) get value for free.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell/Monster support
hooks.why: Saffira, Dragon Queen sends a Ritual Spell from the Deck to the GY, Radiance and Sauravis shuffle Ritual Spells from the hand/GY, and Saffira adds a LIGHT Ritual Monster, so outside cards that search, recover or send Ritual Spells/Monsters are engine pieces.

hooks.label: LIGHT self-summoning monsters
hooks.why: Prayers of the Voiceless Voice requires LIGHT monsters as Tributes, and Blessing/Ritual Summons need bodies, so outside LIGHT monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand give material without using your Normal Summon.

profile.plan: A Machine deck that flips its monsters between Attack and Defense Position, switching between two different sets of effects and getting counters, ATK and removal every time a battle position changes.

hooks.label: Battle position changers
hooks.why: Every Morphtronic has separate Attack and Defense Position effects, and Morphtronic Map gains a Morph Counter, Morphtronic Cord destroys a Spell/Trap and Morphtronic Clocken builds to a burn every time a battle position changes.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Nearly the whole archetype is Machine-Type, Morphtronic Converter Special Summons Machine monsters and Factory of 100 Machines boosts a Machine monster with every banished Morphtronic.

hooks.label: Cards that equip themselves
hooks.why: Morphtronic Videon gains 800 ATK or DEF for each Equip Card on it and Morphtronic Vacuumen sends an Equip Card away for burn damage, while Repair Unit, Cord, Engine and Rusty Engine are all Equip Spells.

hooks.label: Dice-roll cards
hooks.why: Morphtronic Celfon, Telefon and Smartfon all Special Summon, recover or search based on the result of a six-sided die, so cards that roll or manipulate dice turn their numbers into the good results.

profile.plan: A Level 2 Beast and Fish swarm that Special Summons extra copies of itself out of the Deck, flooding the board and the Graveyard to set up Rank 2 Xyz Summons.

hooks.label: Mills or discards your monsters
hooks.why: Nimble Angler Special Summons up to 2 Level 3 or lower Nimble monsters from the Deck whenever it is sent from the hand or Deck to the GY, so any outside card that mills or discards starts the entire engine.

hooks.label: Fish that want to be milled
hooks.why: Nimble Sunfish sends 1 Fish-Type monster from your Deck to the GY when it is destroyed by battle, so a Fish with an effect in the Graveyard gets dumped there for free.

hooks.label: Beast support
hooks.why: Nimble Beaver, Nimble Momonga, Nimble Musasabi and Super-Nimble Mega Hamster are all Beast-Type, and Mega Hamster can only fetch Beast-Type monsters, so Beast support covers most of the deck.

hooks.label: Level 2 self-summoners
hooks.why: Every Nimble monster is Level 2 and the deck's payoff is Rank 2 Xyz, so outside Level 2 monsters that Special Summon themselves extend the swarm without using up the Normal Summon that Nimble Beaver needs.

profile.plan: A Fiend deck that equips its own monsters to Extra Deck Plunder Patroll monsters summoned by matching the opponent's monster Attributes, turning equips into draws and disruption.

hooks.label: Gives opponent a monster
hooks.why: Whitebeard, Redbeard and Blackbeard can Special Summon a Plunder Patroll Extra Deck monster with the same Attribute as a monster your opponent controls, so giving the opponent a monster with a chosen Attribute unlocks that Summon.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: The deck needs the opponent to control a monster of a specific Attribute to Summon each Extra Deck Plunder Patroll, and Plunder Patroll Booty already declares an Attribute to change an opponent's monster.

hooks.label: Discarded monsters
hooks.why: Goldenhair in the GY, Bluebeard, Shipyarrrd, Moerk, Brann and Lys all discard a card as a cost, so monsters that do something when discarded give you value for the cost.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Plunder Patroll monster is a Fiend, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Synchro Summon deck: it Normal Summons Tuners (Synchron monsters, Level 1 Tuners), extends into Level 7 or 8 Dragon Synchro Monsters, and keeps recycling Synchro material from the GY while locked into Synchro-only Extra Deck Summons.

hooks.label: Synchro Material triggers
hooks.why: The deck Synchro Summons over and over, so outside monsters that trigger when they are used as Synchro Material turn every Summon into a search, a Token or a revival.

hooks.label: Self-reviving Tuners
hooks.why: Synchro World, Synchro Rumble and Synchro Panic all Special Summon Tuners out of the GY, and Wheel Synchron banishes itself from the GY, so outside Tuners that bring themselves back are free Synchro Material.

hooks.label: Synchro GY revival
hooks.why: Synchro Zone revives non-Tuner Synchro Monsters sent to the GY and treats them as Tuners, and Synchro Creed draws for each Synchro Monster on the field, so outside cards that keep putting Synchro Monsters back on the field extend that loop.

profile.plan: A Winged Beast deck that stacks extra Normal Summons to Tribute Summon Level 7-8 WIND monsters, then revives its small birds from the GY whenever the opponent's Spell & Trap Zone is empty.

hooks.label: Winged Beast / WIND support
hooks.why: Every Simorgh monster is a WIND Winged Beast and Elborz, the Sacred Lands of Simorgh only boosts and reduces Tributes for WIND Winged Beast monsters, so support for that Type and Attribute lifts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Simorgh, Lord of the Storm and Simorgh of Darkness Tribute a WIND Winged Beast as a Quick Effect cost, so an outside monster that does something when it is Tributed pays for their negations for free.

hooks.label: Winged Beasts that want discarding
hooks.why: Simorgh Onslaught and Simorgh Repulsion both discard 1 Winged Beast monster as their cost, so an outside Winged Beast with an effect when it is discarded turns that cost into value.

hooks.label: Clears the opponent's backrow
hooks.why: Simorgh, Bird of Beginning, Bird of Bringing, Bird of Calamity and Bird of Protection only Special Summon themselves from the GY while the opponent controls no cards in their Spell & Trap Zone, so anything that empties that zone switches them on.

hooks.label: Tribute Summonable WIND bosses
hooks.why: Simorgh, Bird of Ancestry lets both players Tribute Summon WIND monsters with 1 less Tribute and Simorgh of Darkness revives itself off any Tribute Summon of a WIND monster, so high-Level WIND monsters that Tribute Summon themselves slot straight in.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon effects
hooks.why: Simorgh, Bird of Beginning, Simorgh, Bird of Perfection and Elborz all hand out additional Normal Summons, and five Simorgh monsters have effects that trigger on being Normal Summoned, so more Normal Summons per turn is more searches and revivals.

profile.plan: An Equip Spell engine: pile 0-ATK Bamboo Swords onto one monster, use Cursed Bamboo Sword to let it attack directly while Golden Bamboo Sword draws, then lock the opponent out of their Main Phase 1 and Draw Phase.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: Golden Bamboo Sword only draws while a "Bamboo Sword" Equip Spell is on the field and Original Bamboo Sword equips one from the Deck, so any card that adds an Equip Spell from the Deck or GY keeps the engine stocked.

hooks.label: Equips from the Deck
hooks.why: Original Bamboo Sword's Graveyard effect equips a "Bamboo Sword" Equip Spell from the Deck, so outside cards that equip an Equip Spell from the Deck do the same job without using the archetype's own swap.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Equip Spells
hooks.why: Cursed Bamboo Sword searches a "Bamboo Sword" card when it is sent to the Graveyard, so any outside card that destroys or sends your own Equip Spells there turns into a search.

hooks.label: Monsters that attack directly
hooks.why: Cursed Bamboo Sword grants a direct attack and Original Bamboo Sword destroys every monster the opponent controls once that direct attack deals battle damage, so a monster that can already attack directly is the perfect carrier for the 0-ATK Swords.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell support
hooks.why: Burning Bamboo Sword and Soul Devouring Bamboo Sword are Continuous Spells whose phase-skipping effects only work while they stay face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone, so cards that search or place Continuous Spells keep the lock online.

profile.plan: A deck that destroys its own cards with card effects so its monsters revive in the next Standby Phase, Ritual Summoning Winged Beast bosses while it does so.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Sacred Phoenix of Nephthys, Cerulean Sacred Phoenix, Disciple, Matriarch, Defender and Chronicler all revive or search only after a card effect destroys them and sends them to the GY, so any outside card that destroys your own monsters is an activator.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when destroyed
hooks.why: The deck destroys its own cards nearly every turn, so outside monsters with an effect that triggers when they are destroyed by a card effect get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Sacred Phoenix of Nephthys, Cerulean Sacred Phoenix and both Link monsters are all Winged Beast, so support for that Type lifts every boss in the deck.

hooks.label: Token makers
hooks.why: Hand of Nephthys must Tribute itself plus 1 other monster and Rebirth of Nephthys Tributes monsters for its Ritual Summon, so free Tokens are extra fodder for both.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 LIGHT Beast-Warrior deck that keeps one Beast-Warrior 'Bujin' on the field while 'Bujingi' hand/Graveyard monsters are sent to the GY or banished to protect and pump it, then Xyz Summons Beast/Beast-Warrior/Winged Beast Rank 4 bosses.

hooks.label: Sent from hand to GY
hooks.why: Yamato, Mahitotsu, Bujincandescence, Bujinunity and Bujintei Tsukuyomi all send cards from your hand to the Graveyard, so outside monsters with an effect when sent there get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Yamato, Mikazuchi, Hirume, Susanowo and Kagutsuchi are all Beast-Warrior-Type, and Kagutsuchi's Xyz Summon specifically asks for Beast-Warrior materials.

hooks.label: Mills LIGHT Level 4s
hooks.why: Kagutsuchi sends the top 5 cards of your Deck to the Graveyard, and Hirume, Mahitotsu and Bujincarnation all need Bujin names (every one a Level 4 LIGHT monster) sitting in the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Refills banished monsters
hooks.why: Every Bujingi pays by banishing itself from the Graveyard, and Hirume and Mahitotsu banish Bujin from the GY, so outside cards that move banished LIGHT monsters back to the Graveyard reload the whole engine.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Material
hooks.why: Susanowo, Kagutsuchi, Tsukuyomi and Amaterasu all pay for their effects by detaching Xyz Material, and Bujin Regalia - The Jewel shows the deck wants extra material attached to its Rank 4s.

profile.plan: A Warrior Link deck that Normal Summons Gouki to search when they are sent from the field to the GY, then Link climbs into large protected Ogre monsters.

hooks.label: Sends your own Gouki to GY
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Gouki searches a 'Gouki' card when sent from the field to the GY, so an outside card that Tributes, destroys, or sends your Warrior/EARTH monster to the GY turns that into a search.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: All Gouki monsters are Warriors, and Gouki The Powerload Ogre asks for 2+ Warrior monsters, so outside Warrior support searches, revives or boosts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends monsters from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Gouki Re-Match and Gouki Face Turn Special Summon Gouki from the GY, so outside cards that send Warrior/EARTH monsters from the Deck to the GY set up those revival plays.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon Spells
hooks.why: Gouki Thunder Ogre lets the turn player Normal Summon an extra monster, and Gouki Suprex and Bearhug have effects when Normal Summoned, so outside Spell cards that grant extra Normal Summons stack with that.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Xyz engine of Level 4 EARTH Warriors that Special Summon themselves from the hand or GY, searched out by Onomatopaira and cheated onto the field by Onomatopia, so the deck can Xyz Summon Utopia and other Rank 4 monsters.

hooks.label: Sent from hand to the GY
hooks.why: Onomatopaira sends 1 card from your hand to the GY and Dodododraw sends a Dododo monster there from the hand or field, so outside monsters that trigger when they are sent to the GY are turned on for free.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior support
hooks.why: Dododo Warrior, Dododo Witch, Dododo Buster, Dododo Driver and Dodododo Warrior are all EARTH Warriors, so any card that supports Warriors or EARTH monsters lifts the whole core.

hooks.label: Detached Xyz material payoff
hooks.why: Dodododo Warrior adds a Zubaba monster when it is detached to activate an Xyz Monster's effect, so outside monsters with effects on being detached as Xyz material get the same free value.

hooks.label: Level 4 self-Special Summoners
hooks.why: Dododo Buster and Dodododo Warrior Special Summon themselves from the hand as Level 4s while Gogogoglove and Onomatokage do it from the GY, so outside Level 4 monsters that summon themselves the same way are extra Rank 4 material.

hooks.label: Level modulation
hooks.why: Dododo Driver only shifts Levels on Dododo monsters, and Buster and Dodododo Warrior turn themselves into Level 4s, so outside effects that raise or lower a monster's Level let the deck match materials for a Rank it could not otherwise make.

profile.plan: A Beast-Warrior toolbox that floods the field with monsters of four different Attributes, spends 'Ancient Warriors Saga' Continuous Spells/Traps as fodder to search and negate, and destroys the opponent's board while they control more monsters than you.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Ancient Warriors monster is a Beast-Warrior, and Double Dragon Lords needs 2 Beast-Warrior monsters including a WIND one, so generic Beast-Warrior search, revival and stat boosts apply to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Masterful Sun Mou, Virtuous Liu Xuan, Double Dragon Lords and Ambitious Cao De all send a card from your hand or field to the GY as a cost, so outside monsters that trigger when sent there get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Places Continuous Spell/Traps
hooks.why: Graceful Zhou Gong, Eccentric Lu Jing, Deceptive Jia Wen and Ingenious Zhuge Kong all send a Continuous Spell/Trap you control to the GY as a cost, so the deck wants extra Continuous Spells/Traps it can spend.

hooks.label: Continuous Spells with GY effects
hooks.why: The deck constantly sends its own face-up Continuous Spells/Traps from the Spell & Trap Zone to the GY as cost, so outside Continuous Spells/Traps that do something when they are sent there are never wasted.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent monsters
hooks.why: Loyal Guan Yun, Virtuous Liu Xuan, Valiant Zhang De, Rebellious Lu Feng and Ambitious Cao De only Special Summon themselves or destroy when your opponent controls more monsters than you, so cards that hand the opponent a monster turn them on.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: Sun-Liu Alliance and Borrowing of Arrows require Ancient Warriors monsters with 2 or more different Attributes on the field, so outside cards that change a monster's Attribute help satisfy that condition.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of Fairy monsters that sets up odd and even Pendulum Scales to Pendulum Summon multiple 'Solfachord' monsters, triggering searches and extra effects, and uses the Extra Deck face-up for recovery.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: All monsters in this deck are Fairy, so cards that search, revive or boost Fairies work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Adds two different Scales
hooks.why: The deck needs one odd and one even Pendulum Scale, so cards that add two Pendulum Monsters with different Scales from the Deck set up both Pendulum Zones at once.

hooks.label: Recovers two different Scales
hooks.why: The deck sends Pendulum Monsters to the Extra Deck face-up, and its cards return them to hand; an outside card that adds two such monsters with different Scales is a perfect recovery.

hooks.label: Triggers on Pendulum Summon
hooks.why: The deck Pendulum Summons multiple monsters every turn, so any card that reacts to a Pendulum Summon adds extra value.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Pendulum Monster
hooks.why: The deck needs bodies on the field for Link plays and Pendulum Summons, so Pendulum Monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand provide free material.

hooks.label: Searching Pendulum Monster
hooks.why: The deck relies on Pendulum Monsters in hand to set Scales, so an outside Pendulum Monster that searches on its own adds consistency and can be used as a Scale.

profile.plan: A Link-climbing deck that Special Summons its Level 3 and 4 Beasts from the hand beside each other, makes Tri-Heart in the Extra Monster Zone to flip the whole field into Defense Position, then swings with multi-attacking, piercing Scareclaw Links the opponent can barely answer.

hooks.label: Visas Starfrost partners
hooks.why: Reichphobia searches Visas Starfrost, and Light-Heart, Arrival, Straddle, Sclash, Defanging and Decline all revive, protect or gain bonuses from it, so any card that names Visas Starfrost plugs straight into the deck.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Scareclaw Twinsaw Tributes a Scareclaw monster and Scareclaw Alternative Tributes three as cost, so outside monsters with an effect that triggers when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Turns monsters to Defense Position
hooks.why: Reichheart draws and Reichphobia destroys a card once 3 or more Defense Position monsters are on the field, and Tri-Heart is unaffected by the activated effects of Defense Position monsters, so forcing the opponent's board into Defense Position feeds every payoff.

hooks.label: Piercing damage enablers
hooks.why: Belone gives piercing to a Scareclaw monster in the Extra Monster Zone while Tri-Heart flips the opponent's whole field into Defense Position, so extra piercing turns each of Tri-Heart's multi-attacks into damage.

hooks.label: Defense Position Token makers
hooks.why: Reichheart's draw, Reichphobia's destruction and Tri-Heart's three-monster requirement all count Defense Position monsters on the field, so free Defense Position Tokens reach those thresholds before Tri-Heart lands.

profile.plan: A Rock deck that assembles Alpha, Beta and Gamma — Level 4 EARTH Normal Monsters — and melds them into its Level 8 bosses Valkyrion and Berserkion, which bring their own materials back when they are Tributed or destroyed.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon cards
hooks.why: Imperion Magnum the Superconductive Battlebot must be Fusion Summoned from Valkyrion the Magna Warrior and Berserkion the Electromagna Warrior, and the archetype contains no Fusion Spell of its own.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Every card in the archetype is a Rock monster, so cards that search, revive or boost Rocks work on Alpha, Beta, Gamma and both bosses alike.

hooks.label: Summons Level 4 Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Valkyrion the Magna Warrior Tributes Alpha, Beta and Gamma from the hand or field and Berserkion the Electromagna Warrior banishes them from the GY, so anything that puts Level 4 Normal Rocks into play keeps both bosses live.

hooks.label: Mills Rock monsters
hooks.why: Berserkion Special Summons itself by banishing its three materials from the GY and its destruction effect banishes a Level 4 or lower Magnet Warrior from the GY, so sending Rocks from the Deck to the GY loads it.

hooks.label: Banished Rock recovery
hooks.why: Berserkion banishes Alpha, Beta and Gamma from the hand, field or GY to Summon itself and later revives the banished ones, so cards that pull banished Rocks back into the GY or hand give you material for the next Valkyrion or Berserkion play.

profile.plan: A DARK Fiend deck that empties its own hand to unlock Infernity effects, then revives and Synchro Summons from the Graveyard for explosive combos.

hooks.label: Discards itself from hand
hooks.why: Infernity effects like Infernity Sage and Infernity Knight discard your hand, so monsters that discard themselves help reach an empty hand while providing a body.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Infernity Sage, Infernity Inferno and Wave-Motion Inferno send your whole hand to the GY, so outside cards with discard or hand-to-GY triggers get their effects for free.

hooks.label: DARK Fiend support
hooks.why: Almost every Infernity monster is a DARK Fiend, and their effects call for DARK and Fiend materials, so generic support for either Type or Attribute fits.

hooks.label: DARK monsters banished from GY
hooks.why: Infernity Queen and Infernity General banish DARK monsters from the Graveyard as cost, so outside DARK monsters with a banish trigger give extra value.

hooks.label: DARK monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Infernity Paranoia Tributes a DARK monster to Special Summon an Infernity from Deck or GY, so outside DARK monsters with a Tribute trigger pay for themselves.

profile.plan: A Reptile deck that sends LIGHT and DARK Reptiles from the Deck to the GY, then revives its Level 8 bosses from the GY by Tributing monsters.

hooks.label: Sends Reptile to GY
hooks.why: Nauya, Nunu, Water Lily and Serpent Strike all send Reptile monsters from the Deck to the GY, so any outside card that does the same is another way to load the GY for the revival effects.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Ogdoadic monster is a Reptile and Nunu locks you into Reptile Special Summons, so generic Reptile support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Keurs, Aleirtt, Ogdoabyss, Aron and Amunessia all Tribute monsters as cost to revive themselves from the GY, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get value.

hooks.label: Triggers from hand to GY
hooks.why: Nauya and Nunu send themselves from hand to GY, and Zohah, Flogos and Serpent Strike send a card from hand to GY, so outside monsters that trigger when sent from hand to GY fit.

hooks.label: Sends opponent's cards to GY
hooks.why: Aron and Amunessia trigger when a monster your opponent controls or from their hand/Deck is sent to the GY, so outside cards that send opponent's cards to the GY are payoffs.

profile.plan: A WIND Synchro deck that uses Psychic and Winged Beast Tuners to climb into Synchro monsters, recycles Gusto monsters from the Graveyard, and redirects battle damage with Daigusto Sphreez.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Every Gusto monster is WIND, so cards that search, revive or boost WIND monsters work for the whole deck.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Most Gusto monsters, including Pilica, Caam, Musto and the Synchro bosses, are Psychic, so Psychic support cards find and revive them.

hooks.label: Summons WIND Psychic from Deck
hooks.why: Emergency Teleport-style cards Special Summon a WIND Psychic like Pilica, Winda or Kamui straight from the Deck to start Synchro Summoning.

hooks.label: Dumps a WIND monster to GY
hooks.why: Gulldo, Falco and Squirro trigger when sent from the field to the GY, and Vedir sends a Gusto from Deck to the GY, so effects that put a WIND monster into the GY fuel the deck's revival loops.

hooks.label: WIND monsters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Tailwind of Gusto discards a WIND monster as cost and Gusto Griffin triggers when sent from hand to GY, so outside WIND monsters with discard effects get value.

profile.plan: A Blue-Eyes support shell that searches Level 1 LIGHT Tuners and Blue-Eyes Spell/Traps, cheats big LIGHT Dragons out of the hand, and links away into a Tribute outlet that revives Blue-Eyes monsters.

hooks.label: Blue-Eyes White Dragon Spell/Traps
hooks.why: Wishes for Eyes of Blue searches 1 Spell/Trap that mentions "Blue-Eyes White Dragon", so outside Spell/Traps printing that name are tutorable setup pieces.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Wishes for Eyes of Blue discards 1 card as its cost, so outside monsters with an effect that triggers when they are discarded give you that effect for free.

hooks.label: Dragon and LIGHT support
hooks.why: Spirit with Eyes of Blue locks you out of Special Summoning anything but Dragon monsters, and every payoff monster here is a LIGHT Dragon, so generic Dragon/LIGHT support always applies.

profile.plan: A Link-climbing deck of Insect, Plant and Reptile monsters that Special Summon themselves by feeding or banishing from the GY, then revive their Insect/Plant/Reptile Link bosses from the Graveyard — all under a hard lock into those three Types.

hooks.label: Insect, Plant, Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Ragnaraika monster is an Insect, Plant or Reptile, and Evil Seed, Skeletal Soldier, Selene Snapper and the rest lock you into Special Summoning only those Types, so support for them helps the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills Insects, Plants, Reptiles
hooks.why: Ragnaraika Armored Lizard banishes an Insect, Plant or Reptile from the GY to summon itself, Ragnaraika Mantis Monk banishes two from the GY, and Ragnaraika Samurai Beetle revives a Level 4 or lower one, so filling the GY with those Types fuels everything.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded or milled
hooks.why: Ragnaraika Bloom discards a card after searching, Ragnaraika Armored Lizard discards an Insect, Plant or Reptile as its cost, and Ragnaraika the Evil Seed sends one from the hand to the GY, so outside monsters of those Types with a send/discard trigger get used for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished from the GY
hooks.why: Ragnaraika Armored Lizard banishes an Insect, Plant or Reptile from the GY to summon itself and Ragnaraika Mantis Monk banishes two as its cost, so outside monsters with an effect when banished from the GY trigger for free.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Insects, Plants, Reptiles
hooks.why: The Ragnaraika Link Monsters need 2 or more Insect, Plant and/or Reptile monsters as material, and the deck can only Special Summon those Types, so outside monsters of those Types that Special Summon themselves are free Link material.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Fiend control deck that activates its "Magical Musket" Quick-Play Spells and Traps from the hand during either player's turn, triggering the monsters' column effects to search, summon and recover.

hooks.label: Discard fodder
hooks.why: Magical Musketeer Kidbrave discards a "Magical Musket" card to draw 2, so outside cards that do something when discarded from the hand get value for free.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Magical Musket Mastermind Zakiel can be Tribute Summoned by Tributing 1 "Magical Musket" monster, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed are extra value.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Magical Musket monster is a Fiend, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sets Traps from Deck
hooks.why: The deck relies on its "Magical Musket" Traps, and cards that Set Traps directly from the Deck like Trap Trick can grab them without using the Normal Draw.

hooks.label: Searches Counter Traps
hooks.why: Magical Musket - Last Stand is a powerful Counter Trap, so outside cards that add Counter Traps from the Deck like Guiding Ariadne help find it.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that destroys its own Pendulum Zone cards to search and summon, while mixing with Dracoverlord, Igknight, Dinomist and Majespecter to assemble Master Peace and Forge of the True Dracos.

hooks.label: Dracoverlord Pendulum Monsters
hooks.why: Draco Face-Off reveals a 'Dracoslayer' and a 'Dracoverlord' Pendulum Monster from your Deck, so outside Dracoverlord Pendulum Monsters are the missing half of that search.

hooks.label: Igknight monsters
hooks.why: Ignis Phoenix, the Dracoslayer adds a non-Pendulum 'Igknight' from your Deck and Special Summons an 'Igknight' from your Deck when destroyed, so outside Igknight monsters are extra targets.

hooks.label: Dinomist Pendulum Monsters
hooks.why: Dinomight Powerload, the Dracoslayer adds a face-up 'Dinomist' Pendulum Monster from your Extra Deck, so outside Dinomist Pendulum Monsters give that effect targets.

hooks.label: Majespecter Pendulum Monsters
hooks.why: Majesty Pegasus, the Dracoslayer is treated as a 'Majespecter' card and its Pendulum effect needs a 'Dracoslayer' or 'Majespecter' in your other Pendulum Zone, so outside Majespecter Pendulum Monsters help enable it.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monsters that trigger when destroyed
hooks.why: Luster Pendulum and Master Pendulum can destroy a card in your Pendulum Zone, so outside Pendulum Monsters with an effect when they are destroyed while in the Pendulum Zone get that trigger for free.

profile.plan: A wall of face-down EARTH Insect Flip monsters that trade themselves for removal and, when the opponent's card effects clear them, refill the field with two more Krawlers, grinding toward the X-Krawler Link monsters and Deus X-Krawler's blanket monster-effect negation.

hooks.label: Insect and EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Krawler is an EARTH Insect, and X-Krawler Neurogos and Synaphysis ask for Insect or EARTH materials, so support for either the Type or the Attribute lifts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Flips your own monsters
hooks.why: Krawler Spine, Receptor, Axon, Dendrite, Glial and Ranvier all only get their FLIP effects when they are flipped face-up, and World Legacy Pawns and Krawler Soma re-set them face-down, so any outside card that changes your own monsters' battle position re-uses those effects.

hooks.label: Flip monster support
hooks.why: The whole Main Deck is Flip monsters and World Legacy in Shadow triggers when your Flip monster is destroyed by battle, so cards that search, revive or protect Flip monsters feed straight into the deck's engine.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck of Rock monsters that Ritual Summon through their own monster effects during either Main Phase, Tributing monsters from the hand or field to bring Megaliths out of the Deck and GY and stacking Ritual Monsters in the GY.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: Megalith Ophiel Ritual Summons a Ritual Monster from the hand and Megalith Phul recovers one from the GY, so outside cards that add Ritual Monsters from the Deck or GY are extra starters.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: Megalith Unformed is the deck's only Ritual Spell and Ritual Summons a Megalith straight from the Deck, so outside cards that add Ritual Spells set up the best opening.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon triggers
hooks.why: Megalith Phul, Och, Ophiel and Hagith Ritual Summon as Quick Effects during either Main Phase, so an outside card that triggers whenever you Ritual Summon fires even on the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Monsters that pay off when Tributed
hooks.why: Every Megalith Ritual Summon Tributes monsters from your hand or field, so an outside monster with an effect when it is Tributed turns material you were spending anyway into value.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Every Megalith monster is a Rock EARTH monster, and Megalith Unformed and Megalith Emergence Summon them from the Deck and GY, so generic Rock support reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Megalith Unformed needs materials whose total Levels equal exactly twice the Ritual Monster's Level, and Megalith Promotion doubles Levels, so outside cards that change Levels help hit those exact totals.

profile.plan: A Fiend/DARK control deck that equips 'Evil Eye of Selene' to a monster for protection and stacking ATK (paying LP every activation), adds an Evil Eye card on each Normal Summon, and Link Summons into Gorgon/Zerrziel for quick-effect removal.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: The whole deck is gated on 'Evil Eye of Selene' (and 'Evil Eye of Gorgoneio') being in the Spell & Trap Zone, so any outside card that adds an Equip Spell from the Deck or GY keeps the engine online.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Evil Eye monster is a Fiend, and 'Evil Eye Reemergence' locks your Special Summons to Fiends for the turn, so Fiend-only support never clashes with the deck.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: 'Serziel, Watcher of the Evil Eye' and 'Medusa, Watcher of the Evil Eye' both add an Evil Eye card when Normal Summoned, so an extra Normal Summon each turn turns those triggers into a second search.

hooks.label: Low-LP payoffs
hooks.why: 'Evil Eye of Selene' bleeds 500 LP on every activation and 'Evil Eye of Gorgoneio' gives the equipped monster ATK equal to the LP gap, so the deck deliberately sits with LP are lower than the opponent's.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Fiends
hooks.why: 'Gorgon, Empress of the Evil Eyed' and 'Zerrziel, Ruler of the Evil Eyed' need bodies for Link Material, and 'Evil Eye Reemergence' forbids non-Fiend Special Summons for the turn, so self-summoning Fiends are free material.

profile.plan: Wind-Up monsters each carry a once-while-face-up effect you cash in by Normal Summoning them, and the deck shifts Levels and swarms small bodies to Xyz Summon Rank 3, 4 and 5 Machine monsters.

hooks.label: Flip-down reset
hooks.why: Every Wind-Up monster's effect can only be used once while it is face-up, so outside cards like Book of Moon that flip your own Wind-Up face-down let it become a new face-up card and use that effect again.

hooks.label: Level changers
hooks.why: Wind-Up Shark, Soldier, Dog and Warrior only move their own Levels a fixed amount, so outside cards that change Levels give every other Wind-Up the reach to make Rank 3, 4 or 5.

hooks.label: Xyz Material refill
hooks.why: Zenmaister gains 300 ATK per attached material while Zenmaines, Zenmaioh, Zenmaity and Zenmaiday all pay for their effects by detaching, so outside cards that attach extra material keep the toolbox running.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: The deck starts by Normal Summoning a Wind-Up so its once-while-face-up effect, Wind-Up Shark's Special Summon and Wind-Up Factory's search all switch on, so outside cards granting additional Normal Summons start more of them in one turn.

profile.plan: Summons a Synchro Monster, then uses Assault Mode Activate to Tribute it and Special Summon its /Assault Mode boss from the Deck, with trap searchers and Synchro enablers finding the two halves.

hooks.label: Normal Trap searchers/setters
hooks.why: Assault Mode Activate is the deck's key Normal Trap, so outside cards that add or set Normal Traps from the Deck find it when Psi-Reflector or Assault Beast cannot.

hooks.label: Special Summons a Level 1 Psychic
hooks.why: Psi-Reflector is a Level 1 Psychic Tuner whose search effect triggers on any Special Summon, so outside cards that Special Summon a Level 1 Psychic from the Deck or hand start the engine.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 1 Tuners
hooks.why: Psi-Reflector is the deck's Level 1 Tuner; outside Level 1 Tuners that Special Summon themselves from the hand or GY provide the other material for the Synchro Summons that lead into Assault Mode Activate.

hooks.label: Synchro Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Assault Mode Activate and Assault Mode Zero Tribute a Synchro Monster as the cost to Special Summon an /Assault Mode monster; outside Synchro monsters with an effect when Tributed give extra value.

hooks.label: Summons a Synchro from Extra Deck
hooks.why: The deck must Tribute a Synchro Monster for its key Trap; outside cards that Special Summon a Synchro Monster directly from the Extra Deck put that Tribute on the field without assembling materials.

hooks.label: Discards a Beast-Warrior
hooks.why: Assault Beast searches Assault Mode Activate when discarded, so outside cards that discard a Beast-Warrior turn into a search for the deck's key Trap.

profile.plan: A deck of giant 4000-5000 ATK DARK Dragons that can only be Special Summoned by banishing specific Extra Deck monsters, and die instantly unless a Field Spell is kept face-up.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Malefic Cyber End Dragon, Malefic Stardust Dragon and Malefic Truth Dragon all destroy themselves if there is no face-up Field Spell, so anything that adds or places a Field Spell from the Deck keeps the whole board alive.

hooks.label: Field Spell protectors
hooks.why: The deck collapses the moment its Field Spell leaves the field, which is why Malefic Stardust Dragon and Malefic Territory exist only to shield it, so outside cards that stop a Field Spell being destroyed do the same job.

hooks.label: Recycles banished cards
hooks.why: Malefic monsters summon themselves by banishing Cyber End Dragon, Stardust Dragon or Rainbow Dragon from the Extra Deck, Deck or hand, and Malefic Selector banishes Malefic cards from the GY, so returning banished cards to the Deck or hand re-arms the deck.

hooks.label: Ignoring Summoning conditions
hooks.why: Malefic monsters can only be Special Summoned by their own banish procedure, and Malefic Divide and Malefic Paradigm Shift bypass this with 'ignoring its Summoning conditions', so outside cards with the same wording cheat out the 4000-5000 ATK bosses.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Malefic monster, from Malefic Cyber End Dragon to Malefic Truth Dragon, is DARK, so outside cards that support DARK monsters apply to the entire archetype.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster deck whose monsters gain a Level every Standby Phase, so their ATK/DEF grow, and which banishes other Spellcasters to raise Levels, revive Synchro bosses and let Fortune Lady Light float into the Deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Fortune Lady Past banishes Spellcaster monsters from your hand, field and/or GY as cost and Fortune Lady Every banishes a Spellcaster from the GY to revive itself, so a Spellcaster with an effect when it is banished gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: Banishes your own cards
hooks.why: Fortune Vision counters when a card you control is banished by card effect and Fortune's Future and Fortune Lady Rewind only work on banished Fortune Lady monsters, so outside cards that banish your own monsters switch those on.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Fortune Lady monster is a Spellcaster, and both Fortune Lady Past and Fortune Lady Every banish Spellcaster monsters as fuel, so cards that search, revive or boost Spellcasters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Raises a monster's Level
hooks.why: Fortune Lady ATK/DEF are Level x 200 to 400 and Fortune Lady Every banishes a monster off the field off its Level, so outside effects that raise a Spellcaster's Level make every Fortune Lady bigger.

profile.plan: A Warrior Xyz deck that floods the field with Level 4 (and Level 1) Warrior bodies and piles them under Rank 4 Heroic Champions whose ATK doubles and effects scale with their materials.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Heroic monster is a Warrior and each Heroic Champion Xyz Summon demands Warrior materials (Excalibur, Kusanagi, Claivesolish, Rhongomyniad), so any card that searches, revives or boosts Warriors works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Level 4 Warriors
hooks.why: The deck wants cheap extra Level 4 Warrior bodies for its Rank 4 Xyz, the way Assault Halberd and Morning Star Special Summon themselves from the hand.

hooks.label: Level 1 Warrior bodies
hooks.why: Jarngreipr needs 2 Level 1 Warrior materials and Knuckle Sword turns your Warriors into Level 1, so outside Level 1 Warriors that come out on their own extend the Rank 1 line.

hooks.label: Pays your own LP
hooks.why: Claivesolish pays LP down to 500, and Morning Star, Heroic Call and Heroic Envoy all gain extra effects while your LP are 500 or less, so any card that pays LP turns those on.

hooks.label: Warriors into the GY
hooks.why: Jarngreipr revives a Level/Rank 4 Warrior from the GY, Heroic Call Special Summons a Warrior from hand or GY, and Magnum Excalibur shuffles 3 Warriors back, so dumping Warriors in the GY fuels the deck.

hooks.label: Extra Xyz Material
hooks.why: Rhongomyniad gains a new effect for every material attached (5 lets it destroy all your opponent's cards) and Magnum Excalibur pays 2 materials to double its ATK, so cards that attach material to an Xyz Monster are extra value.

profile.plan: A Machine Synchro toolbox whose Genex monsters search each other by Level and whose Synchros demand non-Tuner material of a chosen Attribute, so the deck Normal Summons repeatedly and manipulates Attributes to assemble Genex Controller combos.

hooks.label: Attribute-changing cards
hooks.why: Genex Ally Changer and Genex Ally Chemistrer only exist because Hydro, Windmill, Geo and Thermal Genex demand non-Tuner material of one specific Attribute, and Arms of Genex Return Zero banishes a same-Attribute monster from your GY, so any outside card that rewrites Attributes unlocks those lines.

hooks.label: WATER monsters for the GY
hooks.why: Genex Undine sends a WATER monster from the Deck to the Graveyard to add Genex Controller, so outside WATER monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY are triggered for free.

hooks.label: Opponent's Graveyard banishers
hooks.why: Genex Ally Bellflame places 2 Genex Counters and gains 100 ATK each time a card in the opponent's Graveyard is banished, so outside cards that banish the opponent's Graveyard feed it.

hooks.label: Bounce-ready monsters
hooks.why: Genex Ally Birdman returns a face-up monster you control to the hand to Special Summon itself, so outside monsters with an effect when they are returned to the hand get a free trigger.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon cards
hooks.why: Genex Undine, Genex Neutron, Genex Power Planner, R-Genex Turbo, Genex Ally Crusher, Genex Army and Genex Solar only pay off on a Normal Summon or Tribute Summon, and Repair Genex Controller already hands out one extra Normal Summon, so additional Normal Summons are pure value.

hooks.label: Normal Monster Summoners
hooks.why: Genex Controller, a Level 3 Normal Tuner that every Genex Synchro lists by name, is normally only searched to hand, so outside cards that Special Summon a Normal Monster straight from the Deck put the key Tuner onto the field.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck of EARTH Machine monsters that force themselves into battle and constantly change battle position, triggering draws, banishes, counters and revives, while swarming the field with Karakuri bosses.

hooks.label: EARTH Machine support
hooks.why: Every Karakuri monster is an EARTH Machine, so cards that search, revive or boost EARTH Machine monsters work for the entire deck.

hooks.label: Changes to face-up Defense Position
hooks.why: Bureido draws, Bureibu banishes and Karakuri Anatomy places counters whenever a face-up Karakuri's battle position changes and remains face-up, so cards that switch a monster to face-up Defense Position trigger them.

hooks.label: Special Summons Level 4 or lower Machine from Deck
hooks.why: Karakuri has many low-ATK Machines like Inashichi, Ninishi and Shinkuro, so cards like Machine Duplication that Special Summon Level 4 or lower Machine monsters from the Deck give you extra Synchro materials.

hooks.label: Self-reviving Machine Tuners
hooks.why: Karakuri Synchro Summons need Tuners, and cards like Deskbot 001 that Special Summon themselves from the GY give you extra Tuners without using your Normal Summon.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Fairy deck whose Valkyries protect each other behind a chain of Continuous Spells, manipulate the top of the opponent's Deck and GY, and banish the opponent's cards to pump their own ATK.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Valkyrie monster is a Fairy, and Goddess Skuld's Oracle locks you into Fairy Summons for the turn, so cards that search, revive or boost Fairies work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Continuous Spells for the GY
hooks.why: Valkyrie Funfte sends a Spell/Trap from the Deck to the GY and Valkyrie Sigrun sends a face-up Spell/Trap you control to the GY, so outside Continuous Spells that do something when sent to the GY are dumped for free.

hooks.label: Spells that summon from hand
hooks.why: Valkyrie Erste only triggers when she is Special Summoned from the hand by a Spell effect, exactly what Ride of the Valkyries does, so more Spells that Special Summon a Fairy from hand give her extra uses.

hooks.label: Banishes the opponent's GY
hooks.why: Valkyrie Erste and Apple of Enlightenment banish monsters from the opponent's GY, and Valkyrie Dritte and Valkyrie Funfte each gain ATK for every banished opponent's monster.

hooks.label: Extra Battle Phase attackers
hooks.why: Mischief of the Time Goddess skips straight into another Battle Phase, and Pegasus Wing and Fortune Chariot let your Valkyries attack directly, so cards that reward or repeat a Battle Phase fit the deck's damage plan.

profile.plan: A FIRE deck of 200-DEF monsters that Synchro Summons, thins itself with Firedog and Poun, and grinds the opponent down by banishing their Graveyard and burning for battle damage.

hooks.label: FIRE Attribute support
hooks.why: Every Flamvell monster is FIRE, and the Synchro plays are built from FIRE Tuners and FIRE materials, so anything that supports the FIRE Attribute lifts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Pyro-Type support
hooks.why: Flamvell Archer Tributes a face-up Pyro-Type monster and Ancient Flamvell Deity needs non-Tuner Pyro materials, while most Flamvell monsters are Pyro.

hooks.label: Revives 200 DEF FIRE
hooks.why: The entire archetype is FIRE monsters with 200 DEF, so a mass revival of exactly those monsters (the Rekindling pattern) rebuilds the board after Firedog and Poun have loaded the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Banishes the opponent's GY
hooks.why: Neo Flamvell Sabre, Neo Flamvell Origin and Neo Flamvell Shaman all reward a small opponent Graveyard, and Neo Flamvell Lady triggers whenever a card is banished from the opponent's GY.

hooks.label: FIRE monsters sent to GY
hooks.why: Neo Flamvell Lady and Flamvell Baby send FIRE monsters from the hand to the Graveyard as cost, and Poun, Neo Flamvell Hedgehog and Flamvell Counter all feed on FIRE monsters in the Graveyard.

profile.plan: A Warrior/FIRE Rank-4 Xyz deck that fights the whole Battle Phase, repeatedly detaching Xyz Material for protection, ATK boosts and burn, while reviving its monsters from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Warrior and FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Battlin' Boxer monster is a FIRE Warrior, and King Dempsey itself searches Level 4 or lower FIRE Warrior monsters, so Type and Attribute support reaches the entire deck.

hooks.label: Foolish Burial effects
hooks.why: Glassjaw and Uppercutter both only trigger when a card effect sends them to the Graveyard, and Headgeared already sends a Battlin' Boxer from the Deck to the GY.

hooks.label: Xyz Material feeders
hooks.why: Lead Yoke, Nova Kaiser and King Dempsey all spend Xyz Materials for destruction protection, ATK and targeting immunity, so anything that puts more material on your Xyz Monsters fuels their best effects.

hooks.label: Level changers
hooks.why: Big Bandage and Promoter shift the Levels of your Battlin' Boxer monsters so the deck can reach Rank 3 and Rank 5 Xyz such as Cheat Commissioner, Comet Cestus and General Kaiser.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic cards
hooks.why: Number C105 Comet Cestus and Number C79 General Kaiser only gain their extra effects while they have Star Cestus and Nova Kaiser attached, which is exactly what a Rank-Up Spell supplies.

profile.plan: The deck Special Summons its Level 1 monsters onto the opponent's field in face-down Defense Position, then flips them face-up in the Main Phase so their FLIP effects wreck the opponent's board and hand the monster back, while face-down monsters on the opponent's field lock them out of Normal Summons and feed Giant Mimighoul's destruction and burn.

hooks.label: Flips enemy monsters
hooks.why: Mimighoul Dungeon stops anyone who controls a face-down monster from Normal Summoning or attacking with this turn's Special Summons, Giant Mimighoul attacks directly and destroys face-up cards based on the opponent's face-down count, and Mimighoul Master can flip a face-down monster up in the opponent's Main Phase, so outside position-changers feed every payoff in the deck.

hooks.label: Free Level 1 bodies
hooks.why: Giant Mimighoul and Mimighoul Throne are Rank 1 and need Level 1 material, and the archetype only has one non-Level 1 body, so outside Level 1 monsters that put themselves on the field are extra Xyz material.

hooks.label: Fills the opponent's field
hooks.why: Mimighoul Slime and Mimighoul Armor only Special Summon themselves face-up when your opponent controls more monsters than you or any monster at all, Mimighoul Flower wants a face-down monster on the field, and Giant Mimighoul scales off the opponent's face-down monsters, so outside cards that hand the opponent bodies turn those on.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Mimighoul monster, including the Rank 1 Xyz monsters, is EARTH, so outside cards that search, revive, protect or boost EARTH monsters work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A defensive Spellcaster toolbox of Level 1-5 girls that punish attacks by swapping in another Spellcaster and halving the attacker's ATK, backed by hand-discard boosts and Graveyard recovery.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Magician Girl is a Spellcaster, and Chocolate Magician Girl, Lemon Magician Girl and Performapal Sky Magician Girl all specifically name Spellcaster-Type monsters in their effects, so anything that searches, revives or boosts Spellcasters powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Spellcasters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Chocolate Magician Girl discards 1 Spellcaster-Type monster as a cost to draw, so an outside Spellcaster monster with an effect that triggers when it is discarded gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcasters that want milling
hooks.why: Performapal Sky Magician Girl sends 1 Level 4 or lower LIGHT Spellcaster monster from the Deck to the GY when Special Summoned, so a LIGHT Spellcaster with a Graveyard trigger is free value.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell enablers
hooks.why: Performapal Sky Magician Girl Special Summons itself from the hand while you control a Continuous Spell, so cards that fetch or place a Continuous Spell turn her on.

hooks.label: Spellcaster dumpers
hooks.why: Chocolate Magician Girl revives a Spellcaster-Type monster from the Graveyard and Apple Magician Girl recovers Magician Girls from there, so outside cards that send Spellcaster-Type monsters from the Deck to the GY set those plays up.

profile.plan: A coin-toss deck that summons Fairy/LIGHT monsters with 'Arcana Force' effects, using Light Barrier to pick the Heads results, aiming to skip the opponent's turn with The World or summon huge Level 10 bosses.

hooks.label: Coin tossing cards
hooks.why: The deck's Level 7 monster Special Summons itself while a card with a coin tossing effect is on the field, and the Level 10 Fusion can add such a card from the Deck.

hooks.label: Coin toss redo
hooks.why: The whole deck hinges on coin toss results, so being able to redo a bad Tails is powerful.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Fairy, so cards that search, revive or boost Fairies work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is LIGHT, so LIGHT support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: The Level 8 monster can be Tribute Summoned and the Level 4 monster can be treated as two Tributes, so cards that help Tribute Summon speed up the deck.

profile.plan: An Xyz toolbox that summons Rank 4 and Rank 5 'Number' monsters and pays for effect after effect by detaching materials, then refills those materials or recurs the monsters.

hooks.label: ZW - Equip Monsters
hooks.why: Ultimate Leo Utopia Ray and Ultimate Dragonic Utopia Ray equip a 'ZW -' monster straight from the Deck or Extra Deck, so including ZW monsters turns those Numbers into free equips and effect negations.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when detached
hooks.why: Almost every Number effect pays by detaching Xyz material (Utopia Dragonar detaches 2, the Utopia Rays, C32, Spider Shark and Buzzking each detach 1), so monsters with an effect when they are detached or used as material get used for free.

hooks.label: Xyz Material replenishers
hooks.why: The Numbers burn through materials quickly because nearly every effect detaches, so cards that attach cards to an Xyz Monster as material keep them alive and loaded.

hooks.label: LIGHT Warrior support
hooks.why: The Utopia half of the Extra Deck - Number 99, Number F0, both Ultimate Utopia Rays, Utopia Rising and Emissary of Light - is entirely LIGHT Warriors, so LIGHT/Warrior support reaches most of the deck's boss monsters.

hooks.label: Xyz Material Spell/Trap support
hooks.why: The deck is built entirely around Xyz Material - detaching it for every effect, attaching the opponent's monsters with Silent Honor ARK and Buzzking, and moving it between monsters with Utopia Rising - so cards that interact with Xyz Material fit the whole strategy.

profile.plan: A Thunder/LIGHT deck of low-ATK monsters that attack directly, trigger on battle damage, and Synchro Summon using Tuners plus non-Tuner Thunder monsters.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Almost every monster in this deck is a Thunder-Type, and the Synchro Monsters require non-Tuner Thunder monsters, so cards that support Thunder-Type monsters fit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Grants direct attacks
hooks.why: Many of this deck's monsters only trigger when they inflict battle damage by a direct attack, so cards that let your Thunder or LIGHT monsters attack directly enable those effects.

hooks.label: Battle damage triggers
hooks.why: Most of this deck's effects trigger when a monster inflicts battle damage by a direct attack, so outside cards that trigger when the opponent takes battle damage stack with them.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder triggers
hooks.why: One of this deck's Tuners Tributes itself and non-Tuner monsters from your hand or field to Special Summon a Synchro Monster, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed are free material.

hooks.label: Summons low-Level Thunder
hooks.why: This deck's Continuous Trap punishes the Summon of Level 4 or lower Thunder monsters and its Spell wants differently named Thunder monsters on field, so outside cards that Special Summon low-Level Thunder monsters help.

profile.plan: An Xyz ladder of LIGHT Machines and EARTH Rocks that floods the field with self-Special-Summoning Level 3 to 6 monsters, shifts their Levels to hit an exact Rank, then turns detach effects into burn, ATK-crushing and negation.

hooks.label: Level 5 and 6 extenders
hooks.why: Chronomaly Vimana and Number 33: Chronomaly Machu Mech both need 2 Level 5 monsters and Number 6: Chronomaly Atlandis needs 2 Level 6 monsters, so outside Level 5/6 monsters that Special Summon themselves are Xyz material that never costs your Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Attaches itself as Xyz material
hooks.why: Chronomaly Vimana attaches a monster from the GY to itself as material and Chronomaly Temple - Trilithon can send itself to the GY in place of a detach, so outside cards that attach themselves from the GY keep the Xyz engine fed.

hooks.label: Level changing effects
hooks.why: Chronomaly Golden Jet raises every Chronomaly monster's Level by 1 and Chronomaly Sol Monolith sets one to Level 6, so outside effects that change a monster's Level let the deck reach the exact Rank for its Rank 3, 4, 5 or 6 Xyz Monsters.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Chronomaly Xyz Monster — Vimana, Machu Mech, Atlandis, Chateau Huyuk and Crystal Chrononaut — is a Machine, so Machine-type support searches, revives or protects the deck's bosses.

hooks.label: Shrinks an opponent's monster
hooks.why: Number 36: Chronomaly Chateau Huyuk destroys any opponent's monster whose current ATK differs from its original ATK and Number 33: Chronomaly Machu Mech burns for that same difference, so outside cards that lower an opponent's monster's ATK turn both effects on.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Chronomaly Temple - Trilithon pays 500 LP for an extra Normal Summon of a Chronomaly monster, and Chronomaly Nebra Disk, Gordian Knot, Winged Sphinx and Mayan Machine all trigger when Normal Summoned, so outside effects that grant extra Normal Summons get more of those triggers per turn.

profile.plan: Turns the opponent's monsters' ATK to 0, then cashes them in: searching Reptile monsters, drawing, stealing, destroying, Tributing them for Vaskii and Synchro Summoning DARK Reptile bosses.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Reptilianne monster is a Reptile, and Echidna and Melusine both search Reptile monsters from the Deck, so Type support reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Zeroes out ATK
hooks.why: Echidna's search, Viper's take-control, Hydra's destroy-and-draw and Vaskii's Summon all require face-up monsters with 0 ATK, and the archetype can only zero one monster at a time.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Medusa and Ramifications send 1 card from your hand to the Graveyard as their cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with Reptiles
hooks.why: Nyami needs a Reptile in your GY to activate and Recoil needs a DARK Reptile in the GY to revive, so outside cards that send Reptiles from the Deck to the GY switch both on.

profile.plan: A pair of LIGHT and DARK Field Spells that swap each other out, with LIGHT/DARK paired monsters that Tribute themselves to tag in their counterpart from the Deck and fuse into 3000 ATK bosses.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Dream Mirror of Joy and Dream Mirror of Terror must sit in the Field Zone for any Dream Mirror Quick Effect or Field Spell bonus to apply, and each one banishes itself to fetch the other, so cards that find or place a Field Spell are the deck's real consistency engine.

hooks.label: Field Spell protection
hooks.why: Every Dream Mirror monster needs its Field Spell in the Field Zone to Tribute itself, so cards that keep a Field Spell from being destroyed or removed keep the whole archetype switched on, exactly what Dream Mirror Fantasy and Dream Mirror Recap already try to do.

hooks.label: Field Spell recovery
hooks.why: Dream Mirror of Joy and Dream Mirror of Terror banish themselves from the Field Zone to fetch each other, so outside cards that pull a banished or Graveyard Field Spell back to the hand, Deck or Field restart the loop that Dream Mirror Recap does internally.

hooks.label: LIGHT and DARK support
hooks.why: Every Dream Mirror monster is LIGHT or DARK, the Field Spells only apply while you control a Dream Mirror monster of the matching Attribute, and the Oneiros Fusions need two Dream Mirror monsters with different Attributes, so cards that work with LIGHT and DARK monsters help every line.

profile.plan: A Water Dragon combo deck: it digs out the Dinosaurs Hydrogeddon, Oxygeddon and Duoterion, feeds them to the Bonding Spell/Trap line (Tributed from the hand and field, or shuffled out of the GY) and cheats out Water Dragon / Water Dragon Cluster, which then refill the field with the materials from the GY.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Hydrogeddon, Oxygeddon, Duoterion and Carboneddon are all Dinosaurs, and every Bonding Spell/Trap asks for those names in the hand, field or GY, so anything that searches, revives or recycles a Dinosaur finds the materials.

hooks.label: Mills Dinosaurs into the GY
hooks.why: Water Dragon revives 2 Hydrogeddon and 1 Oxygeddon from the GY, Duoterion revives one of the three on Summon, and Bonding - DHO shuffles them back out of the GY, so every Dinosaur sent to the GY becomes material.

hooks.label: Mills Bonding Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Bonding - D2O returns itself to the hand from the GY once Water Dragon or Water Dragon Cluster leaves the field, and Bonding - DHO banishes itself from the GY to add a Water Dragon, so sending the Bonding Spell/Trap line to the GY turns on their graveyard effects.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Magnet Bonding Fusion Summons a Rock Fusion Monster by shuffling Rock monsters from your hand, field, GY and banishment into the Deck, so Rock searchers, millers and revival cards feed that second axis.

profile.plan: A Pendulum Spellcaster deck that farms Spell Counters on your own field every time a Spell Card resolves, then removes them to negate monster effects, banish monsters, Special Summon Mythical Beasts and shrink attackers.

hooks.label: Spell Counter generators
hooks.why: Every Mythical Beast effect pays by removing Spell Counters from your field while only making them when a Spell resolves, so outside cards that place Spell Counters directly are the deck's fuel.

hooks.label: Spell Counter-holding Spellcasters
hooks.why: Master Cerberus, Jackal King and Medusa all remove Spell Counters from your field, and Medusa's Pendulum effect revives a monster in your GY that can hold a Spell Counter, so outside Spellcaster monsters that carry counters are both batteries and revive targets.

hooks.label: Spells that return from the GY
hooks.why: The whole archetype only gains Spell Counters when a Spell Card resolves, so outside Spell Cards that put themselves back into the hand from the GY can be activated over and over for free counters.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: All six Mythical Beasts are Spellcaster monsters, so any card that specifically helps Spellcasters works on the entire deck.

profile.plan: A graveyard-and-banished toolbox: every Nemeses monster Special Summons itself from the hand by shuffling one of your banished monsters back into the Deck, and Archnemeses Protos cashes three banished monsters of different Attributes into a board-wide Attribute wipe.

hooks.label: Banishes your GY monsters
hooks.why: Every Nemeses monster Special Summons itself from the hand by shuffling one of your banished monsters into the Deck, so outside cards that banish monsters from your GY or field create the banished targets the deck runs on.

hooks.label: Banishes itself from the GY
hooks.why: The Nemeses pay for their own Special Summon by shuffling a banished monster back into the Deck, so a monster that banishes itself from the GY is both that cost and, with Keystone and Adrastea, a card that comes back.

hooks.label: Banishes from the Deck
hooks.why: The Nemeses all Special Summon themselves from the hand by shuffling one of your banished monsters into the Deck, so a card that banishes a monster straight from the Deck hands the engine a target without spending a card.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: Archnemeses Protos pays by banishing three monsters from the GY and/or face-up field and Keystone banishes itself, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished get their trigger while fueling the engine.

hooks.label: Revives from the banished pile
hooks.why: Nemeses Adrastea already Special Summons a banished or Graveyard Nemeses, and the deck's monsters end up banished after paying costs, so outside cards that Special Summon from the banished pile extend the same plays.

profile.plan: A Fish/WATER Synchro deck that banishes its own monsters as cost and fuel, then brings them back from the banished pile on later Standby Phases, Synchro Summoning on the opponent's turn with its Level 2 Fish Tuners.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Fish
hooks.why: Psiics, Zep, Snopios, Eanoc and Ghoti Chain all banish Fish monsters from the hand, field or GY as their cost, and every Ghoti monster has an effect that triggers when it is banished.

hooks.label: Banished-payoff monsters
hooks.why: The deck banishes its own monsters constantly with Paces, Shif, Zep and Ghoti Chain, so outside monsters that do something when they are banished get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Fish support
hooks.why: Every Ghoti monster is a Fish, and Arionpos, Psiics and Eanoc all add Fish monsters from the Deck, so cards that search or revive Fish work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Revives banished Fish
hooks.why: Eanoc Special Summons a banished Level 4 or lower Fish monster and Ghoti Chain Special Summons a banished Ghoti monster, so outside cards that reach into the banished pile to summon Fish extend those plays.

profile.plan: A Thunder/LIGHT swarm deck that Normal Summons its monsters to trigger searches and Special Summons, then uses the Graveyard to revive or banish Thunder monsters for big plays.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Every Batteryman monster is a Thunder-Type, and Batteryman Solar, Industrial Strength and D all reference Thunder monsters, so generic Thunder support advances the whole deck.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: All Batteryman monsters are LIGHT, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT monsters work on the entire archetype.

hooks.label: Thunder GY triggers
hooks.why: Batteryman Solar sends a Thunder monster from the Deck to the GY, so outside Thunder monsters that trigger when sent to the GY get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Thunder banish triggers
hooks.why: Batteryman Industrial Strength banishes Thunder monsters from the GY as a cost, so outside Thunder monsters that trigger when banished turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Batteryman Charger, 9-Volt and AAA all trigger when Normal Summoned, so effects that grant an extra Normal Summon let you use more of them in one turn.

hooks.label: Mills Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Batteryman Industrial Strength and Battery Charger need Thunder monsters in the GY, so outside cards that send Thunder monsters from the Deck to the GY set up those plays.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck built around Equip Spells: Power Tool Dragon and Braver Dragon fetch and attach them, Ultimaya Tzolkin cheats out Power Tool or Level 7/8 Dragon Synchros when you Set a Spell/Trap, and Double Tool C&D plus Power Break turn the equipped state into damage.

hooks.label: Equip Spell search
hooks.why: Power Tool Dragon only reveals three Equip Spells from the Deck, so outside cards that add an Equip Spell to the hand give the deck more consistent access.

hooks.label: Sets Spell/Trap
hooks.why: Ultimaya Tzolkin Special Summons a Power Tool Synchro or Level 7/8 Dragon Synchro whenever a Spell/Trap is Set on your side of the field, so cards that Set from the Deck or GY trigger it.

hooks.label: Level changers
hooks.why: Ultimaya Tzolkin needs two Level 5 or higher monsters with the same Level, so effects that change a monster's Level help line up the material.

profile.plan: A Sacred Beast deck that Special Summons its three Level 10 bosses (Fiend, Thunder and Pyro) from the hand, Deck, GY and banishment by discarding and sending its own cards to the GY, then closes with 4000-ATK beats and their three-material Fusion.

hooks.label: Level 10 no-Tribute bosses
hooks.why: Sacred Beasts Released adds a Level 10 Pyro, Thunder or Fiend monster that cannot be Normal Summoned/Set from the Deck, Phantasmal Summoning Beast Special Summons one from hand, and the Phantasm Fusion needs three such monsters as material.

hooks.label: Discard-payoff monsters
hooks.why: Summoner of the Sacred Beasts and Sacred Beasts Released discard cards as a cost, and each Sacred Beast can be revealed to add a card then discard 1, so any monster that does something when discarded is paid for.

hooks.label: Sent-to-GY payoff monsters
hooks.why: Fallen Paradise of the Sacred Beasts sends 3 same-type cards from your hand and/or face-up field to the GY, so monsters that trigger when sent to the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: Fills the GYs with Traps
hooks.why: Uria gains 1000 ATK/DEF for each Trap in either GY, and the deck already loads Continuous Spells/Traps, so effects that send Traps to the GY make Uria enormous.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Raviel, Martyr of the Sacred Beasts, Phantasmal Summoning Beast and the Fusion are all Fiends, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends serve the deck's core.

profile.plan: Excavates the top of the Deck to send Plant monsters to the GY, triggering effects that revive, search, destroy and Xyz Summon.

hooks.label: Plant-Type support
hooks.why: Every Sylvan monster is a Plant-Type, so cards that search, revive or boost Plants work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Plant monsters with GY effects
hooks.why: Sylvan effects excavate and send Plant monsters from the Deck to the GY, and cards like Mount Sylvania and Orea send them from hand or field to the GY, so any Plant that triggers when sent there gets value.

hooks.label: Excavates your Deck
