hooks.why: Sylvan monsters like Hermitree and Cherubsprout only trigger their GY effects when they are excavated and sent to the GY by a card effect, so any outside card that excavates starts them off.

hooks.label: Stacks the top of the Deck
hooks.why: Excavation only sends Plant monsters to the GY if they are on top, so cards that place a Plant monster from your GY on top of the Deck guarantee the next Sylvan effect.

hooks.label: Sends Plants to the GY
hooks.why: Mount Sylvania and Orea send Plant monsters from the hand or field to the GY as cost, so outside cards that do the same keep the GY full and trigger 'sent to the GY' effects.

hooks.label: Revives Plant monsters
hooks.why: The deck fills the GY with Plant monsters via excavation and costs, so outside cards that Special Summon a Plant from the GY provide material for Sylvan Princessprite, Dancepione or Orea.

profile.plan: A combo deck that swarms the field with Warrior/DARK 'Flower Cardian' monsters, often Special Summoning them by Tributing each other or ignoring their Summoning conditions, to Synchro Summon into Level 6, 8 and 10 Warrior Synchro monsters with powerful control effects.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Flower Cardian monster is a Warrior, so outside cards that support Warriors work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Flower Cardian monster is DARK, so outside cards that support DARK monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Deck stacking
hooks.why: Flower Cardian monsters draw and reveal cards, needing a Flower Cardian on top to get their bonus, and Flower Stacking places three on top; outside cards that look at or reorder the top of the Deck make those draws reliable.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Pine and Zebra Grass have effects when Normal Summoned, and other Flower Cardian monsters can be Normal Summoned and then Tributed to Special Summon a larger one, so an extra Normal Summon starts the combo.

hooks.label: Synchro material recycling
hooks.why: The deck Synchro Summons using many Flower Cardian monsters, and outside cards that return a Synchro to the Extra Deck and Special Summon its materials from the GY let you Synchro Summon again.

hooks.label: Synchro swapping
hooks.why: The deck has multiple Synchro Monsters of the same Level (e.g., Boardefly and Moonflowerviewing are both Level 6), so outside cards that trade a Synchro for another of the same Level fit.

profile.plan: A Pendulum archetype of Machine Flip monsters that hides itself in face-down Defense Position and flips up on the opponent's turn for Quick Effect negations, building E.C. Counters that Enneapolis cashes in for burn.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-up
hooks.why: Every Enneacraft Pendulum Effect places an E.C. Counter each time a monster is flipped face-up, and Enneapolis lets you return or Pendulum-place an Enneacraft that is flipped face-up during the Main Phase, so outside cards that flip your set monsters up trigger both.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-down
hooks.why: The negation Quick Effects of Atori.MAR, Asta.PIXEA, Archa.TAIL, Atil.SPIA and the rest only work while the card itself is face-down, so an outside card that turns your face-up Enneacraft face-down re-arms them.

hooks.label: Face-down Special Summon
hooks.why: Every Enneacraft's hand effect locks you into Special Summoning only in face-down Defense Position for the rest of the turn, so outside cards that Special Summon a monster face-down Defense Position add bodies without breaking the lock.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: All fourteen Enneacraft monsters are Machine, so cards that search, revive or boost Machines cover the whole deck, LIGHT and EARTH halves alike.

hooks.label: Flip monster support
hooks.why: The Main Deck Enneacraft are all Flip monsters whose FLIP effects only fire when they are flipped face-up, so outside cards that support Flip monsters feed the deck's main line.

hooks.label: Extra Deck Pendulum recovery
hooks.why: Enneacraft Release banishes itself from the GY to add a face-up 'Enneacraft' monster from the Extra Deck to the hand, and every Enneacraft that leaves the field goes face-up to the Extra Deck, so outside cards that recover Pendulum monsters from the Extra Deck recycle the same pool.

profile.plan: Level 3 and 4 EARTH Rock 'Magnet Warrior' monsters that search each other, Special Summon from the Deck, and revive from the Graveyard, assembling three named pieces into the Level 8 Magna Warrior bosses.

hooks.label: EARTH Rock support
hooks.why: Every Magnet Warrior is an EARTH Rock monster — Magnetic Field only works while you control a Level 4 or lower EARTH Rock monster, Omega Plus destroys a Rock monster as its cost, and Sigma Minus Fusion Summons using Rock monsters from the hand.

hooks.label: Sends Rock monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Delta and Sigma Plus both have effects that trigger when they are sent to the GY, and Delta needs three Level 4 or lower Magnet Warriors in the GY to bring out Valkyrion.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Rock monsters
hooks.why: Omega Plus destroys 1 other Rock monster in your hand or face-up field to Special Summon itself, and Sigma Minus needs Rock monsters in the hand as Fusion material, so Rock monsters that bring themselves out keep bodies and material available.

hooks.label: Low-Level EARTH Rock Summoners
hooks.why: Magnetic Field only works while you control a Level 4 or lower EARTH Rock monster and Gamma's Summon trigger Special Summons from the hand, so outside cards that put Level 4 or lower EARTH Rock monsters onto the field from the Deck keep the engine and the Tribute/fusion fodder coming.

hooks.label: Rock monsters with destruction triggers
hooks.why: Omega Plus destroys 1 other Rock monster in your hand or face-up field to Special Summon itself, so any Rock monster that has an effect when it is destroyed turns that cost into extra value.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of EARTH Machine monsters that can Normal Summon themselves for free, but only unlocks its bounce, burn, double-attack and low-Level immunity payoffs by Tribute Summoning the big Qli forms.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summon enablers
hooks.why: Qliphort Stealth, Disk, Shell and Cephalopod only get their effects when Tribute Summoned (and Carrier and Helix trigger when Tributed), so cards that grant extra Tribute Summons or stand-in Tributes are the engine this deck needs.

hooks.label: Level 5 Normal Monster searchers
hooks.why: Qliphort Scout and Qliphort Monolith are both Level 5 Normal Monsters, so cards that add a Level 5 or higher Normal Monster from the Deck grab the deck's starter and its best Pendulum Scale.

hooks.label: Machine-Type support
hooks.why: Every Qli monster is a Machine and Qliphort Genius is a Link-2 that needs 2 Machine monsters as material, so generic Machine support applies to the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Rank-Up Xyz deck built on the Number 101–107 monsters and their 'Number C' upgrades: it searches Rank-Up-Magic Quick-Play Spells, banishes and Tributes its own Xyz Monsters, then revives them from the GY or banishment.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Quick-Play Spells
hooks.why: Seventh Ascension takes a Rank-Up-Magic Quick-Play Spell from the Deck and Seventh Force adds one from the Deck, so every such Spell is a live payoff the archetype can pull out.

hooks.label: Number Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Seventh Tachyon needs a 'Number' Xyz Monster with 101–107 in its name, and Seventh Eternity, Seventh Force and Rebirth of the Seventh Emperors all target or attach your Number Xyz Monsters.

hooks.label: Xyz Material refill
hooks.why: Seventh Eternity detaches all materials from the targeted Xyz Monster to revive a Number, and Rebirth of the Seventh Emperors attaches Number monsters as material, so extra Xyz Material is fuel for both.

hooks.label: Xyz Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Rebirth of the Seventh Emperors Tributes all Xyz Monsters you control as its activation cost, so an Xyz Monster with an effect when Tributed gives value for a cost the deck would pay anyway.

profile.plan: Turn HERO monsters on the field into Masked HERO Fusion Monsters with Mask Change, lock the opponent's Graveyard and hand with Dark Law, and keep reviving the Fusions from the Graveyard and banishment.

hooks.label: Dumps Extra Deck Fusions
hooks.why: Legacy of a HERO returns 2 Fusion Monsters from the GY to the Extra Deck to draw 3, and Masked HERO Atomic revives a Masked HERO from the GY or banishment, so anything that sends your own Fusion Monsters to the GY feeds both.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Masked HERO Furnace reveals itself to add "Mask Change" or "Polymerization" and then discards a card, so monsters that gain an effect when they are discarded get that value for free.

hooks.label: Punishes the opponent's searches
hooks.why: Masked HERO Dark Law banishes 1 random card from the opponent's hand whenever they add a card from the Deck to the hand, so outside cards that punish the same search make the lock airtight.

hooks.label: Recycles Quick-Play Spells
hooks.why: Masked HERO Atomic Sets a "Change" Quick-Play Spell from the GY during the End Phase, so outside cards that put or reuse Quick-Play Spells in the GY keep the deck's Mask Change engine running.

profile.plan: Make a Level 1 "Majestic Dragon" Tuner meet Stardust Dragon (or another Dragon Synchro) to Synchro Summon the Majestic bosses, which negate, banish and copy whatever the opponent does.

hooks.label: Stardust Dragon cards
hooks.why: Majestic Star Dragon names "Stardust Dragon" as material and Majestic Absorption and Majestic Mirage only work on "Stardust Dragon" or a Synchro Monster that mentions it.

hooks.label: Summons Level 1 monsters
hooks.why: The Synchro line starts from the Level 1 Majestic Dragon or from Converging Wills Dragon, so anything that Special Summons a Level 1 monster gets the combo going.

profile.plan: A WATER-leaning Xyz toolbox that equips Xyz Monsters from the field and GY to other monsters as Equip Spells, detaches materials as costs, and ladders Rank 3/4 bodies into bigger Xyz bosses.

hooks.label: Fish, Aqua and Sea Serpent support
hooks.why: Armored Shark is a Fish that Special Summons a Fish from the GY, and Xyz Poseidon Splash Special Summons a Fish, Sea Serpent or Aqua monster from the GY.

hooks.label: Xyz Monsters with GY triggers
hooks.why: Armored Shark sends a WATER Xyz Monster from the Extra Deck to the GY, so outside Xyz Monsters that do something when sent to the GY get that for free.

hooks.label: Revives Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Armored Xyz and Full-Armored Xyz turn an Xyz Monster in the GY into an Equip Spell, so extra ways to Special Summon an Xyz Monster from the GY give the deck more targets to equip.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic cards
hooks.why: Xyz Force and Xyz Poseidon Splash both need an Xyz Monster that has an Xyz Monster as material, and CXyz Hope Chaos Barian Dragon evolves a Number C monster.

hooks.label: Number / Utopia support
hooks.why: Endless Bond revives Number 39: Utopia and rewards LIGHT Utopia and Utopic Xyz Monsters, and Unbreakable Xyz Barrier attaches them from the GY.

profile.plan: Places its own monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as face-up Continuous Spells, pays 2000 LP to Special Summon them and search, then uses Millennium Ankh to show five 'Forbidden One' cards and bring out 'The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate'.

hooks.label: Adds Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Millennium Ankh needs five 'Forbidden One' cards shown from the hand, Deck or field, and the four Exodia limbs are Normal Monsters, so anything that adds or Special Summons Normal Monsters from the Deck assembles the requirement.

hooks.label: Illusion monster support
hooks.why: Maiden of the Millennium Moon and Fiend Reflection of the Millennium are Illusion monsters, and Maiden's protection effect names Illusion monsters, so search, revival and boosting cards for the Illusion Type work on them.

hooks.label: Life Point gain
hooks.why: Every Millennium monster can Special Summon itself from the Spell & Trap Zone only by paying 2000 LP (or revealing Millennium Ankh), so outside Life Point gain keeps the engine affordable over several turns.

hooks.label: Forbidden One / Exodia support
hooks.why: Millennium Ankh shows five 'Forbidden One' cards to Special Summon 'The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate', so outside cards that read 'Forbidden One' feed the same win condition.

profile.plan: A WATER Fish Synchro deck that keeps reviving its own Fish from the GY and turning them into Tuners, climbing into White Aura Synchros that wipe the opponent's board and come back from the dead.

hooks.label: Fish support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck monster and every White Aura Synchro is a Fish, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Fish powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is WATER, and the Synchro requirements ask for WATER Tuners and WATER non-Tuners, so WATER-only support always fits.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Every White Aura monster revives itself by banishing 1 other WATER monster from your GY, so outside monsters that do something when banished from the GY get that for free.

hooks.label: Revives Fish from the GY
hooks.why: White Sunfish, White Aura Porpoise, White Circle Reef and Arbitration of White all Special Summon Fish out of the GY and then treat them as Tuners, so more GY revivals for Fish keep the Synchro climb going.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of 500 ATK EARTH Machines that floods the field with Deskbots, pumps every Machine it controls, and turns its own Pendulum Zone destruction into Deck summons, revival and recovery.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Deskbot is a Machine, and Deskbot 002 and Deskbot Base give +500 ATK/DEF to Machine monsters you control, so Machine search, revival and boost cards lift the whole board.

hooks.label: Mass Machine Special Summon
hooks.why: Deskbot 001 revives itself from the GY when 2 or more Machine monsters are Special Summoned at the same time, and the deck wants a wide Machine board for Deskbot 002, 003 and 009.

hooks.label: Destroys your own cards
hooks.why: Deskbot 005 and Deskbot 006 both trigger when they are destroyed while in the Pendulum Zone, reviving or recovering a Deskbot, so any effect that destroys a card you control turns a Scale into advantage.

hooks.label: Field Spell support
hooks.why: Deskbot Base is the archetype's own Field Spell, boosting every Deskbot and fuelling hand fixes and the game-ending banish, so cards that fetch or protect Field Spells keep the deck's engine online.

profile.plan: Summon Rank 4 and Rank 6 Dragon/FIRE Evolzar Xyz Monsters using Dinosaur-Type monsters as material, and use their detach effects to negate and destroy the opponent's cards.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: All Evolzar Xyz Monsters require Dinosaur-Type monsters as Xyz Material, so cards that search, revive, or support Dinosaurs help assemble the needed materials.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Material
hooks.why: The Evolzar monsters detach Xyz Material for their negation and destruction effects, so cards that attach more material let them keep using those effects.

hooks.label: Special Summons Dinosaurs
hooks.why: The deck needs to gather two Dinosaurs of the same Level quickly, so cards that Special Summon Dinosaur-Type monsters from the Deck or hand accelerate the Xyz Summon.

profile.plan: A WIND Spellcaster deck that Special Summons its monsters from hand and Deck to Synchro Summon Level 7 and 8 WIND Synchro Monsters, using burn damage to trigger destruction effects.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning WIND monsters
hooks.why: The deck Special Summons multiple WIND monsters from hand to Synchro Summon, and the WIND lock means any outside WIND monster that Special Summons itself from hand is another body.

hooks.label: Effect damage dealers
hooks.why: One of the Synchro Monsters can destroy a card whenever your opponent takes effect damage, so any outside card that inflicts effect damage triggers it.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is WIND, and the deck's effects lock you into Special Summoning only WIND monsters, so outside cards that support WIND monsters fit the whole deck.

hooks.label: WIND Spellcaster support
hooks.why: All monsters in the archetype are Spellcaster/WIND, so cards that support both that Type and Attribute work on every monster in the deck.

profile.plan: Ritual Summon the Demise and Ruin bosses — even straight from the Deck — by Tributing exact-Level material, then use Demise's 2000-LP effect to blow up the whole field.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: Every Demise and Ruin boss is a Ritual Monster that End of the World, Cycle of the World or Turning of the World Ritual Summons, so cards that add a Ritual Monster from the Deck are the deck's setup.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: The deck can only Ritual Summon through its Ritual Spells, and Turning of the World even Ritual Summons from the Deck, so cards that fetch a Ritual Spell are pure consistency.

hooks.label: Other Ritual Monsters
hooks.why: Demise, Supreme King and Ruin, Supreme Queen only get their extra effects if every monster used for the Ritual Summon was a Ritual Monster, and Supreme King protects all your Ritual Monsters, so outside Ritual Monsters are both material and protected boss monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: End of the World Tributes monsters from the hand or field and Cycle of the World Tributes from the field as material, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Ritual material from the GY
hooks.why: Cycle of the World, End of the World and Turning of the World all need Ritual Summon material, and Supreme King and Supreme Queen reward using Ritual Monsters, so cards that banish themselves from the GY to count as Ritual material slot straight in.

hooks.label: Fiend and Fairy support
hooks.why: Every boss is either a Fiend/DARK Demise or a Fairy/LIGHT Ruin, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends and Fairies work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A WATER Fish/Sea Serpent/Aqua deck that floods the field with Level 7 bodies and low-Level GY fodder to Xyz Summon "Number" and Atlantean/Mermail bosses, then recycles them from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Fish, Sea Serpent, Aqua support
hooks.why: Every Abyss- monster is Fish, Sea Serpent or Aqua, and Abyss-steam even counts the different Types among them to draw.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Poseidra Abyss's GY effect and Abyssrhine both discard a card to the GY as a cost, so monsters with an effect when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: Sends WATER to the GY
hooks.why: Nephilabyss Special Summons itself from the GY when a monster is sent from the hand or Deck to the GY, and Poseidra Abyss and Abyssrhine rely on putting WATER monsters there.

hooks.label: Sends WATER to activate
hooks.why: Mermail King - Neptabyss searches an "Abyss-" Equip Spell whenever a WATER monster is sent to the GY to activate a card or effect.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck that repeatedly Ritual Summons WATER Ritual Monsters using Gishki Ritual Spells, where Gishki Shadow, Vision and Grimness each count as the whole material requirement, and their Ritual Monsters shuffle, bounce and negate as they come back to the hand.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: Every Gishki Ritual Summon needs a Ritual Spell plus a Ritual Monster, and Gishki Shadow and Gishki Vision each only fetch a 'Gishki' one; generic Ritual tutors get the Ritual Monsters and Ritual Spells the deck still lacks.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Every Gishki monster and every Gishki Ritual Monster is WATER, and Evigishki Neremanas revives a WATER monster from the Graveyard, so Attribute-wide support reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: GY Ritual materials
hooks.why: Gishki Aquamirror, Gishki Nekromirror and Forbidden Arts of the Gishki Tribute monsters for a Ritual Summon almost every turn, so a monster that banishes itself from the Graveyard as Ritual material supplies a Level for free.

hooks.label: Opponent's Tokens
hooks.why: Gishki Nekromirror can Tribute 1 face-up monster your opponent controls and Forbidden Arts of the Gishki Tributes face-up monsters from anywhere on the field, so granting the opponent Tokens hands you free Ritual material.

profile.plan: A DARK Machine Synchro deck that punishes LIGHT monsters with battle effects and locks, while using discard costs and Normal Monster support to extend.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Ally of Justice monster is a Machine, so cards that search, revive or boost Machines work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Ally of Justice monster is DARK, so cards that support DARK monsters can search or revive them.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Cyclone Creator, Searcher and Decisive Armor all discard or send cards from your hand to the Graveyard as a cost, so outside monsters that trigger when discarded or sent there get used for free.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: The deck runs two Normal Monsters, Clausolas and Ally Mind, so cards that support Normal Monsters can search or revive them.

profile.plan: Set your Toy monsters from the hand into the Spell & Trap Zone as Spells, then send or destroy those face-down cards so they Special Summon themselves, using Toy Box to fetch them, pop the opponent's attackers, and clear your own back row.

hooks.label: Pops your own Set Spells
hooks.why: Toy Soldier and Toy Tank both read 'If this Set card in the Spell & Trap Zone is sent to the GY: You can Special Summon this card', so any outside card that destroys or sends your own face-down Spell/Trap to the GY is a free Summon.

hooks.label: Monsters that Set themselves as Spells
hooks.why: Toy Box sends a face-down card you control to the GY for its attack trigger and can destroy up to 2 cards in your Spell & Trap Zone, so outside monsters that place themselves in the Spell & Trap Zone as Spells are extra fuel that trigger on their way out.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 4 LIGHTs
hooks.why: Toy Soldier adds a Level 4 LIGHT monster from the Deck while you control Toy Box, so outside Level 4 LIGHT monsters that Special Summon themselves are the best things it can search.

hooks.label: Sees the opponent's hand
hooks.why: The Black Goat Laughs locks Special Summons and on-field effects of monsters sharing a declared original name, so cards that reveal or look at the opponent's hand or Deck tell you the right name to declare.

hooks.label: Sets Spells/Traps from the Deck
hooks.why: Toy Box spends face-down cards you control as cost and can destroy your own Spell/Trap cards, so outside cards that Set Spell/Trap cards directly onto the field keep it stocked with ammunition.

profile.plan: An Insect-only deck that floods the field with free Special Summons and Tokens, then Link and Fusion Summons by banishing Insects from its own Graveyard.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every Beetrooper monster is an Insect, and Armor Horn, Scout Buggy, Giant Atlas and Cruel Saturnas all forbid Special Summoning anything except Insect monsters.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Insects
hooks.why: The deck is locked into Insects and constantly needs bodies as Link and Fusion material, so Insects that Special Summon themselves (often by banishing Insect monsters from the GY, which this deck already does) are free extension.

hooks.label: Insects banished from the GY
hooks.why: Assault Roller, Armor Horn, Beetrooper Landing and Fly & Sting all banish Insect monsters from your GY as a cost, so an Insect with an effect when it is banished gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: Insects that want Tributing
hooks.why: Scale Bomber, Giant Beetrooper Invincible Atlas and Beetrooper Squad all Tribute Insect monsters as a cost, so an Insect that triggers when Tributed is pure value here.

hooks.label: Insects that want the GY
hooks.why: Armor Horn, Giant Beetrooper Invincible Atlas and Beetrooper Landing use Insect monsters as Link or Fusion material, so Insects with an effect when they are sent to the GY pay off with every play.

profile.plan: A control deck of Fairy monsters that banish themselves from the field to fire the Continuous Spell/Trap 'Canvas' effects they are granted, then return in the next Standby Phase.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every The Weather monster is a Fairy, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Fairies work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Recovers banished monsters
hooks.why: Each The Weather monster banishes itself from the field as the cost of a Canvas effect and only returns in the next Standby Phase, so effects that Special Summon or return banished monsters get it back early.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell/Trap with a GY effect
hooks.why: The Weather Painter Thunder and The Weather Painter Sun send a face-up Continuous Spell/Trap you control to the GY as a cost, so an outside Continuous Spell/Trap that does something when it is sent to the GY turns that cost into value.

hooks.label: Rewards banishing your monsters
hooks.why: Every The Weather monster banishes itself from the field to activate a Canvas effect, so cards that trigger or gain counters each time your cards are banished fire on every one of those costs.

profile.plan: An Aqua/FIRE Level 4 Xyz deck built around the Normal Monster Gunkan Suship Shari: reveal it in hand, get it on the field, and use it as Xyz material for Rank 4 and Rank 5 'Dreadnought' bosses that draw, attack twice, attack directly and negate effects.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Gunkan Suship Shari is a Normal Monster that nearly every Gunkan effect demands in hand, on the field or as Xyz material, so anything that searches or revives Normal Monsters starts the whole engine.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: Every Gunkan monster and every Gunkan Xyz Monster is Aqua, so cards that search, revive or boost Aqua monsters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Gunkan Suship Shirauo-class Carrier only grants its Extra Deck 'Gunkan' monsters destruction protection and DEF-based ATK while a face-up card is in a Field Zone, and Gunkan Sushipyard Seaside Supper Spot is that card, so a way to find a Field Spell keeps the boss live.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 4/5 material
hooks.why: Ikura, Uni, Shirauo and Shari Red all Special Summon themselves from the hand while you control Shari or an Xyz with Shari as material, and the deck needs Level 4 bodies for the Rank 4 Dreadnoughts and Level 5 bodies for Gunkan Suship Uni-class Super-Dreadnought.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Gunkan Suship Uni changes a Gunkan monster's Level to 4 or 5, so outside Level-changing effects let you convert Level 4 bodies into the two Level 5 materials for Uni-class Super-Dreadnought.

profile.plan: A Machine toolbox where every monster has ATK equal to its DEF: the Gizmeks Special Summon themselves, dig out more Machines with matching ATK/DEF, then banish themselves from the GY or Deck to ladder into bigger bodies and a counter-based Field Spell lock.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Gizmek is a Machine, and Naganaki, Taniguku, Arakami and Inaba only search, revive or boost Machine monsters whose ATK equals their own DEF, so any card that supports Machines works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills Machine monsters
hooks.why: Naganaki, Taniguku, Arakami and Inaba all banish themselves from the GY as a cost, and Sacred Scrolls banishes the cards it excavates face-down, so outside cards that send Machine monsters from the Deck to the GY load those Graveyard effects.

hooks.label: Banishes face-down
hooks.why: Sacred Scrolls banishes the cards it does not add face-down, and Naganaki can only recover your banished face-down Machine monsters whose ATK equals their own DEF, while Makami wants 6 or more of your cards banished.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Makami discards 1 monster as a cost to search a monster whose ATK equals its own DEF, so an outside monster with an effect when it is discarded gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: Machines that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Naganaki Tributes 1 Machine monster whose ATK equals its own DEF as a cost to Special Summon a lower-Level one from the Deck, and Yata is Special Summoned by Tributing a Normal Summoned monster, so a Machine with an effect when Tributed is a free bonus.

hooks.label: Link monsters for the Extra Monster Zone
hooks.why: Kaku only Special Summons itself from the hand while a monster is in the Extra Monster Zone and then equips that face-up monster, and Okami Special Summons itself with 2 or more monsters Special Summoned from the Extra Deck on the field before destroying them all.

profile.plan: An Illusion deck whose monsters cannot be destroyed in battle and which steals the opponent's monsters from their hand, Deck, Extra Deck, Graveyard and field, then uses them as Fusion material and attackers.

hooks.label: Makes the opponent draw
hooks.why: Godos, Gaigas and Breus Special Summon themselves from the hand whenever a card is added to the opponent's hand, so any card that makes the opponent draw or add a card is a free body.

hooks.label: Illusion support
hooks.why: Every Hecahands monster is an Illusion, and the Fusion Monsters list an Illusion monster as material.

hooks.label: Steals the opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Hecahands Bait, Dandalos and Xeno take or Special Summon monsters owned by the opponent, which Jauzah and Tartaros can then treat as 'Hecahands' Fusion material.

hooks.label: Sends your Illusion monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Ibtel, Yadel and Mankibuel all have effects when they are sent to the GY, so cards that send an Illusion monster from the hand or Deck there are extenders.

hooks.label: Fills the opponent's Graveyard
hooks.why: Godos Special Summons a monster from the opponent's GY and Gaigas from the top of their Deck, so cards that send the opponent's monsters to the GY give the deck more to steal.

hooks.label: Grants direct attacks
hooks.why: Hecahands Dandalos already lets your Hecahands Fusion Monsters attack directly, and every Hecahands monster survives battle, so extra direct-attack effects turn the deck into damage.

profile.plan: A Fiend Link Summoning deck that swaps between Ki-sikil and Lil-la to trigger draw and destruction effects, then climbs into Trouble Sunny or the Level 8 boss for control and recursion.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Evil★Twin monster is a Fiend, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Fiends
hooks.why: The deck climbs through Link Monsters and can lock itself into Fiend Extra Deck summons, so Fiend monsters that Special Summon themselves provide easy Link material.

hooks.label: Tribute triggers
hooks.why: GG EZ, Trouble Sunny and Evil★Twins Ki-sikil & Lil-la all Tribute monsters, so effects that trigger when a monster is Tributed get extra value.

hooks.label: Easy Link Monsters
hooks.why: Evil★Twins Ki-sikil & Lil-la Special Summons itself by Tributing 2 Link Monsters, so any Link Monster that Special Summons itself is fodder.

hooks.label: Fiend GY setup
hooks.why: The deck revives Ki-sikil and Lil-la from the GY, so sending Fiend monsters from the Deck to the GY sets up those plays.

hooks.label: Fiend Link Material
hooks.why: The deck Link Summons its Fiend monsters, so Fiend monsters that trigger when used as Link Material provide extra advantage.

profile.plan: A blind-guess control deck: SPYRAL monsters declare a card type, flip over the top card of the opponent's Deck and convert a correct call into a free Special Summon, a search or a draw, while Super Agent, Double Helix and the MISSION cards grind the opponent's board down.

hooks.label: Stacks the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Super Agent, Tough, Double Helix and SPYGAL Misty all declare a card type and reveal the top card of the opponent's Deck, so a card that lets you look at or reorder that top card turns every call into a guaranteed Summon, search or draw.

hooks.label: Level 1 Machine Summons
hooks.why: Quik-Fix (500 ATK) and SPYRAL GEAR - Drone (100 ATK) are Level 1 Machines whose on-Summon effects search and stack the opponent's Deck, so effects that Special Summon a Machine from the Deck give extra copies of the engine.

hooks.label: Discard and GY fodder
hooks.why: Quik-Fix revives itself from the Graveyard by discarding a card, and SPYRAL GEAR - Last Resort sends another card you control to the Graveyard to hand out a direct attack, so monsters that trigger when they are discarded or sent to the Graveyard are free material.

hooks.label: Clears your own field
hooks.why: Master Plan adds SPYRAL Resort plus a SPYRAL monster when it is sent from the field to the Graveyard, and Sleeper, SPYRAL GEAR - Fully Armed and Charming Resort Staff all trigger when they are destroyed, so cards that send or destroy your own monsters turn the board into searches and revives.

hooks.label: Field Spell support
hooks.why: SPYRAL Resort searches a SPYRAL monster every turn and shields the rest of the board from targeting, and Master Plan fetches it, so outside cards that add or put a Field Spell from the Deck onto the field keep the Resort available.

profile.plan: A Synchro combo deck whose Level 2 Fairy Tuners Special Summon themselves while you control Visas Starfrost or a 1500 ATK/2100 DEF monster, and replace themselves from the Deck when they are destroyed.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Tuners
hooks.why: Mannadium Meek, Mannadium Fearless and Mannadium Torrid each Special Summon themselves from the hand while you control Visas Starfrost or a monster with 1500 ATK/2100 DEF, so outside low-Level Tuners that bring themselves out are the same free Synchro material.

hooks.label: Tuner Summoners
hooks.why: Mannadium Torrid and Mannadium Meek Special Summon a replacement Tuner from the Deck when destroyed and Mannadium Trisukta revives a Level 2 Tuner from the GY, so extra ways to put low-Level Tuners on board extend every Synchro play.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monster
hooks.why: Mannadium Riumheart and Mannadium Abscission both destroy a monster you control to start the combo, and each Mannadium Tuner Special Summons a replacement from the Deck when destroyed by card effect, so any outside effect that destroys your own monster is another trigger.

hooks.label: Floats when destroyed
hooks.why: Riumheart and Abscission destroy a monster you control as the cost of their effects, so an outside monster with an effect that triggers when it is destroyed gets that activation for free.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Mannadium Meek, Mannadium Fearless, Mannadium Torrid and Mannadium Trisukta are all Fairy, so cards that search, revive or protect Fairies reach nearly every monster the deck plays.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that gains LP and takes effect damage to place Resonance Counters on its Fiend and Fairy Pendulum monsters, then uses those counters to Link Summon and control the field.

hooks.label: Discarded by Vaalmonica
hooks.why: Angello Vaalmonica and Dimonno Vaalmonica discard a card to place themselves in the Pendulum Zones, so outside monsters that trigger when discarded get value for free.

hooks.label: Triggers on effect damage
hooks.why: Dimonno Vaalmonica places a Resonance Counter each time you take effect damage, and the deck's own Normal Spells deal 500 damage to you, so outside cards that trigger when you take effect damage get extra value.

hooks.label: Triggers on LP gain
hooks.why: Angello Vaalmonica places a Resonance Counter each time you gain LP, and the deck's own Normal Spells gain 500 LP, so outside cards that trigger when you gain LP get extra value.

hooks.label: Sends Spell/Trap to GY
hooks.why: Angello and Dimonno banish a 'Vaalmonica' Normal Spell/Trap from the GY to apply its effect, so outside cards that send a Spell/Trap from the Deck to the GY enable that.

hooks.label: Continuous LP gain
hooks.why: Angello Vaalmonica places a Resonance Counter each time you gain LP, so a Continuous Spell/Trap that gains LP repeatedly places multiple counters over the duel.

profile.plan: Live☆Twin summons one tiny Cyberse twin as your only monster, and it drags its partner out of the Deck, so the deck loops Ki-sikil and Lil-la into the Evil★Twin Link monsters while draining and taxing the opponent's attacks and Life Points.

hooks.label: Discard fodder with GY effects
hooks.why: Live☆Twin Home discards 1 card as its cost, so outside monsters that do something when discarded are pure value.

hooks.label: Triggers when you gain LP
hooks.why: Ki-sikil gives 500 LP every time an opponent's monster declares an attack and Sunny's Snitch gives 200 LP each time the opponent Summons, so cards that reward gaining LP get a steady stream.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every Live☆Twin monster is a Cyberse, so search, revival and stat boosts aimed at Cyberse monsters apply to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Punishes attack declarations
hooks.why: Lil-la makes the opponent pay 500 LP to attack, Ki-sikil pays you 500 LP for it and Channel can Tribute a twin to negate the attack, so outside cards that fire on an opponent's attack declaration are always live.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck that uses Beast, Fiend, and Illusion monsters as material for its Fusion Monsters, then recurs those Types from the GY or banished pile during the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Beast/Fiend/Illusion GY triggers
hooks.why: The archetype's Fusion Monsters send 1 Beast, Fiend, or Illusion monster from your Deck to the GY when Fusion Summoned, so monsters of those Types that trigger when sent to the GY get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Beast/Fiend/Illusion searchers
hooks.why: The deck's Fusion Monsters need Beast, Fiend, or Illusion monsters as material, so cards that search or Special Summon those Types from the Deck provide the material.

hooks.label: Self-reviving Beast/Fiend/Illusion
hooks.why: The Fusion Monsters can Special Summon a Beast, Fiend, or Illusion monster from the GY or banished pile during the opponent's turn, so monsters of those Types that can revive themselves are perfect targets.

hooks.label: Quick-Play Fusion Spells
hooks.why: The archetype has a Quick-Play Spell that Fusion Summons using Beast or Fiend material, so other Quick-Play Fusion Spells can serve as additional copies or follow-up.

hooks.label: Beast/Fiend/Illusion millers
hooks.why: The archetype's Fusion Monsters revive Beast, Fiend, or Illusion monsters from the GY or banished pile, so effects that send those Types from the Deck to the GY set up the revive.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Fiend Ritual-material monsters and Rank 2-4 Xyz monsters: the Ritual Djinns banish themselves from the Graveyard as material for any Ritual Summon, while the Xyz Djinns repeatedly pay for negations, boosted ATK and extra attacks by detaching Xyz Materials.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon enablers
hooks.why: Six Djinns (Releaser, Demolisher, Presider, Disserere, Prognosticator, Cursenchanter) banish themselves from the Graveyard as one of the monsters required for a Ritual Summon, so any outside card that Ritual Summons gets a free material from the GY.

hooks.label: Buries Fiends in the GY
hooks.why: Releaser, Demolisher, Presider, Disserere, Prognosticator and Cursenchanter can only be banished as Ritual material while they sit in the Graveyard, so effects that send Fiend or DARK monsters from the Deck there set them up.

hooks.label: Fiend and DARK support
hooks.why: Every Ritual Djinn and almost every Xyz Djinn (Melomelody, Maestroke, Muzurhythm, Temtempo, Humhumming, Number 65) is a Fiend and DARK, so Type- and Attribute-wide support reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 3 Xyz fodder
hooks.why: Melomelody, Muzurhythm, Temtempo and Humhumming all need 2 Level 3 monsters, so outside cards that Special Summon Level 3 monsters feed the deck's main Xyz plays.

hooks.label: Extra Xyz Material
hooks.why: Every Djinn Xyz Monster pays for its effect by detaching Xyz Material (Number 65 detaches 2 at once), and Maestroke can even detach instead of being destroyed, so cards that attach more material buy extra uses.

profile.plan: The deck equips Inzektor monsters to each other as Equip Spells, then sends those Equip Cards to the Graveyard to trigger Dragonfly and Centipede into swarming the field and Xyz Summoning Rank 5 and 6 Insect monsters.

hooks.label: Sends DARK monsters to GY
hooks.why: Inzektor Dragonfly and Centipede can equip Inzektor monsters from the hand or Graveyard, so filling the GY with DARK Inzektors (all of them are DARK) gives them targets.

hooks.label: Searches Equip Spells
hooks.why: The deck relies on its Equip Spells like Inzektor Sword - Zektkaliber and Inzektor Axe - Zektahawk to boost and trigger effects, so cards that add Equip Spells from the Deck or GY give consistent access.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every Inzektor monster is an Insect, so cards that search, revive, or protect Insect-Type monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Equip Spells
hooks.why: Inzektor Dragonfly and Centipede gain effects when an Equip Card is sent to the GY while equipped to them, so outside cards that destroy your own Equip Spells can manually trigger those effects.

hooks.label: Grants extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: The deck needs to Normal Summon multiple Inzektor monsters to equip them to each other, so cards that give an extra Normal Summon help start combos.

profile.plan: A Warrior toolbox of six differently-Attributed monsters that swarms the field, fuses into Rihan by sending three 'Six Samurai' with different Attributes from the field to the GY, and repeatedly saves a lone Six Samurai by banishing its own copies out of the GY.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: All six Secret Six Samurai are Warriors and Rihan's Fusion Summon sends Warrior 'Six Samurai' from the field to the GY, so Type support reaches every card in the deck.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: Rihan needs 3 'Six Samurai' monsters with different Attributes and Kizaru only searches a monster whose Attribute differs from every monster you control, so effects that change a monster's Attribute unlock those lines.

hooks.label: Mills your Deck
hooks.why: Every Secret Six Samurai protects by banishing itself from the GY and Hatsume banishes 2 Six Samurai from the GY and/or field to revive one, so outside cards that send Warrior monsters from the Deck to the GY stock that resource.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Fuma Special Summons a 'Six Samurai' monster from the Deck when it is destroyed by battle or card effect, so cards that destroy your own Warrior monsters turn into a free recruit.

hooks.label: Banished-trigger monsters
hooks.why: Each Secret Six Samurai can banish itself from the GY to save a lone Six Samurai from destruction, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished are used for free.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Genba recovers a banished 'Six Samurai' when it is Normal Summoned and Doji sends a 'Six Samurai' from the Deck to the GY whenever another is Normal or Special Summoned, so extra Normal Summons of Warriors extend and set up the GY at once.

profile.plan: An Insect/WIND Synchro deck that swarms with low-Level monsters, climbs into Synchro Monsters (often using Synchro Tuners as material), and wins through battle damage and effect damage (burn), with a sub-theme of banishing Insects from the GY for large payoffs.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every Battlewasp monster is an Insect, and Sting the Poison, Halberd the Charge and Sachi the Ceremonial Bow all ask for Insect monsters as material or Tribute, so generic Insect search, revival and protection help the whole deck.

hooks.label: Banishes Insect from GY
hooks.why: Ballista the Armageddon banishes all Insect monsters from your GY to shrink the opponent's monsters, and Grand Partisan the Revolution gains ATK for each banished Insect, so cards that banish Insects from your GY fuel both.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished from GY
hooks.why: Ballista the Armageddon banishes every Insect in your GY at once, so any monster with an effect when it is banished from the GY gets that effect for free during the same play.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Insect
hooks.why: Grand Partisan the Revolution Special Summons itself and destroys cards when it is banished, so effects that banish your own Insect monster from the field turn it into a board wipe.

profile.plan: A Level 8 boss deck that stuffs its Graveyard with Spells and Traps, banishes them to Special Summon its own monsters for free, and cheats out Illusion or Spellcaster Tuner Synchro monsters while protecting its field.

hooks.label: Sends Spells/Traps to the GY
hooks.why: Play the Diabell and Like the Diabell both trigger when a Spell/Trap is sent to the GY, and Diabellstar Vengeance and Diabellze the White Witch need Spells/Traps in the hand or GY to banish or send as their Summon cost.

hooks.label: Spell/Trap that pays off in the GY
hooks.why: Play the Diabell and Like the Diabell banish 3 Spells/Traps from the GY including themselves, and Filia Diabell and Curse of Diabell both reward being banished or sent to the GY, so outside Spells/Traps with the same trigger get used for free.

hooks.label: Illusion and Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Diabellze the White Witch is an Illusion, Diabellstar, the Seeker of Sinful Spoils is a Spellcaster, and Play the Diabell sends an Illusion or Spellcaster monster to the GY, so support for those two Types powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra face-up Spell/Trap presence
hooks.why: Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest gains 700 ATK/DEF for each Spell/Trap on the field and returns cards on the field to the hand up to the number of Spells/Traps you control, so cards that flood the field with Continuous, Equip or Field Spells make it huge and clear the opponent's board.

profile.plan: A Fiend beatdown deck that piles monsters into the Graveyard as Tributes so its Maju Garzett bosses grow to huge ATK, while Gren Maju Da Eiza turns every banished card into 400 ATK.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Emperor Maju Garzett can only be Special Summoned by Tributing 3 monsters and Maju Garzett wants 2 Tributes, so cards that Special Summon Tokens hand the deck its Tribute fodder for free.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Great Maju Garzett's ATK becomes twice the original ATK of the monster Tributed for it, and Legendary Maju Garzett Tributes every monster you control, so monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand give big Tributes without spending the Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Every Maju Garzett needs monsters fed to the Graveyard as Tributes, so outside monsters that do something when they themselves are Tributed get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Banishes your own cards
hooks.why: Gren Maju Da Eiza's ATK and DEF are 400 times the number of your banished cards, so cards that banish your own monsters from the Deck or Graveyard directly grow it.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Maju monster is a Fiend, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Fiends work on the whole deck, including the Garzett bosses.

profile.plan: A FIRE Synchro deck that dumps Laval monsters into the Graveyard so its Tuners and Synchros can climb, then banishes those Graveyard monsters as fuel for burns, destruction and revival.

hooks.label: Dumps FIRE to the Graveyard
hooks.why: Laval Coatl, Laval Burner, Soaring Eagle Above the Searing Land and Laval Lakeside Lady all demand 3 or more differently named Laval monsters in the Graveyard, while Laval Miller, Laval Volcano Handmaiden and Molten Conduction Field show the deck lives off sending FIRE cards from the Deck to the GY.

hooks.label: FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Laval monster is FIRE and every Laval Synchro Summon (Lavalval Dragun, Lavalval Salamander, Laval Stennon, Laval Dual Slasher, Lavalval Exlord) requires non-Tuner FIRE monsters as material.

hooks.label: Damage when discarded
hooks.why: Lavalval Salamander, Laval Stennon, Laval the Greater, Lavalval Dragun and Laval Magma Cannoneer all send cards from the hand to the Graveyard, so FIRE monsters that do something on being sent there are free value.

hooks.label: Floats when destroyed
hooks.why: Laval Archer destroys 1 FIRE monster you control to Special Summon itself, so FIRE monsters that trigger when destroyed turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Recovers banished FIRE
hooks.why: Laval Judgment Lord, Searing Fire Wall, Dustflame Blast, Prominence and Burgeoning Whirlflame all banish FIRE monsters from the Graveyard as fuel, so effects that return banished FIRE monsters keep the engine supplied.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Xyz deck of Level 4 LIGHT Warrior 'tellarknight' monsters whose effects all trigger when they are Summoned, looping Deneb, Altair, Vega and Unukalhai to fill the board and Graveyard before overlaying.

hooks.label: LIGHT Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck tellarknight is a Level 4 LIGHT Warrior, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT or Warrior monsters work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Level 4 self-Summoners
hooks.why: Deneb, Altair and Vega only get their effects when Summoned and the deck needs two Level 4 bodies for its Xyz Summons, so outside Level 4 LIGHT Warriors that Special Summon themselves are free material.

hooks.label: Summons your Level 4s
hooks.why: Unukalhai, Deneb, Altair, Vega and the rest only activate when they are Summoned, so an outside card that Special Summons a Level 4 LIGHT Warrior from the Deck, hand or Graveyard starts the engine without using the Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Darktellarknight Batlamyus detaches a material and discards 1 card as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded get that trigger for free.

hooks.label: Xyz Material payoffs
hooks.why: Batlamyus detaches a material as a cost and Hexatellarknight grows its Xyz Monsters by 200 ATK/DEF for each material, so cards that attach material to an Xyz Monster keep feeding both.

profile.plan: Returns its own WIND monsters to the hand to trigger Divine Wind of Mist Valley, Thunderbird and Apex Avian, generating Special Summons, negations and Synchro plays.

hooks.label: Returns your WIND monsters to hand
hooks.why: Divine Wind of Mist Valley and Mist Valley Thunderbird trigger when a WIND monster you control returns to the hand, so any card that can return your own WIND monster is another starter.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Most Mist Valley monsters are Winged Beast, so generic Winged Beast support like Swallow's Nest or Icarus Attack works with the whole deck.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Apex Avian, Executor, Thunderbird and Thunder Lord are all Thunder, so Thunder-specific support can search or revive them.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that searches and places Pendulum Monsters to set scales, Pendulum Summons multiple monsters of different Levels, and recycles face-up Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck, with a Level 7+ Fusion boss that Tributes for damage.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monster searchers
hooks.why: Pendulum Treasure, PenduLuMoon and Beyond the Pendulum all add Pendulum Monsters from the Deck, so outside cards that search Pendulum Monsters give the deck more consistency.

hooks.label: Extra Deck Pendulum recovery
hooks.why: Exceed the Pendulum and PenduLuMoon add face-up Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck to the hand, so outside cards that do the same recycle your Pendulum Summons.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Master Spirit Tech Force - Pendulum Ruler Tributes a monster to destroy a card, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Pendulum Summon triggers
hooks.why: Beyond the Pendulum triggers when two monsters with different Levels are Pendulum Summoned, and Extra Pendulum grants an extra Pendulum Summon, so outside cards that trigger on Pendulum Summon fit the same timing.

profile.plan: A Pendulum stun deck that keeps its Amorphage scales alive by Tributing a monster every Standby Phase, locking both players out of the Extra Deck and out of Spells, Traps, monster effects and Chain Link 2+, and drawing or searching each time its own monsters are Tributed.

hooks.label: Monsters that want Tributing
hooks.why: Every Amorphage Pendulum effect demands you Tribute 1 monster each Standby Phase or the scale destroys itself, so outside monsters that do something when they are Tributed pay that upkeep for free.

hooks.label: Tributes your own monsters
hooks.why: Amorphous Persona draws a card whenever an Amorphage monster you control is Tributed and Amorphage Infection adds an Amorphage card when a monster in your hand or field is Tributed, so outside cards that Tribute your monsters turn into advantage.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: Amorphous Persona can banish itself from the Graveyard to Tribute Pendulum Monsters whose Levels total exactly 8 and Ritual Summon Amorphactor Pain, so Ritual Summoning helpers give the deck a second, non-Pendulum win condition.

hooks.label: Dragon and EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Amorphage monster is a Dragon and every one is EARTH, so cards that search, revive, boost or protect Dragons or EARTH monsters work on the entire deck.

profile.plan: A Pyro DARK beatdown/control deck that leans on the Field Spell "Obsidim, the Ashened City" to flood the board with its own Special Summons, turns the opponent's monsters into Pyro on your turn, and Fusion Summons Pyro Fusions while handing the opponent bodies it can then take back.

hooks.label: Pyro support
hooks.why: Every Ashened monster and Fusion is a Pyro, and Embers of the Ashened asks for 2 Pyro materials, so anything that searches, revives or boosts Pyro monsters works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Priestess, King, Hero, Shaman and Spearhead only Special Summon themselves while "Obsidim, the Ashened City" is in the Field Zone, so outside ways to grab or place a Field Spell turn on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent a monster
hooks.why: Ashened for Eternity steals back a monster your opponent controls that you own and King and Spearhead get their bonuses while the opponent controls a 2800+ ATK monster, so cards that Special Summon a monster onto the opponent's field set both up.

profile.plan: A WATER Fish deck that Xyz Summons Rank 3 to 5 'Shark' monsters, treating the Graveyard as a second hand and Tributing its own monsters as cost to keep bodies coming.

hooks.label: Fish and WATER support
hooks.why: Almost every Main Deck Shark monster is a Fish and a WATER monster, so Fish/WATER search, revival and ATK support reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning WATER monsters
hooks.why: Crystal Shark, Dream Shark, Hydrojet Shark and Cutter Shark all Special Summon themselves from the hand or GY, so other WATER monsters that do the same give Xyz Material without spending the Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Monsters with Tribute triggers
hooks.why: Veiss Shark Tributes a Fish monster as cost and Cutter Shark Tributes a targeted monster to Summon itself, so outside monsters that gain an effect when they are Tributed get their payoff for free.

hooks.label: Mills WATER monsters
hooks.why: Crystal Shark, Dream Shark and Cutter Shark all Summon themselves from the GY, so outside effects that send WATER monsters from the Deck to the GY load the Graveyard with live recursion targets.

hooks.label: WATER Graveyard recovery
hooks.why: Cutter Shark adds a WATER monster from the GY in the End Phase while Crystal Shark and Dream Shark keep returning from the GY, so outside cards that revive or recover WATER monsters sustain the loop.

profile.plan: A Warrior/DARK deck that wins by connecting with its low-ATK monsters to trigger battle-damage effects that discard, mill, destroy, bounce and search; Dark Scorpion Combination lets the whole team attack directly for 400 damage each.

hooks.label: Warrior ATK boosters
hooks.why: The Dark Scorpions have only 1000-1800 ATK, so they need ATK boosts to inflict the battle damage that triggers effects like Don Zaloog's discard or Cliff's Spell/Trap destruction.

hooks.label: Warrior direct attackers
hooks.why: Dark Scorpion Combination lets the team attack directly, and direct attacks guarantee the battle damage that triggers every Dark Scorpion effect.

hooks.label: Multiple attack enablers
hooks.why: More attacks per turn means more battle damage triggers for effects like Meanae's search or Chick's bounce.

hooks.label: Warrior-Type support
hooks.why: Every Dark Scorpion is a Warrior, so cards that search, revive or boost Warrior-Type monsters support the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Don Zaloog, Cliff, Burglars and Gorg all send cards from the opponent's Deck to the GY, so additional milling cards stack the disruption.

profile.plan: A Beast beatdown deck that fuses two Normal Monsters into the 4200 ATK Master of Oz or uses Koalo-Koala to pop monsters, with Sea Koala softening targets and Vampiric Koala turning battles into Life Points.

hooks.label: Beast-Type support
hooks.why: Every Koala is a Beast-Type monster, and both Sea Koala ('You must control a Beast-Type monster') and Koalo-Koala ('send 1 Beast-Type monster from your hand to the Graveyard') are unusable without Beasts around them.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Big Koala is a Level 7 Normal Monster and the main Fusion material for Master of Oz, so cards that search, revive or protect Normal Monsters assemble the boss directly.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon support
hooks.why: Master of Oz and Koalo-Koala are Fusion Monsters summoned with Polymerization from named materials, so outside Fusion Summoning and Fusion recovery cards build the deck's biggest plays.

hooks.label: Beast that triggers in the GY
hooks.why: Koalo-Koala sends a Beast-Type monster from your hand to the Graveyard as its cost, so Beast-Type monsters with a Graveyard or discard trigger get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Free Beast bodies
hooks.why: Sea Koala can only zero an opponent's monster while you control another Beast-Type monster, so outside cards that Special Summon Beasts switch its effect on and provide material for the Fusions.

hooks.label: Reusable Flip effects
hooks.why: Des Koala's FLIP burn scales with the opponent's hand, so outside cards that flip your own Flip monsters face-down again let it burn a second or third time.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Warrior deck that Special Summons its Silent Swordsman monsters by Tributing Warriors, levels them up through your Standby Phases, and shuts the opponent's Spells down with LV5, LV7 and their own activations.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Warriors
hooks.why: Silent Swordsman can only be Special Summoned from the hand by Tributing 1 Warrior-Type monster, so Warriors that Special Summon themselves from anywhere are free fodder for it.

hooks.label: Warriors that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: The deck pays for Silent Swordsman by Tributing a Warrior-Type monster, so an outside Warrior with an effect that triggers when it is Tributed gives you value for the cost.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Silent Paladin only searches Silent Swordsman LV3 on a Normal Summon, and you still need a Warrior body left over to Tribute for Silent Swordsman, so an extra Normal Summon gets both done in one turn.

hooks.label: Warrior and LIGHT support
hooks.why: Every Silent Swordsman monster is a LIGHT Warrior, and Silent Paladin even recovers LIGHT 'LV' monsters from the Graveyard, so support that names Warrior-Type or LIGHT monsters lifts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Shining Sarcophagus cards
hooks.why: Silent Swordsman Zero can negate an activation that targets Shining Sarcophagus, or a monster that mentions it, you control, so cards built around that card are natural partners.

profile.plan: A toolbox of transformation cards: Mask Change swaps a HERO you control for an Attribute-matched Masked HERO, DoomZ Change trades a DoomZ card for recovery and a Special Summon, and Galaxy-Eyes Photon Change Dragon turns itself into Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon.

hooks.label: HERO monsters
hooks.why: Mask Change can only target a "HERO" monster you control and turns it into a Masked HERO, so any outside HERO monster is both the enabler and the material for the Summon.

hooks.label: HERO monsters with GY effects
hooks.why: Mask Change sends the targeted HERO to the GY as part of its own effect, so an outside HERO that triggers when it is sent to the GY gets turned on by the same play.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: Mask Change reads the sent monster's Attribute on the field to choose which Masked HERO it Summons, so an outside effect that changes a HERO's Attribute lets you pick from the whole Masked HERO pool.

hooks.label: DoomZ cards
hooks.why: DoomZ Change destroys a "DoomZ" card from your hand, Deck or face-up field and its destruction effect adds one back and Special Summons a "DoomZ" monster, so outside DoomZ cards are the fuel and the payoff it needs.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Spell/Trap
hooks.why: DoomZ Change only recovers a card and Special Summons from the GY if it is destroyed by a card effect, so outside effects that destroy a Spell/Trap you control can trigger it after it resolves.

hooks.label: Galaxy-Eyes monsters
hooks.why: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Change Dragon banishes itself to Special Summon "Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon" from the Deck or GY, so the rest of the Galaxy-Eyes pool is the natural company for it.

profile.plan: An Extra-Deck-light deck of 2500 ATK/DEF monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand while another 2500-stat monster is on the field, use their own bodies as Quick-Effect removal, and keep coming back from the GY during the opponent's End Phase.

hooks.label: 2500 ATK or DEF monsters
hooks.why: Regenesis Sage, Warrior, Dragon, Lord and Overlord all Special Summon themselves from the hand while a monster with 2500 original ATK or DEF is on the field, and 'Regenesis' plus 'Regenesis Cycle' add or revive exactly those 2500-stat monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters that reward being banished
hooks.why: 'Regenesis Lord' is Summoned by banishing a face-up 2500 ATK/DEF monster you control and 'Regenesis Overlord' by banishing two 2500 ATK or DEF monsters from the GY, while 'Regenesis Code' and 'Regenesis Cycle' banish themselves from the GY, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Revives banished monsters
hooks.why: The deck banishes its own 2500 ATK/DEF monsters for 'Regenesis Lord' and 'Regenesis Overlord' and already brings them back with 'Regenesis Code' and 'Regenesis Birth', so outside cards that Special Summon a banished monster give it extra bodies.

hooks.label: Column placement cards
hooks.why: 'Regenesis Commands' negates the effects of every opponent's card sitting in the same column as your 'Regenesis' monsters, so outside cards that place or move cards between columns line the lock up.

hooks.label: Flips opponent's monsters face-down
hooks.why: 'Regenesis Birth' turns an opponent's monster face-down and 'Regenesis Commands' stops face-down monsters from changing battle position while 'Regenesis Lord' deals piercing damage to Defense Position monsters, so more cards that flip the opponent's monsters face-down extend that lock.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Fusion Summoning Spells and Traps that pulls material from the hand, field, Deck, GY or banished pile for whatever Fusion Monster you need, plus payoffs for Fusion Monsters that end up in the GY.

hooks.label: Zombie monsters and support
hooks.why: Ghost Fusion Fusion Summons using only Zombie monsters you control and can banish a Zombie from your hand, Deck or GY as extra material.

hooks.label: Psychic monsters and support
hooks.why: Teleport Fusion banishes Psychic monsters from your field or GY as Fusion Material and revives a banished Psychic when your Extra Deck Psychic is destroyed.

hooks.label: Fusion Monsters that want the GY
hooks.why: Lev Shaddoll Fusion sends a Fusion Monster from the Extra Deck to the GY and Tributes a Fusion Monster, and Surprise Fusion Tributes a Fusion Monster, so Fusion Monsters with a Tribute or GY trigger get the cost for free.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with monsters
hooks.why: Ghost Fusion, Trickstar Diffusion and Teleport Fusion take their Fusion Material from the GY or banished pile, so any card that sends monsters to the GY arms them.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Mementotlan Fusion gains extra Material when a monster you control was destroyed by card effect this turn, and Penetration Fusion needs a monster destroyed by battle this turn.

profile.plan: A DARK Fiend control deck that Tributes its own monsters to keep Setting Normal Traps from the Deck and Graveyard, grinding the opponent down with an endless stream of Traps.

hooks.label: Normal Trap searchers
hooks.why: Lilith, Lady of Lament reveals 3 Normal Traps from the Deck for the opponent to pick, and Malice and Loris re-Set Normal Traps from the GY, so the deck needs ways to find and load even more Normal Traps.

hooks.label: Free DARK Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Lilith, Lady of Lament Tributes 1 DARK monster and Malice Tributes 2 monsters as cost, so monsters that put themselves on the field for free keep the engine running every turn.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Lilith and Malice Tribute your own monsters as cost, and Alice, Lady of Lament already rewards being Tributed, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get that trigger for free.

hooks.label: Cards that Tribute your monsters
hooks.why: Loris, Lady of Lament Sets a Normal Trap from the GY whenever another monster is Tributed, so any outside card that Tributes your own monsters turns its cost into a free Trap.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Lady of Lament monster is a Fiend, and Alice searches a Fiend whose combined ATK and DEF equal 2000, so cards that support, revive or search Fiends work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Spellcaster deck whose bosses cannot be Normal Summoned and instead Tribute a Spellcaster (or a Level 7 or lower Spellcaster/Warrior) from the field, then grow huge with a full hand while turning every opponent draw into Spell Counters, Levels and extra draws.

hooks.label: Makes the opponent draw
hooks.why: Silent Magician LV4 places a Spell Counter each time the opponent draws, Silent Magician Zero gains a Level each time the opponent draws, and Silent Magician, the Silent Fighter lets you draw the same number when the opponent draws by a card effect.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Silent Magician monster is a Spellcaster, and Silent Magician must be Special Summoned by Tributing a Spellcaster-Type monster, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Spellcasters serve the whole deck.

hooks.label: Spell Counter cards
hooks.why: Silent Magician LV4 needs 5 Spell Counters (max. 5) before it can send itself to the Graveyard and Special Summon Silent Magician LV8, so any outside card placing Spell Counters on it speeds up the deck's win condition.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Silent Magician needs a Spellcaster on the field to be Tributed and Silent Magician, the Silent Fighter needs a Level 7 or lower Spellcaster or Warrior, so cheap Spellcaster/Warrior monsters that put themselves onto the field are the deck's Summoning fuel.

hooks.label: Shrinks the opponent's hand
hooks.why: Silent Magician gains 500 ATK per card in your hand, Silent Magician, the Silent Fighter negates all opponent Spell Cards while you hold 6 or more cards, and Silent Burning only works when you have more cards in hand than the opponent.

profile.plan: A deck of Level 7 and 8 WATER Beast/Beast-Warrior monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand by Tributing another Level 7 or higher monster from the hand, then Synchro Summons Level 7 Ursarctic monsters by sending a Level 8 Tuner and a Level 1 Synchro to the GY, grinding advantage with Ursarctic Radiation draws and Ursarctic Big Dipper's counters.

hooks.label: Level 7+ GY triggers
hooks.why: Every Ursarctic monster (Mikpolar, Miktanus, Mikbilis, Megapolar, Megabilis, Megatanus) Special Summons itself by Tributing a Level 7 or higher monster from your hand, and that monster lands in the GY, so outside Level 7+ monsters that do something when Tributed or sent to the GY are pure profit.

hooks.label: WATER Beast support
hooks.why: All the Main Deck Ursarctic monsters are WATER Beasts or Beast-Warriors (and the Bosses are WATER too), so generic support for those Types or the WATER Attribute boosts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Cards that like being discarded
hooks.why: Ursarctic Departure discards 1 card as its cost to add two Ursarctic monsters from the Deck, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded turn that cost into value.

profile.plan: A hand-based Thunder deck: reveal Blitzclique monsters from hand to destroy a card and Special Summon a Thunder monster from the hand, then search more Blitzclique whenever any card is destroyed by card effect.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Every Blitzclique monster is a Thunder monster, Blitzclique Alternator searches a Thunder monster from the Deck and Blitzclique - Steppleader recovers one from the GY, so Thunder-specific support powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Bounce your Thunder to hand
hooks.why: The reveal effects only Special Summon Thunder monsters from the hand, and both Whisker Blitzclique and Blitzclique - Breakaway return a Thunder monster you control to the hand as a cost, so outside cards that bounce Thunder monsters re-arm the engine.

hooks.label: Thunder that summons itself
hooks.why: Blitzclique effects lock you into Special Summoning Effect Monsters only from the hand, so Thunder monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand are free bodies the deck can still use, and Thunder ones can be searched by Alternator or returned by Whisker.

hooks.label: Triggers on destruction
hooks.why: Surge, Crackle, Grain and Emi all search whenever another card is destroyed by card effect, and almost every Blitzclique effect destroys a card, so outside cards that trigger on destruction fire constantly.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Blitzclique card is EARTH, so cards that support or search EARTH monsters apply to the entire archetype.

profile.plan: A deck that mixes Normal Monsters with 'Magikey' monsters to Fusion, Ritual, Synchro and Xyz Summon, using the Attributes of monsters in the GY to trigger extra effects.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: The deck's Fusion, Ritual, Synchro and Xyz monsters all need Normal Monsters as material, and a key Spell sends one from Deck to GY if you control a Normal Monster.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: Many of the deck's Extra Deck monsters compare the opponent's monster's Attribute to a Normal Monster or a monster in your GY, so changing Attributes helps trigger them.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The deck sends Normal Monsters from the Deck to the GY as material, and Tributes monsters for Ritual Summons, so outside monsters with GY effects get value.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: The deck Ritual Summons Ritual Monsters from the hand, so adding them from the Deck is useful.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Wyrm deck that banishes its own cards from the Deck and GY on purpose: each banished Metaphys card comes back during the next Standby Phase to search, banish more cards or Special Summon a big Wyrm, with the Fusions of that loop being Executor and Tyrant Dragon.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Deck/GY
hooks.why: Every Metaphys monster has an effect that triggers when it is banished and returns in the next Standby Phase, so any outside card that banishes your own Wyrm LIGHT monsters from the Deck or GY starts the deck's engine.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being banished
hooks.why: Metaphys Ragnarok, Daedalus, Ascension and Asymmetaphys banish cards from the hand, Deck and GY, so outside monsters that do something when they are banished get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Every Metaphys monster, including Executor and Metaphys Horus, is a Wyrm, and Metaphys Ragnarok is a Wyrm Tuner, so cards that search, revive or protect Wyrms work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Summons banished monsters
hooks.why: Metaphys cards only come back from banishment in the Standby Phase of the next turn, so outside cards that Special Summon your banished Wyrm monsters put Executor, Tyrant Dragon or Daedalus on the field immediately.

hooks.label: Lets Ragnarok connect
hooks.why: Metaphys Ragnarok only Special Summons a Level 5 or higher Metaphys monster from the Deck when it inflicts battle damage, so cards that let a monster attack directly turn that payoff on.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Visas Starfrost storyline boss monsters — an Aqua Fusion, a Rank 7 Xyz and a LIGHT Synchro — that the deck builds towards and then uses for repeated removal, banishing and multi-attacks.

hooks.label: Aqua monsters
hooks.why: Tearlaments Kaleido-Heart is a Fusion of 'Tearlaments Reinoheart' plus 2 Aqua monsters, so anything that gives you Aqua monsters to fuse with feeds it directly.

hooks.label: Mills Aqua to the GY
hooks.why: Tearlaments Kaleido-Heart triggers whenever an Aqua monster is sent to your GY by card effect, shuffling a card your opponent controls into the Deck, so outside cards that send Aqua monsters from the Deck to the GY start that removal.

hooks.label: Level 7 self-summoners
hooks.why: Kashtira Arise-Heart is Xyz Summoned with 3 Level 7 monsters, so outside Level 7 monsters that can Special Summon themselves supply its material without eating your Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished
hooks.why: Kashtira Arise-Heart banishes every card that would be sent to the GY instead, so outside monsters and cards with an effect when they are banished get that effect for free.

profile.plan: A deck that keeps its own LP below the opponent's so every Gold Pride monster Special Summons itself for free, then turns those bodies into Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link bosses that bounce back to the Extra Deck in the End Phase to fetch their base forms.

hooks.label: Pays your own LP
hooks.why: Leon, Captain Carrie, Roller Baller, Nytro Head and Eliminator only Special Summon themselves from the hand while your LP are lower than the opponent's, so an outside card with an LP cost switches the whole deck on.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent LP
hooks.why: The deck's condition is your LP being lower than the opponent's, so a card that raises the opponent's LP without touching yours enables Captain Carrie, Leon, Roller Baller and Eliminator just as well as a cost.

hooks.label: Triggers on a monster leaving
hooks.why: Star Leon, Chariot Carrie, Pin Baller, Eradicator and Nytro Blaster all return themselves to the Extra Deck during the End Phase, so an outside card that triggers whenever your monster leaves the field fires for free every turn.

hooks.label: Level 3 self-summoners
hooks.why: Chariot Carrie asks for 2 Level 3 monsters and Leon is the only Level 3 Tuner, so extra Level 3 monsters that Special Summon themselves supply Rank 3 and Synchro 6 material without using up the Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Level 5 self-summoners
hooks.why: Leon (Level 3) plus a Level 5 body makes the Level 8 Eradicator and Roller Baller's Fusion plays, so outside Level 5 monsters that Special Summon themselves are the missing Synchro material.

profile.plan: An all-Pendulum deck of WIND Spellcaster monsters that search on Summon and can't be targeted or destroyed by the opponent, whose Spells and Traps Tribute a WIND Spellcaster to stun, banish or remove the opponent's board.

hooks.label: WIND Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Majespecter monster is a WIND Spellcaster-Type monster, and Majespecter Tempest, Tornado, Cyclone, Storm and Majesty's Pegasus all Tribute a WIND Spellcaster-Type monster, so anything that supports that Type or Attribute works for the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggered when Tributed
hooks.why: Majespecter Tempest, Tornado, Cyclone, Storm and Majesty's Pegasus pay for themselves by Tributing a WIND Spellcaster-Type monster, so a WIND Spellcaster that does something when it is Tributed gets that for free.

hooks.label: Summons a WIND Spellcaster
hooks.why: The deck must keep a WIND Spellcaster-Type monster on the field to pay the Tribute costs of Majespecter Tempest, Tornado, Cyclone, Storm and Majesty's Pegasus, so cards that Special Summon one from the Deck, hand or GY keep the removal online.

hooks.label: Tributes your own monsters
hooks.why: Majespecter Draco - Ryu Special Summons a Level 6 or lower WIND Spellcaster from the Deck every time a monster is Tributed while it is on the field, so outside cards that Tribute your monsters hand you extra Summons.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monster searchers
hooks.why: The Main Deck Majespecters are all Pendulum Monsters with scales of 2 and 5, so cards that add Pendulum Monsters to the hand or Pendulum Zone keep the scales set and the Extra Deck full for Pendulum Summons.

hooks.label: Field Spell support
hooks.why: Majesty's Pegasus is a Field Spell that Tributes a WIND Spellcaster to Special Summon a Level 4 or lower Majespecter from the Deck, and no Majespecter searcher can reach it by name, so cards that add or reuse Field Spells find the deck's best card.

profile.plan: A Machine/Cyberse hybrid that Fusion Summons Cyber Dragon-style bosses and Ritual Summons Cyberse monsters, using Cyber Dragon names, Link and Synchro plays and GY dumping on the way.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Cyberse Desavewurm, Cyberse Contract Witch, Cyberse Sage and Cyberse Code Magician are all Cyberse, and their effects only ever Special Summon, add or send Cyberse monsters, so generic Cyberse support works on the whole half of the deck.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster support
hooks.why: Cyberse Sage and Cyberse Code Magician are Ritual Monsters summoned by Cynet Ritual, and Cyberse Contract Witch adds a Ritual Monster from the Deck, so outside Ritual search and Ritual Summon support fits.

hooks.label: Fusion Spell support
hooks.why: Cyber Jormungardr adds a Polymerization from the Deck or GY, and Cyber Dragon, the Luminous Mech Dragon and Cyberse Sage Fusion Summon, so outside cards built around Polymerization and Fusion Summoning fit.

hooks.label: Machine Fusion support
hooks.why: Cyber End Dragon, the Final Strike Dragon needs 3 Machine monsters with 2100 or more ATK as material and Cyber Dragon, the Luminous Mech Dragon Fusion Summons a Machine Fusion Monster, so outside Machine support helps build the Fusion.

hooks.label: Cyberse that trigger in the GY
hooks.why: Cyberse Code Magician sends a Cyberse monster from the Deck to the GY and Cyberse Sage can add a Cyberse monster back from the GY, so outside Cyberse monsters with an effect when sent to the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: Equip Spell support
