hooks.why: Attachment Cybern equips itself to a Dragon or Machine 'Cyber' monster and Special Summons from the GY when sent there while equipped, and Cyber Jormungardr equips a Cyber Dragon as an Equip Spell, so outside Equip Spell cards fit.

profile.plan: Traps that Special Summon themselves as monsters, using Continuous Trap counts and column placement to negate effects and take control.

hooks.label: Continuous Trap monsters
hooks.why: The deck's cards count other Continuous Traps you control and can send a Continuous Trap in your Monster Zone to negate a Summon, so more Continuous Trap monsters mean more negates and bigger effects.

hooks.label: Column manipulation
hooks.why: Several of the deck's cards care about columns, destroying or taking control of monsters in their column, so outside cards that mention columns help set that up.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Two of the deck's monsters are Fairy-Type, so Fairy support helps them.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Most of the deck's monsters are EARTH, so EARTH support helps them.

hooks.label: Illusion support
hooks.why: One of the deck's monsters is an Illusion-Type that negates effects based on the number of Illusion monsters you control, so more Illusion monsters mean more negates.

hooks.label: Normal Trap support
hooks.why: Some of the deck's cards are Normal Traps that can be searched by effects that add Normal Traps from the Deck, improving consistency.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck of WIND Machine monsters that Normal Summons low-Level pieces and Tuners to climb into WIND Synchro monsters, locking itself into WIND Summons and Pendulum Summoning with its own scales.

hooks.label: WIND monster support
hooks.why: Every Speedroid is a WIND monster and Marble Machine, CarTurbo and Cork Shooter all lock you into WIND-only Special Summons, so cards that search, revive or boost WIND monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: All eleven Speedroid monsters are Machines, so any card that supports, revives or tutors Machine monsters can pick up the deck's pieces.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Marble Machine, Ultra Hound and Fuki-Modoshi Piper all trigger only when Normal Summoned, so anything granting an extra Normal Summon turns each of them into a search, a mill or an excavate.

hooks.label: Rewards being discarded
hooks.why: Speedroid Wheel discards 1 card as its cost to Special Summon from the Deck, so outside monsters that do something when discarded get their effect for free off that card.

profile.plan: An Xyz climb deck: it puts Rank 4 Utopia Xyz Monsters on the field, equips ZW - monsters to them for huge ATK, and uses Rank-Up-Magic to promote them into bigger Number bosses.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: ZS - Ascended Sage adds a Rank-Up-Magic Normal Spell from the Deck and Zexal Construction searches one, so any Rank-Up-Magic Spell is a ready-made way to climb into a higher Rank Xyz.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 4/5 monsters
hooks.why: ZS - Ascended Sage and ZS - Armed Sage Special Summon themselves from the hand while you control no cards or exactly one Level 4 monster, and Zexal Catapult makes your whole field Level 4 or 5, so outside monsters that drop themselves onto the field at those Levels are free Xyz material.

hooks.label: Xyz Material providers
hooks.why: Zexal Field attaches an Xyz Monster from the Extra Deck or GY as material, while ZS - Utopic Sage and ZW - Dragonic Halberd pay by detaching 2 and 1 material, so cards that attach material keep the Xyz Monsters running.

hooks.label: Extra Deck to GY
hooks.why: Zexal Field attaches an Xyz Monster from your Extra Deck or GY to a newly Summoned Xyz Monster, so outside cards that send Extra Deck monsters to the GY stock that fuel up.

hooks.label: Number Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: ZS - Ouroboros Sage revives a non-LIGHT "Number" monster from the GY and ZS - Utopic Sage lets only "Number" monsters attack that turn, so Xyz Monsters from the Number line slot straight into the deck's plays.

hooks.label: Utopia monsters
hooks.why: Zexal Entrust adds or Special Summons a "Utopia" monster from the GY and Zexal Alliance revives one, while ZS - Ascended Sage and ZS - Armed Sage hand their granted effects to a "Utopia" Xyz Monster that used them as material.

profile.plan: A WATER/Fairy deck that stacks Fog Counters on every face-up monster, then removes them to destroy cards, rip the opponent's hand apart or Special Summon Smoke Balls, backed by monsters that cannot be destroyed by battle but kill themselves if left in Defense Position.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Every Cloudian except Eye of the Typhoon is a WATER monster, and Nimbusman can Tribute any number of WATER monsters for its Tribute Summon, so WATER searchers, revivers and boosters feed the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Turbulence, Cirrostratus, Acid Cloud, Altus, Nimbusman and Smoke Ball are all Fairy-Type, so generic Fairy support revives and searches the monsters that actually place Fog Counters.

hooks.label: WATER Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Nimbusman is a Level 5 that can Tribute any number of WATER monsters for its Tribute Summon and places a Fog Counter on itself for each one, so cards that put extra WATER monsters on the field make it enormous.

hooks.label: Forces the battle step
hooks.why: Sheep Cloud, Poison Cloud and Ghost Fog only pay off when they are destroyed by battle, while the rest of the Cloudians are safe in Attack Position, so cards that drag attacks out turn them into Tokens, burn damage and Fog Counters.

hooks.label: Hands the opponent monsters
hooks.why: Cloudian Squall and Storm Dragon place Fog Counters on face-up monsters on either side of the field, and Altus removes Fog Counters from anywhere on the field, so giving the opponent a monster gives you an extra counter to spend and a bigger Nimbusman.

hooks.label: Mills WATER Fairies
hooks.why: Turbulence Special Summons Smoke Ball from either Graveyard, Summon Cloud revives a Level 4 or lower Cloudian from either Graveyard, and Storm Dragon banishes a Cloudian from yours to Summon itself, so filling the Graveyard with WATER Fairy monsters sets up all three.

profile.plan: A WIND Machine Synchro ladder: make Tuners, ride Levels 4 through 8 into Hi-Speedroid Synchro monsters that pierce, burn, double their ATK and recur themselves from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: WIND Machine support
hooks.why: Every Hi-Speedroid is a WIND Machine — Kitedrake's material line demands a WIND Machine Tuner and Rubber Band Shooter needs two WIND monsters — so cards that support that Type and Attribute lift the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level-changing effects
hooks.why: Hi-Speedroid Hagoita Tributes itself to raise the Level of every monster on the field by 1, so a second card that shifts Levels lets the deck land on the exact Synchro Level it needs at any moment.

hooks.label: Machine monsters to mill
hooks.why: Hi-Speedroid Kendama banishes a Machine-Type monster from the Graveyard to burn 500 damage, and Chanbara and Puzzle only work while monsters sit in the GY, so cards that send Machines from the Deck or hand to the Graveyard feed those costs.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck that races out Level 10 Aesir gods (Odin, Thor, Loki) with a Nordic Tuner plus 2+ non-Tuner monsters, drops Fenrir and Jormungardr onto the opponent's field as punishment, and grinds with Nordic Relic Spells/Traps while the gods revive themselves from the GY in the End Phase.

hooks.label: Battle position changers
hooks.why: Jormungardr the Nordic Serpent is Special Summoned to your opponent's field in Defense Position and deals 3000 damage to its controller the moment it is changed to Attack Position, so outside cards that flip your opponent's Defense Position monsters to Attack turn it into a burn piece.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Tuners
hooks.why: Odin, Thor and Loki each require a Tuner plus 2+ non-Tuner monsters, so Tuners that Special Summon themselves from the hand, Deck or GY supply the Tuner half without spending your Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Mills Tuners to the GY
hooks.why: Each Aesir's End Phase revival banishes its named Tuner from your GY, so outside cards that send Tuners from the Deck to the GY keep that cost available.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Every Aesir Synchro asks for a Tuner plus 2+ non-Tuner monsters, so a single card that Special Summons Tokens supplies the extra bodies for a Level 10 Synchro Summon.

profile.plan: A scattered set of Angel cards that mostly share the Fairy/LIGHT and Plant/EARTH bodies, winning through Tribute Summoned Level 5-7 Angels, Counter Trap negation backed by LIGHT Fairy searches, and Angel of Zera growing off the opponent's banished cards.

hooks.label: Counter Trap negations
hooks.why: Harvest Angel of Wisdom adds a Counter Trap back from the GY when it dies, and Power Angel Valkyria adds a LIGHT Fairy from the Deck every time you negate an activation.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fairy support
hooks.why: Power Angel Valkyria, Guardian Angel Joan, Harvest Angel of Wisdom and Angel O7 are all LIGHT Fairies, so Fairy/LIGHT support reaches the deck's whole board.

hooks.label: Easily Tribute Summoned bosses
hooks.why: Angel O7 only gains its Effect Monster lock when it is Tribute Summoned, so the deck is built around Tribute Summoning its Level 5-7 Angels and wants outside monsters that Tribute Summon themselves the same way.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Angel O7's payoff and Queen Angel of Roses' one-Plant Tribute Summon both reward getting high-Level Angels onto the field through a Tribute Summon.

hooks.label: Plant-Type support
hooks.why: Queen Angel of Roses is Tribute Summoned with a single Plant, Fallen Angel of Roses Special Summons itself by returning a Plant you control, and Angel Trumpeter is a Plant Tuner.

hooks.label: Banishes the opponent's cards
hooks.why: Angel of Zera gains 100 ATK for each of the opponent's banished cards, so anything that banishes the opponent's cards grows it while it sits on the field.

profile.plan: An EARTH Fairy deck that discards its own monsters from the hand to search, mill and revive EARTH monsters from the GY, locked into EARTH monster effects while it builds up to five EARTH bodies for Vera and Vernusylph in Full Bloom.

hooks.label: EARTH monster support
hooks.why: Every Vernusylph hand effect ends with "you cannot activate non-EARTH monster effects for the rest of this turn", and both Vera the Vernusylph Goddess and Vernusylph in Full Bloom count 5 or more EARTH monsters you control, so the deck is nothing but EARTH.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Vernusylph monster is a Fairy, and Vernusylph of the Misting Seedlings searches an EARTH Fairy monster straight from the Deck.

hooks.label: Discarded EARTH monsters
hooks.why: Each Vernusylph hand effect discards itself plus 1 monster or 1 "Vernusylph" card as cost, so a second EARTH monster that does something when discarded gets that effect for free, while non-EARTH monsters are shut off by the EARTH-only lock.

hooks.label: Mills EARTH monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Vernusylph of the Awakening Forests sends 1 EARTH monster that can be Normal Summoned/Set from the Deck to the GY, and every other Vernusylph effect then revives an EARTH monster from the GY, so outside cards that fill the GY with EARTH monsters do the same setup.

hooks.label: Self-summoning EARTH monsters
hooks.why: Vera's negation and Vernusylph in Full Bloom's +1000 ATK both want 5 or more EARTH monsters on the field, and Vernusylph Corolla turns every EARTH monster you control into a protected "Vernusylph".

profile.plan: An anti-Synchro Machine deck: its Meklord Emperors Special Summon themselves from the hand whenever a face-up monster you control is destroyed by a card effect, then equip the opponent's Synchro Monsters and gain their ATK.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monster
hooks.why: Meklord Emperor Wisel, Granel and Skiel, plus Nucleus Infinity Core, only Special Summon themselves from the hand or Deck when a face-up monster you control is destroyed by a card effect and sent to the GY.

hooks.label: Recursive Machine monsters
hooks.why: Meklord Assembly destroys one of your monsters as a card effect and Obbligato blows itself up, so outside Machines that do something when they are destroyed or discarded give you the body back.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Meklord is a Machine, and both Army Deployer Obbligato and Astro the Eradicator lock the rest of the turn into Machine-only Special Summons, so Machine search, revival and boosting is always live.

hooks.label: Machines into the Graveyard
hooks.why: Astro Dragon Triskelion banishes three differently named Meklords from your GY and Astro the Eradicator returns three from it, so outside cards that send Machines from the Deck to the GY stock that fuel.

hooks.label: Level 1 Machine summoners
hooks.why: Nucleus Infinity Core and all three Emperor monsters are Level 1 Machines that search or Special Summon themselves the moment they hit the field, so effects that Special Summon Level 1 Machines from the Deck start the engine twice over.

hooks.label: Punishes Synchro Summons
hooks.why: Wisel, Granel and Skiel each steal an opponent's Synchro Monster to equip, and Astro Dragon Asterisk burns 1000 whenever a Synchro Monster is Special Summoned, so cards that lock or punish Synchro Summons stack with the deck's own hate.

profile.plan: A Level 4 LIGHT Spellcaster deck that renames the opponent's Effect Monsters 'Prince of Fairies' to strip their effects, then uses those renamed bodies as Fusion material for its Spellcaster Fusions or Xyz Summons into Wiccat while locked into Spellcaster Special Summons.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Fairy Tail monster is a Spellcaster, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Spellcasters work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Fairy Tail Tales and the GY effect of Tails of the Fairy Tails each grant a Normal Summon of a Spellcaster, and Rochka only triggers when it is Normal Summoned, so extra Normal Summons squeeze more out of them.

hooks.label: Fuses with opponent's board
hooks.why: Tails of the Fairy Tails lets you Fusion Summon using 'Prince of Fairies' your opponent controls as material, so outside cards that Fusion Summon using the opponent's monsters extend the same trick.

profile.plan: A Dragon deck that Fusion Summons Light and Darkness Dragonlord from a Level 8 LIGHT and a Level 8 DARK Dragon, using hands and field, while Light End and Dark End Sublimation/Evaporation Dragons cheat themselves out by banishing a Level 8 Dragon from the Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every monster here is a Dragon and Light End Sublimation Dragon and Dark End Evaporation Dragon lock you into Dragon-only Special Summons for the turn, so generic Dragon support applies to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Special Summons high-Level Dragons
hooks.why: Knight Armed Dragon, the Armored Knight Dragon Special Summons itself from the hand whenever you Special Summon a Level 5 or higher Dragon monster, so outside cards that put such a Dragon on the field give you a free body.

hooks.label: Searches Level 8 Dragons
hooks.why: Light and Darkness Dragonlord and both End Dragons Fusion Summon using monsters from the hand or field, so outside cards that add Level 8 Dragon monsters to the hand supply the material.

profile.plan: A deck of WIND Beast-Warrior/Beast/Rock monsters that chain Normal Summons into each other, bounce the opponent's cards, then return themselves to the hand in the End Phase so the field is empty for the next turn's play.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Every Yosenju monster, Main Deck and Pendulum alike, is WIND, so cards that search, revive or buff WIND monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Bounces opponent's cards
hooks.why: Mayosenju Hitot gains 500 ATK for every card returned to the hand or Deck by your card effect, and Kama 1, the Mayosenju and Yosenju Misak already bounce, so outside bounce effects pile on.

hooks.label: Returns your own monsters to hand
hooks.why: Yosen Whirlwind triggers whenever a face-up Yosenju you control returns to the hand, and Mayosenju Hitot counts that return too, so cards that bounce your own monsters convert into extra removal.

hooks.label: Empty-field starters
hooks.why: Yosenjus' Sword Sting and Yosenju Oroshi Channeling can only be activated while you control no monsters, which happens naturally because the Kamas and Mayosenju return themselves to the hand in the End Phase.

hooks.label: Pendulum Scale providers
hooks.why: Mayosenju Daibak and Hitot cannot be Special Summoned except by Pendulum Summon, and Yosenju Oroshi Channeling and Sabu only fetch the Shinchu scales, so outside cards that search Pendulum monsters or put scales in the Pendulum Zone supply the big monsters.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Kama 1, Kama 2 and Kama 3 each Normal Summon another Yosenju from your hand immediately when they are Normal Summoned, so an extra Normal Summon keeps the chain going.
phrases: in addition to your Normal Summon

profile.plan: A Machine Pendulum Synchro deck that plays no Spells/Traps, dodging between the Pendulum Zone, face-up Extra Deck and GY while attacking from Defense Position with big DEF.

hooks.label: Discard payoff monsters
hooks.why: Wakaushi discards 1 monster to Special Summon from the Deck and Motorbike discards itself to search, so any monster that does something when discarded turns those costs into value.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Superheavy Samurai is a Machine, and Motorbike raises a Machine's Level, Security revives an EARTH Machine and Soulgaia Booster equips to a Machine monster.

hooks.label: Dumps Machines in the GY
hooks.why: Security Tributes itself to Special Summon an EARTH Machine with 1500 or less ATK from the hand or GY, and Commander Shanawo Special Summons a Superheavy Samurai Monster Card from the GY, so anything that sends Machine monsters to the GY hands them targets.

profile.plan: Four Level 4 Warriors with 1700 ATK that Special Summon themselves by discarding a Level 5 or higher DARK or LIGHT monster, then trade further DARK/LIGHT discards for Deck-to-GY sends or banishes.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Dark Grepher and Lightray Grepher both discard a DARK or LIGHT monster as a cost, so an outside DARK or LIGHT monster with an effect when it is discarded is activated for free.

hooks.label: DARK monsters sent from Deck
hooks.why: Dark Grepher's once-per-turn effect sends a DARK monster from your Deck to the GY, so outside DARK monsters with a GY effect get loaded for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: Lightray Grepher banishes a LIGHT monster from your Deck, so outside LIGHT monsters with an effect when they are banished are turned on by it.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: All four Grepher cards are Warrior monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Warriors work on the entire deck.

profile.plan: Fusion Summon Frightfur Fusion Monsters using Fluffal and Edge Imp monsters as materials from the hand, field or Graveyard, then use their effects to destroy cards and gain advantage.

hooks.label: Fluffal monsters
hooks.why: Frightfur Fusion Monsters list Fluffal monsters as Fusion Materials, and Frightfur Meister can Special Summon Level 4 or lower Fluffal monsters from the Deck.

hooks.label: Edge Imp monsters
hooks.why: Frightfur Fusion Monsters list Edge Imp monsters as Fusion Materials, and Frightfur Jar checks for an Edge Imp to destroy a card.

hooks.label: Polymerization support
hooks.why: Frightfur Factory banishes a Polymerization or Fusion Spell from your Graveyard to Fusion Summon, and the deck needs Fusion Spells to start its plays.

hooks.label: Fiend/Fairy banished from GY
hooks.why: Frightfur Fusion banishes Fusion Materials from your Graveyard, so Fiend or Fairy monsters that trigger when banished from the GY get their effects for free.

profile.plan: A stall-control deck built on the Continuous Spell 'Shining Sarcophagus', which searches a card that mentions it each turn while its monsters wall up and its Traps turn the opponent's attacks into board wipes.

hooks.label: Dark Magician cards
hooks.why: Dark Magic Mirror Force only burns 500 per destroyed monster while you control 'Dark Magician', so outside cards that are, search or protect Dark Magician turn the deck's main removal into damage.

hooks.label: Spell/Trap protection
hooks.why: The deck lives off 'Shining Sarcophagus' (a Continuous Spell) and 'Stronghold the Hidden Fortress' (a Continuous Trap); both shrug off monster effects but not Spell/Trap removal, so outside protection for your face-up Spell/Trap Cards keeps the engine alive.

hooks.label: Mills Spells to the GY
hooks.why: 'Turn Silence' banishes itself from the GY during damage calculation to end the Battle Phase, and 'Shining Sarcophagus' wants a Spell to discard, so outside cards that send Spells from the Deck to the GY stock the GY for free.

hooks.label: Forces the attack
hooks.why: 'Dark Magic Mirror Force' and 'Stronghold the Hidden Fortress' both fire when an opponent's monster declares an attack, and 'Moremarshmallon' funnels every attack at itself, so outside cards that make the opponent attack turn the wall into removal.

profile.plan: A slow Trap-heavy control deck: get Temple of the Kings (or Treasures of the Kings, which copies its name) into the Field Zone, Set Apophis Traps and stack up Spells/Traps and Traps in the GY so The Man with the Mark searches, Anubis the Last Judge can Special Summon itself, and Verdict of Anubis wipes the opponent's board.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Treasures of the Kings is a Field Spell that becomes 'Temple of the Kings' in the Field Zone, and every monster effect in the deck is gated on controlling Temple of the Kings, so any card that fetches a Field Spell starts the whole engine.

hooks.label: Sets Traps from the Deck
hooks.why: Treasures of the Kings Sets an 'Apophis' Trap from the Deck, and Verdict of Anubis needs 3 or more other Spells/Traps you control, so any card that Sets Traps from the Deck builds both requirements at once.

hooks.label: Sends Traps to the GY
hooks.why: Treasures of the Kings only re-adds a monster while you have a Trap in the GY or 2+ Set cards, and Anubis the Last Judge needs 3 or more differently named Traps/Temple cards in the GY to Special Summon itself, so milling Traps is fuel.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Anubis the Last Judge triggers when a Spell/Trap you control is destroyed by card effect, destroying an opponent's card, so cards that blow up your own backrow turn into free removal.

hooks.label: Apophis cards
hooks.why: The Man with the Mark protects 'Apophis' monsters you control and Treasures of the Kings Sets an 'Apophis' Trap straight from the Deck, so the deck already calls for those cards without naming them as Temple cards.

profile.plan: A deck of Level 10 Dragon, Wyrm, Dinosaur and Sea Serpent monsters that searches and places the 'Ryu-Ge Realm' Continuous Spells to weaken, bounce and negate the opponent's board, then keeps reviving itself from the GY and banishment.

hooks.label: Mills your own hand and Deck
hooks.why: Kairo Ryu-Ge Emva Special Summons itself from the GY in the Main Phase once 2 or more monsters were sent from the hand and/or Deck to the GY that turn, so any outside card that mills or discards monsters turns it on.

hooks.label: Banishes your own monsters
hooks.why: Genro Ryu-Ge Hakva Special Summons itself from banishment once 2 or more other monsters are banished, and Ryu-Ge War Zone already sends a Dinosaur, Sea Serpent and Wyrm to the hand, GY and banishment, so any effect that banishes your monsters from Deck or GY feeds it.

hooks.label: Floats when destroyed
hooks.why: Sosei Ryu-Ge Mistva destroys up to 2 cards you control when it Special Summons itself, while Tensei Ryu-Ge Anva and Ryu-Ge End both place a Ryu-Ge Spell/Trap when they are destroyed, so outside cards with an effect when destroyed get turned on by the same play.

hooks.label: Dragon, Wyrm, Dinosaur and Sea Serpent support
hooks.why: Ryu-Ge War Zone locks you into Special Summoning only Dragon, Dinosaur, Sea Serpent and Wyrm monsters for the rest of the turn, which covers every monster the deck plays.

hooks.label: Places Continuous Spells
hooks.why: Sosei Ryu-Ge Mistva places up to 2 'Ryu-Ge' Continuous Spells from the Deck, and every Realm Quick Effect costs a Continuous Spell placed on the bottom of the Deck, so outside cards that put Continuous Spells onto the field keep the engine running.

profile.plan: A slow Machine deck that Sets its Geargia monsters face-down so their flip effects search and destroy, then revives them into Rank 3 and Rank 4 Machine Xyz plays.

hooks.label: Machine-Type support
hooks.why: Every Geargia monster is a Machine, Gear Gigant X asks for 2 Level 4 Machine monsters and Geargiagear Gigant XG for 3 Level 3 monsters, and Geargiauger searches Level 4 EARTH Machines.

hooks.label: Flips your Set monsters up
hooks.why: Geargiarmor, Geargianchor and Geargiattacker only search or destroy when they are flipped face-up, so effects that turn your own face-down monsters up set those off yourself.

hooks.label: Fills the Graveyard with Machines
hooks.why: Geargiano revives a Level 4 Machine from the Graveyard, Geargia Change Special Summons Geargiano monsters from the Graveyard and Gear Gigant X adds from the Graveyard, so loading Machines there is worth it.

hooks.label: Reacts to being detached
hooks.why: Gear Gigant X detaches an Xyz Material every turn and Geargiagear Gigant XG detaches one in the Battle Step, so monsters that do something when they are detached get used for free.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Geargiano Mk-II and Geargiauger only fire off a Normal Summon and Geargiarmor wants to be Set, so extra Normal Summons get more of those effects online in one turn.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck whose small Cyberse, Psychic, Warrior and Spellcaster monsters Special Summon themselves from the hand by revealing a Ritual Monster, then Ritual Summon Libromancer bosses by Tributing from hand or field so they get direct attacks, doubled battle damage and protection.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: Libromancer Fire, Geek Boy, Magigirl and Agent all Special Summon themselves from the hand by revealing a Ritual Monster, and the Ritual Summons need one in hand, so anything that adds a Ritual Monster to hand switches the whole engine on.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: Every Ritual Summon in the deck goes through Libromancer Bonded or Libromancer First Appearance, and the archetype's own search for them is thin (Geek Boy and Origin Story), so outside cards that add a Ritual Spell from the Deck or GY find the missing half.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: First Appearance, Magigirl and Bonded all Ritual Summon by Tributing monsters from your hand or field, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed are free material rather than a cost.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Doombroker attacks directly, Fireburst gets its double damage and battle protection, and Firestarter and Mystigirl get their protections only when the Ritual Summon uses a monster on the field, so outside cards that Special Summon Tokens supply that material for free.

hooks.label: Extra attacks and direct attacks
hooks.why: Doombroker can attack directly and shuffles a monster into the Deck when it deals battle damage, and Fireburst doubles its own battle damage and attacks twice, so outside cards that add attacks or let Ritual Monsters push damage through fit the deck's win route.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Machine/Fairy/Thunder deck that turns its own Tuners into Equip Cards and loops Equip Spells, Synchro Summoning Vylon monsters that send those Equip Cards to the Graveyard for searches and removal.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: Vylon Cube and Vylon Delta both add an Equip Spell Card from the Deck, and the whole deck needs a constant supply of them, so any outside card that fetches Equip Spells is another engine piece.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster support
hooks.why: Every Vylon monster is LIGHT, Vylon Charger gives all your LIGHT monsters 300 ATK per Equip Card, and the Synchro Monsters demand LIGHT materials.

hooks.label: Union Monster support
hooks.why: Vylon Tesseract and Vylon Pentachloro are Union Monsters that equip themselves to a Vylon monster and reward it with a revival or a destruction, so cards built around Union Monsters keep that half of the deck running.

hooks.label: Pops your own Equip Spells
hooks.why: Vylon Filament, Vylon Material, Vylon Segment and Vylon Component all add a Vylon Spell when they are sent from the field to the Graveyard, and Vylon Element Special Summons Vylon Tuners when a Vylon Equip Card is destroyed, so outside cards that destroy your own Equip Spell turn into searches and bodies.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Dragon Xyz deck that stacks Level 4 and Level 8 LIGHT monsters, turns them into Rank 4 and Rank 8 Dragon Xyz Monsters, and keeps those Xyz loaded with material.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster support
hooks.why: Galaxy War Drake and Galaxy Defense Robot Orbital 7 lock you into Special Summoning only LIGHT monsters, Galaxy Photon Dragon and Galaxy Summoner only boost or retune LIGHT monsters, and Galaxy Journey revives LIGHT or DARK banished monsters.

hooks.label: LIGHT Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Xyz boss here is a LIGHT Dragon: Galaxy-Eyes Tachyon Primal only attaches itself to a Dragon Xyz Monster, and Numeron Creation needs 3 LIGHT Dragon monsters with 3000 or more original ATK on the field.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic cards
hooks.why: Neo Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon - Photon Howling, Galaxy-Eyes Antimatter Dragon and Number S38: Titanic Galaxy all Xyz Summon themselves on top of an Xyz Monster you already control, which is exactly what a Rank-Up-Magic card does.

hooks.label: Number Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Numbers Last Hope and Numeron Creation can only Xyz Summon a 'Number' Xyz Monster, and Galaxy Hundred can Special Summon a 'Number' monster straight out of the opponent's Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Level 8 LIGHT material
hooks.why: Neo Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon - Photon Howling asks for 3 Level 8 monsters while Galaxy Photon Dragon, Galaxy Summoner and Galaxy War Drake turn LIGHT monsters into Level 8, so free Level 8 LIGHT bodies are extra Xyz material.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Xyz deck of Level 4 LIGHT Warrior tellarknight monsters that churns out Delteros, Triverr and Ptolemaeus, spending Xyz Materials for spot removal, hand disruption, a field-wide bounce and an upgrade into the Rank 5 Constellar Diamond.

hooks.label: Level 4 LIGHT bodies
hooks.why: Delteros and Ptolemaeus each ask for three Level 4 monsters as Xyz Material, so outside monsters that Special Summon themselves are extra Rank 4 fodder.

hooks.label: Value when used as material
hooks.why: Delteros, Triverr and Ptolemaeus all pay Xyz Materials for their effects, so outside monsters that give something when they are used as Xyz Material get spent for free.

hooks.label: Attaches itself as Xyz Material
hooks.why: Constellar Diamond and Ptolemaeus only keep their effects while they have Xyz Material, so outside cards that attach themselves to an Xyz Monster keep them loaded between detaches.

hooks.label: Warrior and LIGHT support
hooks.why: Capella, Delteros, Triverr and Ptolemaeus are LIGHT Warriors and Constellar Diamond is LIGHT, so support that searches, revives or boosts Warrior or LIGHT monsters works across the deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when bounced
hooks.why: Triverr returns every other card on the field to the hand when it is Xyz Summoned, so outside cards with an effect when they are returned to the hand trigger off your own Xyz Summon.

profile.plan: A loose pile of Normal Monsters and WATER Reptiles that wins by piercing with Lion Alligator, Tribute Summoning Level 5 beaters like Cyber-Tech Alligator and Spawn Alligator, and fusing into Alligator's Sword Dragon.

hooks.label: Reptile-Type support
hooks.why: Lion Alligator only grants piercing battle damage while you control another Reptile-Type monster, and Spawn Alligator must be Tribute Summoned by Tributing a Reptile-Type monster, so generic Reptile support advances both.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Alligator's Sword, Toon Alligator and Cyber-Tech Alligator are all Normal Monsters, and Alligator's Sword is a named Fusion Material, so cards that search, revive or protect Normal Monsters build the whole deck.

hooks.label: Reptile Summoners
hooks.why: Spawn Alligator Special Summons the Reptile-Type monster that was Tributed for its Tribute Summon, so cards that Special Summon Reptile-Type monsters supply the Tribute and then come back for free.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon support
hooks.why: Alligator's Sword Dragon is the deck's only Extra Deck monster and names both materials, so any effect that Fusion Summons or supplies Fusion Material gets it onto the field.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Cyber-Tech Alligator and Spawn Alligator are Level 5 monsters whose payoff only happens on a Tribute Summon, so extra Normal Summons and Tribute Summon enablers are how the deck gets them out.

profile.plan: A control deck that Tributes its small Psychic searchers to banish cards and cheat out the Level 8 Myutant bosses, then Fusion Summons Synthesis and Ultimus using the banished pile as material.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: M-05, ST-46, Mutant, GB-88 and every Level 8 Myutant banish a card from your hand or face-up field as part of their effects, so a monster that pays you back when it is banished makes that cost free.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: M-05, ST-46, GB-88, Mutant and both Fusion Monsters are Psychic, so cards that search, revive or boost Psychics work on the whole engine.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: M-05 and ST-46 only search when they are Normal or Special Summoned, so a second Normal Summon lets you fetch a Myutant monster and a Myutant Spell/Trap in the same turn.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon support
hooks.why: Myutant Fusion and Myutant Cry Fusion Summon Synthesis and Ultimus out of the hand, field, GY, Deck and banished pile, so cards that enable Fusion Summons or supply Fusion Material keep the bosses coming.

hooks.label: Field Spell tutors
hooks.why: GB-88 can only use its effect while Myutant Evolution Lab is in the Field Zone, and the Field Spell is the deck's revival, ATK and draw engine, so getting it out is what the deck is missing.

profile.plan: An aggro FIRE Warrior deck that cheats "Flame Swordsman" and its Fusion upgrades out of the Extra Deck with its own Spells and Trap, stacks Equip Spells for ATK boosts and extra attacks, and turns every monster it sends to the GY into another Special Summon.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck monster is a FIRE Warrior, Salamandra Fusion can only equip a FIRE Warrior monster, and Dark Flare Swordsman restricts attacks to Warrior monsters.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Flame Swordsrealm sends 1 monster from your hand or face-up field to the GY to Special Summon "Flame Swordsman", so outside monsters with a "sent to the GY" trigger get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Flips your own monsters face-down
hooks.why: Flame Swordsdance's GY effect Tributes 1 face-down Defense Position monster to Special Summon from the Deck or Extra Deck, so cards that Set or flip your own monsters supply that cost.

hooks.label: Cheats out Extra Deck Fusions
hooks.why: Flame Swordsrealm, Salamandra Fusion and Flame Swordsdance all Special Summon "Flame Swordsman" or a Fusion Monster that mentions it straight from the Extra Deck, so outside cards that Special Summon Fusion Monsters from the Extra Deck are more of the same.

profile.plan: A control deck of Rock EARTH monsters that Set and flip themselves face-down, then Flip Summon to bounce or shuffle the opponent's whole board while Beast LIGHT boss monsters burn through battle.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-up
hooks.why: Guardian Sphinx and Pharaonic Guardian Sphinx only clear the opponent's board when Flip Summoned, and both can turn themselves face-down again, so any card that flips a face-down Rock up restarts the loop.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Guardian Sphinx, Criosphinx, Hieracosphinx, Exxod and Pharaonic Guardian Sphinx are all Rock EARTH monsters, so Rock support reaches nearly the whole deck.

hooks.label: Bounces opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Criosphinx makes the owner of any monster returned from the field to the hand discard a card, and Guardian Sphinx's Flip Summon returns the opponent's entire board, so extra bounce effects stack the discard punishment.

hooks.label: Special Summons face-down
hooks.why: Hieracosphinx stops the opponent attacking face-down Defense Position monsters and both Guardian Sphinxes Flip Summon out of that position, so cards that Special Summon Rocks face-down add both defense and Flip Summon fuel.

profile.plan: A Warrior/EARTH Level 4 beatdown deck that uses Normal Monster support and aims to inflict battle damage with Celtic Guard of Noble Arms to draw cards.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Celtic Guardian is a Normal Monster, so cards that search, revive or boost Normal Monsters work with it.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: All Celtic Guard monsters are Warriors, so cards that support Warrior-Type monsters fit.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: All Celtic Guard monsters are EARTH, so cards that support EARTH monsters fit.

hooks.label: Battle damage enablers
hooks.why: Celtic Guard of Noble Arms draws cards when it inflicts battle damage, so cards that let your monsters attack directly, deal piercing damage or attack multiple times help.

hooks.label: Battle damage triggers
hooks.why: Celtic Guard of Noble Arms has an effect when it inflicts battle damage, so outside cards that trigger on battle damage being inflicted give extra value.

profile.plan: A Warrior deck built around slow Level 5 and Level 8 Tribute monsters — Swamp and Lava Battleguard pump each other, King Tributes Warriors for extra attacks, and Echoes/Rage/Howling turn the opponent's monsters into bounce fodder.

hooks.label: Rewarded for being Tributed
hooks.why: Battleguard King Tributes any number of Warrior-Type monsters and Battleguard Cadet Tributes itself, so outside Warrior monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Bounces monsters to the hand
hooks.why: Battleguard Echoes can activate an effect every time a monster is returned from the field to the hand, and Howling and Rage only bounce the opponent's monsters, so more bounce effects keep Echoes live.

hooks.label: Warrior-Type support
hooks.why: Every Battleguard is a Warrior, and Battleguard King Tributes Warrior-Type monsters while Battleguard Rage and Battleguard Howling only work with Warrior-Type monsters you control.

profile.plan: A Fairy Synchro deck that parks its Extra Deck monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, banishes cards in matching columns, and hands its own monsters to the opponent while two Field Spells grow off each parked Angelechy.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Angelechy monster (Destrier, Shatranga, Bastion, Castellan, Enlisted, Seneschal) is a Fairy, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Fairies works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Angelechy Endgame Problem and Angelechy Problem are the deck's engines and Endgame Problem scales off the Angelechy monsters in your Spell & Trap Zone, so outside cards that add or place a Field Spell are extra copies of the key piece.

hooks.label: Sets Traps from Deck or GY
hooks.why: Angelechy Endgame Problem's 3+ effect lets you activate a Trap the turn it was Set, and the deck's Normal Traps (Disturbance, Verdict, Opening to e4) all have Graveyard effects, so outside cards that Set Traps give that line more ammunition.

profile.plan: Level-up Dragons: Horus the Black Flame Dragon LV4 and LV6 each have to destroy a monster by battle and then send themselves to the Graveyard in the End Phase to bring out the next form, ending on the 3000 ATK LV8 that negates Spell Cards and cannot be Summoned any other way.

hooks.label: Piercing and extra attacks
hooks.why: LV4 (1600 ATK) and LV6 (2300 ATK) must destroy a monster by battle in the same turn to level up, so outside cards that grant piercing or let a monster attack again make that kill happen through bigger or multiple defenders.

hooks.label: Weakens the opponent's monsters
hooks.why: The level-up only counts when Horus destroys a monster by battle, and its ATK is low, so outside cards that drop the opponent's monsters' ATK or turn them into Attack Position give LV4 and LV6 a legal kill every turn.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: LV4, LV6 and LV8 are all Dragon-Type and the deck lives on LV6's Spell immunity and LV8's Spell negation, so outside cards that search, revive or protect Dragons work on the entire core.

hooks.label: FIRE support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck, including Horus' Servant, is FIRE, so outside cards that support FIRE monsters boost the low-ATK level-up forms or recover them.

profile.plan: Rank-Up Xyz Summoning: turns an Xyz Monster into a higher-Rank 'Number C' or 'CXyz' monster and uses the detached materials for burn and control effects.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic spells
hooks.why: The archetype's own Rank-Up-Magic cards summon CXyz monsters by ranking up an Xyz Monster, so other Rank-Up-Magic cards provide additional ways to do the same.

hooks.label: Self-attaching Xyz Material
hooks.why: CXyz monsters like Dark Fairy Cheer Girl, Comics Hero Legend Arthur, and Coach Lord Ultimatrainer detach Xyz Material to activate their effects, so cards that turn themselves into material give them extra uses.

hooks.label: Xyz Monster revival
hooks.why: Rank-Up-Magic Admiration of the Thousands targets Xyz Monsters in the Graveyard to attach as material, so cards that revive or fill the Graveyard with Xyz Monsters support it.

profile.plan: A Machine Link deck that Special Summons small R.B. monsters, pays Life Points to destroy them for negation and removal, and gains LP back to keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every R.B. monster is a Machine, so cards that support Machine monsters (search, revive, boost) help the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers on Machine destruction
hooks.why: Many R.B. cards (Ga10 Cutter, Driller, Rocket, Lambda Cannon, Lambda Blade, Pile Bunker, Next Phase) destroy your own Machine monsters as a cost, so outside cards that trigger when a Machine monster you control is destroyed get value.

hooks.label: Removes your own Machine
hooks.why: R.B. Funk Dock Special Summons an R.B. monster when a face-up R.B. monster leaves the field by card effect, so outside cards that destroy, return, or banish your own Machine monsters trigger it.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Machines
hooks.why: The R.B. main deck monsters Special Summon themselves from hand when you control no face-up monsters or only R.B. monsters, so outside Machine monsters that can do the same provide free Link material.

hooks.label: Life Point gain
hooks.why: Most R.B. monster effects pay LP as a cost (500-1500), so outside cards that gain LP let you use those effects more often.

profile.plan: A Warrior/EARTH deck that tags its monsters in and out, returning a U.A. to the hand to Special Summon a bigger one from hand, and leaning on U.A. Stadium to search every time it Normal Summons a U.A.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every U.A. monster is a Warrior (and EARTH), so cards that search, revive or power up Warriors work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell tutors
hooks.why: U.A. Stadium and U.A. Hyper Stadium are the deck's engine, and Hyper Stadium asks you to reveal a Field Spell from hand to gain its extra Normal Summon, so cards that fetch or place Field Spells keep it online.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: U.A. Stadium only searches when a U.A. monster is Normal Summoned, and U.A. Hyper Stadium grants one additional Normal Summon, so any effect that gives more Normal Summons is another search.

hooks.label: Discarded monsters
hooks.why: U.A. Perfect Ace discards a card as the cost of its Quick Effect negation, so monsters that do something when they are discarded turn that cost into value.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Fusion Summoning Spells that pull materials from the hand, field, Deck, GY, banishment and Extra Deck, each aimed at a specific Type or Attribute of Fusion Monster.

hooks.label: Fusion Material trigger
hooks.why: Heavy Polymerization, Super Duper Polymerization, Face Card Fusion and Future Fusion Nova all use monsters as Fusion Material, so a monster that does something when used as material gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: Discard payoff
hooks.why: Fusion Draft discards 1 card as its cost, so a monster that triggers when discarded turns that cost into value.

profile.plan: A Ritual-climb deck: it Ritual Summons a 'Nouvelles' monster with a 'Recipe' Ritual Spell, then each Ritual Monster's Quick Effect Tributes itself plus an Attack Position monster to Special Summon the next Level Nouvelles from the hand or Deck, turning the opponent's board into the next course.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: Every Nouvelles boss except the two Pendulum monsters must be Ritual Summoned from the hand, and Balameuniere de Nouvelles only adds a 'Nouvelles' or 'Recipe' card, so generic Ritual Monster tutors find the body the chain needs.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: A Nouvelles Ritual Monster can only be Ritual Summoned with a 'Recipe' card, which is a Ritual Spell, and Nouvelles Restaurant "At Table" only fetches one when it is activated, so other Ritual Spell tutors keep the climb going.

hooks.label: Recovers Ritual Monsters from the GY
hooks.why: Poeltis, Foie Glasya, Confiras and Buerillabaisse Tribute a Nouvelles Ritual Monster as the cost of their Quick Effect, so the bosses pile up in the GY and cards like Preparation of Rites that add a Ritual Monster back to the hand refill the Recipe materials.

hooks.label: Attack Position enablers
hooks.why: Every Nouvelles Quick Effect can only Tribute an Attack Position monster on either field, and Recettes de Nouvellez only forces the opponent's monsters to Attack Position while you control a Nouvelles Monster Card, so outside effects that turn defenders into attackers give the chain more food.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: The 'Recipe' Ritual Spells and every Nouvelles Quick Effect Tribute monsters as cost, so outside cards that do something when they are Tributed (or used as Ritual material) get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Chef de Nouvelles raises an Effect Monster's Level by up to 3 and the Recipe Book raises a freshly Summoned Ritual Monster's Level by 1, because the 'Recipe' Ritual Spells and the Quick Effect chain care about exact Levels, so other Level-changing effects help line up a Ritual Summon.

profile.plan: Each 'Signature move' is the iconic finisher of a different boss monster — Yubel, Gate Guardian, Red Dragon Archfiend, Galaxy/Tachyon, Metalzoa — so the deck runs several small engines side by side and wants generically-shared support.

hooks.label: Effect negation enablers
hooks.why: Tachyon Spiral of Destruction destroys every face-up card the opponent controls whose effects are negated, so any outside card that negates a face-up card's effects turns it into a board wipe.

hooks.label: DARK monsters that float
hooks.why: Nightmare Pain destroys 1 DARK monster in your hand or face-up field as its cost, so DARK monsters that do something when they are destroyed turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Fish, Sea Serpent, Aqua or WATER support
hooks.why: Virtue Stream targets 1 Fish, Sea Serpent or Aqua monster you control and its Graveyard effect rewards a WATER monster, so cards supporting those Types or the WATER Attribute fit.

hooks.label: Metalmorph Traps
hooks.why: Metalzoa X reveals itself in hand to Set a 'Metalmorph' Trap from the Deck and is brought out by Max Metalmorph, so Metalmorph Traps are directly searchable in this deck.

profile.plan: A Field Spell deck that keeps Golden Castle of Stromberg on the field, summons its own Level 4 monsters straight from the Deck, banishes ten cards every Standby Phase, and punishes any attack with destruction and burn.

hooks.label: Field Spell support
hooks.why: Golden Castle of Stromberg must sit in the Field Zone for Hexe Trude's free Normal Summon, Iron Knight's Warrior search, Prinzessin's equip and Iron Cage's removal, so cards that find or guard a Field Spell keep the whole deck switched on.

hooks.label: Attack punishment
hooks.why: Golden Castle of Stromberg already destroys any monster that declares an attack and burns for half its ATK, so cards that trigger on an attack declaration stack more of the same deterrent.

hooks.label: Forces the opponent to attack
hooks.why: The Castle's attack trigger destroys the attacker and inflicts half its ATK as damage, so effects that force the opponent's monsters to attack turn their own board into burn.

hooks.label: Banished-pile payoffs
hooks.why: Golden Castle of Stromberg banishes 10 cards from the Deck face-down every Standby Phase, so a huge banished pile builds itself for cards that grow with it.

hooks.label: Wants to hit the GY
hooks.why: Iron Cage sends a monster you control to the GY and later revives it, so monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY get a free activation out of it.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that moves its monsters between Monster Zones to trigger effects, and places monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells to Special Summon or use as Fusion material.

hooks.label: Moves monsters to adjacent zones
hooks.why: Every monster in this archetype triggers when it moves to another Monster Zone, so outside cards that move monsters let you trigger them.

hooks.label: Consumes Continuous Spells
hooks.why: The deck places its own Pendulum monsters and the opponent's monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, so outside cards that send Continuous Spells to the GY have fodder.

hooks.label: Pendulum Zone / S/T Zone movers
hooks.why: The deck places its Pendulum monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, so cards that move them back to the Pendulum Zone or Special Summon them (like 'Pendulum Switch') are ideal.

hooks.label: Pendulum Fusion support
hooks.why: The deck's Fusion Monsters are Pendulum monsters, and one of its monsters can Fusion Summon using monsters from Pendulum Zones, so cards that Fusion Summon using Pendulum monsters as material (like 'Pendulum Fusion') help.

hooks.label: Pendulum Link monsters
hooks.why: The deck can still Special Summon from the Extra Deck despite its lock, and its monsters are Pendulum, so Link monsters that support Pendulum (like 'Heavymetalfoes Electrumite') are easy to summon and powerful.

profile.plan: Infects the opponent's Deck with Parasite Paracide to burn them and turn their monsters into Insects, while using Union equips and Fusion Parasite as support.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Most Parasite monsters are Insect-Type, and Parasite Paracide turns the opponent's monsters into Insects, so Insect support works for the whole deck.

hooks.label: Equip Spell support
hooks.why: Lunatite and Soltite become Equip Spell Cards, and Parasite Paranoid equips itself as an Equip Card, so cards that search or support Equip Spells help the deck.

hooks.label: Makes opponent draw
hooks.why: Parasite Paracide is placed in the opponent's Deck and triggers when they draw it, so forcing the opponent to draw speeds up the infection and damage.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-up
hooks.why: Parasite Paracide's Flip Effect only triggers when it is flipped face-up, so cards that flip it for you activate it without waiting for an attack.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster deck that leans on Legion the Fiend Jester's extra Tribute Summon and its search for Spellcaster Normal Monsters, with Jester Confit as a free body and Jester Lord as a backrow-fed beater.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summon effects
hooks.why: Legion the Fiend Jester's extra Tribute Summon is only worth it when you can Normal Summon and Tribute Summon in the same turn, so cards granting an additional Tribute Summon double the payoff.

hooks.label: Tributing your Spellcasters
hooks.why: Legion the Fiend Jester searches a Spellcaster Normal Monster when it is sent from the field to the GY, so Spellcaster effects that Tribute a Spellcaster turn it into a search.

hooks.label: Fills the Spell & Trap Zones
hooks.why: Jester Lord gains 1000 ATK for each card in the Spell & Trap Card Zones while it is your only monster, so cards that place Spells and Traps face-up on the field feed it directly.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: All three Jesters are DARK Spellcasters, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Spellcasters apply to the entire deck.

profile.plan: A Umi/Normal Monster control deck: Pacifis, the Phantasm City searches Phantasm Spiral cards and makes Level 8 WATER Wyrm Tokens, while the Phantasm Spiral Equip Spells turn a Normal Monster into a battle engine that cheats out Phantasm Spiral Dragon.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Phantasm Spiral Battle and Phantasm Spiral Power only work while every monster you control is a Normal Monster, and all three Equip Spells can only be equipped to a Normal Monster, so the whole deck is built on Normal Monsters.

hooks.label: Summons Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Pacifis, the Phantasm City adds a Phantasm Spiral card whenever you Normal or Special Summon exactly 1 Normal Monster, and the Equip Spells need a Normal Monster on the field to attach to, so outside cards that put Normal Monsters on the field or into the hand feed the engine.

hooks.label: Umi cards
hooks.why: Pacifis, the Phantasm City is always treated as "Umi", which lets all three Phantasm Spiral Traps be activated from the hand, so cards that reference, search or protect "Umi" directly upgrade the deck's trap line.

hooks.label: Equip Spell retrieval
hooks.why: Phantasm Spiral Assault asks for Phantasm Spiral Dragon equipped with 3 differently named Phantasm Spiral Equip Spells, so outside cards that add Equip Spell Cards from the Deck or Graveyard assemble the win condition.

hooks.label: Extra attacks and piercing
hooks.why: Phantasm Spiral Grip, Wave and Crash all trigger when the equipped Normal Monster destroys a monster by battle, inflicts battle damage or battles, so outside cards that grant a Normal Monster extra attacks or piercing battle damage fire those effects more often.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Phantasm Spiral Dragon and the Phantasm Spiral Token that Pacifis, the Phantasm City Special Summons are both WATER, so cards that support the WATER attribute boost the deck's only bodies.

profile.plan: Aqua WATER monsters that want to be destroyed so they equip themselves to an opponent's monster and steal it, then Synchro Summon with an Aqua Tuner into Graydle Dragon.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Aqua monster
hooks.why: Graydle Eagle, Graydle Alligator and Graydle Cobra only equip themselves to an opponent's monster and take control of it when a card effect destroys them and sends them to the Graveyard, so outside cards that blow up your own Aqua monsters are activators.

hooks.label: Aqua and WATER support
hooks.why: Every Graydle monster is an Aqua WATER monster and Graydle Dragon asks for WATER and Aqua material, so cards that search, revive or boost Aqua or WATER monsters advance the whole deck.

hooks.label: Monsters that want destroying
hooks.why: Graydle Split can be equipped to any face-up monster you control and later destroys it to Summon two Graydle monsters, so outside monsters with an effect when they are destroyed and sent to the Graveyard get that trigger for free.

profile.plan: A Pyro control deck that turns its own Pyro-Type monsters into ammunition: the Blaze Accelerator cards send them from the hand or Deck to the Graveyard as a cost to destroy the opponent's monsters, at the price of giving up attacks.

hooks.label: Pyro monsters for the GY
hooks.why: Blaze Accelerator and Tri-Blaze Accelerator send a Pyro-Type monster from your hand to the Graveyard as a cost, and Volcanic Blaze Accelerator does the same from the Deck, so Pyro monsters with an effect when they are sent there get it for free.

hooks.label: Pyro support
hooks.why: Every effect in the archetype is paid for with a Pyro-Type monster, so cards that search, revive or boost Pyro-Type monsters feed the whole engine.

hooks.label: Pyro recovery from the GY
hooks.why: The deck spends Pyro-Type monsters as costs over and over, so outside cards that bring Pyro-Type monsters back from the Graveyard keep it supplied with ammunition.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Xyz deck whose Level 4 Heraldic Beasts flood the field, recycle each other out of the Graveyard, and turn into Psychic-Type 'Number' Xyz Monsters that reattach and re-use Xyz Material.

hooks.label: Mills monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Heraldic Beast Leo searches a Heraldic Beast when it is sent to the Graveyard, and Advanced Heraldry Art, Heraldry Reborn, Unicorn, Aberconway and Twin-Headed Eagle all need Heraldic Beasts sitting in the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Psychic-Type support
hooks.why: Augmented Heraldry shields Psychic-Type Xyz Monsters and restricts your Summons to Psychic-Type Xyz Monsters and Heraldic Beast monsters, and Unicorn revives a Psychic-Type Xyz Monster from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Number Xyz monsters
hooks.why: Heraldic Beast Gryphon counts as 2 materials for a 'Number' Xyz Monster needing 3 or more materials, and the deck's Xyz Summons may only use monsters with 'Heraldic Beast' or 'Number' in their original names as material.

hooks.label: Monsters that pay off being Tributed
hooks.why: Charged-Up Heraldry Tributes 1 monster as its cost to Special Summon 2 Heraldic Beasts from the Deck, so an outside monster that triggers when it is Tributed is free value there.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of FIRE Warrior Normal Monsters: it destroys its own Pendulum Zone scales to search FIRE Warriors, swarms the field with Level 3-6 bodies, and overlays them (or drops Igknight Champion and Lancer by blowing up its own cards).

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: All eight Igknight monsters are Normal Monsters, so cards that add or Special Summon Normal Monsters from the Deck or Graveyard refill the Pendulum Zones and supply extra Level 3-6 material.

hooks.label: Searching Pendulum Monsters
hooks.why: The deck is built entirely from Pendulum Monsters and Igknight Reload shuffles spare Pendulum Monsters from the hand back into the Deck to draw, so anything that adds a Pendulum Monster to the hand keeps the scale engine supplied.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Igknight monster is a Warrior and the deck's searches only reach Warriors, so generic Warrior support touches the whole deck.

profile.plan: Summons the three Sacred Beasts as Level 10 monsters, then banishes them with Dimension Fusion Destruction to bring out Armityle the Chaos Phantasm ignoring its Summoning conditions, or fuses three Level 10 monsters into Phantasm Emperor Trilojig to burn the opponent.

hooks.label: Fiend and DARK support
hooks.why: Armityle the Chaos Phantasm and Phantasm Emperor Trilojig are both Fiend and DARK, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends/DARK monsters work on the deck's bosses.

hooks.label: Revives from the GY
hooks.why: Phantasm Emperor Trilojig burns the opponent whenever another monster is Special Summoned from the GY to your field while you control it, so outside cards that revive monsters turn into repeatable damage.

profile.plan: A Flip monster deck that sets monsters face-down, uses FLIP effects to search and Special Summon, and sends its own cards from Deck to GY to build towards a Link 3 boss that gains ATK from the GY and linked zones.

hooks.label: Sends from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Tindangle Dholes and Tindangle Intruder trigger when a Tindangle card is sent from the Deck to the GY, and Acute Cerberus needs Tindangle monsters in the GY.

hooks.label: Special Summons face-down
hooks.why: Tindangle Intruder Special Summons itself from the GY when a monster is Special Summoned to your field in face-down Defense Position, and the deck's Flip monsters want to be set.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-up
hooks.why: The deck is full of Flip monsters whose FLIP effects only trigger when they are flipped face-up, so outside cards that flip them are extra activators.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Tindangle monster is a Fiend, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Tindangle Jhrelth and Stairs of Mail discard cards as a cost, so outside cards that benefit from being discarded turn that cost into value.

profile.plan: A Cyberse DARK deck that Link Summons big monsters using its own monsters as material, triggering their effects when sent to the GY, and the Link monsters grow stronger with different Attributes and card types.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is Cyberse, and most effects search, revive or send Cyberse monsters, so generic Cyberse support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Cynet Spell/Trap
hooks.why: A Level 5 monster in the archetype can add a 'Cynet' Spell/Trap from the Deck to the hand when sent to the GY as Link Material.

hooks.label: A.I. Spell
hooks.why: The Synchro monster can add an 'A.I.' Spell from the Deck to the hand when sent to the GY as Link Material.

hooks.label: Link Material triggers
hooks.why: The deck Link Summons constantly, so outside Cyberse monsters that do something when used as Link Material (like several archetype monsters do) get their effects for free.

profile.plan: A Beast-Type deck that Special Summons low-Level Beasts from the Deck and Graveyard, using them to destroy cards, search, and swarm while supporting Winged Beast, Insect, and Plant monsters.

hooks.label: EARTH Beast support
hooks.why: Every Mystical Beast of the Forest monster is an EARTH Beast, so support for that Type and Attribute works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Valerifawn discards a card as cost, and Carpiponica triggers when sent from hand to GY, so monsters that activate when discarded get value.

hooks.label: Beast that triggers when banished
hooks.why: Cerynemesia banishes a Beast monster from your hand or field to Special Summon an EARTH Beast from the Deck, so a Beast with a banished trigger turns that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Triggers when sent from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Kittytail sends a monster from your Deck to the GY, so any monster that activates when sent from the Deck to the GY gets its effect for free.

hooks.label: Sends Beast from Deck to GY
hooks.why: The deck relies on putting Beasts in the Graveyard for Valerifawn, Uniflora, and Carpiponica, so effects that send a Beast from the Deck to the GY set up those plays.

profile.plan: A deck-out deck that repeatedly forces the opponent to send cards from the top of their Deck to the Graveyard — Iron Chain Dragon on battle damage, Iron Chain Snake via a battle-destroyed equipped monster, Poison Chain in an End Phase you did not attack — while Iron Chain Coil and Repairman keep its own board of battle-ready monsters alive.

hooks.label: Extra opponent deck milling
hooks.why: Iron Chain Dragon and Poison Chain both win by making the opponent send cards from the top of their Deck to the Graveyard, so any outside card that mills the opponent stacks toward the deck-out.

hooks.label: EARTH monster support
hooks.why: Every Iron Chain monster — Dragon, Snake, Coil, Blaster and Repairman — is EARTH, so cards that search, revive or boost EARTH monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Shrinks the opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Iron Chain Snake already strips 800 ATK/DEF from an opponent's monster, and Iron Chain Dragon and Iron Chain Repairman only trigger when they deal battle damage or destroy by battle, so more ATK reduction sets up those hits.

hooks.label: Fills your GY with EARTH
hooks.why: Iron Chain Repairman Special Summons a Level 4 or lower Iron Chain monster from the Graveyard and Iron Chain Dragon banishes Iron Chain monsters from the Graveyard for ATK, so sending your own EARTH monsters from the Deck to the GY feeds both.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck that excavates the top of its Deck to fuse 'GMX' monsters with Dinosaurs, gaining LP and burning the opponent every time they Summon, while the Fusion bosses revive and recycle Dinosaur material from the GY and banished pile.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every GMX Fusion Monster asks for a Dinosaur material (COMPREX wants two or more), Selande searches a Level 3 or lower Dinosaur, and ALLOS revives a Dinosaur from the GY or banishment, so anything that searches, summons or boosts Dinosaurs powers the whole engine.

hooks.label: Low-Level Dinosaurs with summon effects
hooks.why: Selande Special Summons a Level 3 or lower Dinosaur from the Deck and Selandea Special Summons a Level 4 or lower Dinosaur from the hand, GY or banishment, so small Dinosaurs that do something when they hit the field get used for free.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent monsters
hooks.why: Noma Fusion Summons whenever a monster is Normal or Special Summoned to the opponent's field, while COMPREX burns them 800 LP and VELOX gains 200 LP per opponent Summon, so cards that hand the opponent a monster advance the deck's whole game plan.

hooks.label: Monster-effect revival
hooks.why: Selande, Kimridge, Selandea and Noma all trigger when they are Special Summoned by a monster effect, so an outside monster that revives a monster from the GY turns into another way to fire those effects.

hooks.label: Generic Fusion Summoning
hooks.why: The GMX Fusion Monsters only need a 'GMX' monster plus Dinosaur material, and Noma and 55th Experiment Report shuffle that material back from the field, GY and banishment, so any outside Fusion Summon effect is an extra copy of the deck's finisher.

profile.plan: A Pendulum-Fusion deck of DARK Plant monsters that fuses with Polymerization, shrinks the opponent's monsters to Level 1 with Predator Counters, and turns its own Fusion Material into searches and counters.

hooks.label: Predator Counter cards
hooks.why: Triantis, Longinephila and Daredevil all place or count Predator Counters, and Daredevil destroys Spells/Traps equal to the monsters that have one.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Every Predap monster is a Plant, and Predaprimitive locks you into Plant or Dragon Special Summons for the turn.

hooks.label: Effects when used as material
hooks.why: Bufolicula and Triantis trigger when they are sent to the GY or added to the Extra Deck face-up because they were used as Fusion Material, so outside monsters with the same trigger get that value for free.

hooks.label: Polymerization support
hooks.why: Predaprimitive adds a Polymerization or Fusion Spell from the Deck, Longinephila Sets Polymerization from the GY or banishment, and Bal Teah banishes a Polymerization from the GY to Fusion Summon.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent a monster
hooks.why: Predaprimitive and Bal Teah both trigger when a monster is Special Summoned to the opponent's field, so cards that hand the opponent a monster let you Fusion Summon from the GY on their turn.

profile.plan: A WATER Machine Pendulum deck that swarms the field with Pendulum Summons, uses Tribute effects for extra attacks and disruption, and recycles its monsters through the Extra Deck when they are destroyed.

hooks.label: Machine self-destruct support
hooks.why: All monsters in this deck are Machine Pendulum monsters, so when a card effect destroys them, they go to the Extra Deck face-up and trigger the deck's effects that reward destruction and recycling.

hooks.label: Extra Deck Pendulum support
hooks.why: The deck's Pendulum monsters go to the Extra Deck face-up when destroyed or Tributed, so cards that Special Summon, add to hand, or place from the Extra Deck can reuse them.

hooks.label: Places Pendulum monsters in the Pendulum Zone
hooks.why: The deck relies on having the right Pendulum Scales, and it already has a trap that places them from the Deck; outside cards that do the same from Deck or Extra Deck help set up.

hooks.label: Grants extra attacks or piercing
hooks.why: The deck's monsters have effects that reward extra attacks and piercing damage, and its Field Spell protects the battle phase, so outside cards that grant those abilities stack with them.

hooks.label: WATER Level reduction
hooks.why: The deck's Level 5 monsters can be Normal Summoned without Tribute if a card reduces their Level by 1, and such a card also boosts their ATK/DEF.

profile.plan: Level 4 EARTH Rock monsters that keep reviving each other from the Graveyard in Defense Position, building toward Rank 4 Xyz Summons like Number 55: Gogogo Goliath.

hooks.label: Rock-Type support
hooks.why: Six of the nine Gogogo cards are Rock-Type, and Number 55: Gogogo Goliath adds a Level 4 EARTH Rock-Type monster from the GY, so Rock/EARTH support touches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Dumps monsters from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Gogogo Giant, Gogogo Ghost and Number 55: Gogogo Goliath all recover Gogogo or Level 4 EARTH Rock monsters from the Graveyard, so any outside card that sends them there from the Deck sets up the engine.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Gogogo Giant's effect only triggers when it is Normal Summoned, and Gogogo Golem - Golden Form must be Special Summoned by Tributing a Gogogo monster, so an extra Normal Summon gives both the payoff and the Tribute.

hooks.label: Revives EARTH Rocks from the GY
hooks.why: Special Summoning a Gogogo monster from the Graveyard triggers Gogogo Gigas to revive itself, so outside cards that Special Summon a Level 4 EARTH Rock from the GY start that loop.

hooks.label: Self-reviving EARTH Rock monsters
hooks.why: Gogogo Gigas Special Summons itself from the Graveyard whenever a Gogogo monster is Summoned, so more Level 4 EARTH Rock monsters that revive themselves slot straight into the same Rank 4 loop.

profile.plan: Summons the low-Level Reptile Evoltiles, Tributes them to bring the FIRE Dinosaur Evolsaurs out of the Deck, and stacks the Level 4s into Evolzar Xyz Monsters.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Evo-Instant Tributes a Reptile-Type monster and every Evoltile is a Reptile, so Reptile searchers, revivers and Xyz like King of the Feral Imps keep the engine supplied with Tribute fodder.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every Evolsaur is a Dinosaur that the Evoltiles Special Summon from the Deck, so Dinosaur support such as Fossil Dig or Souleating Oviraptor accelerates the exact same play.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Evo-Force and Evo-Instant Tribute your own monsters as their cost, so any monster with an effect that triggers when it is Tributed gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: Tributes your Reptiles
hooks.why: Evoltile Najasho Special Summons an Evolsaur from the Deck when it is Tributed and Evo-Instant needs a Reptile Tribute, so outside cards that Tribute your Reptile monsters start the whole chain.

hooks.label: Flip monster support
hooks.why: Evoltile Westlo and Evoltile Lagosucho are Flip monsters that Special Summon from the Deck when flipped, so cards that flip your Reptiles face-up or Set them turn into free Summons.

profile.plan: B.E.S. is a deck of high-Level Machines that arrive with counters, cannot be destroyed by battle, and self-destruct when those counters run out — B.E.F. Zelos and Boss Rush keep reloading them from the hand and Deck while Tetran, Derringer Core and Super B.E.S. Metal Slave spend counters as removal and search.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every B.E.S. monster is a Machine, and B.E.F. Zelos already boosts, protects and Special Summons them, so cards that search, revive or boost Machines work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell search
hooks.why: B.E.F. Zelos is the deck's engine — it tutors Boss Rush, gives 500 ATK/DEF and targeting/destruction protection, and Special Summons a B.E.S. from the hand — so any card that adds a Field Spell from the Deck starts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra counter placers
hooks.why: Big Core, Big Core MK-2, Big Core MK-3, Crystal Core, Tetran, Covered Core, Blaster Cannon Core and Metal Slave all self-destruct once they battle off their last counter, and Tetran, Derringer Core and Metal Slave spend counters for their effects, so outside cards that put more counters on your Machines extend every one of them.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder Tokens
hooks.why: Big Core, Crystal Core, Tetran, Covered Core and Big Core MK-2 only get their counters by being Normal Summoned, which means Tributing monsters, so cards that Special Summon Tokens feed those Summons.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: The Level 5 to 8 B.E.S. monsters are Tribute Summoned to get their counters, and Boss Rush shuts off Normal Summoning entirely, so cards that grant an extra Normal Summon or let you Tribute Summon without Tributing push the deck's main line through faster.

profile.plan: Special Summons an Elemental Lord from the hand by having exactly 5 monsters of its Attribute in the GY, then uses its powerful on-Summon effect while accepting a skipped Battle Phase if it leaves the field.

hooks.label: Attribute-specific mill
hooks.why: Each Elemental Lord needs exactly 5 monsters of its own Attribute in the GY, so any card that sends a monster of that Attribute from the Deck to the GY directly builds toward the Summon condition.

hooks.label: Discards Level 8 monsters
hooks.why: Trade-In and similar cards discard a Level 8 monster to draw, which both puts an Elemental Lord (or another Level 8 of the needed Attribute) into the GY and digs for the Lord itself.

hooks.label: Tributes Level 8 monsters
hooks.why: Advance Draw and similar cards can Tribute a Level 8 Elemental Lord for extra draws after it has attacked, accepting the skipped Battle Phase as a fair trade for the advantage.

hooks.label: Banishes from your GY
hooks.why: The Summon condition demands exactly 5 monsters of one Attribute, so cards that banish a monster from your own GY let you trim an overshot count back to exactly 5.

profile.plan: A Fiend/DARK Rank 4 ladder that swarms Level 4 bodies, Xyz Summons Number 104: Masquerade, then Rank-Ups into Number C104 to negate monster effects and halve the opponent's Life Points.

hooks.label: Fiend / DARK support
hooks.why: Umbral Horror Ghost, Ghoul, Unform, Will o' the Wisp and Thousand are all Fiend/DARK, Ghost even Special Summons a Level 4 or lower Fiend from the hand, so Fiend and DARK support cards work on the whole Main Deck.

hooks.label: Level 4 DARK extenders
hooks.why: The deck needs Level 4 bodies on the field to Xyz Summon Number 104: Masquerade and then Rank it up, so outside Level 4 DARK monsters that Special Summon themselves are free material.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic cards
hooks.why: V Umbral Horror banishes itself from the GY to Special Summon a 'Number' Xyz Monster 1 Rank higher than a 'Masquerade' Xyz you control, using it as material, which is exactly what Rank-Up-Magic Spells do.

hooks.label: Xyz Material support
hooks.why: Shining Umbral Horror can be treated as 2 materials for a 'Number' Xyz Monster that requires 3 or more materials, and V Umbral Horror transfers materials through its Rank-Up, so effects that attach or reuse Xyz Material advance the plan.

hooks.label: Xyz Summon triggers
hooks.why: Thousand Umbral Horror Special Summons itself from the GY and Shining Umbral Horror Special Summons itself from the hand whenever an Xyz Monster is Summoned, so the deck constantly fires off 'when an Xyz Monster is Special Summoned' effects.

profile.plan: Turns the opponent's whole board face-down and then sends their face-up or face-down cards to the GY, climbing into Level 10 Aqua LIGHT monsters, a Rank 10 Xyz and Tribute Summons that eat the opponent's face-down monsters.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: Every Tistina monster is Aqua, from the Level 10 bosses down to the small GY enablers, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Aqua monsters work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Flips opposing monsters face-down
hooks.why: Crystal God Tistina, Demigod of the Tistina and Embrace of the Tistina all convert the opponent's monsters to face-down Defense Position, after which Tainted of the Tistina can Tribute Summon itself with one and Hound of the Tistina lets your monsters attack directly.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Divine Domain Baatistina is the deck's engine card and Miasma Dragon Tistina Special Summons itself from the GY while a card is in the Field Zone, so any way to fetch or place a Field Spell keeps the deck running.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon enablers
hooks.why: Tainted of the Tistina can be Tribute Summoned face-up by Tributing a face-down monster the opponent controls, and Breath of the Tistina grants an extra Normal Summon, so cards that fuel or reward Tribute Summoning fit.

hooks.label: Sends your Aqua monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Sentinel, Hound and Returned of the Tistina Special Summon themselves or attach from the GY, and Tainted and Miasma Dragon Tistina trigger when they are sent to the GY, so outside cards that send your own monsters from the Deck or hand there set up those effects.

profile.plan: A WATER Sea Serpent deck that Special Summons its own monsters to mill the Deck and recycle Level 4 or lower WATER monsters from the Graveyard, then Synchro Summons into a Synchro Tuner while locking itself into WATER.

hooks.label: Special Summons the Sea Serpents
hooks.why: Deep Sea Minstrel, Deep Sea Artisan and Deep Sea Sentry each trigger when Special Summoned, milling your Deck and recovering a Level 4 or lower WATER monster, so any outside card that Special Summons one of them starts the chain.

hooks.label: Discard fodder WATER monsters
hooks.why: Deep Sea Minstrel discards itself plus a WATER monster and Deep Sea Repetiteur discards a Level 4 or lower WATER monster, so outside WATER monsters that do something when discarded are free value.

hooks.label: WATER monsters that discard for cost
hooks.why: Deep Sea Sentry triggers when it is sent to the GY to activate a WATER monster's effect, so an outside WATER monster whose effect discards or sends a card to the GY as cost switches it on.

hooks.label: WATER monsters that like being milled
hooks.why: Deep Sea Artisan, Deep Sea Sentry and Deep Sea Minstrel each send one to three cards off the top of your Deck to the GY when Special Summoned, so outside WATER monsters with an effect when sent to the GY are always live.

hooks.label: WATER support
