hooks.why: Every Deep Sea monster is a WATER Sea Serpent, and Deep Sea Repetiteur stops you Special Summoning anything but WATER monsters for the rest of the turn, so outside support that names WATER monsters boosts the whole deck.

profile.plan: A column-control deck: it puts S-Force monsters opposite the opponent's monsters so each of their monsters loses ATK, loses its effect or is banished when it leaves the field, while banishing its own cards from hand to pay for Quick Effects.

hooks.label: Column movers
hooks.why: Gravitino, Lapcewell, Orrafist and the Link monsters only reach an opponent's monster that stands in the same column as one of your S-Force monsters, so any card that moves a monster to another Main Monster Zone lets you line the whole field up.

hooks.label: Monsters for the opponent
hooks.why: Every S-Force payoff needs the opponent to actually control a monster opposite yours, so cards that Special Summon a monster or Token to the opponent's field (Kaiju, Lava Golem, Ojama Trio) give Rappa Chiyomaru, Gravitino and S-Force Chase something to lock and banish.

hooks.label: Banished-pile payoffs
hooks.why: S-Force World Sorting and the Graveyard effect of S-Force Origin both trigger whenever another card is banished, and the deck banishes S-Force cards from the hand several times a turn, so cards that reward banishing keep getting triggered for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Most of the engine that actually does something, including Gravitino, Orrafist, Lapcewell, Signify and the Link monsters Justify and Mystify, is LIGHT, so LIGHT searchers, revivers and boosters hit the cards the deck wins with.

profile.plan: Xyz Summon Rank 7 Dragon Rulers by using Level 7 Dragon monsters as material, while Level 2 Dragon Rulers discard themselves to search and set up the GY, then banish themselves from the GY to revive the Xyz monsters.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: All Dragon Ruler monsters are Dragon Type, so cards that search, revive or protect Dragons work for the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Dragon from Deck to GY
hooks.why: The Level 2 Dragon Rulers need Dragon monsters in the GY to banish for their revival effects, and Eclipse targets Level 4 or lower Dragon Rulers in the GY.

hooks.label: Searches low-Level Dragon
hooks.why: Spectral and Nebulus are Level 2, so cards that add Level 4 or lower Dragon monsters from the Deck to the hand can fetch the starters.

hooks.label: Dragon discard/banish triggers
hooks.why: Spectral and Nebulus discard a Dragon monster as cost and banish a Dragon monster from the GY as cost, so Dragon monsters with effects when discarded or banished get value.

hooks.label: LIGHT/DARK discard/banish triggers
hooks.why: Spectral can discard a LIGHT monster and Nebulus can discard a DARK monster, and their GY effects banish a LIGHT or DARK monster, so LIGHT or DARK monsters with discard or banish effects are useful fodder.

profile.plan: A Warrior deck built on Continuous Traps that Special Summon themselves as Warrior Effect Monsters, so the same cards sit in the Spell & Trap Zone and the Monster Zone to boost Warriors, protect them, burn the opponent and negate their cards.

hooks.label: Continuous Trap search and setup
hooks.why: Lightning Tydeu, Slayer Eteo and Swift Capane only do anything once they are face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone, and Glorious Adra and Fierce Parthe place them from the Deck and hand, so any outside card that finds, Sets or puts Continuous Traps on the field starts the whole engine.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Argostars monster and every Trap Monster they become is a Warrior, and Lightning Tydeu's 500 ATK/DEF and Slayer Eteo's and Swift Capane's destruction protection only apply to Warrior monsters you control.

hooks.label: Traps that become monsters
hooks.why: Home Stadium inflicts 500 damage each time a Continuous Trap is Special Summoned from the Spell & Trap Zone and negates a face-up opponent's card when one activates in your Monster Zone, so outside Continuous Traps that Special Summon themselves as Effect Monsters feed the same payoffs.

hooks.label: Traps milled from the Deck
hooks.why: Adventurous Arion detaches 2 materials to place up to 3 Argostars Continuous Traps from your GY face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone, so outside cards that send Continuous Traps from the Deck to the Graveyard stock that pool before Arion uses it.

hooks.label: Warriors with a Normal Summon payoff
hooks.why: Giantslaying adds an Argostars monster and then Normal Summons 1 Warrior monster, and Glorious Adra's Normal Summon stops the opponent from responding to your Continuous Traps, so outside Warriors that do something when Normal Summoned fit the extra Summon.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck whose Winged Beast Ritual monsters bounce the opponent's board, return themselves to the hand in the End Phase and leave Shinobird Tokens behind, while its Spirit monsters bounce back every turn to trigger Continuous Spell/Trap payoffs.

hooks.label: Spell/Traps naming Spirit monster
hooks.why: Shinobaroness Shade Peacock adds 1 Spell/Trap from the Deck that mentions 'Spirit monster', so any outside Spell/Trap with that text becomes tutorable by her.

hooks.label: Triggers on a WIND monster bouncing
hooks.why: Every Shinobird Spirit and Ritual monster returns itself to the hand in the End Phase, so outside cards that trigger when a WIND monster you control returns to your hand get a free activation every turn.

hooks.label: Bounces your own Spirit monster
hooks.why: Shinobird Power Spot and Shinobird Salvation both trigger when a face-up Spirit monster you control returns to your hand, so outside cards that return your own Spirits to hand fire them on demand.

hooks.label: WIND Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype, Ritual and Spirit alike, is a WIND Winged Beast, so effects that boost, search or revive that Type or Attribute apply to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: The Ritual monsters return to the hand in the End Phase and must be Ritual Summoned again with 'Shinobird's Calling', so the deck constantly needs outside cards that add a Ritual Spell from the Deck.

profile.plan: A Warrior deck that sends its own monsters from the hand to the GY to activate effects and change their Attributes in the GY, building up different Attributes to boost its Field Spell and summon Elemental Lords.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Elementsaber monster is a Warrior, so cards that search, revive or boost Warriors support the entire deck.

hooks.label: Elemental Lord bosses
hooks.why: The deck can search, revive, send and recover 'Elemental Lord' monsters, and its GY Attribute-changing lets it gather the 5 same-Attribute monsters those bosses need.
phrases: exactly 5 monsters of the same Attribute

hooks.label: Tribute-trigger monsters
hooks.why: Elemental Training Tributes 1 monster to Special Summon an Elementsaber from the Deck, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed give you that effect for free.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Palace of the Elemental Lords is the deck's engine, so cards that add a Field Spell from the Deck to the hand get it out faster.

hooks.label: Chaos monsters
hooks.why: The GY effects let each Elementsaber become any Attribute, so you can set up the LIGHT and DARK banish requirements for Chaos monsters.
phrases: banish 1 LIGHT and 1 DARK monster from your GY

profile.plan: A Level 4 LIGHT Fairy engine that Tributes or bounces its own monsters to Special Summon and reuse Level 7 LIGHT Dragon bosses from the hand.

hooks.label: Tribute-summonable Level 7 Dragon
hooks.why: Starry Knight Sky grants an extra Normal Summon usable for a Level 7 LIGHT Dragon, so a Dragon that can be Tribute Summoned with a single Tribute turns that extra Summon into a body.

hooks.label: Cards that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Starry Knight Astel and Starry Knight Orbitael Tribute a LIGHT monster you control as a Quick Effect cost, so outside LIGHT monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get that effect for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Starry Knight monster is a LIGHT Fairy, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT Fairies keep the engine supplied with Tribute and bounce fodder.

hooks.label: LIGHT Dragon support
hooks.why: The whole payoff of the deck is Special Summoning and recycling a Level 7 LIGHT Dragon from the hand, so support that finds or revives LIGHT Dragons fuels the same plays.

profile.plan: A Plant Link ladder: 0-ATK Sunavalon Link Monsters cannot be targeted for attacks, refund any damage you take and Special Summon Sunvine Link Monsters from the Extra Deck, climbing into a Link-4 boss backed by a Continuous Trap lockdown.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: All seven Sunavalon monsters are Plant, and Dryas, Melias, Dryades, Dryanome and Daphne all ask for Plant monsters as Link Material, so Plant searchers and revivers feed the whole deck.

hooks.label: Special Summons Plant monsters
hooks.why: Dryas needs a Level 4 or lower Plant monster and Melias, Dryades, Dryanome and Daphne need Plant monsters, so outside effects that Special Summon Plant monsters from the hand, Deck or GY are extra material.

hooks.label: Floats when Tributed
hooks.why: Sunavalon Daphne Tributes 1 monster to return Plant Link Monsters from the GY to the Extra Deck and Dryatrentiay Tributes a Link Monster it points to, so monsters that trigger when Tributed turn that cost into free value.

hooks.label: Rewards gaining LP
hooks.why: Dryas, Dryades and Dryanome all gain back the battle or effect damage you take and Special Summon a Sunvine monster from the Extra Deck, so outside cards that trigger when you gain LP sit on the same loop.

hooks.label: Damages you on purpose
hooks.why: Dryas, Dryades and Dryanome only gain LP and summon a Sunvine 'if you take battle or effect damage', so cards that deal effect damage to your own LP trigger the Summon on your own turn.

profile.plan: Pay half your Life Points to destroy and banish the entire field and both Graveyards, turning the banished pile into massive ATK for Gandora's Dragon monsters.

hooks.label: Shining Sarcophagus cards
hooks.why: Gandora-G the Dragon of Destruction can Special Summon a Level 7 or lower monster that mentions "Shining Sarcophagus" from the Deck, and Special Summons itself from the hand while you control it.

hooks.label: Banished/destroyed triggers
hooks.why: Gandora and Gigarays Gandora destroy and then banish all other cards on the field, so your own outside cards get banished and can trigger.

hooks.label: Banishes from the GY
hooks.why: Gandora monsters gain 300 ATK for each banished card, and Gigarays Gandora can banish all cards in the GYs, so more banishing from the GY increases the ATK boost.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Gandora the Dragon of Destruction cannot be Special Summoned and must be Normal or Flip Summoned, so extra Normal Summons help you get it out alongside your other plays.

hooks.label: Banished ATK gainers
hooks.why: Gandora monsters gain 300 ATK for each banished card, and cards that also scale with the banished pile become huge after Gandora banishes the whole field and GYs.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Gigarays Gandora must send 2 other monsters from your hand and/or field to the GY to Special Summon itself, and Gandora the Dragon of Destruction needs 2 Tributes, so monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand provide free material.

profile.plan: A DARK Fiend deck that Tribute Summons high-Level Steelswarm monsters, using extra Normal Summons and Tribute fodder to trigger destruction, bouncing and Special Summon negation.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: The deck already gets extra Normal Summons from its Level 4 Warrior and Level 4 Fiend, so outside cards that grant another Normal Summon let it Tribute Summon more high-Level monsters in one turn.

hooks.label: Tributing opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Its Tribute Summon effects need Tributes, so cards that let you Tribute an opponent's monster for a Tribute Summon turn the opponent's board into fuel.

hooks.label: Tributed monsters that float
hooks.why: The deck Tributes monsters every turn for its high-Level Summons, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed give value without spending a card.

hooks.label: Multiple-Tribute monsters
hooks.why: One of its Level 2 monsters counts as 2 Tributes, so outside monsters that also count as multiple Tributes help summon the Level 9 and 10 bosses with fewer cards.

hooks.label: Fiend and DARK support
hooks.why: All its main-deck monsters are DARK Fiends, so outside cards that search, revive or boost Fiends or DARK monsters support the entire deck.

hooks.label: Tribute Summoned bosses
hooks.why: The deck is built to Tribute Summon high-Level monsters, so outside monsters with effects when Tribute Summoned can be summoned with the same fodder and add removal or pressure.

profile.plan: A Plant Link climb: Sunvine Link-1s are built from Plant Normal Monsters to back up the Sunavalon board with LP gain, ATK boosts and Graveyard revival, all locked into Plant Extra Deck monsters.

hooks.label: Sends Plants to the GY
hooks.why: Sunvine Shrine revives a Level 4 or lower Plant Normal Monster from the GY and Sunvine Cross Breed revives any other Plant there, so cards that put Plants in the Graveyard hand them targets.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Every Sunvine card is a Plant and both Sowing and Shrine lock your Extra Deck into Plant monsters, so generic Plant support covers the whole strategy.

hooks.label: Link Monsters worth Tributing
hooks.why: Sunvine Cross Breed Tributes 1 Link Monster as its cost, so outside Link Monsters with an effect when Tributed, or that plus a Plant revival, pay for themselves.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster/WATER deck of high-DEF Normal Monsters that uses Glacier Aqua Madoor to discard cards for battle protection and monster destruction, while Lightray Madoor rewards banishing LIGHT monsters.

hooks.label: Normal Monster searchers
hooks.why: Glacier Aqua Madoor needs a Normal Monster in hand to destroy an opponent's monster, so searching Normal Monsters fuels its effect.

hooks.label: Normal Monster revival
hooks.why: The deck's main monsters are Normal Monsters, and Glacier Aqua Madoor can protect them in battle, so reviving them keeps the board and the hand full.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: All four Madoor monsters are Spellcasters, so cards that support Spellcasters apply to every card in the deck.

hooks.label: Discard payoffs
hooks.why: Glacier Aqua Madoor discards a card as cost to protect a Normal Monster or destroy an opponent's monster, so cards that trigger when discarded turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Banishes LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Lightray Madoor Special Summons itself from the hand if 3 or more LIGHT monsters are banished, so cards that banish LIGHT monsters enable it.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster toolbox: each Awakening of the Possessed monster Special Summons itself from the hand or Deck by sending a face-up Spellcaster plus a small monster of its own Attribute to the GY, then replaces itself with a 'Possessed' or 'Spiritual Art' card when it leaves the field.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Awakening of the Possessed is Summoned by sending a face-up Spellcaster you control to the GY, and Spiritual Power Recovery Potion revives Spellcasters, so cards that search, revive or boost Spellcasters fuel the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends your monster to the GY
hooks.why: Each Awakening adds a 'Possessed' Spell/Trap or a 'Spiritual Art' card from the Deck when it is sent from the field to the GY, so outside effects that send your own monster there turn into searches.

hooks.label: Revives Spellcasters from the GY
hooks.why: The Awakenings and Spiritual Power Recovery Potion dump Spellcaster monsters into the GY as material, so effects that Special Summon a Spellcaster from the GY get a whole toolbox back.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: An Awakening only Special Summons itself once a face-up Spellcaster and a small monster of its own Attribute are already on your field, so extra Normal Summons get both halves of the cost down in one turn.

profile.plan: A Ritual/Flip deck: it Ritual Summons Tarotrei or Tarotreith, keeps a board of face-down monsters, and flips them up and down to fire FLIP effects, search the Ritual pieces and grind the opponent down.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Tarotrei and Tarotreith can turn a face-up monster face-down again, so outside cards that set a spent Flip monster face-down let you reuse its FLIP effect and keep a face-down board for Black Cat-astrophe.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Prediction Ritual and Underworld Ritual of Prediction Ritual Summon by Tributing monsters whose total Levels are 9 or more, so outside monsters that do something when they are Tributed (like Bibliomuse coming back face-down) pay for themselves twice.

hooks.label: Ritual searchers
hooks.why: Crystaldine fetches a Ritual Monster, Arrowsylph a Ritual Spell and Bibliomuse both, so outside cards that add Ritual Monsters or Ritual Spells from the Deck or Graveyard get you to Tarotrei or Tarotreith faster.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Prediction Princess monster, including both Ritual monsters, is a Fairy, so outside cards that search, revive or protect Fairies work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Forces Defense Position
hooks.why: Petalelf turns the opponent's Attack Position monsters to Defense Position and locks them there, and Astromorrigan then destroys Defense Position monsters for burn damage, so more cards that put the opponent's monsters in Defense Position feed the same payoff.

profile.plan: A WATER Fish toolbox of Level 1-4 Tuners that keep reviving themselves from the Graveyard, chaining into WATER Synchro Monsters and turning every discard and mill into another body.

hooks.label: Mills WATER monsters
hooks.why: Launcher, Blaster, Archer and Doctor all Special Summon themselves from the Graveyard, so any outside card that puts WATER monsters from the Deck into the GY arms every one of them at once.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Fishborg Blaster discards 1 card and Fishborg Archer discards 1 WATER monster as the cost of reviving themselves, so outside cards with an effect when discarded get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be milled
hooks.why: Fishborg Planter sends the top card of your Deck to the GY to revive itself, so outside monsters that do something when sent from the Deck to the GY come back for free on the same mill.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Every Fishborg is a WATER monster and every Synchro restriction in the deck demands WATER, so generic WATER support reaches the whole archetype.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that stacks face-up Zefra monsters in the Extra Deck to fuel Chosen of Zefra and Divine Strike, then summons Zefraath by Tributing three Zefra and uses Oracle of Zefra to trigger on Ritual, Fusion, Synchro and Xyz Summons.

hooks.label: Tributes opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Zefraath's once-per-turn effect can Tribute any 1 monster to Special Summon a Zefra from the Deck, so cards that let you Tribute an opponent's monster turn that into removal plus a Summon.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Zefraath can Tribute 1 monster to Special Summon a Zefra from the Deck, and its own Special Summon Tributes all monsters you control, so free Tokens are extra fodder that do not cost you cards.

hooks.label: Tributed triggers
hooks.why: Zefraath Tributes monsters for both its Special Summon and its once-per-turn Deck Summon, so outside monsters with a 'when this card is Tributed' effect get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Oracle of Zefra is the deck's main starter, adding a Zefra monster when activated and triggering on Extra Deck Summons, so cards that add or Set a Field Spell from the Deck get it consistently.

hooks.label: Face-up Extra Deck Fusion
hooks.why: Oracle of Zefra triggers when you Special Summon using a Zefra monster as Material, and Zefraath stacks Zefra Pendulum monsters face-up in the Extra Deck, so Fusion Spells that use face-up Pendulum monsters in the Extra Deck turn those into Oracle triggers.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Pendulum
hooks.why: Chosen of Zefra and Zefra Divine Strike count and banish face-up Zefra monsters in the Extra Deck, so cards that destroy your own Pendulum cards in the Pendulum Zones turn them into face-up Extra Deck fuel.

profile.plan: A Warrior/DARK Level 4 deck that floods the board with Butterspy bodies for Rank 4 Xyz, shrinks opposing monsters by moving their battle positions, and trades its own field monsters for Deck searches.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Blue Mountain Butterspy, Swallowtail Butterspy and Morpho Butterspy are all Warriors, so anything that searches, revives or protects Warriors builds the whole board.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Blue Mountain Butterspy Special Summons itself from the hand whenever you Normal Summon a Warrior monster, so each extra Normal Summon is another free body and another trigger.

hooks.label: Battle position changers
hooks.why: Morpho Butterspy makes an opponent's monster lose 1000 ATK and DEF every time its battle position changes, so outside cards that flip or reposition opposing monsters become repeatable removal.

hooks.label: Sends your field monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Moonlit Papillon Special Summons a Level 4 or lower Butterspy from the Deck when it is sent from the field to the Graveyard, so cards that Tribute or send your own monsters turn into searches.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 4 Warriors
hooks.why: Blue Mountain Butterspy is a Level 4 Warrior that Special Summons itself for free, and the deck needs more such bodies to reach Rank 4 for Photon Alexandra Queen.

profile.plan: Special Summons Gate Guardian by Tributing Sanga of the Thunder, Kazejin and Suijin, and banishes those three from the hand, field or GY to fuse them into Gate Guardian Fusions that negate the opponent's effects.

hooks.label: Thunder, Aqua and Spellcaster support
hooks.why: The only Fusion Materials the deck ever uses are Sanga of the Thunder, Suijin and Kazejin — a Thunder, an Aqua and a Spellcaster — so anything that searches, revives or supports those Types finds or reuses a piece.

hooks.label: Dumps materials to the GY
hooks.why: Gate Guardians Combined is Special Summoned by banishing Sanga of the Thunder, Kazejin and Suijin from the hand, field and/or GY, so any card that sends those monsters from the Deck to the GY arms the Fusion before you even draw them.

hooks.label: Searches or revives a material
hooks.why: Every Fusion needs its named materials in the hand, on the field or in the GY, so cards that add or Special Summon a Thunder, Aqua or Spellcaster from the Deck or GY put another Sanga, Suijin or Kazejin within reach.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon enablers
hooks.why: Sanga, Kazejin and Suijin are Level 7 monsters that need two Tributes each, and Gate Guardian itself is Special Summoned by Tributing all three, so extra Normal Summons and Tribute-cost reducers get the pieces onto the field.

hooks.label: Recovers banished materials
hooks.why: Every Gate Guardian Fusion Summon banishes Sanga, Kazejin and Suijin, and Combined can banish them from the hand, so cards that bring banished monsters back to the hand or Deck give the deck its material to fuse with again.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck that drops the Level 1 Relinquished the Wicked Eye of Illusion by Tributing two monsters, then steals your opponent's Effect Monsters as Equip Spells so it can attack with their stats and bounce the damage back.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: Relinquished the Wicked Eye of Illusion is a Ritual Monster, so cards that Ritual Summon it or fetch Ritual Monsters and Ritual Spells get it onto the field without needing its own two-Tribute procedure.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Relinquished the Wicked Eye of Illusion can Special Summon itself from the hand by Tributing 2 monsters, and Samsara D Lotus Tributes itself for both of its effects, so free Tokens are the cheapest fuel for the deck.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Both Samsara D Lotus and the Summoning procedure of Relinquished the Wicked Eye of Illusion pay with Tributes, so outside monsters with a 'when this card is Tributed' trigger turn that cost into a bonus.

hooks.label: Xyz material reload
hooks.why: Sacrifice Level-Up banishes 2 materials from an Xyz Monster to Special Summon a higher Rank one, so any card that attaches materials to an Xyz Monster gives it more fodder.

hooks.label: DARK Fiend and Illusion support
hooks.why: Samsara D Lotus is a DARK Fiend and Relinquished the Wicked Eye of Illusion is a DARK Illusion, so Attribute- and Type-wide search, revival and stat effects hit the entire deck.

profile.plan: A Level 1 Machine Link-1 spam deck that lines its Link Monsters up so they co-link, then uses those co-linked effects to attack directly, banish, destroy and burn, recycling the Links from the GY and banish pile again and again.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Appliancer monster, in the Main Deck and the Extra Deck, is a Machine, so cards that search, revive or boost Machines work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 1 extenders
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Appliancer is a Level 1 monster and each Link-1 asks for one 'Appliancer' as material, so effects that Special Summon Level 1 monsters put material on board.

hooks.label: Direct attack enablers
hooks.why: Vacculephant and Propelion can attack directly while un-co-linked and Dryer Drake grants another monster a second attack, so effects that force or add direct and extra attacks turn the tiny Link-1s into damage.

hooks.label: Link Monster revival
hooks.why: Reuse, Test, Kappa Scale and Conversion all bring Appliancer Link-1s back from the GY, so the deck banks Link Monsters there; outside effects that Special Summon Link Monsters from the GY add even more bodies.

hooks.label: Sent-from-hand GY effects
hooks.why: Vacculephant sends a card from your hand to the GY as a cost and the deck is constantly filling the GY, so monsters that trigger when they are sent there get used for free.

profile.plan: An EARTH Warrior beatdown deck that drops Level 5 and higher War Rock monsters without Tributes, attacks every Battle Phase, and turns each of your EARTH Warrior's battles into searches, revives, ATK boosts and removal.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior support
hooks.why: Every War Rock monster is an EARTH Warrior, and Gactos, Fortia, Orpis, Mammud, Skyler and Mountain all check for an EARTH Warrior monster, so anything that names Warrior or EARTH is live.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Gactos Special Summons itself whenever an EARTH Warrior is Normal Summoned, and Orpis and Mammud are Level 5 Warriors that can be Normal Summoned without Tributing, so an extra Normal Summon means another body and another Gactos.

hooks.label: Tribute-free big Warriors
hooks.why: Orpis, Mammud and Mountain only work while you control no monsters or only Warrior monsters, so a Level 5 or higher Warrior you can Normal Summon without Tributing is a free big body that never breaks that condition.

hooks.label: Battle Phase Summons
hooks.why: Mountain, Spirit, Generations, Skyler and Bashileos all Special Summon during a Battle Phase in which your EARTH Warrior battles, so outside cards that put a Warrior on the field in the Battle Phase keep the pressure on.

hooks.label: Warriors revived from the GY
hooks.why: Skyler revives a Level 5 or lower Warrior from the GY every Battle Phase and Spirit revives War Rock monsters, so outside Warriors that trigger when Special Summoned from the GY get their effect for free.

profile.plan: A FIRE Warrior Synchro deck that equips its own Warrior monsters as Equip Spells and uses Level 1 Tuners with Level 4 or lower FIRE Warriors to climb into Synchro monsters.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Ricciardetto locks you into Warrior monsters for the rest of the turn after its Summon, and every Infernoble Knight monster is a Warrior, so generic Warrior support advances the deck.

hooks.label: FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Infernoble Knight monster is FIRE, and the deck Synchro Summons FIRE Warrior monsters, so FIRE support fits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Warrior Equip Spells
hooks.why: Bradamante can equip a Warrior you control with an Equip Spell from the Deck, and Turpin and Captain Oliver reward controlling monsters equipped with Equip Cards.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: Bradamante equips an Equip Spell from the Deck, and Turpin and Captain Oliver need Equip Cards to function, so outside cards that add Equip Spells from the Deck or GY give more equips.

profile.plan: A Warrior/LIGHT Fusion deck that floods its own field with Dual Avatar monsters and Spirit Tokens, then Fusion Summons repeatedly and destroys its own monsters to search, recover and climb into big Empowered bosses.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Dual Avatar card, including the Spirit Tokens and the Fusion Monsters, is a Warrior, so cards that search, revive or boost Warriors work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: All Dual Avatar monsters, Tokens and Fusions are LIGHT, so LIGHT-only support reaches every card the deck puts on the field.

hooks.label: Extra Fusion Summons
hooks.why: Dual Avatar Invitation is the deck's main Fusion Summon and it costs a discard, so outside cards that Fusion Summon turn the Tokens and Dual Avatar monsters already on board into another Fusion Monster.

hooks.label: Fusion Material grabbers
hooks.why: Dual Avatar Invitation Fusion Summons using monsters from the hand or field as Fusion Material, and Empowered Kon-Gyo and Mitsu-Jaku name Yuhi and Kokoku as material, so cards that summon or treat a monster as Fusion Material get those names out.

profile.plan: A Trap-control deck: it Sets 'Attraction' Traps, equips them onto the opponent's monsters, and moves them around with 'Amazement' monsters that Special Summon themselves whenever a Trap is activated.

hooks.label: Trap searchers and recyclers
hooks.why: The entire engine is 'Attraction' Traps, and Comica, Delia, Bufo and Precious Park all Set them from the Deck or GY, so outside cards that fetch or recover a Trap Card keep the loop supplied.

hooks.label: Mills Traps into the GY
hooks.why: Arlekino banishes 'Attraction' Traps from the GY to destroy cards and Precious Park re-Sets them from there, so sending Trap Cards from the Deck to the GY turns straight into removal.

hooks.label: Trap usable the turn it is Set
hooks.why: Precious Park exists to let you activate an 'Attraction' Trap the turn it was Set, and Arlekino Special Summons itself whenever a Trap Card is activated, so any outside card that unlocks a freshly Set Trap speeds the deck up.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent a monster
hooks.why: Attraction Traps can only be equipped to an opponent's monster and Arlekino equips one from the Deck whenever the opponent Summons, so outside cards that put a monster on the opponent's field turn both effects on.

profile.plan: A Crystal Beast deck that places its monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, then Special Summons them or banishes them to fuel an Ultimate Crystal boss that can wipe the field.

hooks.label: Banishes your own monsters
hooks.why: Ultimate Crystal Rainbow Dragon Overdrive gains 7000 ATK while 7 Crystal Beast monsters are banished, so outside cards that banish monsters from your Deck or GY help reach that count.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monster
hooks.why: Crystal Miracle and Crystal Aegis destroy a Crystal Beast you control to negate or make a Token, and any effect that destroys a Crystal Beast places it in the Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell, triggering the GY effects of Miracle, Aegis, Boon and Brilliance.

hooks.label: Benefits from Continuous Spells
hooks.why: Golden Rule and the Crystal Beast mechanic fill your Spell & Trap Zone with Continuous Spells, so cards that reward you for controlling many Spell/Trap cards (like Mage Power) get huge value.

hooks.label: Draws with high LP
hooks.why: Crystal Boon gains LP equal to the combined ATK of two Crystal Beasts, so outside cards that reward you for having 9000 or more LP (like Ancient Leaf) become live.

hooks.label: Special Summons banished monsters
hooks.why: Overdrive can Special Summon any number of your banished Crystal Beast monsters, and outside cards that also Special Summon banished monsters can extend the same resource.

profile.plan: Level 4 LIGHT Fairies swarm the field and Xyz Summon Rank 4 monsters with three or more materials, granting those Xyz Monsters bonus effects and using Number 102's detach to shrink the opponent's board.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Star Seraph monster is a Level 4 LIGHT Fairy, so cards that search, revive or boost Fairies work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon
hooks.why: Star Seraph Scepter searches on Normal Summon and Star Seraph Scout Special Summons from hand on Normal Summon, so another Normal Summon triggers another effect.

hooks.label: Special Summons LIGHT Fairies
hooks.why: Scepter searches when it is Special Summoned and Scale Special Summons a Star Seraph from hand when it is, so an outside card that Special Summons a Level 4 LIGHT Fairy triggers them.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 4 LIGHT
hooks.why: Star Seraph Sentry needs 3 Level 4 LIGHT monsters, and Sovereignty already Special Summons itself from hand, so more monsters that come down on their own give the third material without spending the Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Xyz Material
hooks.why: The deck Xyz Summons using 3 or more monsters and Scepter/Scale reward 3+ material Xyz Monsters, so outside monsters that trigger when used as Xyz Material get used for free.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Material
hooks.why: Star Seraph Scepter and Scale grant bonus effects to an Xyz Monster Summoned with 3 or more materials, and Number 102: Star Seraph Sentry detaches material to negate, so extra materials are extra uses.

profile.plan: The deck uses Vassal monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand as Tribute fodder, then Tributes them for Tribute Summons to trigger their effects and summon powerful high-Level monsters.

hooks.label: High-Level Tribute Summon monsters
hooks.why: The archetype's monsters Special Summon themselves from the hand to serve as Tribute fodder, so the deck needs powerful high-Level monsters that reward being Tribute Summoned.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoffs
hooks.why: The deck's plan is to Tribute Summon repeatedly, so cards that trigger when a monster is Tribute Summoned provide extra advantage.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: The archetype's monsters have effects when Tributed for a Tribute Summon, so outside monsters with the same trigger get value from the deck's Tribute Summons.

hooks.label: Discard fodder
hooks.why: One monster lets you discard a card to Special Summon itself, so outside cards that trigger when discarded give extra value.

hooks.label: Banished from GY fodder
hooks.why: One monster lets you banish a Level 5 or higher monster from the GY to Special Summon itself, so outside cards that trigger when banished from the GY give extra value.

profile.plan: A dice-roll toolbox: Dice Jar burns whoever rolls lower, Dice It mills or banishes by the result, Dice Re-Roll fixes a bad roll and Dice Try! negates any opposing dice-roll card, so the deck wants every other card that touches a six-sided die.

hooks.label: Dice-rolling cards
hooks.why: Dice Re-Roll gives any die roll a second chance and Dice Try! covers dice-roll effects, so every outside card that rolls a six-sided die works with the deck's whole game plan.

hooks.label: Flip monster support
hooks.why: Dice Jar only burns when it is flipped face-up, so outside cards that flip a face-down monster face-up or turn a monster face-down let you reuse its FLIP effect again and again.

hooks.label: Speedroid monsters
hooks.why: Dice Roll Battle banishes a 'Speedroid' monster from the GY and a 'Speedroid' Tuner from the hand to Synchro Summon, so Speedroid names in hand and Graveyard are direct material for it.

hooks.label: Banished from the GY
hooks.why: Dice It banishes cards from your Graveyard equal to the die result, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished from the GY turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Deck-to-GY millers
hooks.why: Dice It can send up to 6 cards from the top of your Deck to the Graveyard, and Dice Roll Battle needs 'Speedroid' monsters sitting in the Graveyard, so outside milling effects stock both.

profile.plan: A deck of nothing but vanilla beaters: low-Level Normal Monsters of every Type and Attribute, plus a handful of Level 5-6 vanillas that need a Tribute, so the outside cards must be the effects the deck itself has none of.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: All 26 cards in the archetype are Normal Monsters, so any outside card whose text names Normal Monsters works on every monster in the deck.

hooks.label: Summons or recovers Normal Monsters
hooks.why: The deck is pure Normal Monsters with no way of its own to extend or rebuild, so outside cards that Special Summon or add a Normal Monster from the Deck, GY or hand are its whole engine.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: B. Dragon Jungle King, Royal Guard, Crow Goblin, Ill Witch, Winged Egg of New Life, Leo Wizard, Machine Attacker and Rock Spirit are Level 5-6 vanillas that need a Tribute, so extra Normal Summons and Tribute-cheating effects turn a slow hand into a board.

hooks.label: Tributes a Normal Monster
hooks.why: Every monster here is a Normal Monster, so outside cards that Tribute a Normal Monster as a cost, such as White Elephant's Gift or Order to Charge, always have fodder in this deck.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck that brings out Level 7+ LIGHT Dragon Synchro monsters (Ancient Fairy Dragon and Ancient Fairy Life Dragon), protects them, forces the whole board into Defense Position with World of Spirits, and then attacks out of Defense using DEF.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: World of Spirits is the deck's Field Spell, it improves Ancient Fairy Life Dragon's search while on the field, and Regulus the Fairy Beast recycles a Field Spell out of the GY for a draw, so cards that fetch or place Field Spells feed the whole engine.

hooks.label: Defense Position attackers
hooks.why: World of Spirits flips Special Summoned monsters to Defense Position and destroys Attack Position monsters in the End Phase, so monsters that can still attack from face-up Defense Position (applying DEF, as Ancient Fairy Life Dragon does) share the deck's whole gameplan.

hooks.label: Self-reviving Tuners
hooks.why: Spore the Fairy Seed Special Summons itself from the GY while you control Ancient Fairy Dragon or a LIGHT Beast, Plant or Fairy, so other Tuners with the same self-revival give the deck repeated, free Synchro material.

profile.plan: A WIND Machine Pendulum deck that fills both Pendulum Zones with scales of 0-1 and 7-10 to Pendulum Summon, Synchro Summons into Rockks with its four Tuners, and grinds value from the 'Symph Amplifire' Field Spell and its Symphonic Counters.

hooks.label: Discarded card payoffs
hooks.why: Guitaar's Pendulum effect discards 1 card to Special Summon a Symphonic Warrior from the Deck, so outside cards that do something when they are discarded turn that cost into free value.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Rockks, Guitariss and DJJ only get their bonus effects while 'Symph Amplifire' is in your Field Zone, so outside cards that add or place a Field Spell from the Deck set up the whole deck.

hooks.label: Machine WIND support
hooks.why: Every Symphonic Warrior is a WIND Machine, so cards that support Machine monsters or WIND monsters search, revive or boost the entire deck.

hooks.label: Synchro Material payoffs
hooks.why: The deck runs four Tuners (Basses, Piaano, Drumss and Guitariss) and Synchro Summons Rockks, so outside monsters with an effect when they are used as Synchro Material pay for themselves as material.

hooks.label: Flip Monster support
hooks.why: DJJ Special Summons a Symphonic Warrior from the Deck in face-down Defense Position and its Pendulum effect flips a face-down Symphonic Warrior face-up, and Synthess is a Flip monster whose FLIP effect searches, so outside cards that flip face-down monsters face-up speed both up.

profile.plan: An equip-control deck: Allure Queen LV3, LV5 and LV7 steal the opponent's monsters and equip them to themselves, then send themselves to the Graveyard to Level Up into the next form, backed by a Link-3 boss that revives the line.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent monsters
hooks.why: Allure Queen LV3, LV5 and LV7 can only equip a monster that is sitting on the opponent's field, so cards that Special Summon a monster to the opponent's side of the field hand them something to steal.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Allure Queen monster is a Spellcaster, and Golden Allure Queen's Link Summon demands 3 Spellcaster monsters, so search, revival and swarming for the Type all fit.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when discarded
hooks.why: Chaos Allure Queen Special Summons itself by discarding 1 other LIGHT or DARK monster, so a monster that gains value from being discarded pays that cost for free.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with LIGHT and DARK monsters
hooks.why: Chaos Allure Queen equips a monster from either Graveyard to itself and then Special Summons a DARK Allure Queen only if the equipped card was LIGHT or DARK, so sending those monsters to the Graveyard sets up its best play.

hooks.label: Free Spellcaster bodies
hooks.why: Golden Allure Queen is a Link-3 that needs 3 Spellcaster monsters on the field, so effects that Special Summon Spellcaster monsters from the Deck or Graveyard give it Link Material.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Machine deck of Union monsters that equip themselves as Equip Spells, then banishes X-Cross Cannon, Y-Yare Head and Z-Zillion Tank from the field or GY to bring out the Level 9 Fusion XYZ-Hyper Dragon Cannon.

hooks.label: Union monster support
hooks.why: Y-Yare Head and Z-Zillion Tank are Union monsters that equip themselves to a Machine and X-Cross Cannon equips a Union monster straight from the Deck, so cards that search or recruit Union monsters keep the engine going.

hooks.label: LIGHT Machine support
hooks.why: Every A-to-Z monster is a LIGHT Machine, and X-Cross Cannon, Y-Yare Head and Z-Zillion Tank all lock Extra Deck Summons to LIGHT, so support for that Type and Attribute boosts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills LIGHT Machines to the GY
hooks.why: XYZ-Hyper Dragon Cannon is Special Summoned by banishing X-Cross Cannon, Y-Yare Head and Z-Zillion Tank from your field and/or GY, so any effect that sends LIGHT Machine monsters to the GY sets up the Summon.

hooks.label: Banishes your own LIGHT Machines
hooks.why: Z-Zillion Tank equips a banished Level 4 LIGHT Machine monster to itself and A-to-Z Energy Load shuffles up to six banished LIGHT Machine monsters back into the Deck, so cards that banish your own LIGHT Machines from the hand, Deck or GY feed both.

profile.plan: A deck that hard-Normal Summons Level 10 DARK Fiends by Tributing three monsters each, then wins on the Wicked Gods' massive stats, the Avatar's Spell/Trap lockdown and the Eraser's board wipe.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: All three Wicked Gods say they cannot be Normal Summoned or Set except by Tributing 3 monsters and cannot be Special Summoned, so Tokens are pure Tribute fodder that costs you no cards.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: The Wicked Avatar, Dreadroot and Eraser all need a three-monster Tribute Summon, so extra Normal Summons and effects that let a high-Level monster be Tribute Summoned for less make them playable at all.

hooks.label: Tributing the opponent's board
hooks.why: Each Wicked God eats 3 Tributes, so effects that let you pay that cost with monsters your opponent controls save your own field for the next one.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monster
hooks.why: The Wicked Eraser wipes every card on the field when it is destroyed and sent to the GY, and can only self-destruct during your Main Phase, so outside effects that destroy it on the opponent's turn turn it into a one-sided board wipe.

hooks.label: Divine-Beast monsters
hooks.why: Divine Evolution can pump any monster whose original Type is Divine-Beast as well as the Wicked Gods, giving you a second target that the same stat boost and unnegatable attack trigger apply to.

profile.plan: Summons HERO and Neos Fusion Monsters ignoring their Summoning conditions by using materials from the hand, field, GY, and banishment, while also enabling Dark Fusion plays with Evil HEROes.

hooks.label: Neos support cards
hooks.why: Instant Contact and Favorite Contact both depend on 'Elemental HERO Neos', so any card that mentions it or 'Neo-Spacian' directly supports the deck's core play.

hooks.label: Dark Fusion support
hooks.why: Dark Contact can Fusion Summon using 'Dark Fusion' and also adds it from the Deck, so cards that mention 'Dark Fusion' (like Dark Calling or Evil HERO monsters) are direct partners.

hooks.label: Supreme King's Castle support
hooks.why: Dark Contact can add 'Supreme King's Castle' from the Deck, and that Field Spell enables Fusion Summons using materials from the Deck, greatly expanding the deck's plays.

hooks.label: HERO monsters with GY effects
hooks.why: Favorite Contact and Dark Contact use materials from the GY, so HERO monsters that do something when sent to the GY (like Elemental HERO Shadow Mist) get extra value.

hooks.label: Evil HERO monsters
hooks.why: Dark Contact summons Fusion Monsters that must be Special Summoned with 'Dark Fusion', which are typically 'Evil HERO' Fusions, so having 'Evil HERO' monsters as materials is necessary.

hooks.label: Revive Normal Elemental HERO
hooks.why: Instant Contact needs Elemental HERO Neos on the field or in the GY to avoid its drawbacks, so reviving it from the GY is a direct enabler.

profile.plan: A Rock deck that constantly swaps Field Spells, sending them to the GY to search, summon and boost, while Normal Summoning Rock monsters to trigger draws and LP gain.

hooks.label: Field Spell tutors
hooks.why: Triamid Loading searches a Triamid Spell/Trap when a Field Spell is placed, and the Triamid monsters send Field Spells to the GY to activate more from the Deck, so any card that adds or places a Field Spell keeps the engine running.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Every Triamid monster is a Rock, Triamid Dancer and Triamid Fortress boost Rock monsters, and Triamid Pulse banishes Rock monsters from the GY, so generic Rock support strengthens the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rock mill
hooks.why: Triamid Pulse banishes Rock monsters from the GY to destroy cards or revive monsters, and Triamid Dancer shuffles Triamid cards from the GY, so filling the GY with Rock monsters provides fuel.

hooks.label: Rock revival
hooks.why: Triamid Pulse can Special Summon a Rock monster from the GY, so effects that do the same give you more bodies for Tribute or Xyz Summons.

hooks.label: GY Field Spells
hooks.why: Triamid Sphinx gains 500 ATK for each Field Spell with a different name in your GY, and the Triamid Field Spells themselves have effects when sent to the GY, so outside Field Spells with a GY trigger add value.

profile.plan: Mills Skull Servant and King of the Skull Servants into the GY to power up King of the Skull Servants's ATK, then revives them with Wightlord and Wight Reanimator while locked into Zombie Special Summons.

hooks.label: Mills Zombie monsters
hooks.why: Wightlord sends cards from the top of the Deck to the GY based on the number of Skull Servant and King of the Skull Servants in the GY, and Wight Reanimator sends a Skull Servant or a card that mentions it from the Deck to the GY, so outside cards that mill Zombies do the same.

hooks.label: Revives Zombie from GY
hooks.why: Wightlord banishes itself from the GY to Special Summon a Skull Servant or King of the Skull Servants, and Wight Reanimator Special Summons one from the GY, so outside cards that revive Zombies give more ways to put your boss back on the field.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Wight monster is a Zombie and both Wight Reanimator and Moissa Wight restrict you to Special Summoning only Zombies for the rest of the turn, so cards that search, revive or boost Zombies work with the whole deck.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Skull Servant is a Normal Monster and the Wight cards search it, so outside cards that Special Summon or add Normal Monsters from the Deck give you more copies to mill or revive.

profile.plan: A WIND Machine Synchro/Pendulum deck that tunes roid monsters into Clear Wing bosses, locking itself into WIND Special Summons while chipping with lots of small attackers.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Darumaknocker, Colonel Clackers and Wing Synchron all forbid Special Summoning anything but WIND for the rest of the turn, and Dominobutterfly can only Pendulum Summon WIND.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every roid monster is Machine, and Einroid even sends 2 Level 4 or lower Machine monsters from the Deck to the GY as setup.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Machine
hooks.why: Einroid and Colonel Clackers both trigger when they are destroyed by battle or card effect, turning your own destruction into a Deck dump or a Tuner Summon.

hooks.label: Extra attacks
hooks.why: Meteor Rush - Monochroid Special Summons itself once 5 or more attacks have been declared this turn and gains 1000 ATK per attack, so anything that piles up attacks feeds it.

hooks.label: Clear Wing monsters
hooks.why: Darumaknocker destroys a monster while you control a "Clear Wing" monster, Colonel Clackers gives one 700 ATK, and Glider #2 banishes itself while you control one.

profile.plan: A Dinosaur deck of huge bosses that Special Summon themselves back from the GY whenever they are destroyed, as long as a Normal Monster is shuffled from the GY into the Deck.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every Transcendosaurus is a Dinosaur, so cards that search, revive, protect or boost Dinosaurs work on the entire deck.

hooks.label: Sends Normal Monsters to the GY
hooks.why: The shared revive effect needs a Normal Monster sitting in the GY, so any card that puts one there switches the loop on.

hooks.label: Dinosaurs that want destroying
hooks.why: Meteorus destroys 2 Dinosaur monsters from your hand or field and Gigantozowler destroys one, so Dinosaurs with an effect when they are destroyed get used for free.

profile.plan: Normal Summon Level 6 FIRE monsters for free or cheap, use their targeting protection to stay on board, and overlay them into Rank 6 Xyz such as Hazy Flame Basiltrice, which banishes and grows with material.

hooks.label: FIRE monster support
hooks.why: Every Hazy monster is FIRE, and their effects ask for FIRE monsters in hand, field or Graveyard, so generic FIRE support advances the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 6 FIRE without tribute
hooks.why: Hazy Pillar and Hazy Glory reduce the Tribute for a Level 6 Hazy, so outside Level 6 FIRE monsters that Normal Summon themselves without Tributing are immediate Xyz material.

hooks.label: FIRE monsters that want to be sent to GY
hooks.why: Hazy Flame Sphynx, Mantikor and Peryton send FIRE monsters from your hand or field to the Graveyard, so outside FIRE monsters with a Graveyard trigger get their effect for free.

hooks.label: FIRE monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Hazy Flame Peryton Tributes itself and Hyppogrif Tributes another FIRE monster, so outside FIRE monsters that trigger when Tributed fit the deck's costs.

hooks.label: Attaches FIRE as Xyz Material
hooks.why: Hazy Pillar attaches a Hazy Flame from hand or field to an Xyz Monster, and Basiltrice detaches for its banish, so outside cards that attach FIRE monsters as material extend the same play.

hooks.label: Revives FIRE from GY
hooks.why: Hazy Flame Sphynx can Special Summon a FIRE monster from the Graveyard, and Hydra attaches one from there, so outside cards that revive FIRE monsters give the deck more material.

profile.plan: Dustons are harmless 0-ATK Level 1 Fiends that cannot be Tributed or used as material, so the deck hands them to the opponent with House Duston and Diamond Duston to clog their field, then sits behind Starduston's Special-Summon/Flip/Set-Spell lock while the colour Dustons burn, discard and recycle themselves.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Red, Blue, Green and Yellow Duston all do something when they are destroyed on the field, so any outside effect that destroys your own Fiends turns a Duston into burn damage, a hand banish, a bounce or a Deck shuffle.

hooks.label: Stocks the opponent's field
hooks.why: Starduston destroys itself the moment you control more monsters than the opponent, and House Duston and Diamond Duston only Special Summon when monsters are being placed on both sides, so cards that put monsters or Tokens on the opponent's field keep the lock and the clog intact.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Duston, including Starduston and the copies you hand to the opponent, is a Fiend, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 1 support
hooks.why: White Duston and every colour Duston is a Level 1 monster, so cards that tutor or support Level 1 monsters fetch the pieces the deck needs.

hooks.label: Fills the Graveyard with Fiends
hooks.why: Diamond Duston's Graveyard effect banishes a Duston from the Graveyard to revive itself on the opponent's field, and Starduston is Summoned by sending Dustons to the Graveyard, so effects that send Fiends from the Deck to the Graveyard supply that fuel.

profile.plan: A Level 3 Dragon Xyz deck that keeps attaching and detaching Xyz Materials, using Level 3 Normal Monsters as fuel for Rank 3 Xyz Summons and adding materials back to hand for follow-up.

hooks.label: Summons Level 3 Normals
hooks.why: Materiactor Gigadra and Zeptwing need a Level 3 Normal Monster in hand, Deck or GY, and Meltthrough uses one as Xyz Material, so outside cards that Special Summon Level 3 Normal Monsters provide extra material.

hooks.label: Effects when discarded
hooks.why: Materiactor Exareptor discards 1 other card and Gigadra discards 1 card as cost, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded get value.

hooks.label: Effects when detached
hooks.why: Materiactor Exagard, Gigaboros and Annulus detach Xyz Materials as cost, so outside monsters that trigger when detached as material get free effects.

hooks.label: Attaches itself as material
hooks.why: Materiactor Critical and Annulus consume Xyz Materials, and Exagard/Gigaboros want materials attached, so outside cards that attach themselves as Xyz Material fuel them.

profile.plan: A Plant Link combo deck that uses Sunseed Genius Loci as a Normal Monster material, with Shadow and Twin turning it into Link Summons for Sunavalon and Sunvine monsters.

hooks.label: Summons Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Sunseed Genius Loci is a Level 1 Plant Normal Monster that the deck needs on the field and in the GY, so effects that Special Summon Normal Monsters from the Deck set it up.

hooks.label: Sends Plant Normal to GY
hooks.why: Sunseed Twin revives a Level 4 or lower Plant Normal Monster from the GY, so effects that send Genius Loci from the Deck to the GY enable that revival.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Every Sunseed monster is a Plant, and the deck's Link Summons require Plant materials, so cards that search, revive or boost Plants work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Plant Token generators
hooks.why: The deck needs multiple Plant monsters on the field to Link Summon, and cards like Dandylion provide Plant Tokens that can be used as Link Material.

profile.plan: A support suite that loads the GY with Fiend and Infernoid monsters, empties and refills the hand, recycles banished Infernoids, and keeps Level 8 DARK Dragon Synchro and Infernity bosses alive.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Void Apocalypse sends a Fiend from the Deck to the GY, Void Breach and Void Reignition only work with no monsters or all Fiend monsters, and every Infernoid is a Fiend.

hooks.label: Mills Fiend monsters
hooks.why: Void Apocalypse sends 1 Fiend monster from your Deck to the GY, so any outside card that puts Fiends straight into the GY fuels Infernoid Summons the same way.

hooks.label: Discards your whole hand
hooks.why: Void Reignition and Contract with the Void discard your entire hand, which loads the GY and leaves the empty hand that Void Cauldron and Infernity monsters want.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Void Reignition and Contract with the Void throw away your whole hand as a cost, so monsters that do something when they are discarded get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Infernity cards
hooks.why: Contract with the Void revives an Infernity monster from the GY and Void Cauldron shields your Infernity monsters while banishing Infernity cards as the cost.

profile.plan: Digital Bug changes its own monsters' battle positions to trigger effects, then Xyz Summons Insect-Type monsters and ranks them up from Rank 3 to 5 to 7, while disabling and destroying the opponent's Defense Position monsters.

hooks.label: Battle position changers
hooks.why: Centibit and LEDybug only trigger when they are changed from Attack to Defense, and Corebage attaches a material whenever any monster's battle position changes.

hooks.label: LIGHT Insect support
hooks.why: Every Digital Bug monster is LIGHT Insect, so cards that support LIGHT or Insect monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Material
hooks.why: Corebage attaches an Insect from the GY as material, and Scaradiator attaches destroyed monsters, so outside cards that attach Insect materials keep the Rank-up chain going.

hooks.label: Level changers
hooks.why: Registrider can make two Level 3 Insects into Level 5 or 7, so outside cards that change Levels help reach the requirements for Corebage and Rhinosebus.

hooks.label: Summons Level 3 Insects
hooks.why: Centibit and Websolder Special Summon Level 3 Insect monsters from the Deck or hand, so outside cards that do the same extend the Xyz Summoning.

profile.plan: A FIRE Reptile and Dinosaur deck that sends its own monsters from the Deck to the GY to change Levels and Types, then Xyz Summons Rank 6 Evolzar monsters with cheaper effects.

hooks.label: FIRE Reptile/Dinosaur with GY effects
hooks.why: Evolsaur Lios sends a FIRE Reptile or Dinosaur from the Deck to the GY, so outside cards of those exact specs that do something in the GY get sent for free.

hooks.label: Reptile/Dinosaur that benefit from being Tributed
hooks.why: Evoltile Pholis can Tribute a Reptile or Dinosaur to protect your monsters, so outside Reptile or Dinosaur monsters with an effect when Tributed turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: The Evoltile monsters are Reptiles and Pholis Tributes Reptile or Dinosaur monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Reptiles help the deck.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: The Evolsaur monsters are Dinosaurs and Lios sends FIRE Dinosaurs to the GY, so cards that support Dinosaurs fit the deck.

profile.plan: Link Summons EARTH Cyberse monsters into co-linked positions, using Tokens, GY revival and hand-discard costs to build a boss that soaks up attacks and negates effects.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every G Golem monster is Cyberse, and both Rock Hammer and Pebble Dog lock you out of Special Summoning anything other than Cyberse monsters for the rest of the turn.

hooks.label: EARTH Link material
hooks.why: Crystal Heart, Invalid Dolmen and Dignified Trilithon all require EARTH monsters as Link material, so outside cards that Special Summon an EARTH monster from the Deck or GY are extra material.

hooks.label: Discard fodder Cyberse
hooks.why: Rock Hammer and Invalid Dolmen both discard a Cyberse monster as a cost, and Pebble Dog triggers when it is sent from the hand to the GY, so Cyberse monsters that reward being discarded are free value.

hooks.label: Mills EARTH monsters
hooks.why: Gravity Balance revives two same-named EARTH monsters from the GY or banished and Stubborn Menhir revives an EARTH monster from the GY, so outside cards that send EARTH monsters from the Deck to the GY set both up.

profile.plan: A Ninja toolbox that uses its Spells and Traps to Set, Tribute and revive Ninja monsters, and to flip monsters face-down for control.

hooks.label: Ninja monsters
hooks.why: The whole archetype supports Ninja monsters: it Sets them from the Deck, Tributes one to Summon another, revives them and brings them back from the GY.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: The Continuous Trap that Tributes a monster to Special Summon a Ninja from the Deck makes any monster that does something when Tributed give extra value.

hooks.label: Ninja monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: The Equip Spell that banishes a Ninja from your GY to destroy a card makes a Ninja that does something when banished give a second effect for free.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Spell/Trap
hooks.why: The Equip Spell triggers when sent from the field to the GY, so a card that destroys your own Spell/Trap can turn it into a revival for a banished Ninja.

profile.plan: An Xyz control deck that summons Number 69: Heraldry Crest to copy the opponent's Xyz Monster, then upgrades into Shatter Stream and Dark Matter Demolition to rename and negate the opponent's monsters, while Heraldry Record punishes Xyz detaches.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic cards
hooks.why: Number C69: Heraldry Crest of Horror is a Rank 5 'C' Xyz that gains its detach effect only when it has Number 69 as material, so Rank-Up-Magic cards summon it properly and provide that material.

hooks.label: Xyz Material attach
hooks.why: Dark Matter Demolition needs five Level 4 materials and Shatter Stream transfers materials, so cards that attach Xyz Material directly fuel their detach effects.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Heraldry Xyz Monster is Psychic, and Flash of Heraldry rewards controlling a Psychic Xyz, so any card that searches, summons or protects Psychic monsters helps build the board.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: All Heraldry Xyz Monsters are LIGHT, so cards that search, summon or boost LIGHT monsters give the deck the Main Deck bodies it otherwise lacks.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 4
hooks.why: Number 69, Shatter Stream and Dark Matter Demolition need three to five Level 4 materials, so Level 4 monsters that Special Summon themselves provide Xyz fodder without using the Normal Summon.

profile.plan: A Level 8 Beast-Warrior beatdown deck that cheats out its bosses by piling up Tributes or banishing Machine and Beast-Warrior fodder, then wipes the opponent's board.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Beast King Barbaros destroys every card the opponent controls when it is Tribute Summoned with 3 Tributes, and King Beast Barbaros Special Summons itself by Tributing monsters whose Levels total 8.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Beast King Barbaros asks for 3 Tributes and King Beast Barbaros for monsters whose Levels total 8 or more, so free Tokens are the cheapest fodder for either Summon.

hooks.label: Tributes opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Beast King Barbaros needs 3 Tributes and King Beast Barbaros needs Level 8 worth of them, so effects that Tribute the opponent's monsters pay that cost without giving up your own board.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Beast King Barbaros, Barbaros Ür and King Beast Barbaros are all Beast-Warrior, so cards that search, revive or strengthen Beast-Warriors work on every monster the deck plays.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes three monsters for Beast King Barbaros and Level 8 worth for King Beast Barbaros, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished
hooks.why: Barbaros Ür Special Summons itself by banishing a Machine and a Beast-Warrior from your hand, field or GY, and King Beast Barbaros banishes a Barbaros monster, so monsters that do something when banished cost nothing.

profile.plan: A Gemini deck that keeps its monsters as Normal Monsters, Normal Summons them a second time to unlock their effects, and overlays the Level 8 members into Methydraco.

hooks.label: Gemini support Spell/Trap
hooks.why: The deck only functions through a Gemini monster's second Normal Summon, so cards that search, equip or revive Gemini monsters keep the engine moving.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: A Gemini monster only gains its effects when it is Normal Summoned again while face-up, and Poly-Chemicritter Dioxogre even protects that Normal Summon from negation, so another Normal Summon doubles the deck's output.

hooks.label: Revives Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Gemini monsters are treated as Normal Monsters while in the Graveyard, so a card that Special Summons a Normal Monster from the GY brings one back to be Normal Summoned for its effect.

hooks.label: Level-changing cards
hooks.why: Methydraco needs two Level 8 Gemini materials while the Chemicritter engine runs on Level 2s, and Oxy Ox already copies a Gemini's original Level to the whole board.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Hydron Hawk discards a card as the cost of reviving a Gemini from the GY, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded pay that cost for you.

profile.plan: A Link-climbing deck that puts its two Level 2 DARK twins on board for free, turns them into Fiend boss monsters and grinds the opponent down with Lil-la Rap's burn every time a monster comes back from the GY.

hooks.label: Fiend Extra Deck support
hooks.why: Lil-la Sweet's GY revival locks your Extra Deck to Fiend monsters, so anything that searches, revives or boosts Fiends plays straight into the deck's Link bosses.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Live☆Twin Lil-la Sweet and Lil-la Treat are both DARK, so generic DARK support searches, revives and protects the entire monster line-up.

hooks.label: Mills your monsters
hooks.why: Lil-la Sweet Special Summons itself from the GY and Lil-la Treat banishes itself from the GY, so sending DARK monsters from the Deck to the GY turns them on.

hooks.label: Revives from the GY
hooks.why: Lil-la Rap makes the opponent lose 1000 LP every time you Special Summon a monster from the GY, so any extra revival effect in the deck is another burn.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell support
hooks.why: Lil-la Rap is the deck's damage engine and only burns while it stays face-up, so cards that search, recover or shield Continuous Spells keep the loop alive.

profile.plan: A Rank 3 Rock Xyz deck that swarms Level 3 Rock-Type monsters and turns them into Gorgonic Guardian, which strips an opponent's monster of its ATK and effects and then destroys anything left sitting at 0 ATK.

hooks.label: Rock-Type support
hooks.why: Every Gorgonic monster is a Rock, Gorgonic Gargoyle Special Summons itself whenever you Normal Summon a Rock-Type, and Gorgonic Cerberus turns your whole Rock field into Level 3.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Both Gorgonic Gargoyle (on Normal Summon of a Rock-Type) and Gorgonic Cerberus (on its own Normal Summon) only trigger off Normal Summons, so an extra Normal Summon turns into an extra body for a Rank 3.

hooks.label: Drops a monster to 0 ATK
hooks.why: Gorgonic Guardian can destroy any monster on the field with 0 ATK, and Gorgonic Golem zeroes the ATK of whatever destroyed it in battle, so outside effects that set an opponent's ATK to 0 hand Guardian an immediate kill.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Material
hooks.why: Gorgonic Guardian detaches an Xyz Material every turn to zero an opponent's monster, so anything that replenishes its materials keeps the lock running.

hooks.label: Number Xyz monsters
hooks.why: Gorgonic Umbral Horror locks the Extra Deck to "Number" Xyz Monsters and can be treated as 2 materials for a "Number" Xyz Monster that requires 3 or more materials.

profile.plan: A Spell-heavy control-beatdown deck: Morgana the Witch of Eyes searches Morganite Spells, and those rest-of-Duel Spells lock out hand monster effects in exchange for doubled battle damage, double attacks on monsters, free high-Level Normal Summons and free Spell/Trap activation.

hooks.label: Free Level 5+ Normal Summons
hooks.why: Guilt-Gripping Morganite lets you Normal Summon Level 5 or higher monsters without Tributing for the rest of the Duel, so a high-Level monster with an effect when it is Normal Summoned costs you no Tribute.

hooks.label: Spell/Traps that pay LP
hooks.why: Guilt-Gripping Morganite stops you paying LP to activate Spell/Trap Cards, so any Spell or Trap with an LP cost in its text becomes free.

hooks.label: Sends Spells to the GY
hooks.why: All three Morganite Spells only pay off from the GY or banishment, and Morgana the Witch of Eyes needs 3 differently named Morganite Spells in the GY/banished, so anything that loads Spell Cards into the GY sets both up.

hooks.label: Piercing attackers
hooks.why: Succumbing-Song Morganite doubles the battle damage your monsters inflict in battle and lets them attack monsters twice per Battle Phase, so piercing attackers push doubled damage through Defense Position walls twice.

hooks.label: Spellcaster and DARK support
hooks.why: Morgana the Witch of Eyes, the deck's only monster and its Morganite Spell searcher, is a Level 4 DARK Spellcaster, so support for Spellcasters or DARK monsters searches, revives and protects her.

profile.plan: A WATER/Aqua beatdown deck that stacks the Aquarium Continuous Spells to double a battling Aquaactress's ATK and protect its board, using those same Spells to revive an Aqua-Type from the Graveyard whenever they leave the field.

hooks.label: Aqua-Type support
hooks.why: Every Aquaactress monster is an Aqua-Type, and the Graveyard effects of Aquarium Stage, Aquarium Set and Aquarium Lighting can only revive Aqua-Type monsters and then lock you into Aqua-Type Special Summons, so Aqua-only support is never wasted.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: All Aquaactress monsters are WATER, and Aquarium Stage's battle protection and Aquarium Set's 300 ATK/DEF bonus only apply to WATER monsters you control, so generic WATER support strengthens the whole board.

hooks.label: Sends your Continuous Spell to the GY
hooks.why: Aquarium Stage, Aquarium Set and Aquarium Lighting each Special Summon an Aqua-Type monster from the Graveyard when they are sent from the field to the Graveyard, so any outside card that sends or destroys your own Continuous Spell turns them into a free revival.

hooks.label: Mills Aqua-Type monsters
hooks.why: Aqua Story - Urashima needs an Aquaactress in the Graveyard to be usable, and the Aquarium Spells revive Aqua-Type monsters from there, so outside cards that send Aqua-Type monsters from the Deck or hand to the Graveyard set up both at once.

hooks.label: Extra attacks
hooks.why: Aquarium Lighting doubles your battling Aquaactress monster's ATK and DEF during damage calculation, so outside cards that grant additional attacks or let it attack every monster turn that one doubling into several battles.

profile.plan: A Ritual- and Tribute Summon deck: Amorphactor Pain and Master Peace land to stop the opponent's Main Phase and negate their monsters, while Lector punishes Pendulums.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: Amorphactor Pain is a Ritual Monster Ritual Summoned with "Amorphous Persona", and its Main Phase 1 skip only happens on a Ritual Summon, so anything that Ritual Summons or fetches the pieces gets the deck's biggest payoff online.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Master Peace, the True Dracoverlord needs 3 Tributes to Normal Summon, so cards that Special Summon Tokens hand it three free bodies and leave the hand untouched.

hooks.label: Self-replacing Continuous Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Master Peace can Tribute Continuous Spells/Traps you control as Tribute Summon material, so Continuous Spells and Traps that pay you back when they leave the field turn into free material.

hooks.label: Easy Tribute Summon monsters
hooks.why: The deck is built around Tribute Summoning - Master Peace's Quick Effect only works while it is Tribute Summoned - so outside monsters that can Tribute Summon themselves cheaply give it more bosses and more material.

hooks.label: Monsters that reward being Tributed
hooks.why: Master Peace eats 3 Tributes every time it hits the field, so any monster with an effect when it is Tributed gives the deck value for material it was going to spend anyway.

profile.plan: A Cyberse combo deck that reveals a 2300 ATK Cyberse monster to fetch an @Ignister of the matching Attribute, then turns its Continuous Spells and Traps into revives, debuffs and Battle Phase Special Summons.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: A.I. Meet You, A.I. Connect and A.I.'s Show only search, Special Summon or protect Cyberse monsters, and both A.I. Spells lock the turn to Cyberse Special Summons and Cyberse monster effects, so Type-wide support helps every card.

hooks.label: Special Summons a Cyberse monster
hooks.why: You and A.I. triggers whenever a Cyberse monster with 2300 original ATK is Special Summoned, and A.I.'s Show and FA.I.ghting Spirit reward having extra Cyberse bodies on the field.

hooks.label: Special Summons Tokens
hooks.why: You and A.I. makes @Ignister Tokens and A.I. Challenge You drops every opponent monster by 100 ATK for each card you control, so outside Token makers add both Link material and extra debuff.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Normal and Quick-Play Spells that take an Xyz Monster you already control (or revive from the GY) and Rank it up into a higher-Rank 'Utopia', 'Utopic', 'ZW -' or 'Number' Xyz Monster, transferring its materials and then reusing themselves from the GY as material.

hooks.label: Sends Spells to the GY
hooks.why: Utopiforce attaches itself as material from the GY and Zexal Force banishes itself from the GY to draw, so their second effects only exist if something put these Rank-Up-Magic Spells into the GY.

hooks.label: Xyz Material suppliers
hooks.why: Every Rank-Up-Magic card transfers the target's materials, and Utopiforce, Ultimate Force and Magical Force attach themselves as material, so effects that add Xyz Material make the upgraded Xyz Monster stronger.

hooks.label: Spellcaster Xyz support
hooks.why: Rank-Up-Magic Magical Force revives a Rank 4 Spellcaster Xyz from the GY and Ranks it up into a Rank 5 Spellcaster Xyz, so cards that support Spellcaster Xyz Monsters extend the same line.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster support
hooks.why: Hyper Rank-Up-Magic Ultimate Force can only Rank up a Rank 9 or lower 'Utopia' or 'Utopic' Xyz whose original Attribute is LIGHT, and the Utopia line it summons is LIGHT.

profile.plan: A Warrior deck that puts Level 6 monsters on board (often Normal Summoned for free) to Xyz Summon Photon Strike Bounzer, whose Xyz Material detaches negate the opponent's monster effects and burn for 1000.

hooks.label: Free Level 6 bodies
hooks.why: Photon Strike Bounzer needs two Level 6 monsters and Hammer Bounzer already Normal Summons itself without Tributing, so other Level 6 monsters that do the same give easy Xyz Material.

hooks.label: Discard payoffs
hooks.why: Blade Bounzer discards 1 card as a cost to attack a second time, so outside cards that do something when they are discarded get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Bounzer monster is a Warrior, so cards that search, revive or boost Warriors work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Summons Level 6 monsters
hooks.why: Photon Strike Bounzer asks for two Level 6 monsters and the deck's Level 6 bodies are limited, so outside effects that Special Summon Level 6 monsters supply the material.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Hammer Bounzer can be Normal Summoned without Tribute and Phantom Bounzer wants to reach the field, so extra Normal Summons put two Level 6 monsters out for the Xyz Summon.

profile.plan: An EARTH-heavy X-Saber toolbox: Bruno and Pellina assemble Synchro material while Commander Souza grows with every banished monster and Saber Combination floods the field with X-Sabers.

hooks.label: EARTH monster support
hooks.why: X-Saber Bruno banishes another EARTH monster to Special Summon itself and Synchro Summons using only EARTH monsters, and Commander Souza asks for EARTH Synchro material.

hooks.label: Banishes monsters from the GY
hooks.why: Commander Souza gains 200 ATK for every banished monster and can banish a Saber card from the GY instead of being destroyed, so effects that clear monsters out of the GY make it bigger and harder to kill.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Steamed Sabersaurus is a Dinosaur Xyz that destroys a Dinosaur from your hand or face-up field for its effect and hands another Dinosaur 2000 ATK during the Damage Step.

hooks.label: EARTH monsters that like being banished
hooks.why: X-Saber Bruno banishes an EARTH monster from your hand, face-up field or GY as a cost, so outside EARTH monsters with an effect when they are banished get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Equip Spell support
hooks.why: ZW - Pegasus Twin Saber and Sky Striker Mecha - Adil Saber both turn themselves into Equip Spells that grant 1000-1500 ATK, so cards that search, revive or reward Equip Spells keep that plan running.

profile.plan: A Trap deck that Tributes a face-up monster to Special Summon a big no-Normal-Summon Machine straight from the hand, Deck or GY, then equips the Trap to it for protection, and uses Time Engine to revive a destroyed monster for a board wipe and burn.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Max Metalmorph and Flame Coating Metalmorph both pay for themselves with "Tribute 1 face-up monster", so any card that fills your field with Tokens keeps the Traps live.

hooks.label: Monsters that want Tributing
hooks.why: The Metalmorph Traps Tribute a face-up monster as their activation cost, so a monster with an effect that triggers when it is Tributed gives you that effect for free.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Time Engine hands out its board wipe and burn only around a Level 5 or higher Machine monster, and the boss monsters Max Metalmorph produces are Machines, so Machine searchers and revivers serve the whole deck.

hooks.label: Floaters when destroyed
hooks.why: Time Engine only triggers when a monster you control is destroyed by battle or an opponent's card effect and then Special Summons that same monster back, so monsters that already replaced themselves on destruction get doubled value.

profile.plan: A Reptile/Dinosaur deck where FIRE Reptile Evoltiles Tribute themselves or each other to Special Summon FIRE Dinosaurs from the Deck, then stack Reptile and Dinosaur material onto Dragon Xyz Monsters.
