hooks.label: Reptile Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Evoltile Megachirella Tributes 1 Reptile monster to Summon from the Deck and Evo-Branch destroys a Reptile to Summon an Evoltile, so outside cards that put Reptile bodies on the field are the deck's fuel.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Megachirella and Casinerio Tribute a monster as their cost and Elginero only pays off when it is Tributed to the GY, so outside monsters with a Tribute trigger get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Evoltile is a Reptile and its costs ask for Reptile monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Reptiles work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Evoltile is a FIRE monster and every card the deck Summons with them is a FIRE Dinosaur, so generic FIRE support applies to both halves.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck that builds a base Synchro Monster, Tributes it to a Trap to Special Summon the Level 7-12 /Assault Mode upgrade from the Deck, and gets the base back when the boss is destroyed.

hooks.label: Dumps Tuners in the GY
hooks.why: Red Nova Dragon/Assault Mode banishes one card your opponent controls for each Tuner in your Graveyard, so effects that send or discard Tuners straight there turn it into removal.

hooks.label: Trap tutors
hooks.why: Every /Assault Mode monster can only be Special Summoned by Assault Mode Activate, and Crimson Blader/Assault Mode already searches that Trap, so other cards that add or Set a Trap from the Deck find the enabler faster.

hooks.label: Revives Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: Assault Mode Activate sends the Tributed Synchro Monster to the Graveyard and the /Assault Mode monsters only bring back their own base, so extra ways to Special Summon a Synchro Monster from the GY put a valid Tribute back on board.

profile.plan: A control deck that empties and banishes its own Extra Deck face-down, then Special Summons Dreaming Nemleria from the face-up Extra Deck to banish the opponent's cards, while Level 10 Beast monsters like Reveil recur themselves from the hand and GY.

hooks.label: Banishes the Extra Deck face-down
hooks.why: Reveil, Repeter and Dreaming Nemleria all pay for their effects with cards banished face-down from the Extra Deck, and Dreaming Nemleria's removal scales with your face-down banished cards.

hooks.label: Level 10 monster payoffs
hooks.why: Reveil and Realized are Level 10 monsters that summon themselves from the hand, GY or Extra Deck, so outside cards that fetch, summon or reward Level 10 monsters support the deck's whole boss line.

hooks.label: Empty Extra Deck payoffs
hooks.why: Dreaming Nemleria can only be Special Summoned while the Extra Deck holds nothing but itself, so cards that require or reward an empty Extra Deck share the deck's setup.
phrases: no cards in your Extra Deck

profile.plan: A Trap-heavy Synchro deck: Level 7-8 monsters Special Summon themselves by bouncing a face-down card you control, it Sets Ashtra Traps that become Level 1 Tuner monsters for an immediate Synchro Summon, and it stuffs Traps into the GY to banish the opponent's field and re-Set them later.

hooks.label: Sets cards face-down
hooks.why: Mikumari, Akasuna, Yoa and Kuzuha all Special Summon themselves by revealing a face-down card you control and returning it to the hand or Extra Deck, so extra ways to Set cards give the deck fuel, and Kuzuha and Ashtraya Mikumari-no-Mikoto both count face-down cards on the field.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Akasuna flips every face-up monster the opponent controls to face-down Defense Position, while Kuzuha destroys one card per two face-down cards on the field and Ashtraya needs three face-down cards, so more cards turned face-down on either side advance both payoffs.

hooks.label: Sends Traps to the GY
hooks.why: Ashtraja Susanoo banishes Traps from the GY to banish cards on the field, Mikumari re-Sets a Normal Trap from the GY and Kuzuha re-Sets an Ashtra Trap from the GY, so loading the GY with Traps powers every payoff the deck has.

hooks.label: Trap that works in the GY
hooks.why: Akasuna's Quick Effect sends a Trap from your hand or face-down field to the GY as a cost and Ashtrashen sends face-down cards to the GY, so Traps that trigger when they hit the GY get their effect for free and then become Ashtraja's banish fodder.

hooks.label: Normal Trap searcher
hooks.why: Ashtra's Domain, Howl and Web are all Normal Traps that turn into Level 1 Tuner monsters for an immediate Synchro Summon, and Mikumari re-Sets a Normal Trap from the GY, so cards that find Normal Traps keep the Synchro engine going.

profile.plan: A Warrior Pendulum deck that trades cards away — discarding for ATK-halving and Graveyard revival — while searching and reviving Warrior and Spellcaster monsters with 2000 or less ATK, plus Normal Monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being discarded
hooks.why: Dragodies' Pendulum effect and Dragonox's monster effect both discard 1 card as the cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Warrior and Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Empowered Warrior is a Warrior, and Dragodies searches, Dragonox revives and Arnis Special Summons Warrior or Spellcaster-Type monsters with 2000 or less ATK, so generic Warrior/Spellcaster support reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Pendulum Scale support
hooks.why: Dragodies and Dragonox are the deck's two Pendulum monsters, sitting at scales 2 and 7 so you can Pendulum Summon the Level 3-5 Warriors, and cards that set up or protect those scales keep that going.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Terratiger needs a Level 4 or lower Normal Monster in hand to Special Summon and Ventdra returns a Dragon, Warrior or Spellcaster Normal Monster from the Graveyard, so cards that search or revive Normal Monsters feed both.

profile.plan: Turns tiny Level 2 'Chrysalis' monsters into Neo-Spacian monsters while 'Neo Space' is on the field, either by Tributing them or with Contact/Cocoon cards, then leans on Neo-Spacian Contact Fusion as the win condition.

hooks.label: Field Spell tutors
hooks.why: Every Chrysalis monster, plus Cocoon Rebirth and Cocoon Veil, only transforms while 'Neo Space' is on the field, so anything that puts a Field Spell from the Deck onto the field or into the hand is the deck's ignition.

hooks.label: Mills monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Cocoon Party Special Summons one Chrysalis per differently named Neo-Spacian in your Graveyard, and Cocoon Rebirth and Cocoon Veil revive Neo-Spacians from either Graveyard, so filling the GY with monsters stocks all three.

hooks.label: Level 2 revival
hooks.why: Every Chrysalis monster is Level 2 and lands in the Graveyard after Tributing itself or being sent by Contact, so effects that Special Summon a Level 2 monster from the Graveyard give the deck another transformation.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Each Chrysalis monster spends your Normal Summon on a 300-800 ATK body and then Tributes itself away, so extra Normal Summons let the deck transform more than one Chrysalis in a turn.

hooks.label: Neo-Spacian support cards
hooks.why: The archetype's entire output is Neo-Spacian monsters from the hand, Deck and either Graveyard, so outside cards that search, revive or fuse with Neo-Spacians are working toward the same board.

profile.plan: An Equip Spell toolbox that protects and powers up FIRE Warrior Noble Knights, then Synchro Summons a Level 5 to search and mill FIRE Warriors for follow-up.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior support
hooks.why: Noble Arms Museum gives all FIRE Warrior monsters 500 ATK and Angelica sends a FIRE Warrior from Deck to GY, so cards that support FIRE Warrior monsters advance the whole deck.

hooks.label: Equip Spells with GY triggers
hooks.why: Cursed Copycat Noble Arms gains 200 ATK/DEF for each Equip Spell in your field and GY, and Camelot can destroy an Equip Card to protect a Noble Knight, so Equip Spells that do something when sent to the GY or destroyed are extra value.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior GY triggers
hooks.why: Angelica sends a FIRE Warrior from your Deck to the GY, so outside FIRE Warrior monsters with effects when sent to the GY get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Noble Knight monsters
hooks.why: Noble Arms Museum can Special Summon a Noble Knight from your Spell & Trap Zone and Camelot protects Noble Knight cards, so outside Noble Knight monsters are direct partners.

hooks.label: Charles-mentioning cards
hooks.why: Angelica adds a card that mentions Infernoble Knight Emperor Charles from your Deck, so any outside card with that text is searchable.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that parks a Pendulum boss face-up in the Extra Deck, then Special Summons its Level 10 Beast Dream Defenders from hand and pays for every effect by banishing cards from the Extra Deck face-down.

hooks.label: Beast support
hooks.why: Oreiller, Couette and everything Dream Tower of Princess Nemleria can fetch are Beasts, so cards that search, revive or boost Beasts work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Both Nemleria Dream Defenders are LIGHT, so Attribute-wide LIGHT support applies to the deck's main bodies.

hooks.label: Sends your Pendulum Monsters off the field
hooks.why: Oreiller and Couette only Special Summon themselves while a Pendulum Monster is face-up in your Extra Deck, and a Pendulum Monster that leaves the field lands there face-up, so cards that destroy, Tribute or send your own Pendulum Monster turn the engine on.

hooks.label: Pendulum Summon support
hooks.why: Dream Tower of Princess Nemleria locks you out of non-Pendulum Extra Deck Special Summons for the turn, so cards built around Pendulum Summoning keep the deck's plays legal.

profile.plan: A reactive control deck of Normal Traps, each one Set in advance and fired at the opponent's Summon: destroy a big Special Summoned monster, banish a weak Summon face-down, or snipe the monster that activates an effect after a Special Summon.

hooks.label: Normal Trap searchers
hooks.why: Every Trap Hole is a Normal Trap that must be Set and can only be used once, so cards like Trap Trick or Lilith that fetch a Normal Trap from the Deck keep the right answer in hand when the opponent Summons.

hooks.label: Mills Traps into the GY
hooks.why: Terrifying Trap Hole Nightmare only gets its extra banish of an opponent's monster if a "Hole" Normal Trap is already in your GY, so cards that send a Trap from the Deck to the GY load that clause for free.

hooks.label: Recycles Traps from the GY
hooks.why: Each Trap Hole is a one-shot Normal Trap, so cards that return a Trap from the GY to the hand give the deck a second copy of whichever answer it already spent.

hooks.label: Gives the opponent Tokens
hooks.why: Terrifying Trap Hole Nightmare and Foolish Trap Hole both require the opponent to have Special Summoned during the turn, so cards that Special Summon Tokens onto the opponent's field switch those Trap Holes on before the opponent does anything.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of Normal Monsters that battles to trigger its scales' effects: searching Level 4+ Normal Monsters, destroying cards on battle damage, and reviving Normal Monsters from the hand when monsters are destroyed by battle.

hooks.label: Normal Monster searchers
hooks.why: Dragoons of Draconia adds a Level 4 or higher Normal Monster from your Deck, so other cards that search Normal Monsters give you more monsters to battle and Pendulum Summon.

hooks.label: Normal Monster summoners
hooks.why: The deck wants Normal Monsters on the field to trigger the Pendulum effects of Sky and Sea Dragoons, so outside cards that Special Summon Normal Monsters from the Deck are extra bodies.

hooks.label: Normal Monster revival
hooks.why: Sea Dragoons of Draconia Special Summons a Normal Monster from your hand when a monster is destroyed by battle, so outside cards that revive Normal Monsters from the Graveyard keep your battle strategy going.

hooks.label: Pendulum searchers
hooks.why: The deck uses Pendulum Summoning to swarm the field with its Normal Monsters, so outside cards that add Pendulum Monsters from the Deck give you more scales and materials.

profile.plan: Synchro Summons Level 12 Dragon Synchro Monsters with huge piles of Tuner and Synchro material, then banishes those bosses to bring out even larger Red Nova Dragon-style monsters.

hooks.label: Tuner Special Summoners
hooks.why: Red Hypernova Dragon asks for 4 Tuners and Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul banishes 2 Tuners, so anything that Special Summons extra Tuners supplies material the deck cannot make on its own.

hooks.label: Dumps Tuners in the GY
hooks.why: Red Hypernova Dragon gains 500 ATK for each Tuner in your GY and Burning Soul banishes 2 Tuners from the GY to Special Summon itself, so sending Tuners from the Deck to the GY is pure value.

hooks.label: Red Dragon Archfiend support
hooks.why: Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul can only Special Summon itself by banishing a 'Red Dragon Archfiend' from your GY, so cards that search, revive or dump that monster make the deck work.

hooks.label: Revives Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: Cosmic Quasar Dragon requires 2+ non-Tuner Synchro Monsters as material, so reviving Synchro Monsters from the GY gives you the materials for the big Synchro Summons.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: All three Cosmic Synchro Monsters are Dragon monsters, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Dragons applies to the entire archetype.

profile.plan: A low-Level Synchro toolbox: Level 2 Warrior pieces tutor "Junk Warrior" and "Synchron" cards and climb into Warrior-named Synchro Monsters, while its Level 4s convert Tributes and discards into free Summons.

hooks.label: Synchron Tuner monsters
hooks.why: Assault Sonic Warrior adds a "Synchron" monster from the Deck, and every monster here is meant to be used as Synchro Material alongside it.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when Tributed
hooks.why: Swiftwind Panther Warrior Tributes another monster from your hand or field for its Quick Effect, so any monster that pays you back for being Tributed gets a free activation.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when discarded
hooks.why: Dragonic Warrior discards 1 card as the cost of Special Summoning a Dragon, so monsters with an effect when discarded are paid for free.

hooks.label: Cards mentioning Dark Time Wizard
hooks.why: Swiftwind Panther Warrior Special Summons a monster that mentions "Dark Time Wizard" from your hand or Deck, or sends a matching Spell/Trap from the Deck to the GY.

profile.plan: An Attribute toolbox that piles up monsters with as many different Attributes as possible in the Graveyards so Elemental Saga Doriado and Elemental Grace Doriado can Special Summon themselves and lock the opponent down, while Doriado's Blessing Ritual Summons Elemental Mistress Doriado.

hooks.label: Ritual searchers
hooks.why: Doriado's Blessing is the only card that can Ritual Summon Elemental Mistress Doriado, so cards that add a Ritual Spell or Ritual Monster from the Deck or GY assemble the Ritual package.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Doriado's Blessing Tributes monsters from your hand or field whose total Levels equal 3 or more, so monsters with an effect when they are Tributed are free Ritual material.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with monsters
hooks.why: Elemental Saga Doriado needs 3 and Elemental Grace Doriado needs 6 different Attributes among the monsters in the GYs, so anything that sends monsters from the Deck to the GY builds toward both thresholds.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Doriado, Elemental Mistress Doriado, Elemental Saga Doriado and Elemental Grace Doriado are all Spellcasters, so cards that search, revive or protect Spellcasters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Banished from the GY
hooks.why: Elemental Grace Doriado banishes 3 monsters from your GY as a cost to negate a Special Summon, so monsters with an effect when they are banished get value out of that cost.

profile.plan: A Crystal Beast deck whose monsters all die unless the Field Spell "Advanced Dark" is on the field, and which dodges destruction by parking itself in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, ready to be Special Summoned back in one burst.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Every Advanced Crystal Beast starts with 'If "Advanced Dark" is not in a Field Zone, send this monster to the GY', so the deck has to find its Field Spell before it can play at all.

hooks.label: Field Spell protection
hooks.why: The same 'Advanced Dark is not in a Field Zone' clause means one removal spell on the Field Spell takes the whole board with it, so keeping the Field Spell alive protects every Advanced Crystal Beast.

hooks.label: Places monsters as Continuous Spells
hooks.why: Sapphire Pegasus places an Advanced Crystal Beast from the hand, Deck, GY or banished pile face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell, and the others park themselves there when destroyed, so more cards that fill the S/T Zone the same way are more fuel for Ruby Carbuncle.

hooks.label: Beast support
hooks.why: Sapphire Pegasus, Amber Mammoth, Amethyst Cat and Topaz Tiger are all Beast-Type, so generic Beast search, revival and ATK boosts hit most of the deck.

hooks.label: Summons out of the Spell & Trap Zone
hooks.why: Ruby Carbuncle Special Summons itself from the Spell & Trap Zone and then Special Summons as many Advanced Crystal Beast Monster Cards as possible from your Spell & Trap Zones, so any effect that Special Summons monsters out of the Spell & Trap Zone does the same trick.

profile.plan: A tiny swarm of WIND Insects that Special Summon themselves from the hand, then use Primitive Butterfly's Level boost to Synchro or Xyz Summon, with Butterflyoke as a battle trap that pins down attackers.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Primitive Butterfly raises the Level of every Insect monster you control, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Insects powers up the whole deck.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Primitive Butterfly and Reed Butterfly are both WIND Insect monsters, so cards that support the WIND Attribute work on the deck's bodies.

hooks.label: Free bodies from an empty field
hooks.why: Primitive Butterfly and Reed Butterfly both Special Summon themselves from the hand while you control no monsters, so outside monsters with the same clause stack bodies for the Level-boosted Synchro or Xyz Summon.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Primitive Butterfly's only effect is adjusting the Levels of your Insect monsters, so outside cards that raise or lower Levels hit the exact Synchro or Xyz Level the deck is built around.

profile.plan: A Warrior beatdown/Fusion deck that Special Summons LIGHT and EARTH Warriors from the hand for free, fuses them into a piercing Level 10 boss, and punishes monsters without a Level.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Star monster is a Warrior (LIGHT or EARTH) and Raijin, Kaiza and Senko all pay off Warrior monsters in hand, Deck and GY, so any card that searches, revives or boosts Warriors fits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning LIGHT/EARTH Warriors
hooks.why: Kaiza, Todoroki and Senko all Special Summon themselves from the hand, and Todoroki's Quick Effect needs LIGHT/EARTH Warrior bodies on the field or in hand as Fusion material.

hooks.label: Tributed LIGHT/EARTH Warriors
hooks.why: Kaiza the Hidden Star Special Summons itself by Tributing 1 LIGHT or EARTH Warrior monster, so outside monsters of those Types/Attributes with an effect when Tributed get value for free.

hooks.label: Monsters sent from hand to GY
hooks.why: Todoroki the Earthbolt Star Special Summons itself by sending 1 other monster from your hand to the GY, so outside monsters that do something when sent from the hand to the GY are free extenders.

hooks.label: Warriors banished from the GY
hooks.why: Kaiza banishes 1 Warrior monster from the GY and Senko banishes itself from the GY, so outside Warrior monsters that trigger when banished from the GY are turned into free effects.

profile.plan: The deck equips 'Amaze Attraction' Normal Traps to monsters, switching between beneficial effects when you control the equipped monster and disruptive effects when your opponent does.

hooks.label: Normal Trap searchers
hooks.why: All Attraction cards are Normal Traps, so cards that search or Set Normal Traps from the Deck or GY find them.

hooks.label: Gives opponent a monster
hooks.why: Attraction Traps equip to a face-up monster your opponent controls to use their disruptive effects, so giving the opponent a monster to equip to is useful.

hooks.label: Makes opponent take your monster
hooks.why: The Attraction Traps have different effects depending on who controls the equipped monster, so giving your opponent control of a monster lets you use the opponent-control effects.

hooks.label: Moves Equip Cards
hooks.why: Attraction Traps become Equip Cards when equipped, so cards that move Equip Cards between monsters let you switch which player controls the equipped monster and thus which effect you can use.

profile.plan: An EARTH Machine deck built on 'Gadget' monsters: it feeds them to a 2500 ATK boss, equips them to a corporal that grows by 1000 ATK each, and unloads them again for free Special Summons, backed by a Machine-only battle trap.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Boot-Up monster is a Machine (and mostly EARTH), Gear Force only works while all your monsters are face-up Machines, and Command Dynamo only equips Machine monsters.

hooks.label: Gadget Machine monsters
hooks.why: Destroyer Dynamo must be Special Summoned by sending 2 'Gadget' Monster Cards from the hand/field to the GY, and Command Dynamo Special Summons itself by equipping 2 Machine 'Gadget' monsters from the field or GY.

hooks.label: Gadget searchers
hooks.why: The deck always needs 'Gadget' Monster Cards in hand for Destroyer Dynamo's Special Summon and in the GY for Command Dynamo to equip, so anything that adds a 'Gadget' monster from the Deck to the hand is an extender.

hooks.label: Discard payoffs
hooks.why: Gear Charge discards 1 card as a cost to add Destroyer Dynamo from the Deck, so monsters that do something when they are discarded turn that cost into free value.

hooks.label: Machine swarm
hooks.why: Gear Force destroys a number of the opponent's Attack Position monsters equal to the Machine monsters you control and only triggers while your whole board is face-up Machine, and Command Dynamo grows by every monster equipped to it.

profile.plan: A Pendulum Spirit Warrior deck that Normal Summons its Level 5 monsters to wipe out every opponent card sitting in the same column as its Pendulum Zones, then bounces them back to the hand to do it again next turn.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Kai-Den Kendo Spirit, Kuro-Obi Karate Spirit, Yoko-Zuna Sumo Spirit and Han-Shi Kyudo Spirit only clear a column when they are Normal Summoned, and each one returns to the hand in the End Phase, so additional Normal Summons are additional wipes.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Every Martial Art Spirit is a Level 5 monster, so putting one on the field means Tribute Summoning it; outside monsters whose effects trigger when they are Tributed turn that cost into card advantage.

hooks.label: Spirit monster support
hooks.why: All four cards are Spirit monsters that return themselves to the hand during the End Phase, so outside cards that search, revive, protect or suppress the return of Spirit monsters help the whole deck.

hooks.label: Warrior and WIND support
hooks.why: Every Martial Art Spirit is a WIND Warrior, so generic Warrior or WIND support can search, revive or boost any card in the archetype.

hooks.label: Pendulum Summon support
hooks.why: Each card's Pendulum Effect sends it from the Pendulum Zone back to the hand as soon as a monster is Pendulum Summoned, so outside cards that set up or repeat Pendulum Summons keep the scales filled and the column removal live.

profile.plan: A Zombie/DARK deck that searches Ghost Fusion and Fusion Summons Zombie Fusion Monsters by banishing Zombie materials from the hand, field and GY, then recycles those banished Zombies.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: All three Underworld monsters are Zombie and Ghost Fusion only uses Zombie monsters as Fusion Material, so any card that searches, revives, mills or boosts Zombies works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Zombies that like being banished
hooks.why: Ghost Fusion banishes Zombie materials from the hand, field and GY, and Ghost Sleeper and Ghost Wyvern both pay you back for banishing your own Zombies.

hooks.label: Cards that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Ghost Sleeper, the Underworld Princess banishes itself and discards a card as a cost to recover a banished Level 4 or higher Zombie, so any card with an effect when discarded pays that cost for free.

profile.plan: A Steelswarm/lswarm control deck that Tribute Summons Fiend-Type DARK monsters, then reuses them with Traps that return them to the hand, revive low-Level ones, and protect them from Spells and Traps.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon enablers
hooks.why: First Step Towards Infestation and Infestation Wave only work on a face-up Tribute Summoned Steelswarm, so the deck wants cards that let it Tribute Summon more easily, including using the opponent's monsters as Tributes.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoffs
hooks.why: The deck's First Step and Wave require a Tribute Summoned Steelswarm, so cards that give value whenever you Tribute Summon turn the same play into extra advantage.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Steelswarm monster is a Fiend-Type monster, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends support the deck's main Tribute Summoned monsters.

hooks.label: DARK Fiend milling
hooks.why: Infestation Tool sends a Steelswarm from the Deck to the GY and Infestation Ripples revives a Level 4 or lower Steelswarm from the GY, so outside cards that send DARK Fiends from the Deck to the GY set up the same Graveyard.

hooks.label: Low-Level Fiend recovery
hooks.why: Infestation Ripples revives a Level 4 or lower Steelswarm from the GY, so outside cards that recover or revive Level 4 or lower Fiend/DARK monsters provide more Tribute fodder for the deck.

hooks.label: Fiend/DARK Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Steelswarm are high-Level Fiends that need Tributes, and cards like Fires of Doomsday give Fiend/DARK tokens that can be Tributed for a Tribute Summon, so outside token generators that specify Tribute Summon help.

profile.plan: A Rank 8 Machine Xyz deck whose three Main Deck monsters all trigger on Normal Summon, Special Summoning each other from the hand and then manipulating Levels and the Graveyard to build Googly-Eyes Drum Dragon.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Elephan, Lio and Monki each only do anything when they are Normal Summoned, so any outside card that gives an extra Normal Summon or Tribute Summon is another chance to fire one of them.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Super Defense Robot is a Machine-Type EARTH monster and Elephan even restricts its Xyz Material to Machine-Type monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Machines work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Graveyard to hand recovery
hooks.why: Lio Special Summons itself from the hand whenever exactly 1 Super Defense Robot or Orbital 7 is added from the Graveyard to the hand, so any outside card that recovers a monster from the GY sets that off.

hooks.label: Banished Machine monsters
hooks.why: Monki banishes a Machine-Type monster from the Graveyard as its cost and Googly-Eyes banishes a Super Defense Robot from the Graveyard to revive itself, so any Machine monster that does something when it is banished gets used for free.

hooks.label: Detached Xyz Material effects
hooks.why: Googly-Eyes Drum Dragon detaches an Xyz Material every turn for its ATK gain, so outside monsters whose effects trigger when they are detached as Xyz Material get a free activation.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Gaia boss monsters — a Synchro, a Fusion and an Xyz — that evolve into each other and pay you off for destroying monsters by battle with FIRE bodies in the GY.

hooks.label: Dumps FIRE monsters
hooks.why: Gaia Blaze adds FIRE monsters from the GY at the end of the Battle Phase and Gaia Prominence revives one when it destroys by battle, so anything that fills the GY with FIRE monsters feeds both.

hooks.label: Pyro FIRE support
hooks.why: Gaia Blaze and Gaia Prominence are both Pyro FIRE monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost Pyro or FIRE monsters work on the two main bosses.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz Material
hooks.why: Gaia Stream gains ATK equal to the combined Levels/Ranks of its materials x200 and detaches one every Damage Step it battles, so effects that keep attaching material keep it big and armed.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Gaia Prominence discards 1 monster to negate an opponent's hand or GY monster effect, so monsters that do something when discarded turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Extra attacks and Battle Phases
hooks.why: Gaia Blaze makes a second attack after destroying by battle and both Blaze and Prominence only pay off for monsters destroyed by battle, so more attacks or another Battle Phase means more triggers.

profile.plan: Ritual Summon Nouvelles Ritual Monsters using Recipe Ritual Spells that Tribute monsters, with support cards that search the pieces, punish Tributes, and support Fiend/DARK.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster and Spell search
hooks.why: The deck needs its Nouvelles Ritual Monsters and Recipe Ritual Spells, so cards that add them from the Deck or GY are key.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: The Recipe Ritual Spells Tribute monsters to Ritual Summon, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when Tributed give value for the cost.

hooks.label: Fiend and DARK support
hooks.why: All Nouvelles Ritual Monsters are Fiend/DARK, so cards that support those work with the whole deck.

hooks.label: Ritual Tribute from GY
hooks.why: The Recipe Ritual Spells need Tributes; cards that can banish themselves from the GY as the entire Tribute for a Ritual Summon provide a free material.

hooks.label: Counter Trap support
hooks.why: Chef's Special Recipe is a key negation, so cards that search or support Counter Traps help find it.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster deck that Special Summons its Fortune Fairies straight from the hand the moment they are drawn, so every extra draw becomes a body and an on-Summon effect.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Chee, Swee, Ann, En and Hu are all Spellcasters, Miracle Stone gives every Spellcaster you control 500 ATK/DEF per differently named Fortune Fairy, and Lucky Loan locks your Summons into Spellcasters.

hooks.label: Self-Summoning Spellcasters
hooks.why: Unacceptable Result only works while you control a Spellcaster and Lucky Loan Special Summons a Spellcaster of original Level 1-5 from your hand or Deck, so Spellcasters that put themselves on the board without a Normal Summon feed both.

hooks.label: Summon-triggered Spellcasters
hooks.why: Lucky Loan Special Summons a Spellcaster whose original Level is 1 lower than the target Fortune Fairy (Levels 2-6, so Levels 1-5) from the Deck, so a Spellcaster with an effect when it is Special Summoned is a free payoff.

hooks.label: Turn a Spellcaster into draws
hooks.why: Once a Fortune Fairy has used its on-Summon effect it is only a 0 ATK Spellcaster, so a card that sends a Spellcaster you control for two draws trades that body for another chance to draw a Fortune Fairy and Special Summon it.

hooks.label: Trap cards that draw
hooks.why: A Fortune Fairy only Special Summons itself when it is drawn, and Chee and Miracle Stone already draw during your own turn, so a Trap that makes you draw lets you flip up a second Fortune Fairy on the opponent's turn.

profile.plan: The deck uses Level 3 or lower EARTH Warrior Puppets as fuel to Special Summon bigger EARTH Warrior monsters from the Deck and GY, then leverages Gimmick Puppet Xyz Monsters for control and revival.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Puppet monster is an EARTH Warrior, and Puppet Pawn, Puppet Queen, Puppet Rook and Promotion all search, Summon or send EARTH Warrior monsters, so support for the Type and Attribute advances every card.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior GY effect
hooks.why: Puppet Rook sends an EARTH Warrior from the Deck to the GY and Promotion sends one from the field to the GY, so outside EARTH Warrior monsters with effects when sent to the GY get triggered for free.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck that Ritual Summons DARK Zombie Ritual Monsters by sending Normal Monster Cards from the hand, Deck and field to the GY, then equips Normal Monsters from the GY onto those Ritual Monsters to give them protection and a huge ATK body.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Pere-Zenet Em Heru, Am Duazenet and the Ritual Monsters all consume Normal Monster Cards as Ritual material, equip them from the GY, or count their ATK, so cards built around Normal Monsters feed the whole engine.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Zenet monster, including the Ritual Monsters, is a Zombie, and Zenet Per Akh even locks you out of non-Zombie monster effects for the turn, so Zombie search, revival and boosts apply to the entire deck.

hooks.label: Equip Spells
hooks.why: Zenetnakht Sphinx, Tauzenet Wadjet and Zenetmes Nekhbet only gain their protection while equipped with an Equip Card, and the deck equips Normal Monsters from the GY, so any outside Equip Spell (or card that fetches one) turns on those protections.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: Pere-Zenet Em Heru and Am Duazenet Ritual Summon a Zenet Ritual Monster straight from the hand or GY using only Normal Monster material from the Deck, so any card that puts a Ritual Monster into the hand or GY is a live starter.

hooks.label: Normal Monster revival
hooks.why: Pere-Zenet Em Heru draws whenever you Special Summon a non-Token Normal Monster, and Zenetnakht Sphinx and Tauzenet Wadjet Special Summon a Normal Monster from the GY after using their Quick Effects, so outside cards that bring back Normal Monsters both extend and draw.

profile.plan: Gladiator Beasts battle to shuffle themselves into the Deck and Special Summon each other, then contact fuse into big Fusion monsters, with support from a Field Spell that searches and summons from the Deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Flavian - Colosseum of the Gladiator Beasts discards a card to search a 'Gladiator Beast' monster, so outside cards with an effect when discarded turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Beast and Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Gladiator Beast Gistel and Claudius are Beasts, and Dareios is a Beast-Warrior, so cards that support those Types help the whole deck.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Claudius and Dareios are DARK, so cards that support DARK monsters work with the deck's boss monsters.

hooks.label: Special Summons Beasts from Deck
hooks.why: Flavian and Dareios both Special Summon Gladiator Beasts from the Deck, and Flavian's End Phase effect rewards having done so, so outside cards that fetch Beasts from the Deck give extra triggers.

hooks.label: Forces the opponent to attack
hooks.why: Flavian's second effect only triggers when an opponent's monster declares an attack, so outside cards that force attacks turn it on.

profile.plan: A grind deck of Continuous Dark Contract Spells and Traps that burn their own controller every Standby Phase, punish the opponent's Extra Deck Summons, and cash themselves in for draws and LP when they are destroyed or sent to the GY.

hooks.label: Sends Spells/Traps to the GY
hooks.why: Dark Contract with the Different Dimension shuffles 2 Dark Contract cards from the GY into the Deck to banish a card, and Dark Contract with Patent License recovers a monster when it is sent to the GY, so outside cards that dump your own Spells/Traps into the GY are fuel for both.

hooks.label: Blows up your own backrow
hooks.why: Contract Laundering destroys as many Dark Contract cards in your Spell & Trap Zone as possible to draw and gain LP, and Dark Contract with the Different Dimension pays LP when it is destroyed, so outside cards that destroy your own Spells/Traps turn those clauses on.

hooks.label: Punishes Extra Deck Summons
hooks.why: Dark Contract with Patent License burns the opponent for 1000 and locks them out of a card type whenever they Special Summon a Fusion, Synchro, Xyz or Link monster matching a D/D/D monster you control, so any card that penalises those Summons stacks with it.

hooks.label: Pendulum Scale support
hooks.why: Dark Contract with Patent License recovers a face-up Pendulum Monster from the Extra Deck, so the deck is built on Pendulum monsters and outside cards that set up or protect your Pendulum Scales keep that engine running.

hooks.label: Prevents the self-inflicted burn
hooks.why: Dark Contract with the Different Dimension makes you take 1000 damage every Standby Phase and Contract Laundering only heals after the fact, so outside cards that stop effect damage keep you alive to keep the Contracts on the field.

profile.plan: The deck Tribute Summons big Machine monsters that become almost immune to card effects, using 'Qli' monsters and multiple-Tribute cards to get them out.

hooks.label: Multiple Tribute providers
hooks.why: One of its Traps can be treated as 3 Tributes for a Tribute Summon, so outside cards that can also count as multiple Tributes let you summon the big monsters without needing three specific Tributes.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: The Apoqliphort monsters must be Normal Summoned, so cards that grant an additional Tribute Summon let you summon more than one in a turn.
phrases: in addition to your Normal Summon/Set

profile.plan: Level 8 Ars Magna monsters banish themselves from the hand to search and buff, then return for free whenever any Fusion, Synchro, Xyz or Link Monster is Special Summoned, feeding the 'Power Patron' Link Monsters the deck is built around.

hooks.label: Extra Deck Summon enablers
hooks.why: Ars Magna the Finite and the Infinite, the Corruption and the Purification and the Division and the Union each Special Summon themselves from banishment only when a Fusion/Link, Xyz/Link or Synchro/Link Monster is Special Summoned, so outside cards that perform those Summons turn your banished monsters into free bodies.

hooks.label: Deck to Graveyard milling
hooks.why: Ars Magna the Division and the Union banishes an 'Ars Magna' card from your GY to draw, and Ars Magna "Philosophorum" banishes up to three 'Ars Magna' monsters from your field or GY to negate effects, so milling Level 8 Ars Magna monsters from the Deck arms both.

hooks.label: Artmage crossover support
hooks.why: Ars Magna "Citrinitas" is always treated as an 'Artmage' (as well as a 'DoomZ' and 'Elfnote') card, so searchers, revivals and triggers printed for those names can reach and use it.

hooks.label: Power Patron Link Monsters
hooks.why: Every payoff is written for 'Power Patron' Link Monsters - tripled original ATK, the first three battle destructions prevented, up to three attacks on monsters, the extra banishes from the Ars Magna monsters and the GY revival of Philosophorum - so those are the monsters the deck exists to field.

profile.plan: A Zombie/DARK Rank 6 Xyz deck that sends Level 6 Zombie monsters from the Deck to the GY, revives them, and turns GY Special Summons into Xyz Summons while negating opponent's monsters.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every monster in this archetype is a Zombie, so cards that support Zombie-Type monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends Zombies to the GY
hooks.why: The archetype sends a Level 6 or higher Zombie from the Deck to the GY, and reuses those Zombies from the GY, so outside cards that send Zombies from the Deck to the GY set up the same engine.

hooks.label: Revives Zombies from the GY
hooks.why: The archetype Special Summons Zombie monsters from the GY and turns any GY Special Summon into an Xyz Summon, so outside revival effects keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Sends Xyz Monsters to the GY
hooks.why: A monster in the archetype can banish itself from the GY to revive a Zombie when an Xyz Monster is sent to the GY, so outside cards that send Xyz Monsters to the GY trigger that revival.

profile.plan: A WIND Aqua Flip deck that Special Summons Flip monsters face-down, flips them face-up for FLIP effects, and uses face-down cards as removal and GY setup.

hooks.label: Flip monster support
hooks.why: All three cards search, summon or revive Flip monsters, so outside cards that support Flip monsters keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Discarded Flip monsters
hooks.why: Earl discards 1 other Flip monster to Special Summon itself, so outside Flip monsters that trigger when discarded get their effects for free.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: Every WAKE CUP! monster is Aqua, so generic Aqua support that searches, revives or boosts Aqua monsters works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Face-down Defense Position support
hooks.why: Macchia and Kuro target face-down Defense Position monsters and Macchia sends face-down cards to the GY, so outside cards that place, protect or punish face-down Defense Position cards fit.

profile.plan: A Rank 7 Xyz deck that draws heavily with Level 7 monsters which Special Summon themselves when drawn, and locks both players out of searching to grind the opponent down.

hooks.label: Search lock
hooks.why: Every Raise Moon draw effect prevents you from adding cards from the Deck to the hand for the rest of the Duel, so outside cards that stop the opponent from searching cost you nothing.

hooks.label: Attaches itself as Xyz material
hooks.why: Jackpot can detach any number of materials to place opponent's cards on the bottom of the Deck, so outside cards that attach themselves to an Xyz give it more ammunition.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Jackpot attaches the top card of the opponent's Deck as material whenever the opponent's cards leave their Deck, so any card that mills the opponent gives you extra materials.

hooks.label: Level 7 self-summoners
hooks.why: The deck is built around Level 7 monsters that Special Summon themselves when drawn, so outside Level 7 monsters that can Special Summon themselves easily become extra material for Rank 7 Xyz.

profile.plan: A stun deck built on the Clear World Field Spell: its DARK monsters ignore Clear World's Attribute penalties while the opponent suffers them, it stalls with battle protection, pokes with direct attacks, and locks down Special Summoned monsters under Clear Vicious Knight.

hooks.label: Field Spell access
hooks.why: Clear Wall only searches while 'Clear World' is on the field, and its battle protection and its switch that makes the opponent eat Clear World's effects both need that Field Spell, so cards that add or set a Field Spell from the Deck start the engine.

hooks.label: Field Spell protection
hooks.why: The whole deck pivots on 'Clear World' staying in the Field Zone: Clear Wall's search, its no-battle-damage clause and the Level 7 clause that hands the opponent Clear World's penalties all turn off the moment the Field Spell leaves the field.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Clear Phantom's search discards two cards including itself, so monsters with an effect when they are discarded are paid for by a cost the deck was already paying.

hooks.label: Opponent's Attribute changers
hooks.why: Clear World punishes the turn player based on the Attributes of the monsters they control, so turning the opponent's monsters into FIRE, WATER, DARK or LIGHT monsters makes them take the damage, the discards and the hand reveals.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Clear monster is DARK, so Attribute-based support that searches, revives or boosts DARK monsters applies to the entire deck.

profile.plan: A fan-made pile of huge Level 8-10 Warrior, Fiend and Fairy bosses that Special Summon themselves by paying steep costs — Tributing Fiends and Fairies or milling high-ATK monsters — then grind the opponent down with battle-destruction burn and Level 10 tokens.

hooks.label: Fiend and Fairy support
hooks.why: Dark Creator is Special Summoned by Tributing 2 Fiend and/or Fairy monsters and makes Fiend tokens, while Demiurge Ema is a Fairy, so Type support reaches every boss in the deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Fiend or Fairy
hooks.why: Dark Creator needs two Fiend and/or Fairy monsters on the field to Tribute for its own Special Summon, and free bodies of those Types supply the cost without using your Normal Summon.

hooks.label: Payoff when Tributed
hooks.why: Dark Creator's Summoning procedure Tributes two Fiend and/or Fairy monsters, so outside monsters that do something when they are Tributed get their effect for free as material.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Dark Creator's token effect stops you Special Summoning for the rest of the turn and Tyler the Great Warrior cannot be Special Summoned at all, so extra Normal Summons and Tribute Summon helpers are how the big bodies actually reach the field.

hooks.label: Piercing and multi-attackers
hooks.why: Tyler the Great Warrior burns for the ATK of every monster it destroys by battle and Dark Creator burns 700 whenever any monster is destroyed by battle, so extra attacks and piercing battle damage convert directly into damage.

archetype: Hunting Scout of the Deep Forest

profile.plan: Fusion Summon EARTH Warrior Fusions, then use their Main Phase immunity and the taunt that forces every opponent's monster to attack your biggest one to win the Battle Phase, reviving the EARTH Warriors that fall.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior support
hooks.why: Every card here is an EARTH Warrior: Hunting Horn fuses Warrior monsters, and both Chevreuil and Faisan revive EARTH Warrior monsters, so support for that Type and Attribute works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Dumps EARTH Warriors to the GY
hooks.why: Faisan Special Summons 2 EARTH Warriors from the GY and Chevreuil Special Summons 1 from the GY or banishment, so sending EARTH Warrior monsters from the Deck to the GY stocks both revival effects.

hooks.label: Punishes the opponent's attacks
hooks.why: Chevreuil forces every opponent's monster that can attack to attack your highest-ATK monster, so any outside card that fires when the opponent declares an attack is guaranteed to be live.

hooks.label: Rewards battle destruction
hooks.why: Chevreuil only revives an EARTH Warrior when another EARTH Warrior you control destroys an opponent's monster by battle, so outside cards that pay off that same destruction reward the deck's battle plan twice over.

profile.plan: A Lava-Golem-style deck: it plants a 3000 ATK Sun God Fusion on the opponent's field to burn them, and keeps putting 'The Immortal Sun God' in the GY so its chanters return from the Graveyard every End Phase.

hooks.label: Discard fodder
hooks.why: Helpoemer, Chanter of the Sun God discards 1 other card to Special Summon itself, so outside cards that do something when they are discarded get turned on for free.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Helpoemer, Gil Garth, Viser Des Shock and Lava Golem are all Fiends, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work across most of the deck.

hooks.label: Deck-to-Graveyard mill
hooks.why: Helpoemer, Makyura and Gil Garth only return themselves in the End Phase if 'The Immortal Sun God' was sent to your GY that turn, so any outside card that sends it from the Deck to the GY starts the whole loop.

hooks.label: Tributes the opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Viser Des Shock, Tormentor of the Sun God Special Summons itself from the hand and burns for 800 whenever a monster is sent to the opponent's GY while you control a Sun God card, and a Tribute puts their monster straight into that GY.

hooks.label: Monsters given to the opponent
hooks.why: Lava Golem, Steelcage of the Sun God Fusion Summons to the opponent's field by sending 1 Sun God monster plus 2 face-up monsters on the field to the GY, so outside cards that hand the opponent monsters or Tokens supply the fodder and their later departure sets off Viser Des Shock.

profile.plan: A Level 2 Fiend swarm that Special Summons itself from the hand by sending Fiends to the Graveyard, then revives Level 2 Fiends to Xyz Summon Rank 2 monsters.

hooks.label: Sends Fiends to the GY
hooks.why: Malicevorous Knife and Spoon revive Malicevorous and Level 2 Fiends from the Graveyard, so outside cards that send Fiends from the Deck or hand to the GY give them targets.

hooks.label: Fiends that trigger in GY
hooks.why: Malicevorous Fork sends a Fiend from your hand to the GY as a cost to Special Summon itself, so outside Fiends with an effect when sent to the GY get that effect for free.

hooks.label: Special Summons Level 2 Fiends
hooks.why: Spoon triggers whenever a Malicevorous monster is Special Summoned, so outside cards that Special Summon Level 2 Fiends from the GY or Deck can trigger it or extend the swarm.

hooks.label: DARK Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Malicevorous monster is a DARK Fiend, so cards that search, revive or boost DARK Fiends work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 2 Fiend support
hooks.why: The deck is built around Level 2 Fiend-Type monsters, so cards that explicitly mention both 'Level 2' and 'Fiend' support the entire strategy.

profile.plan: A 'Number' Xyz deck: it stacks Xyz Materials and Rank-Up-Magic to climb into CXyz and 'Number C' boss monsters, using a small Umbral Horror engine (searched by a Field Spell) as its monster base.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Barian Untopia and Barian's Seventh Untopia are the deck's protection and its Umbral Horror searcher, and both are Field Spells, so anything that finds or puts a Field Spell on the field sets up the whole plan.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: Barian Untopia attaches an opponent's monster as Xyz Material every time a Rank-Up-Magic Spell Special Summons an Xyz Monster, and then protects the CXyz or 'Number C' it brought out.

hooks.label: Umbral Horror monsters
hooks.why: Barian's Hope and Barian's Seal both Special Summon 'Umbral Horror' monsters from the hand or GY, and Barian's Seventh Untopia adds one from the Deck, so the deck's material base is literally that name.

hooks.label: DARK send-to-GY
hooks.why: Barian's Hope and Barian's Seal revive 'Umbral Horror' monsters from the GY, which are DARK Fiends, so effects that send DARK monsters from the Deck to the GY stock the GY for those summons.

hooks.label: Discard payoffs
hooks.why: Barian's Seventh Untopia adds an Umbral Horror and then discards a card every turn, so any monster that does something when it is discarded gets that effect for free.

hooks.label: Number C Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Barian's Seal can only negate while you control a CXyz or 'Number C101'-'Number C107' monster, and Barian Untopia protects and feeds Xyz Material to exactly those monsters.

profile.plan: A spell engine that summons 'Medius the Pure' and revives Fusion, Synchro and Xyz monsters from the Graveyard by banishing its own cards, while manipulating Levels and Tuner status.

hooks.label: Sends Spells to the GY
hooks.why: Theorealize Past Lull, Overdrive and Liberation all have effects that activate by banishing themselves from the GY, so filling the GY with Spells turns them on.

hooks.label: Sends Extra Deck monsters to GY
hooks.why: Past Lull can revive a Fusion, Synchro or Xyz Monster from the GY, so cards that put those monsters there give it targets.

profile.plan: A toolbox of cards that all 'mention Dark Time Wizard': it Special Summons its own monsters from the hand, searches its Spells/Traps, locks the opponent out of Traps with a Jinzo retrain, and grinds with Tokens, dice and counter Traps.

hooks.label: Fusion Summoning
hooks.why: Sleepy Scapegoats locks you into Fusion Monsters for the rest of the turn, so outside cards that Fusion Summon are the only Extra Deck plays the deck can actually make.

hooks.label: Umi support
hooks.why: Fisherman of Legend can Special Summon itself from the hand whenever the opponent activates a monster effect or attacks while 'Umi' is on the field, so any card that supplies or mentions Umi keeps that trigger live.

hooks.label: Jinzo support
hooks.why: Jinzo - Energy Shocker's name becomes 'Jinzo' while it is on the field or in the GY, so cards that support 'Jinzo' search, revive or protect it.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Alligator's Dragon Knight discards 1 card after adding its Spells/Traps, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded get value for free.

hooks.label: Dice-roll support
hooks.why: Graceful & Skull Dice and Reversal Box only pay off on dice rolls and coin calls, so outside cards that re-roll or rig a six-sided die make those effects reliable.

profile.plan: A gimmick deck that gathers three named 0-ATK Rock monsters, shrugs off the effect damage they deal to you, and resolves Triangle O to blow up the whole field and dump all of that self-inflicted damage onto the opponent.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Crystal Skull, Ashoka Pillar and Cabrera Stone are all Rocks, and Crystal Skull recruits a Rock monster with 0 ATK from the Deck, so cards that search, revive or boost Rocks work on the entire archetype.

hooks.label: Sends Rocks to the GY
hooks.why: Triangle O's Graveyard effect needs Crystal Skull, Ashoka Pillar and Cabrera Stone in the GY to shuffle back and draw 3, so anything that ships Rock monsters there sets it up without triggering their destruction damage.

hooks.label: Stops your effect damage
hooks.why: Crystal Skull's End Phase effect only works if you took no effect damage that turn, yet its own Summon burns you for 1000, so cards that prevent effect damage switch that condition on.

hooks.label: Payoffs for taking damage
hooks.why: Crystal Skull burns you for 1000 on Summon and Ashoka Pillar and Cabrera Stone deal 1000-2000 when they are destroyed by battle or card effect, so cards that trigger when you take effect damage get their condition for free.

profile.plan: A WATER Sea Serpent deck built on 'Umi' and 'Atlantis, City of the Sea Dragon': its monsters become 'Umi' on the field, pay every effect by sending a face-up 'Umi' to the GY, then wipe the whole field while their own Umi-named bodies sit safely through it.

hooks.label: Extra Umi cards
hooks.why: Levia-Dragon, Levia-Dragoon and Neo-Daedalus Rage all pay by sending 1 face-up 'Umi' you control to the GY, so any other card that is or counts as 'Umi' is extra fuel for every effect.

hooks.label: Umi searchers
hooks.why: The deck needs a face-up 'Umi' on the field before Daedalus can Special Summon itself or use its Link effects, so cards that add 'Umi' from the Deck keep the engine running.

hooks.label: WATER and Sea Serpent support
hooks.why: Every Daedalus monster is a WATER Sea Serpent, 'Levia-Dragoon - Daedalus' asks for 3 WATER monsters and 'Daedalus Maelstrom' spares only WATER monsters, so generic support for that Type and Attribute powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning WATER bodies
hooks.why: 'Levia-Dragoon - Daedalus' needs 3 WATER monsters and 'Neo-Daedalus Rage' needs 4 monsters, so WATER monsters that Special Summon themselves are free Link material.

hooks.label: Monsters that like being sent to the GY
hooks.why: Neo-Daedalus Rage sends every card on the field to the GY except 'Umi', and only the Daedalus monsters survive that as Umi, so outside monsters with an effect when sent from the field to the GY get value out of the wipe.

profile.plan: A Normal Monster engine: Mocha MOD dumps a weak Normal Monster from the Deck to summon itself and plants a Bunnillin Continuous Spell/Trap, while Soft and Extract pay you off with revival, draws, ATK and removal while you control two or more Normal Monsters.

hooks.label: Special Summons Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Bunnillin Soft and Bunnillin Extract only pay off while you control 2 or more non-Token Normal Monsters, and Soft revives two of them at once, so outside cards that Special Summon Normal Monsters from the hand, Deck or GY are the fastest way to switch the deck on.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Bunnillin Extract Special Summons a Normal Monster from your hand or Deck whenever a card is sent from your opponent's Deck to the GY, so any outside card that mills the opponent turns into a free body.

hooks.label: Sends Normal Monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Bunnillin: Mocha MOD Special Summons itself by sending a Normal Monster with 2000 or less ATK from the Deck to the GY, and those same GY Normal Monsters are what Bunnillin Soft revives two at a time.

hooks.label: Normal Monster searchers
hooks.why: The whole deck is built on having Normal Monsters in hand for Bunnillin Extract to Special Summon and in the GY for Bunnillin Soft, so outside cards that add a Normal Monster from the Deck to hand set up both.

profile.plan: A Ritual deck of Insect monsters that Ritual Summons with Reindsurm Conquest by shuffling Insect and Dragon monsters out of the Graveyard, so it constantly mills and dumps its own cards to reload the next Ritual Summon.

hooks.label: Mills Insect and Dragon monsters
hooks.why: Reindsurm Conquest and the Graveyard effects of Amurusa, Carcasas and Luvian Ritual Summon by shuffling Insect and/or Dragon monsters from the GY into the Deck, so any card that fills the GY with those Types is fuel.

hooks.label: Sends your Insects to the GY
hooks.why: Amurusa, Carcasas and Luvian Ritual Summon an Insect Ritual Monster from the hand when they are sent to the GY, and Carnation, Conquest and Encounter all send your own Insect monsters there to keep the loop going.

hooks.label: Insect or Dragon with a GY effect
hooks.why: Butterfly sends 2 monsters from the Deck to the GY including an Insect and Carcasas sends 2 Reindsurm cards there, so outside Insect or Dragon monsters that do something when sent to the GY trigger for free.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every Reindsurm Ritual Monster is an Insect and Carnation searches Insect monsters from the Deck, so cards that support, revive or search Insects feed the whole deck.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster and Spell searchers
hooks.why: The deck only Ritual Summons through Reindsurm Conquest, so outside cards that add a Ritual Monster or Ritual Spell from the Deck or GY assemble the pieces the deck cannot search for itself.

profile.plan: A LIGHT/FIRE Illusion deck that parks its Knights face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, then Special Summons them back to Synchro Summon and cash in their Graveyard effects.

hooks.label: Extra Deck millers
hooks.why: Zaltys and Aitvaras both trigger when they are sent to the GY from the Extra Deck, so outside cards that send Extra Deck monsters to the GY (or use them as material) fire those effects for free.

hooks.label: Parks monsters as Continuous Spells
hooks.why: Mart and Anu place Knights face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells and Purifire, Mart and Anu Special Summon those Monster Cards back, so outside cards that put monsters into the Spell & Trap Zone feed the same loop.

hooks.label: Sinful Spoils cards
hooks.why: Purifire adds 1 'Sinful Spoils' card or 'Winter Raven' Spell/Trap from the Deck, so a Sinful Spoils engine is directly searchable and shares the Spell & Trap Zone plan.

hooks.label: Illusion support
hooks.why: Every Winter Raven monster is an Illusion, and Illusion of the Winter Raven Witch locks you into Illusion monster effects, so cards that search, revive or boost Illusion monsters work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: The deck cheats out The Winged Dragon of Ra and its Sun God Fusion, then uses their LP costs, huge ATK and board control to dominate.

hooks.label: Divine-Beast support
hooks.why: The Winged Dragon of Ra and its Fusion are Divine-Beast DIVINE monsters, so outside cards that search, protect or revive Divine-Beast or DIVINE cards directly support the deck's bosses.

hooks.label: Level 10 support
hooks.why: The deck's bosses are Level 10, so outside cards that protect or boost Level 10 or higher monsters keep them on the field.

hooks.label: Divine-Beast Tribute Summon
hooks.why: The deck's Ra monster is a Divine-Beast that can be Tribute Summoned, so outside cards that support Tribute Summoning a Divine-Beast monster fit.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Dangers of the Divine requires Tributing 1 monster, so outside cards that Special Summon Tokens provide free Tribute fodder without using a real monster.

hooks.label: LP gain
hooks.why: Dangers of the Divine pays half your LP and the Fusion can pay down to 1 LP, so outside cards that gain Life Points let you keep paying those costs and survive.

hooks.label: Fusion substitutes
hooks.why: The deck's Fusion requires a specifically named monster as material, so outside monsters that can substitute for a named Fusion Material help assemble it.

archetype: Atlantis, City of the Sea Dragon

profile.plan: A 'Umi' deck: every monster renames itself to 'Umi' on the field while the Field Spell shrinks Levels by 1, turning Atlantis into a Sea Serpent/WATER toolbox that summons and searches from the Deck and GY.

hooks.label: Umi cards
hooks.why: Warchief, Siren Vortex, Monster Arms and Advent of Atlantis all have their name become 'Umi' while on the field or in the Spell & Trap Zone, so any outside card that mentions or requires 'Umi' is live.

hooks.label: Sea Serpent and WATER support
hooks.why: Every Atlantis monster is a WATER Sea Serpent, and Call of Atlantis gives all your WATER monsters 500 ATK/DEF, so Type or Attribute support lifts the whole deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell protection
hooks.why: The deck lives off its Field Zone - Advent of Atlantis places Atlantis or 'Umi' from the Deck and Atlantis re-places itself from the GY - so cards that add, place or protect Field Spells keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Special Summoned WATER monsters
hooks.why: Monster Arms of Atlantis revives an Atlantis monster from the GY and Siren Vortex Special Summons a WATER monster from the hand, so outside WATER monsters that pay off being Special Summoned get a free body.

profile.plan: A Psychic deck that banishes its own Deck face-down, then recovers and Special Summons Trirealm Rift monsters from the banished pile while matching Attributes to negate the opponent.

hooks.label: Banishes your Deck face-down
hooks.why: Trirealm Rift Darkness counts total face-down banished cards, and every Trirealm Rift monster banishes from the top of the Deck, so outside cards that banish face-down from your Deck accelerate those thresholds and fuel the archetype's banished-pool effects.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: The archetype's Normal and Special Summon effects banish the top cards of your Deck face-down, so outside monsters with 'If this card is banished' effects get to trigger for free.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Trirealm Rift monster is Psychic, so cards that search, revive or protect Psychic monsters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon for Psychic
hooks.why: The deck's Continuous Spell gives an extra Normal Summon for Trirealm Rift monsters, and the low-Level monsters' effects trigger on Normal Summon, so outside cards that grant extra Normal Summons to Psychic monsters help swarm.

hooks.label: Banished-count payoffs
hooks.why: The deck rapidly banishes cards face-down, so outside monsters that gain ATK or effects from the number of banished cards become large threats.

hooks.label: Attribute-changing cards
hooks.why: Trirealm Rift Judgment and Sky Thunder Yomi match a face-down banished Trirealm monster's Attribute to the opponent's monster to negate or remove it, so outside cards that change the opponent's monster's Attribute let you always match.

profile.plan: A Buster Blader deck: it uses the Destruction Sword monsters as equips and material to get 'Buster Blader' onto the field, makes the opponent's monsters Dragon-Type with Buster Dragon, then Fusion Summons the Dragon Destroyer Swordsman to run them over.

hooks.label: Buster Blader monsters
hooks.why: Dragon Buster, Wizard Buster and Robot Buster only equip to a 'Buster Blader', Buster Whelp and Buster Dragon Special Summon one, and Destruction Swordsman Fusion needs it as Fusion Material.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: The card the whole deck is built around, 'Buster Blader', is a Level 7 Normal Monster, so anything that searches, revives or protects Normal Monsters finds the deck's key piece.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon support
hooks.why: Destruction Swordsman Fusion and Destruction Sword Memories both Fusion Summon 'Buster Blader, the Dragon Destroyer Swordsman', so extra Fusion Summons and Fusion Material tools keep the boss coming.

hooks.label: Sends Traps to the GY
hooks.why: Prologue of the Destruction Swordsman, Destruction Sword Memories and Destruction Sword Flash all do their second job by banishing themselves from the Graveyard, so dumping Trap Cards from the Deck to the GY turns those effects on.

hooks.label: Dragon-Type support
hooks.why: Dragon Buster, Buster Whelp, Buster Dragon and Protector Whelp are all Dragon-Type, the deck's Tuner plays are Dragon, and the Fusion boss lists a Dragon monster as material.
